FAM-001.y1105: Imperial house of Aldmark. Emperor Aldwin reigns and his only son Harald, betrothed to Rowena of Ashmere, is the house's whole future.
FAM-001.arms: a black iron ring on wheat gold, with a thin green border
FAM-001.power: The imperial crown: crown lands around Kingsmere and the Millrun studs; about 1.3 million marks a year in hearth tax, landing tenths and scutage; 110,000 standing troops and a levy of 460,000; the 1,200 knights of the Iron Guard; the Cold Bay squadron of 40 ships; headship of the Seven Halls in the empire and the appointment of the High Hall-Keeper.
FAM-001.branches: the imperial line at Kingsmere; the Dunfield Ironsides, horse-breeders descended from Brand's elder brother, without the iron bones
FAM-001.history: The Ironsides began as horse-breeders at Dunfield on the Millrun. Brand, born in 890, was the second son of Ivo of Dunfield, who kept a stud of 200 mares. As a boy Brand fell 9 m from a hayloft and walked away. At 15 he went through the Millrun ice and sank like an anvil until his brother Wulf dragged him out by the hair. The family learned then what the dynasty still hides: its bones are heavy as stone. Brand won the Millrun fords in 913, took a Wind rider's mace on his ribs and got up, and was named Ironside. He married Edith Fairrush, the king's daughter, in 914 and was crowned in 927 when she died. He was killed at the Millrun in 936. His son Harald, born 916, took the plain in the Wars of Founding and was crowned first Emperor in 951. Harald's breaking of the Glenwash truce in 945 and his marriage to Sigrun Greymane are the house's founding sin and founding bargain. Harald's son Hakon the Oathkeeper (948–1032) gave the Glenwash back to the Greymanes, made the emperor head of the Seven Halls and hid the truce record. He lost both sons of his first marriage, the second, Sigmund, to the Glenwash in 1009, and married Wulfhild Fairrush in his old age. Their son Conrad the Stubborn (1012–1081) fought both Horde Wars and the Oak Line war, married Astrid Greymane and drowned through the Fairrush ice in 1081. Aldwin, born 1049, is the fourth emperor. In 1076 he married Elswyth Tidewell of Greyhaven. She married into the house and is its best counselor; she was born a Tidewell and does not carry the iron bones. After two stillbirths she bore Harald in 1078 and no child after. The whole dynasty now stands on one man of 26 who cannot swim and who nearly drowned in a horse pond at the Lance Yard in 1092. The house has no cadet branch with the iron bones. Brand's elder brother's line still breeds horses at Dunfield without the trait, and Hakon's two elder sons died without sons. Through Edith, Wulfhild and Astrid, the Ironsides carry Fairrush and Greymane blood, which is why the Old Plains Lords are the emperor's kin as well as his critics. The Ironsides are soldiers more than scholars. Each emperor has sworn on the iron ring in the Oath Hall and each has been buried in a mound with sword and ring. They are proud, careful of their dignity and haunted by water. No Ironside boy is taught to swim, because it cannot be done. Instead each learns never to wear mail near a river and to cross by bridges, never by fords.
dead: Brand Ironside (890–936): Won the Millrun fords in 913; first Ironside king. *Ruler:* Brand Ironside (Brand I), Kingdom of Kingsmere, 927–936 (RUL-0017).
Harald Ironside (916–990): First Emperor of Aldmark; broke the Glenwash truce. *Ruler:* Harald Ironside (Harald I the Founder), Empire of Aldmark, 951–990 (RUL-0001).
Sigrun Greymane (922–985): Married into the house in 947; betrayed her brother Ulf for the marriage.
Hakon Ironside the Oathkeeper (948–1032): Iron Reform of 1002; hid the truce record. *Ruler:* Hakon Ironside (Hakon I the Oathkeeper), Empire of Aldmark, 990–1032 (RUL-0002).
Prince Sigmund Ironside (975–1009): Drowned in the Glenwash flood; the first Ironside the prophecy took.
Conrad Ironside the Stubborn (1012–1081): Fought both Horde Wars; drowned in secret. *Ruler:* Conrad Ironside (Conrad I the Stubborn), Empire of Aldmark, 1032–1081 (RUL-0003).
marriages: 914, with House Fairrush: Brand Ironside married Edith Fairrush, heiress of Kingsmere.
947, with House Greymane: Harald married Sigrun Greymane, her dowry the lower Glenwash.
968, with House of Eagleburg: Hakon married Aelfled, granddaughter of Lord Oswin of Eagleburg.
1009, with House Fairrush: Hakon married Wulfhild Fairrush of Yewmarch, mother of Conrad.
1044, with House Greymane: Conrad married Astrid Greymane, mother of Aldwin.
FAM-001.allies: House Ravenscar, House Harrow, House Tidewell, House Ashford
FAM-001.rivals: House Fairrush, House Winterborn, The Line of Gorath, House Valdane
FAM-001.secrets: Harald broke the Glenwash truce of 945, Conrad drowned through the ice, and Aldwin signed the hidden Ashmere clause. Prince Harald nearly drowned in a horse pond in 1092, which only Sir Roland Ashby knows.

FAM-002.y1105: Lords of Yewmarch and its river tolls, heirs of the Kings of Kingsmere. Lady Audra leads the Old Plains Lords in the Oath Moot with Jarl Sigurd Greymane.
FAM-002.arms: a silver barge on a blue river under a golden wheat sheaf
FAM-002.founder: Osbert Fairrush (744–806), first King of Kingsmere
FAM-002.power: Yewmarch, a city of 25,600, and about 30,000 acres around it; the Yewmarch river tolls granted in 927, worth about 9,000 marks a year; a levy of about 2,500; a strong voice in the Oath Moot, which must approve every new tax; friends among the Oath Hall scribes.
FAM-002.branches: the Yewmarch line, heirs of Lord Oswald Fairrush, the male claimant of 927
FAM-002.history: The Fairrushes were river lords of Kingsmere's quays from about 700, when the town was a barge landing on the lower Fairrush. They grew rich carrying the upper valley's grain and lending it in bad years. After the Hungry Years of 766 to 768 eleven valley lords owed them more than they could repay, and on New Year's Day 780 those lords swore to Osbert Fairrush on the iron ring of his timber Oath Hall on the quay. Osbert's silver crown was beaten from 400 Solen sun coins. Six Fairrush kings and one queen held Kingsmere for 147 years: Osbert I the Barge-King; Osbert II; Edmund the Waller, who rebuilt the Oath Hall in stone; Oswy the Horse-Lord; Leofwin the Bent Knee, who paid the Wind Khan tribute; Aldhelm the Unbowed, who stopped it and died of the Black Cough in 916 with both his sons; and Aldhelm's daughter Edith, who ruled 916 to 927 with her husband Brand Ironside. When Edith died in childbirth, the lords crowned Brand over her cousin Oswald Fairrush of Yewmarch. Oswald was paid with the Yewmarch river tolls, and his line has held them since. In 951 the Fairrush lords swore on the iron ring that Osbert's crown had been melted. They lied, and the crown lies in the Yewmarch chapel wall. In 1009 the house gave a daughter, Wulfhild, to old Emperor Hakon; her son Conrad was half Fairrush. It did the family little good, for Conrad favored the Harrows and the Ravenscars. Lady Audra Fairrush, born 1061, was the only surviving child of Lord Oswald Fairrush of Yewmarch and inherited at 22 in 1083. In 1084 she married Sir Hamond of Easterham, a Glenwash knight who serves the Greymanes; their sons Osbert, 18, and Aldhelm carry the Fairrush name. Audra joined Jarl Sigurd Greymane's Old Plains Lords in 1089 when the Edict of the Halls angered the northern lords, and in 1093 she helped force the Oath Moot tax vote that made the emperor end the Northreach Rising. She pays the Oath Hall scribe Merewyn Ashcombe for copies of the old rolls, to prove that the Oath Moot must approve every war tax. The Fairrushes count themselves the true heirs of Kingsmere and the Ironsides as the horse-breeder's line that married in.
dead: Osbert Fairrush the Barge-King (744–806): First King of Kingsmere. *Ruler:* Osbert Fairrush (Osbert I the Barge-King), Kingdom of Kingsmere, 780–806 (RUL-0010).
Edmund Fairrush the Waller (797–857): Built the walls of Kingsmere and rebuilt its Oath Hall in stone. *Ruler:* Edmund Fairrush (Edmund I the Waller), Kingdom of Kingsmere, 830–857 (RUL-0012).
Leofwin Fairrush the Bent Knee (850–903): Paid tribute to the Wind Khan from 881. *Ruler:* Leofwin Fairrush (Leofwin I the Bent Knee), Kingdom of Kingsmere, 879–903 (RUL-0014).
Aldhelm Fairrush the Unbowed (872–916): Stopped the tribute; died of the Black Cough. *Ruler:* Aldhelm Fairrush (Aldhelm I the Unbowed), Kingdom of Kingsmere, 903–916 (RUL-0015).
Queen Edith Fairrush (897–927): Last Fairrush ruler; mother of Harald Ironside. *Ruler:* Edith Fairrush (Edith I the Last Fairrush), Kingdom of Kingsmere, 916–927 (RUL-0016).
Oswald Fairrush of Yewmarch (903–969): Passed over for the crown in 927; founded the Yewmarch line.
marriages: 914, with House Ironside: Edith Fairrush married Brand Ironside.
1009, with House Ironside: Wulfhild Fairrush married Emperor Hakon.
1084, with House Greymane: Audra Fairrush married Sir Hamond of Easterham, a sworn knight of the Greymanes.
FAM-002.secrets: The silver crown of Osbert, sworn melted in 951, lies in the Yewmarch chapel wall. Audra buys copies of Oath Hall records from a sworn scribe and may soon hold the tribute rolls of 881 to 912.

FAM-003.y1105: Marcher lords of the Southern March. Lord Garrick commands the 16,000 men on the Gordush and leads the March Hawks, who want war after May Fair.
FAM-003.arms: a red bull's head over a black harrow on field green
FAM-003.power: The Southern March with its seat at Copperham and the old keep of Harrowsett; command of about 16,000 men on the Gordush line, including the 4,800 paid Gordush Stake-Men; the licenses of the march's half-orcs under the law of 1053; about 22,000 acres of former half-orc farms; tax barns at Hazelhollow and Copperham; a seat on the Imperial Council.
FAM-003.branches: the Copperham line, lords of the Southern March; the Harrowsett line, cousins who keep the old keep and supply the brides
FAM-003.history: The Harrows were soldiers before they were lords. Oswy Harrow (925–988) was captain of Dunwatch when Harald took the Crown Wall forts in 956. He held the road through two winters of orc raids and in 958 was granted Harrowsett Keep and 40 hearths. His sons and grandsons were strong men who married the daughters of other Crown Wall captains and, more and more often, their own Harrowsett cousins, because the march had few families of rank. The bull-blood was in the house from Oswy, hidden in carriers who were merely strong. It showed in full when two carriers married. In 1000 Wulfstan Harrow married his cousin Elfgiva, and their son Gunnar, born 1001, had the arms of a grown man at six. Gunnar Harrow the Bull (1001–1049) was the house's first famous bull. In May 1033 he pulled an old orc war-chief from his horse bare-handed at a border meeting near Crossmarch. In September 1049 he held the Gordush ford with 300 house-men while Emperor Conrad escaped, and died with most of them. Conrad paid the debt in November 1052 with the whole Southern March and its seat at Copperham. Gunnar's son Wulfric was 15, so Gunnar's younger brother Edgar Harrow (1010–1088), a carrier but no bull, took the march for the house. The Harrows pressed Conrad for the Half-Orc License Law of 1053 and took about 22,000 acres of half-orc farms in ten years. Edgar commanded in the Second Horde War (WAR-38) and lost the upper Gordush; in September 1074 Conrad made him hand the march to Wulfric. Wulfric (1037–1086), a full bull like his father, died of a failing heart at 49. Garrick Harrow, born 1058, Gunnar's grandson, took the march at 28. He is a full bull too, and in 1080 he married his Harrowsett cousin Elfrida to keep the blood. He enforced the License Law harder than any lord before him, led Aldmark's second column in the Northreach Rising and still blames Marshal Stane for the Stagflow. In April 1103 Tarn Halfblood burned his tax barns at Hazelhollow and Copperham, and he has sworn on the iron ring to hang Tarn from the Crossmarch gate. His heart flutters on stairs, and his physician gives him two years. His son Gunnar, born 1084, is a full bull; his two daughters are carriers. The Harrows are loved by their soldiers and hated by the half-orcs of the march. They are honest about what they want: land, war and glory. They pay their companies on time, bury their dead facing the Gordush and name their eldest sons for Gunnar.
dead: Oswy Harrow (925–988): Captain of Dunwatch; founded the house at Harrowsett.
Gunnar Harrow the Bull (1001–1049): Threw an orc war-chief bare-handed; died holding the Gordush ford.
Edgar Harrow (1010–1088): First Lord of the Southern March; lost the upper Gordush.
Wulfric Harrow (1037–1086): Lord of the march 1074–1086; died of a bull's heart.
marriages: 1000, with House Harrow: Wulfstan Harrow married his Harrowsett cousin Elfgiva; parents of Gunnar the Bull.
1080, with House Harrow: Garrick married his Harrowsett cousin Elfrida to keep the full bull-blood.
FAM-003.rivals: House Fairrush, The Line of Gorath
FAM-003.secrets: Garrick's heart is failing and he has told no one. The License Law of 1053 was pressed by the Harrows to take half-orc farms, not to keep order.

FAM-004.y1105: Aldmark's spies and night scouts. Lady Ysolde runs the empire's whispers from the Imperial Council, her son the Night School and her daughter the Night Riders.
FAM-004.arms: a black raven with silver eyes on a night-blue field
FAM-004.founder: Hereward Ravenscar (890–958), verderer of the Northmoor chase
FAM-004.power: Wardenship of the Oak Line Shires with its seat at Northmoor, a city of 22,700; the 300 Ravenscar Night Riders; the Night School of Northmoor; a web of agents at Highcastle, Coldhaven, Ostra and in the Southern March, paid from a cipher ledger at Kingsmere; a seat on the Imperial Council as Mistress of Night and Whispers.
FAM-004.history: The Ravenscars were foresters of the Northmoor chase on the Oak Line, named for Raven Scar, a burned hill above their hall. Hereward Ravenscar (890–958), verderer to the last Fairrush kings, tracked deer and poachers by starlight, and his children squinted at noon and walked the woods at night. The house noticed the gift before it had a name for it: owl-eyes. Hereward's granddaughter Maud Ravenscar the Owl (955–1012) made it a weapon. In February 988 she led 200 riders on a moonless night into the orc camp at Graknak and freed 400 captives from the Aldmark march. She used a runaway half-orc guide as well as her eyes. Hakon made her warden of the night patrols, and she built a web of foresters, hall-singers and pedlars who told her what moved on the march. She died in the Long Winter after running grain carts to the Oak Line villages by night, and Hakon gave her house the wardenship of the Oak Line Shires. Maud's son Alaric Ravenscar (992–1066) turned her web into the empire's spy service, kept in a cipher ledger at Kingsmere. His scouts warned Conrad before the Gordush Bend in 1049, and Conrad crossed anyway. Alaric's son Corwin (1040–1072) died in the night storming of Fort Graknak in May 1072, in the same camp his grandmother had raided. His sister Ysolde, 26, inherited. Ysolde Ravenscar, born 1046, married Sir Wystan Holloway of Rosemarch in 1068; he took the Ravenscar name and died of a winter fever in 1089. Their children are Corbin, born 1070, master of the Night School of Northmoor, and Isa, born 1076, captain of the 600 Night Riders. In February 1081 Ysolde arranged the story of Conrad's winter fever and pensioned the two huntsmen at Swanvale. In January 1090 her cook poisoned King Bjorn of Northreach at Kingsmere without the emperor's order. She knows the hidden Ashmere clause, has agents at Highcastle and Coldhaven, and holds Jarl Asta Coldwater's secret promise to keep Coldhaven's ships out of any war. In May 1103 Isa's riders burned an innocent half-orc family at Fenny Ford on an informer's guess. The Ravenscars think of themselves as the empire's eyes and do not ask its leave. They serve the Ironsides loyally and keep secrets even from them. Their children learn to ride at night before they ride by day, and every Ravenscar of the blood wears a hood of dark gauze at noon.
dead: Hereward Ravenscar (890–958): Verderer of Northmoor; first known owl-eyed Ravenscar.
Maud Ravenscar the Owl (955–1012): Night raid on Graknak (988); founded the spy tradition.
Alaric Ravenscar (992–1066): Built the empire's spy service and cipher ledger.
Corwin Ravenscar (1040–1072): Heir, killed in the fall of Fort Graknak.
marriages: 1068, with Holloway of Rosemarch: Ysolde married Sir Wystan Holloway, who took the Ravenscar name.
FAM-004.secrets: Ysolde ordered King Bjorn's poisoning without the emperor's leave; the cook lives in Ostra. Isa's riders burned an innocent family at Fenny Ford in 1103, and Corbin meets an elven watcher at the Oak Line stones every new moon.

FAM-005.y1105: Jarls of the Glenwash and the emperor's own cousins. Jarl Sigurd leads the Old Plains Lords against new taxes; his daughter Ingrid commands the Cold Bay squadron's marines.
FAM-005.arms: a grey horse's head with a long mane on sea green, over three silver salmon
FAM-005.founder: Grim Greymane (about 670–740), sea-thane of the Glenwash mouth
FAM-005.power: The Glenwash Jarldom with its seat at Easterham, a city of 18,900; a levy of about 4,000; the salmon weirs and amber beaches of the lower Glenwash; the jarl's right to judge his own people (1044); the home port of the crown's Cold Bay squadron, whose marines Ingrid Greymane commands.
FAM-005.branches: the Easterham line, jarls of the Glenwash; the Stagflow Greymanes of Northreach, descended from the 200 men who fled in 946
FAM-005.history: The Greymanes are the oldest house on the Northern Plains. Their lore-songs name Grim Greymane, a sea-thane who beached his boats at the Glenwash mouth about 700, as their founder, and they took the title jarl from the fishing chiefs of the Cold Bay shore. From Easterham they ruled the lower Glenwash, its salmon weirs and its amber beaches, and kept their own hall-priests. In 944 Jarl Ulf Greymane swore a truce with Harald Ironside on the iron ring. On its last night in October 945 Harald crossed the Glenwash and killed him at the ford. Ulf's sister Sigrun had told Harald where the camp lay, and her price was marriage. She married Harald in 947, brought the Greymane lands as her dowry and bore him Hakon. The Easterham hall-keeper Wulfgar fled to Wolfhaven with a copy of the truce record, and about 200 Greymane men followed him and settled on the Stagflow. Ulf's son Ragnar (941–1003) was raised at Kingsmere as a ward. When his cousin Hakon became emperor in 990 he gave Ragnar the Glenwash and the title of jarl as a vassal. The Greymanes swore to the Iron Reform in 1002 with the rest of Aldmark and resented it. In 1044 Astrid Greymane, sister of Jarl Thorald, married Emperor Conrad, and her price was the jarldom's right to judge its own people; her son is Emperor Aldwin. Thorald's son Sigurd, born 1044, became jarl in 1066 at 22. He led the Glenwash levy in the Second Horde War and still carries an orc lance scar from the Gashmar fords. In 1089 he stood up in the Oath Moot against the Edict of the Halls, and the Old Plains Lords formed around him. He believes the public story, that Ulf broke the truce, and he is ashamed of it. His daughter Ingrid, born 1072, captains the 600 marines of the Cold Bay squadron at Easterham and is secretly promised to a son of Jarl Asta Coldwater of Northreach. So the Greymanes are at once the emperor's cousins, his port-keepers and his loudest critics. Sigurd hides the Free Hall priestess Aldith Crowe in a net loft at Easterham and writes to Ragna of the Stones at Wolfhaven, who has promised to show him how his forefather was betrayed. Few families in Aldmark have more reason to love the Ironsides, or more reason to hate them.
dead: Grim Greymane (about 670–740): Sea-thane who founded the house at the Glenwash mouth.
Jarl Ulf Greymane (915–945): Killed at the Glenwash Fords when Harald broke their truce.
Ragnar Greymane (941–1003): Ulf's son, raised a ward; restored as jarl in 990.
Empress Astrid Greymane (1025–1070): Wife of Conrad and mother of Aldwin.
marriages: 947, with House Ironside: Sigrun Greymane married Harald Ironside.
1044, with House Ironside: Astrid Greymane married Emperor Conrad.
1093, with House Coldwater: Ingrid Greymane secretly promised to a son of Jarl Asta Coldwater at the Coldhaven talks.
FAM-005.secrets: Their forefather was betrayed, not the betrayer, and Ragna of the Stones has promised to show Sigurd the proof. Sigurd shelters a hidden Free Hall at Easterham against the Iron Reform.

FAM-101.y1105: The first noble house of the Holy See: poor in land, rich in honor, and holding four Luminaries' votes. Its head sits on the High Luminary's council as Warden of the Crowning Stone and leads the Corvane Restoration, which wants her son crowned lay King of the Solen.
FAM-101.arms: a gold sun rising from a black stone, on the dark blue of the old Solen court
FAM-101.founder: Corvan the Sunbringer (24 BR-39 AR), first king of the Solen
FAM-101.power: Land: about 4,000 acres of olive and wine land around Dorata and two town houses in Solenne, worth about 9,000 suns a year. Office: the Wardenship of the Crowning Stone, held by a Corvane in all but about 40 years since 150, and the only lay seat on the High Luminary's council. Votes: the debts of four Luminaries, bought with the house jewels pawned to House Lunetti. Faith: Corvane women judge the Temple's gold leaf, dyes and window glass, and a Corvane stands beside the Crowning Stone at every Return Day rite. No troops beyond 80 household men.
FAM-101.branches: The Crown branch: the male line of Aldric I; ten kings (1-294) and five emperors (294-379); died out in 418; The Stone branch: descendants of Aurelia the Far-Seeing and Marcus of Dorata; hereditary Wardens of the Crowning Stone; the only branch alive in 1105; The Dorata Corvanes: a cadet line of the Stone branch on olive farms at Dorata; died out in the Harbor Pox of 1077
FAM-101.history: House Corvane is the house of Corvan the Sunbringer, first king of the Solen. Corvan was a guard captain's son with no house name; his heirs were called Corvane, 'of Corvan', from the reign of his son Aldric I. Through Corvan's wife Seraphine of Lorina the whole house also descends from Lord Brennus of Lorina, the enemy Corvan beat in the Famine Wars, a fact the Temple's gold-leaf panels leave out. The house has had two branches. The Crown branch, the male line of Aldric I, gave the Solen ten kings from 1 to 294 and five emperors from 294 to 379, among them Aldric II the Conqueror, Maximian the Great and Aldric III the Lawgiver. It lost the throne when Cassian II was poisoned in 379 on the orders of his cousin by marriage, Severan of House Ferrano. Severan married Cassian's two small daughters to his own sons, and the last men of the Crown branch lived out their lives in Temple houses; the last of them, Brother Aldo Corvane, died at the Clarente Temple house in 418. The Stone branch descends from Corvan's daughter Aurelia the Far-Seeing, the Temple's first seer. In 36 AR she married Marcus of Dorata, a captain of her father's guard, on the condition that he take her father's name, and their daughter Luciana Corvane (38-101) had her mother's Sunborn eyes. The Edict of the One Light of 150 made Aurelia's grandson Marcus Corvane the first Warden of the Crowning Stone. The Stone branch never ruled. Half its sons are red-green color-blind, and by old custom a man who cannot read battle banners may not lead troops or serve as a herald, so the house has given the Sunlands no generals. It has given seers, judges of dye and glass, sun-sisters and one High Luminary, Odo II (r. 924-941), born Otho Corvane. Under the Ferrano and Orsano emperors the Corvanes were kept close and poor: honored at every crowning and never given a province. In the siege of 756-759 Warden Tullia Corvane kept the Crowning Stone chapel open as a soup kitchen, and in 760 Benedict the First confirmed the house in its Wardenship in one of the first acts of the Holy See. Since then the house has lived on its olive land at Dorata, the Warden's fees and its name. The Harbor Pox of 1077 killed the last of the Dorata cadets. In 1086 Aurelia Corvane's brother Lucius died without sons and she became head. Her husband Stefan, a Venora knight's son, had taken the Corvane name when they married in 1073, as every Corvane heiress's husband has done since Marcus of Dorata. Their son Cassius, born 1075, is color-blind. Since helping to elect Severin III in 1088, Aurelia has used the house's bought votes to press the Corvane Restoration: a Corvane crowned lay King of the Solen to rule the Holy Coast while the Temple keeps the faith. In 1104 the Marchland lord Marek Ferryman wrote to her asking her to recognize his bought imperial blood, a letter she has kept and not answered.
dead: Corvan the Sunbringer (24 BR-39 AR): First king of the Solen; founder of the house. *Ruler:* Corvan the Sunbringer (Corvan I), Solen Kingdom, 1–39 (RUL-1001).
Aurelia the Far-Seeing (12-84): First seer of the Temple and first known carrier of the Sunborn eyes; founder of the Stone branch.
Aldric II the Conqueror (171-229): Conquered Tamar. *Ruler:* Aldric II the Conqueror, Solen Kingdom, 196–229 (RUL-1007).
Maximian the Great (248-302): Last king and first emperor of the Solen. *Ruler:* Maximian the Great (Maximian I), Solen Empire, 294–302 (RUL-1011).
Aldric III the Lawgiver (271-341): Imposed the Common Reckoning in 318. *Ruler:* Aldric III the Lawgiver, Solen Empire, 305–341 (RUL-1013).
Cassian II (346-379): Last Corvane emperor, poisoned. *Ruler:* Cassian II, Solen Empire, 362–379 (RUL-1015).
marriages: 1 BR, with House Brennus: Corvan married Seraphine, daughter of the dead Lord Brennus, as the price of Lorina's surrender.
36, with Marcus of Dorata: Aurelia's husband took the Corvane name; the Stone branch began.
75, with The salt-lords of Lucerna: Corvan II married Ilena of Lucerna; Lucerna joined the kingdom.
380, with House Ferrano: Cassian II's two daughters were married to Severan's sons, joining the Crown branch's blood to House Ferrano.
1073, with Stefan of Venora: Aurelia Corvane's husband took the Corvane name.
FAM-101.secrets: Aurelia has pawned the house jewels to House Lunetti to buy four Luminaries' debts, and her heir Cassius is color-blind and barred by custom from reading banners. The house's holy story rests on Aurelia's borrowed eclipse tables, the Mirona fire and the six missing years.

FAM-102.y1105: Holders of the Temple farms around Lavino on a lease of 760 that has never been reviewed. The head is 5,000 suns in debt to House Lunetti and keeps the letter that proves the Holy See bought the Lantern Gate.
FAM-102.arms: a gold gate standing open, on black
FAM-102.founder: General Marcus Vell (715-770), who opened the Lantern Gate in 759
FAM-102.power: Land: about 12,000 acres of Temple farmland around Lavino, the old granary town where the Famine Wars began, held at a fixed rent of 1 sun for 10 acres set in 760; the wine and wheat bring about 20,000 suns a year. Troops: about 300 tenant soldiers owing 40 days. Debt: 5,000 suns to House Lunetti against future harvests. Leverage: Marcus Vell's letter of 759.
FAM-102.branches: The Lavino line, holders of the lease; The Vells of the Lantern Guard: younger sons who served in the High Luminary's guard until the last died in the Harbor Pox of 1077
FAM-102.history: Marcus Vell was the son of a gate captain of Solenne and rose to be the general of the city's walls under Constantine IX. In the hunger winter of 758-759, when about 20,000 people died inside the Valerian Wall, High Luminary Benedict offered him a pardon and the Temple estates at Lavino if he would open a gate. On Ash Night 759 he opened the Lantern Gate. Before he did, he wrote to his daughter Livia to explain the price he was paid, and the family has kept that letter ever since. In 760 Benedict gave him a lease of the Lavino farms at a fixed rent, never to be reviewed; Vell died there in 770, called a savior in Solenne and a traitor in every soldier's song. For three centuries the Vells lived quietly on Lavino wine and wheat. Younger sons served in the Lantern Guard; the last of them died nursing pilgrims in the Harbor Pox of 1077. The lease rent, fixed in 760 silver, is now worth a tenth of what the land yields, which is why the Treasury wants it reviewed. Matthias Vell was born at Lavino in 1058 and inherited in 1084. He read the letter the night his father died and has kept it in a lead tube under the chapel altar. He married Adela of Venora in 1091; Lady Aurelia Corvane is godmother to their daughter. He sold Lavino wine to Queen Livia's court through Lucerna during the Truce of the Cedars and borrowed on future harvests when the war resumed in 1096. In 1105 Treasurer Dorn plans to review all old Temple leases to raise money for Livia, and Matthias means to make the Vell lease permanent by letting Dorn and Keeper Quill know the letter exists.
dead: General Marcus Vell (715-770): Opened the Lantern Gate on Ash Night 759.
Livia Vell (741-803): The daughter to whom Marcus wrote his letter; she kept it and passed it down.
marriages: 1091, with A Venora wine family: Matthias Vell married Adela of Venora; Aurelia Corvane stood godmother to their daughter.
FAM-102.secrets: Marcus Vell's letter of 759 shows that High Luminary Benedict bought the opening of the Lantern Gate with a pardon and the Lavino estates.

FAM-103.y1105: A poor knightly house of Clarente, holding only the lease of the old Clarente granary. Its head wants to sell the granary's roof beams, whose tree rings prove the six missing years, to pay 2,600 suns of debt.
FAM-103.arms: a broken silver anchor on blue
FAM-103.founder: Lucius Merel (about 510-575), captain of the southern fleet
FAM-103.power: Land: the lease of the old Clarente granary and 300 acres of salt-pan and wheat land at Clarente, worth about 700 suns a year. Debt: 2,600 suns, 1,200 of them to Rufus Gatewell against the lease. Leverage: the granary's 40 oak roof beams, felled before 1 AR, one of the three proofs of the six missing years; and a claim to lost Holy Coast lands if Justinian IV's hidden order is ever read.
FAM-103.branches: The Clarente line, holders of the granary lease
FAM-103.history: The Merels were a sea family of the Holy Coast. Lucius Merel commanded the southern fleet under Justinian III and was given estates at Clarino and Claria. His grandson Admiral Gaius Merel was ordered by Justinian IV to sail the relief fleet for Qadira on 9 November 602, after Sea Closing and against every admiral's advice. A storm wrecked 64 ships and drowned about 5,000 men. The emperor hid his written order and had Merel beheaded for sailing late, and the family's estates were taken. The order still lies unread in the imperial letter-chests of the Holy See's archive. The Merels became poor knights. In 781 High Luminary Tavian I, as a charity to the admiral's heirs, leased them the old Clarente granary, built before 1 AR and taken by Corvan in the siege of 4 BR, whose roof beams nobody then cared about. Merel sons served as Knights of the Sun and as sergeants of Clarente Tower. Tobias Merel was born at Clarente in 1063, trained at Noon Hall and left before his vows to marry in 1086. Bad harvests and his wife's death in 1099 left him with four children and 2,600 suns of debt, 1,200 of it owed to the innkeeper Rufus Gatewell against the granary lease. In 1103 Brother Lucan Serra told him what the rings in his roof might prove, and he joined the Open Light more for money than faith. In October 1104 he secretly sold two beams through the joiner Bastian of Clarente to a buyer for the Silverbough archive. He means to sell the other 38 for about 3,000 suns before Spring Equinox, while Keeper Quill wants them burned.
dead: Admiral Gaius Merel (about 555-602): Beheaded for the loss of the southern fleet that the emperor ordered to sail.
marriages: 1086, with A Clarente salt-pan family: Tobias Merel left Noon Hall before his vows to marry; his wife died in 1099.
FAM-103.secrets: Tobias has already sold two beams to Eldergrove's archive. Justinian IV's hidden order would clear Gaius Merel and could win back the family's lands.

FAM-104.y1105: Lords of Lorina, the Holy See's second city, and keepers of Lorina Castle and the See's Lorina galleys. Blamed for 1,100 years for the Mirona fire, the house now holds the skulls that prove Corvan's own men set it.
FAM-104.arms: three gold wheat sheaves on black
FAM-104.founder: Caro Brennus (about 430-370 BR), who walled Lorina
FAM-104.power: Land: Lorina (29,200 people) and about 9,000 acres of the Lorina coast, with harbor dues; income about 30,000 suns a year after the tithe. Office: castellans of Lorina Castle, which guards the Sun Road toward Ostra, and captains of the See's 14-galley Lorina squadron. Troops: about 1,200 house and castle men, plus Tessa Marlow's hired company of 440, paid from Lorina's purse. Votes: Lorina's voice in the Needle Court elections through its Luminary.
FAM-104.branches: The Lorina line, lords of Lorina; The Castle line: Petra Brennus, castellan of Lorina Castle and captain of the Lorina galleys
FAM-104.history: House Brennus is older than the Solen crown. Caro Brennus walled Lorina about 400 BR, and his heirs ruled the town and its granaries through the good centuries before the Dimming. In September 6 BR Lord Brennus of Lorina, head of the League of Lorina, seized the Lavino granary that fed Solenne and began the Famine Wars (WAR-01). He died with about 2,400 of his men at Lorina Hills in June 2 BR. His daughter Seraphine, 16, was married to Corvan in September 1 BR as the price of Lorina's surrender, so every Solen king from Aldric I descends from Brennus. The house kept Lorina by oath. But the priest Tavian wrote that Brennus had burned the Mirona granary with 300 people inside, when Corvan's own unpaid spearmen had done it, and for 1,100 years Solenne's children have chanted 'Brennus burned the bread'. The house served the kings and emperors as lords of the eastern Holy Coast. Theodoric I lost to Maximus under Lorina's walls in 657. A Brennus daughter, Lady Serena of Lorina, married Justinian IV in secret in 584, and her son Aurelian was the true heir whom history calls the Pretender. In 755 Lord Aulo Brennus lent Lorina Castle for the secret meeting of Lucan the Grey and Galen Valdane that doomed the last emperor, and in 760 the house swore to the High Luminary and kept its city. Since then the Brennus lords have paid the tithe on time, commanded the See's eastern galleys and quietly hated Solenne. Cato Brennus was born at Lorina in 1047 and became lord in 1072; he rebuilt the harbor wall after the Harbor Pox years emptied the town. His only child Petra, born 1071, learned to row before she learned Old Solen, fought off a Blackreef raider at the mouth of the bay in 1096, and took the castle and the galleys in 1100. In spring 1103 Cato's shepherds broke into a pit outside Mirona's old wall and found 22 hanged men still wearing Solenne-made bronze buckles. He keeps the skulls and buckles in the castle cellar and pays the scrivener Otto Quire for lists of what the archive holds on the Famine Wars; he wants Tavian's letter of December 3 BR, which asked Corvan to 'let Lorina carry the fire'. In August 1104 Petra secretly promised Admiral Nino Castellan of Varenna 12 Lorina galleys for his war on Blackreef and spent 3,000 suns of Lorina's tithe money on new oars.
dead: Lord Brennus of Lorina (died 2 BR): Head of the League of Lorina in the Famine Wars; blamed for the Mirona fire.
Seraphine of Lorina (17 BR-44 AR): Corvan's queen; mother of Aldric I and Aurelia the Far-Seeing.
Lady Serena of Lorina (about 562-630): Secret wife of Justinian IV and mother of Aurelian.
Lord Aulo Brennus (708-772): Host of the secret meeting at Lorina in 755.
marriages: 1 BR, with House Corvane: Seraphine married Corvan as the price of Lorina's surrender.
584, with House Ferrano: Serena of Lorina secretly married Emperor Justinian IV.
1069, with A Palena wool family: Cato Brennus married Donata of Palena, Petra's mother, who died in the Harbor Pox of 1077.
FAM-104.secrets: Cato holds 22 skulls and Solenne-made buckles from the Mirona pit, proof that Corvan's men burned the granary. Petra has promised 12 of the See's galleys to Varenna without the High Luminary's leave. If SEC-21 is read, House Brennus is the mother's house of a lawful emperor.

FAM-105.y1105: A family of Solenne scribes that has given the Needle-Keepers an astronomer in most generations since 316 and has twice seen one walled up for the Needle Heresy. Its living men are Brother Lucan Serra, who leads the Open Light, and Sir Aimon Rastell, Ottavio Serra's unacknowledged son, a Knight of the Sun.
FAM-105.arms: a black needle on white, a gold sun at its tip
FAM-105.founder: Anno Serra (about 290-361), clerk to Master Astronomer Elira Starling
FAM-105.power: No land. A copy-house on the Street of Scribes that copies eclipse tables and calendars for the Temple, about 400 suns a year. One Needle-Keeper's stall held by a Serra in most generations. Knowledge: the family's private copy of Anno Serra's shadow counts, the 'Serra tables', which run back to 316.
FAM-105.branches: The lay line: copyists of eclipse tables on the Street of Scribes, head Corrado Serra (born 1041); The Needle line: sons and nephews given to the Needle-Keepers; Aimon Rastell, Ottavio's son by a sun-sister, raised as a foundling
FAM-105.history: Anno Serra was the clerk who copied Elira Starling's 264 years of noon shadow marks in 316, when she found the six missing years. He was one of the few who knew what the closed council of that year had sealed, and he kept his own copy of the counts. From then on the Serras lived as scribes in Solenne and gave a son or nephew to the Needle-Keepers in most generations, while one lay brother married and kept the copy-house. Twice the family's astronomers followed the numbers too far. In 873 Brother Ennio Serra wrote that the eclipse tables ran true only if six years were added, and Clement III walled him up under the Needle for life. In 1068 Ottavio Serra matched the Dim Chronicle, the elven Grove Count and tree rings in old roof beams, was tried for the Needle Heresy, recanted, and died in his cell in 1069. He had broken his vows: a sun-sister of Solenne bore him a son, Aimon, in 1068, and the boy was raised in the Temple foundling school as the son of an unknown father. His mother told him the truth on her deathbed in 1097. Aimon took the vows of the Knights of the Sun in 1087 and is now the knight chosen to steal his father's copied proof from Silverbough. Ottavio's lay brother Corrado had a son, Lucan, in 1070. Lucan became a Needle-Keeper in 1094, noticed in 1099 that the eclipse tables ran better with six years added, counted six starved rings in a Clarente beam in 1103, and since 1101 has written in cipher to Lirael the Archivist at Silverbough. Aimon, who has read everything he can find about his father, knows that Lucan is his cousin; Lucan does not know that the knight is a Serra.
dead: Anno Serra (about 290-361): Elira Starling's clerk, keeper of the first Serra tables.
Brother Ennio Serra (812-881): Walled up for the Needle Heresy in 873; died in his cell.
Ottavio Serra the Counter (1019-1069): Proved the count six years short; tried in 1068.
FAM-105.secrets: Sir Aimon Rastell is Ottavio Serra's son and has been sent to steal the proof his own father sent north. Lucan Serra writes to Silverbough in a numeral cipher through the half-elf Sister Isaria Vale.

FAM-110.y1105: The royal house of Varenna since 749. The king carries the Lionblood and collapsed with chest pain in November 1104; his only son and heir is 12, and the next heir after the boy is a Castella cousin.
FAM-110.arms: a gold lion standing on its hind legs holding a sword, on Palella blue
FAM-110.founder: Marcus Valdane (about 580-650), toll-holder of the lower Palella who fed Valerian's western army
FAM-110.power: Crown lands of the Crown Coast around Varenna, the royal shipyards and the Lion Hall. Command of 156,000 standing troops and 600,000 at full levy through the Lord Marshal; the Lion Fleet of 90 war galleys and about 140 cogs; the Lion Guard of 1,200 household knights. Income from the hearth tax, a penny in 20 on market sales, the salt tax and the Crown pass tolls, about 1.4 million suns a year, against debts of about 1.1 million to House Lunetti. The Temple owns a sixth of the land and must crown every Valdane.
FAM-110.branches: The royal line of Galen the Bold; The Lionheart's line through Roderic II, ended with Galen III in 916; The Valdanes of Castella (the Long Valdanes), from the Lionheart's son Lothar of Castella; Lionblood carriers; head in 1105 Lord Aldo Valdane of Castella, born 1070; The Long daughters: carrier princesses in the sun-sisters' houses under the Rule of the Long Blood
FAM-110.history: The Valdanes were a family of the lower Palella who held river tolls under the Solen governors and claimed descent from the daughter of Lord Dorian of Varenna, who led the League of the Palella in 40 AR. Marcus Valdane fed Valerian's western army with Palella wheat in 613, and his heirs served the Orsano emperors as tax farmers and captains. Galen Valdane, governor of the Western Sunlands, refused the Schism Tax in 741, won at Aurora in 743, starved out Vitia in 747, and was crowned first King of Varenna by the Temple in 749. He helped take Solenne in 759 and doubled his kingdom in the Treaty of the Needle. His son Lothar I made peace with Ashmere and built the royal shipyards; his grandson Galen II gave way to the Temple in the Tithe Truce of 803; Lothar II ruled 52 years. The Lionblood entered the house with Lothar II's son Roderic, born 835 when his father was 56. Roderic the Lionheart reigned 41 years, banned slavery, founded the Hall of the Lion and broke the Wind riders on the Coast Road in 896. In 891 he made the Rule of the Long Blood to keep his reach inside the house. Of his seven children, four had it: Roderic II, Lothar of Castella and the princesses Marta and Leona, who took the sun-sisters' vows. Isolde, who did not, married King Tancred of Morhaven in 894. Roderic II died at 46 in 908, and his son Galen III died of the Black Cough in 916. The crown passed to the Lionheart's younger son Teodor, and for 146 years the reigning line, Teodor I, Galen IV, Teodor II, Lothar III and Lucilla, had no Lionblood and lived long. The blood lived on in the Valdanes of Castella. In 968 Teodor II married his daughter Mira into House Serafin; her grandson Guido Serafin rose against Queen Lucilla in 1049 and was crushed by Cesare Montaro. Lothar III the Merchant, who had no son, married his heiress Lucilla to her Castella cousin Ettore in 1044 to bring the Lionheart's reach back to the throne. Ettore died of the Valdane heart in 1068 at 44. Their son Roderic III was crowned in 1088. In 1090 he married Bianca Falcone of Morhaven, who came into the house as queen and bore Prince Galen in 1092 after two lost pregnancies. On 18 November 1104 Roderic collapsed in the Lion Hall yard. If he and Galen both died, the crown would pass to Lord Aldo Valdane of Castella, a carrier of 34 with two small sons, whom the court barely knows.
dead: Galen Valdane the Bold (704-773): First King of Varenna. *Ruler:* Galen Valdane the Bold (Galen I), Kingdom of Varenna, 749–773 (RUL-1201).
Roderic the Lionheart (835-902): First Lionblood carrier; victor of the Coast Road. *Ruler:* Roderic the Lionheart (Roderic I), Kingdom of Varenna, 861–902 (RUL-1205).
Isolde Valdane (866-921): The Lionheart's daughter, queen of Morhaven through the siege of 895-897.
Lothar of Castella (873-917): Founder of the Castella branch; died of the Valdane heart at 44.
Lothar Valdane the Merchant (970-1049): Won the Palella trade from Ashmere. *Ruler:* Lothar Valdane the Merchant (Lothar III), Kingdom of Varenna, 1001–1049 (RUL-1211).
Queen Lucilla Valdane (1020-1088): Reigned 39 years; lost the Corsair War. *Ruler:* Queen Lucilla Valdane of Varenna (the Faithful), Kingdom of Varenna, 1049–1088 (RUL-1212).
marriages: 894, with The royal house of Morhaven: Isolde married King Tancred the Steadfast; the war pact of the Siege of Morhaven.
968, with House Serafin: Teodor II's daughter Mira married the lord of Venina, the root of the Serafin claim.
1044, with House Valdane: Lucilla married her Castella cousin Ettore, a Lionblood carrier.
1090, with House Falcone: Roderic III married Bianca Falcone; each kingdom promised the other 2,000 men.
FAM-110.rivals: House Serafin, House Ashford, House Ironside
FAM-110.secrets: The king's collapse of 18 November 1104 is known to his physician, two of his knights and, through Luminary Brandi, to Solenne, but not to his own council. Prince Galen cannot see a face beyond 20 paces. The Lord Treasurer has secretly debased the coin.

FAM-111.y1105: Varenna's first military family and lords of Vitia. Its head is Lord Marshal and leader of the War Party, and three of the realm's generals are Montaros.
FAM-111.arms: a red open hand on silver
FAM-111.founder: Taddeo Montaro (about 850-912), sergeant of Roderic the Lionheart, made castellan of Vitia
FAM-111.power: Land: the citadel of Vitia on its 1,600 m ridge, stocked for two years, and about 2,000 km2 of forest and pasture in the Vitia uplands, about 40,000 suns a year. Command: the Lord Marshal's office over the army of 156,000; the Crown Road army of 18,000 at Ardata; the Laughing Company of 3,000. Men: about 40 cousins with the laughing blood and 1,200 house troops at Vitia.
FAM-111.branches: The Vitia line: Cesare Montaro's children, Dario and Ottavia; The Ardata line: Vittor, son of Cesare's younger brother Bruno; The Laughing Company cousins: about 40 Montaro cousins with the blood, fostered at Vitia
FAM-111.history: The Montaros were hill herders of the Vitia uplands. Taddeo Montaro fought as a sergeant in Roderic the Lionheart's knightly army, and in 891 the king made him castellan of the royal citadel of Vitia, which Galen the Bold had starved out in 747. His grandson Ruggero Montaro, born 927, was the first with the laughing blood. In the winter of 952 he held the wall of the Montessa Gate against Crown foothill bandits all night with a broken shin he did not notice, and the family began to test its children with nettles. For a century the Montaros were castellans and captains, not lords. Cesare Montaro, Ruggero's grandson, born 1010, made them great. When Lord Guido Serafin rose against Queen Lucilla in May 1049, Cesare crushed him at Venina, laughed off three wounds and hanged 60 of his men. Lucilla gave the Montaros Vitia and its uplands as lords, and Cesare raised the Laughing Company of Montaro foot in 1050. He commanded Varenna in the Corsair War (WAR-34) and lost 11 galleys to fire rafts at Gull Isle in 1053; he never forgave Lucerna for the peace of 1056. In March 1071 he killed a man in a duel over an insult about that war, laughed off a thrust under the ribs, and died of it four days later. His son Dario, born 1052, swore to die on a battlefield instead; he led the Laughing Company from 1078 and became Lord Marshal in 1089. Cesare's daughter Ottavia, born 1058, took the Company when Dario rose; her only son Lucca died in 1100 of a sword wound he ignored after a drill, and since then she has quietly warned Queen Bianca of her brother's plans. Their cousin Vittor, born 1060, son of Cesare's younger brother Bruno, commands the Crown Road army. The Serafins still spit at the Montaro name.
dead: Ruggero Montaro the Numb (927-981): First carrier of the laughing blood.
Cesare Montaro, Who Bled Laughing (1010-1071): Crushed the Serafin revolt; commanded in the Corsair War; died of an ignored duel wound.
Bruno Montaro (1014-1062): Cesare's brother, Vittor's father; died of a gangrened foot he walked on for a month.
Lucca Montaro (1079-1100): Ottavia's son, dead of an ignored sword wound.
marriages: 1049, with Knightly houses of Norossa: Cesare married Donella of Norossa; the Montaros began to marry into the knightly families of the Northern Lakes.
FAM-111.secrets: An Ashmere arrowhead near Dario's spine has moved and could kill him in any hard ride. Captain Rinaldo Vasco of the Lion Guard has promised Dario the Lion Hall gates on the day the king dies. Ottavia is betraying the War Party's councils to the queen.

FAM-112.y1105: Lords of Dorium, owners of the largest weaving halls in the Palella valley and holders of the Lord Treasurer's office. They are refusing to pay for either the War Party's strike or the Strait League's galleys.
FAM-112.arms: a silver spindle crossed with a gold key, on Palella blue
FAM-112.founder: Arrigo Calvane (about 880-948), wool buyer of Dorium
FAM-112.power: Land and town: the lordship of Dorium (23,700 people) and its toll on the lower Palella. Trade: about 600 spinning wheels and 400 looms in the Calvane halls, about a fifth of the realm's Palella blue cloth, some 120,000 suns a year. Office: the Lord Treasurer's accounts of the crown and the cloth taxes. Troops: the 8,000 Palella Crossbows are paid by the weaving guilds the Calvanes lead, and their captain takes Calvane silver in secret.
FAM-112.branches: The Dorium line, lords of Dorium since 1017; The Lucerna factors: Calvane cousins who sell Palella cloth at Lucerna and hold ship shares there
FAM-112.history: The Calvanes rose from the wool of the Black Cough. When Teodor the Patient let emptied wheat farms go to sheep after 916, Arrigo Calvane, a wool buyer of Dorium, bought fleeces from a dozen hill valleys and sold them to the Palella weavers, and his heirs built weaving halls of their own. By 1000 the Calvanes were the largest cloth house of the lower Palella and lent money to the crown. Lothar III the Merchant needed silver for the Varenna-Ashmere War (WAR-27), and in 1017 he sold them the lordship of Dorium, whose old lords had died out, for 60,000 suns. The town gave its name to the Peace of Dorium of 1016, which opened the Palella to Varennan barges, and the Calvanes rode that trade. The house's second rise came from the wheel. In 1084 the Camia wheelwright Jacopo Brisa built a spinning wheel from a Ranpuri trader's account of the cotton wheel, and in 1085 Lord Enzio Calvane bought his first twenty wheels and every one Brisa made for the next five years. A spinner at a wheel makes as much yarn as three with a spindle, and within ten years the Calvanes were the richest house in the valley. They pressed Roderic III to make teaching the wheel to foreigners a hanging crime in 1089, which he did. Piero Calvane, born 1049, became head in 1086 and Lord Treasurer in 1092. He cut the crown's debts by a fifth before the Lion Fleet's costs rose again. He pays for the Palella Crossbows through the guilds, and in secret pays their captain Fiora Lanza 200 suns a year to report on the guild. In 1103, to pay the army's arrears, he had the royal mint strike Varennan suns with a tenth less silver, a crime for which ordinary coin clippers are hanged. In 1105 he refuses to pay for General Montaro's spring strike or Admiral Castellan's 40 galleys, because the crown already owes House Lunetti 1.1 million suns. If the runaway spinner Sabina of Camia teaches Ashmere the wheel, the Calvane fortune is the first to fall. The house is not loved. The Montaros call it a house of clerks that buys its swords, the Brisas know that the Calvanes took the profit of Jacopo Brisa's wheel while paying him a wheelwright's price, and the Temple dislikes a Lord Treasurer who asks what its Varennan estates should pay. Piero has no son; his heir is his nephew Enzio, a factor at Lucerna who holds shares in four Lucernan cogs.
dead: Arrigo Calvane (about 880-948): Wool buyer who founded the house's fortune after the Black Cough.
Enzio Calvane (1021-1086): Bought the first spinning wheels in 1085.
marriages: 1071, with Shipowning houses of Lucerna: Piero Calvane married Livia Rossa of a Lucernan ship family, which gave the house its Lucerna factors.
FAM-112.secrets: Piero Calvane secretly debased the Varennan sun in 1103, and he pays the captain of the Palella Crossbows to spy on the Weavers' Guild.

FAM-113.y1105: Wardens of the Crown Road and the Albora Pass, who tax the amber and iron trade from Aldmark. Their head backs the War Party for the promise of Crowbrook while secretly letting an Aldmark company's wagons pass untaxed.
FAM-113.arms: three silver towers on a green mountain
FAM-113.founder: Bertran Ardane the Elder (about 790-851), first Warden of the Crown Road
FAM-113.power: Land: the town of Ardata and the upland valleys below the Albora and Montessa passes. Office: Wardens of the Crown Road, keeping a tenth of all pass tolls, about 25,000 suns a year since the tolls were doubled in 1094. Forts: the three towers of Albora Watch. Troops: about 800 house men; the 18,000-man Crown Road army is quartered on their land.
FAM-113.branches: The Ardata line, Wardens of the Crown Road
FAM-113.history: The Crown Road was built over the Albora Pass by Emperor Octavian in 473 to march armies onto the Grass Sea. After amber was found on the Cold Bay shore in 824, northern traders began to bring it south over the pass to the Sunland markets, and in 826 Lothar II made Bertran Ardane the Elder, a captain of the pass forts, Warden of the Crown Road with a tenth of the tolls. The Ardanes have held the passes since. When Harald Ironside made the northern plains the Empire of Aldmark in 951, the Ardanes became Varenna's first guard against the north, and the Amber Road became an iron road too. The house has never fought a great battle, but its towers have closed the passes to raiders every winter. Bertran Ardane, born 1058, became head in 1087. He rebuilt the three towers of Albora Watch in 1090, doubled the Crown Road tolls in 1094, and in 1098 met Emeric Vane of Aldmark's Iron Road Company at Kingsmere; since 1099 he has let the company's wagons pass untaxed for a private cut of 1 in 10, paid in Aldmark silver. When the Aldmark-Ashmere betrothal was announced in March 1104 he wrote to General Dario Montaro the same week, and Montaro has promised him the lordship of Crowbrook if the War Party takes it. The bandit Remo Casti, whom Bertran sent to the galleys in 1094, now robs his toll wagons and sells news of the passes to Aldmark.
dead: Bertran Ardane the Elder (about 790-851): First Warden of the Crown Road.
FAM-113.secrets: Bertran takes a private cut from the Iron Road Company of Aldmark to let its wagons pass untaxed, while he plans war on Aldmark's new ally.

FAM-114.y1105: Lords of Venina and its marble quarries, of Valdane blood through a princess of 968. Crushed in the revolt of 1049, the house now leads the Tithe Resisters in the Great Council.
FAM-114.arms: a white marble column under a gold star, on green
FAM-114.founder: Aulo Serafin (about 590-660), marble contractor who cut the stone for the Valerian Wall
FAM-114.power: Land: the city of Venina (22,200 people), the hill towns around it and the Galone and Vicula marble quarries, about 30,000 suns a year. Votes: leadership of the Tithe Resisters in the Great Council. Men: about 600 house troops, and a secret line of pay to the tenant leader Agnese of Venina, whose strike covers 40 villages.
FAM-114.branches: The Venina line, lords of Venina
FAM-114.history: Aulo Serafin was a marble contractor of Venina who cut the stone for Valerian II's wall around Solenne between 628 and 636, and his heirs grew rich on imperial building. After the Treaty of the Needle of 760 gave the Venina hills to Varenna, Galen the Bold made the Serafins lords of Venina for opening their quarries to him. In 968 Lord Aldo Serafin married Princess Mira Valdane, daughter of Teodor II, and their grandson Guido Serafin grew up close to the throne. When Lothar III died in April 1049 leaving only a daughter, Guido claimed that a man of the royal blood must rule before a woman and rose at Venina in May. Cesare Montaro crushed him in a day, laughed off three wounds and hanged 60 of his men. Guido died in a Temple house in 1050, and the house kept its lands only by swearing to Queen Lucilla. Clara Serafin was born in 1064, fifteen years after the hangings. She married a cousin in 1082 and took the headship when he died in 1096. In 1100 she found in her grandfather's papers a list of Venina farms taken by the Temple between 738 and 748 and began to ask where the purchase money came from, the question of SEC-28. She has led the Tithe Resisters in the Great Council since 1102. In secret she pays the tenant widow Agnese of Venina, whose grandfather was one of the 60, to lead the tithe strike, and she has offered the Ashen preacher Tullio Ashwell shelter in her quarries.
dead: Princess Mira Valdane (968-1021): Teodor II's daughter; brought royal blood into the house.
Lord Guido Serafin (1011-1050): Rose against Queen Lucilla in 1049.
marriages: 968, with House Valdane: Lord Aldo Serafin married Princess Mira Valdane.
1082, with House Serafin: Clara married a Serafin cousin, Matteo Serafin of Aurora, who died in 1096.
FAM-114.secrets: Clara pays the leader of the tithe strike and shelters an Ashen preacher, either of which could bring the Temple's courts down on her house.

FAM-115.y1105: The wheelwrights and spinners of Camia who built the world's only spinning wheels and now lead the Weavers' Guild of Dorium. One of their daughters has fled to Ashmere with the parts of a wheel.
FAM-115.arms: a blue wheel on white, the guild mark of their workshop
FAM-115.power: Office: the mistress-ship of the Weavers' Guild of Dorium, whose members weave about a third of the realm's blue cloth and pay the 8,000 Palella Crossbows. Trade: 40 wheels of Nella's own at Dorium, about 6,000 suns a year. Knowledge: the making of the spinning wheel's crank and flyer, a monopoly the crown guards with the rope.
FAM-115.branches: The Camia workshop: wheelwrights, run since 1098 by Jacopo Brisa's former apprentice; Nella Brisa's spinning halls at Dorium
FAM-115.history: The Brisas were wheelwrights and wool spinners of Camia on the upper Palella from about 990. In 1083 a Ranpuri pepper trader at Varenna described the hand-turned wheel his people use to spin cotton, and in 1084 Jacopo Brisa, Tomas's grandson, built a wheel for wool in his Camia workshop. House Calvane bought his first twenty wheels in 1085 and every one he made for five years. His sister Nella, born 1057, was among the first women taught the wheel, and within five years she ran 40 wheels at Dorium. In 1089 Roderic III made teaching the wheel to foreigners a hanging crime, and the Brisas became the keepers of a secret worth more than their lives. Jacopo died of a fever in 1098 and left the workshop to his apprentice. In 1101 the apprentice married Jacopo's daughter Sabina, born 1083, who could work the wheel at 9, and beat her when she earned more than he did. Nella was elected Mistress of the Weavers' Guild in 1096 and made the guild pay for the Palella Crossbows. In November 1104 she gave her niece 20 suns and a boatman's name to escape her husband, not knowing that Sabina would take the spindle, the flyer and a drawing of the crank. Sabina fled up the Palella with Lupo Grell's smugglers and crossed into Ashmere at Crowbrook in December. Nella has now sworn to bring her back.
dead: Jacopo Brisa (1052-1098): Built the first spinning wheel for wool in 1084.
marriages: 1101, with The Camia wheelwrights: Sabina married her father's former apprentice, who kept the wheel workshop.
FAM-115.secrets: Nella helped her niece escape and so, without meaning to, sent the secret of the wheel to Ashmere.

FAM-120.y1105: The Doge's house and the greatest bank of Lucerna, about 2.5 million suns, holding the Grain Staple bank and sending food-tasters to princes across the Middle Sea. One of the four families that share the secret fifth of the dragon toll.
FAM-120.arms: a gold cup on dark red
FAM-120.founder: Nicola Doravelli the Nose (about 680-741), first Taster of the Grain Staple
FAM-120.power: Money: the Doravelli bank, about 2.5 million suns in coin and loans, with large loans to the Amber Isles against their clove harvests since 1072, 300,000 suns to Greyhaven for its galley fleet, and the shipowners of the Middle Sea. Rights: the Grain Staple bank, which certifies and lends against every cargo landed. Office: the dogeship. Secret income: a quarter of Lucerna's fifth of the dragon toll, about 2,250 marks a year. Knowledge: about 30 tasters at foreign tables who write home in the Doravelli cipher.
FAM-120.branches: The bank line: the Doge's house at the Staple; The tasters: about 30 Doravellis serving as food-tasters at courts from Greyhaven to Tessar; The Admiral's line: heirs of Admiral Enzo Doravelli (died 1060), shipowners
FAM-120.history: House Doravelli began with a tongue. In 709 Nicola Doravelli, a sampler who chewed a mouthful from every cargo landed at the Grain Staple, refused a load of Tamari grain because it tasted bitter to him, though the weighers found nothing wrong. The shipmaster sold it at Ostra, where it caused the fire-sickness of spoiled grain and killed about 300 people. The Staple made Nicola its taster, and his children, half of whom shared his tongue, tasted every cargo for a century. A Doravelli tasting certificate became as good as coin: merchants borrowed against certified grain, and the tasters became lenders. In 806 the Great Council elected Silvano Doravelli, the first Doge of the house, and he made the Staple's grain certificates the base of the Doravelli bank. The house has given Lucerna five Doges: Silvano, Donato, Silvio the Taster, Marcello and Tiberio. On New Year's Day 967 Doge Silvio Doravelli tasted bitter poison in the council's wine and stopped the toast, saving three councilors who opposed a grain deal with Tessar. The house turned the fame into a trade. In 971 it made the Rule of the Cup, which binds every child of its blood to the house, and from the 970s princes across the Middle Sea hired Doravelli tasters; the kings of Morhaven have kept one since 1012. Marcello Doravelli was Doge when Lucerna joined Isabetta Lunetti in calling in the Tessarian loans in 1044 and seized 38 Tessarian ships. Admiral Enzo Doravelli led Lucerna's galleys in the Corsair War and held them back at the Battle of the Strait in 1052, and in 1056 Doge Pietro Salvi made the Doravellis one of the four families sharing the secret fifth of the dragon toll. Tiberio Doravelli was born in 1040 and proved the tongue at seven. He tasted for King Leone of Morhaven from 1060 to 1072, ran the Staple bank, and was elected Doge in 1096 on the promise that the fifth would continue. He knows every line of the Ratrock clause and the Sabran oil compact, and he knows Jory Flint's map of the Red Widow's dawn route, which he has kept from his own Admiral. His son Nerio, born 1072, tasted a drop of wolfsbane in water at seven, served a Greyhaven lord from 1092 and has tasted for Queen Livia at Tessar since 1099. He writes to his father every week in the Doravelli cipher and has smelled the fire-oil in the queen's cellars.
dead: Nicola Doravelli the Nose (about 680-741): First Taster of the Staple; first known carrier.
Silvano Doravelli (752-822): First Doravelli Doge; founder of the bank. *Ruler:* Doge Silvano Doravelli (the Banker), Lucerna, 806–822 (RUL-1305).
Silvio Doravelli the Taster (925-980): Doge who tasted poison in the council's wine in 967. *Ruler:* Doge Silvio Doravelli the Taster, Lucerna, 965–980 (RUL-1315).
Marcello Doravelli (968-1047): Doge in the Debt War. *Ruler:* Doge Marcello Doravelli, Lucerna, 1027–1047 (RUL-1319).
Admiral Enzo Doravelli (1012-1060): Led Lucerna's galleys in the Corsair War.
marriages: 1038, with House Bassan: Marcello Doravelli's son Lucio married Bianca Bassan; Tiberio is their son, which binds two of the four toll families.
1070, with House Salvi: Tiberio married Chiara Salvi; under the Rule of the Cup their children are Doravellis.
FAM-120.allies: House Salvi, House Bassan, House Vanni, House Lunetti
FAM-120.secrets: The Doge holds the Lucernan copy of the Ratrock clause in his strongroom, knows the Sabran oil compact and Jory Flint's map, and has told none of it to his Admiral. His son has been offered 5,000 crowns by Prince Andros's chancellor to let a dish pass.

FAM-121.y1105: Shipowners and admirals, one of the four families of the secret toll share. The head is Admiral of the Republic and wants a fourth expedition to the upper Tirana gold.
FAM-121.arms: a silver galley on dark red
FAM-121.founder: Marco Salvi (about 680-745), shipmaster of the Tamar grain run
FAM-121.power: Ships: about 40 cogs and grain ships on the Tamar run. Office: Admiral of the Republic, commanding about 60 war galleys and the Arsenal's war fleet. Secret income: a quarter of the toll fifth, about 2,250 marks a year. Losses: half the cost of the failed gold expedition of 1097.
FAM-121.branches: The Lagoon line: shipowners and admirals
FAM-121.history: Marco Salvi was a shipmaster on the Tamar grain run after the contract of 645, and his heirs built a fleet of grain ships on the sea partnership of 726. The house has given Lucerna four Doges. Tomaso Salvi (771-786) widened the Arsenal; Renato Salvi (866-883) built the Lagoon Chain Towers; Fulvio Salvi (948-965) sold grain to Tessaria and its enemies alike. Pietro Salvi, born 1006, was elected Doge in 1047 at 41 and ruled 49 years. He fought the Corsair War beside Varenna and signed the Peace of Ratrock in 1056 with its secret clause, giving the fifth of the dragon toll to his own house, the Doravellis, the Bassans and the Vannis. In 1088 he told the new Master of the Arsenal what the lamp-oil jars were. His son Renzo, born 1054, commanded galleys in the Harbor Pox quarantine of 1076 and became Admiral in 1090. When Pietro died in 1096 the law that no son may follow his father kept Renzo out, and the dogeship went to Tiberio Doravelli. In 1097 Renzo paid half the cost of the Company of the Golden Stream with House Lunetti and sent it out a month late to save money; the Red Widow killed 190 of its 300 men. He now leads the Gold Venture, and he has hired an agent in Madara to buy the survivor Jory Flint behind the Doge's back. Admiral Nino Castellan of Varenna thinks him a friend from the Corsair War and does not know about the toll share.
dead: Doge Pietro Salvi (1006-1096): Signed the Peace of Ratrock and its secret clause. *Ruler:* Doge Pietro Salvi, Lucerna, 1047–1096 (RUL-1320).
Doge Renato Salvi (808-883): Built the Lagoon Chain Towers. *Ruler:* Doge Renato Salvi, Lucerna, 866–883 (RUL-1309).
marriages: 1070, with House Doravelli: Pietro's daughter Chiara married Tiberio Doravelli.
FAM-121.allies: House Doravelli, House Bassan, House Vanni
FAM-121.secrets: Renzo sent the 1097 expedition out late and is trying to buy Jory Flint behind the Doge's back. His house takes a share of the dragon toll that his Varennan friend has sworn to end.

FAM-122.y1105: Weighers of the Grain Staple since 358, lords of the salt pans and windmills of Lavium, and one of the four toll families. Its head is Keeper of the Staple and is squeezing the Holy See over grain while her salt-workers strike.
FAM-122.arms: a gold balance on dark red
FAM-122.founder: Tito Bassan (about 320-392), first weigher of the Grain Staple
FAM-122.power: Office: Keeper of the Grain Staple, which weighs every grain ship crossing the Middle Sea and takes one bushel in twenty. Land: the Lavium flats with their salt pans and nine post windmills; land at Marira in Tamar, taken in repayment in 1088. Trade: a sea-insurance house that posted the Ironjaw bounty. Secret income: a quarter of the toll fifth, and the grain gained from weights heavy by 1 in 100 since 1099.
FAM-122.branches: The Lavium line, lords of the flats; The Staple line, hereditary weighers
FAM-122.history: Tito Bassan was the first weigher of the Grain Staple when Cassian I founded it in 358, and his family has weighed the Staple's grain for 747 years. The weighers' families became Lucerna's first council houses, and in May 758 the Great Council elected Enrico Bassan, Keeper of the Staple, as the first Doge. The house has given Lucerna four Doges: Enrico, Marino, Guido, who died of the Black Cough in 916, and Leonardo. It also took the Lavium flats on the island's windy east, with their salt pans. In 1075 a miller on Bassan land at Lavium built the first post windmill, and the Bassans now own nine. In 1056 Doge Pietro Salvi made the Bassans one of the four families sharing the fifth of the dragon toll. Giulia Bassan was born at Lavium in 1058, learned the counting school's zero at seven, ran her father's windmills from 1080 and became Keeper of the Staple in 1091. She lent grain to Tamar in its Hungry Year of 1088 and was repaid in land at Marira. Since 1099 her weighers have used weights heavy by 1 in 100, and the extra grain goes to Bassan warehouses. In 1103 she raised the milling toll, and the salt-workers of Lavium under Marro of Lavium struck. Her insurers posted a 5,000-crown bounty on Old Ironjaw the same year. In 1105 she is holding back Solenne's spring grain ships until Treasurer Dorn agrees to pay a tenth more.
dead: Doge Enrico Bassan (699-771): First Doge of Lucerna. *Ruler:* Doge Enrico Bassan (the First Doge), Lucerna, 758–771 (RUL-1301).
Doge Guido Bassan (836-916): Fed Morhaven in the siege; died of the Black Cough. *Ruler:* Doge Guido Bassan, Lucerna, 895–916 (RUL-1311).
marriages: 1038, with House Doravelli: Bianca Bassan married into House Doravelli; she was Doge Tiberio's mother.
FAM-122.allies: House Doravelli, House Salvi, House Vanni
FAM-122.secrets: The Staple's weights are heavy by 1 in 100, and the house takes its share of the dragon toll.

FAM-123.y1105: Fig and salt-fish lords of Tibenza and holders of the Night Watch, the harbor police. They run the Ostran front house that passes Lucerna's fifth of the dragon toll.
FAM-123.arms: a green fig tree on gold
FAM-123.founder: Benno Vanni (about 620-690), fig planter of Tibenza
FAM-123.power: Land: the town of Tibenza and the southern fig orchards and fishing coves. Trade: salt fish and dried figs, about 15,000 suns a year. Office: Lord of the Night Watch, with the harbor police and patrol boats. Secret: the Ostran front house that receives Blackreef's payments and pays the four families, a quarter of the fifth, and the forger Ithel Varo in its pay.
FAM-123.history: Benno Vanni planted figs on the Tibenza shore in the 7th century, and his heirs added salt fish and smuggling coves. The house has given Lucerna four Doges: Alvise (799-806), Aldo (851-866), Ernesto (933-948) and Giorgio (1011-1027). Doge Giorgio Vanni secretly paid for Sabra's revolt against Qadir from 1020 and made the oil compact of 1025 that brings 400 jars of fire-oil to the Arsenal every year. Vanni men have often led the Night Watch, which patrols the lagoon by boat and drowns traitors quietly at night. In 1056 Doge Pietro Salvi made the Vannis one of the four toll families and had them set up the front house in Ostra that receives Blackreef's payments. Marco Vanni was born at Tibenza in 1062, joined the Night Watch at 20 and became its Lord in 1094. His father told him of the Ratrock clause in 1090, and Marco took over the front house when his father died in 1098. That year he caught the half-elf forger Ithel Varo with a false seal and offered him work instead of the lagoon. In 1102 the Night Watch drowned the front-house clerk Pio Ferro for trying to sell its ledgers to Varenna. In 1104 Lady Flavia Morello asked Marco for a share in exchange for her silence; he refused her, and now he is hunting her source.
dead: Doge Giorgio Vanni (950-1027): Paid for Sabra's revolt; made the oil compact. *Ruler:* Doge Giorgio Vanni, Lucerna, 1011–1027 (RUL-1318).
FAM-123.allies: House Doravelli, House Salvi, House Bassan, House Lunetti
FAM-123.secrets: The Night Watch drowned Pio Ferro in 1102. The front house's ledgers sit in the Lunetti vault at Ostra, and Ithel Varo keeps true copies of every letter he forged for the house.

FAM-124.y1105: One of Lucerna's oldest council houses, left out of the secret toll share in 1056. Its head leads the Clean Ledger, which hunts the hidden payments and wants the next dogeship for an honest house.
FAM-124.arms: a white ship's ledger on dark red
FAM-124.founder: Davide Morello (about 330-395), grain weigher of the first Staple
FAM-124.power: Ships: shares in about 12 cogs, voted by the head as her late husband's heir. Votes: a seat in the Great Council and the lead of about a dozen council families in the Clean Ledger. Trade: Palella cloth bought from the Weavers' Guild of Dorium. Knowledge: Chiara Benn's sums on the Ostran front house.
FAM-124.history: Davide Morello weighed grain beside the Bassans at the first Staple in 358, and the Morellos were among the first council houses. The house has given Lucerna four Doges: Giacomo (786-799), Carlo (839-851), Ruggero the Careful (916-933), who made the Forty-Day Law of 917 and the Sea Maiden Law of 922, and Andrea (994-1011). In 1056 Lord Bruno Morello spoke in the Great Council against making peace with Blackreef, and Doge Pietro Salvi left his house out when he shared the secret fifth of the dragon toll among four families. Bruno's daughter Flavia was born in 1066. Her husband, the shipmaster Teo Arvo, took the Morello name when they married, and when he died in 1090 she began to vote his ship shares in the Great Council. In 1103 she noticed payments from an Ostran house in a partner's books. In 1104 she asked Marco Vanni for a share in exchange for her silence and was refused, and then she founded the Clean Ledger with a dozen council families. The counting-school mistress Chiara Benn traces the payments for her. Flavia suspects that Beatrice Lunetti of Ostra holds every front-house entry in her memory.
dead: Doge Ruggero Morello the Careful (858-933): Made the Forty-Day Law. *Ruler:* Doge Ruggero Morello (the Careful), Lucerna, 916–933 (RUL-1312).
Lord Bruno Morello (1024-1089): Spoke against the Peace of Ratrock and was left out of the toll share.
marriages: 1084, with Teo Arvo, shipmaster: Flavia's husband took the Morello name; he died in 1090.
FAM-124.rivals: House Doravelli, House Vanni, House Bassan
FAM-124.secrets: Before founding the Clean Ledger, Flavia tried to buy into the toll share herself and was refused.

FAM-011.y1105: Royal house of Ashmere. King Edric, 71, has sunk into a black mood since signing the hidden clause; his only child Rowena is heir and is to marry Prince Harald of Aldmark on 21 June 1105.
FAM-011.arms: a red longbow drawn over a black mountain, on ash grey
FAM-011.founder: Aldred Ashford (738–797), first King of Ashmere
FAM-011.power: The crown of Ashmere: the Crown Vale and Ashmere Castle; the crown's fifth of all copper, a third of its silver; the hearth tax and the arrow tax of 24 arrows a hearth; 60,000 standing troops and a levy of 260,000, including the 2,400 King's Bowmen; the ember mint; the royal chapel and the loyalty of the yeomen, who owe their land to the Ashwater Charter.
FAM-011.branches: the royal line at Ashmere; the Embermere Ashfords, descended from a younger son of Godric II, lords of Embermere
FAM-011.history: The Ashfords were valley reeves under the Solen governors of the Ash March, Northfolk lords who collected the copper fifth and kept the roads. When the governors fled in 741 they became lords of the Ashmere valley. Aldred Ashford, born 738, slept four hours a night and used the rest riding between his rivals. In September 771 he married Hild, heiress of Brightkeep, bought the Hawkmarch, Crowbrook and Swanburg lords with copper shares, and was crowned on Return Day 772. Four years later Mount Cinder buried the Ashwater, and his son Aldred II gave the buried land to the yeomen who would clear it. The Ashfords have leaned on those yeomen against their lords ever since. Eleven Ashfords have reigned. Edwin I built the castle; Godric I the Copper King opened the deep galleries; Aldred III the Bowman made the Butts Law in 894; Edwin II died of the Black Cough in 916; Godric II rebuilt. The Wakeful trait runs in about half the line, and it has made the house both brilliant and dangerous. Cedric the Unsleeping doubled the Hawkmarch toll in a bold fit in 975, provoked the rising of 976 and pardoned the rebels in a black mood. His son Edgar carried the trait but had few fits, and his council never feared him. Edgar married Aelfgifu Hawkmarch in 980 to heal the rising, lost his only son in 998 and made the Law of the Eldest Child in 1001. His cousin Aldric of Embermere challenged it in 1003 and backed down before 6,000 yeoman archers; the Embermere branch has sat outside the Privy Council since. Elsbeth the Wakeful (981–1055) ruled 52 years. She sealed the Yew Compact, won the Brightwash by a night march, lost the river war to Varenna's galleys, and outlived her only son, Crown Prince Aldred, who died in 1051 after a bold ride through sleet. She died in a black mood in 1055. Her grandson Edric, born 1033, has reigned since 1055. He married Gwenith of Swanburg in 1069 and lost her in 1084. Their eldest child and only survivor, Rowena, born 1071, carries the Wakeful blood, commands the King's Bowmen and is betrothed to Prince Harald of Aldmark. In March 1104, in a bold fit, Edric signed the hidden clause that gives Ashmere to the emperor if Rowena bears no son. He signed it without his Chancellor's counter-seal, a custom his own house made after 977. The Ashfords are crowned by their council and their yeomen, bless their heirs in the Sun chapel and swear on the iron ring in the hall, and so they have kept both faiths of Ashmere at arm's length. They are archers first: every Ashford child draws a bow at seven, and every Ashford king shoots at the King's Butts on Return Day.
dead: Aldred I Ashford the Founder (738–797): First King of Ashmere; the first known Wakeful. *Ruler:* Aldred Ashford (Aldred I the Founder), Kingdom of Ashmere, 772–797 (RUL-0030).
Aldred II the Ash-Sower (763–824): Ashwater Charter of 798. *Ruler:* Aldred Ashford (Aldred II the Ash-Sower), Kingdom of Ashmere, 797–824 (RUL-0031).
Aldred III the Bowman (841–903): Butts Law of 894. *Ruler:* Aldred Ashford (Aldred III the Bowman), Kingdom of Ashmere, 872–903 (RUL-0034).
Cedric the Unsleeping (922–979): His bold-fit toll caused the Hawkmarch rising of 976. *Ruler:* Cedric Ashford (Cedric I the Unsleeping), Kingdom of Ashmere, 949–979 (RUL-0037).
Elsbeth the Wakeful (981–1055): First ruling queen; the Brightwash night march. *Ruler:* Elsbeth Ashford (Elsbeth I the Wakeful), Kingdom of Ashmere, 1003–1055 (RUL-0039).
Crown Prince Aldred Ashford (1004–1051): Elsbeth's son and Edric's father; died after a bold ride through sleet.
marriages: 771, with House of Brightkeep: Aldred married Hild of Brightkeep, joining the two largest upland lordships.
980, with House Hawkmarch: Edgar married Aelfgifu Hawkmarch to heal the rising; mother of Elsbeth.
1069, with House of Swanburg: Edric married Gwenith of Swanburg; mother of Rowena.
1104, with House Ironside: Rowena betrothed to Prince Harald of Aldmark, with the hidden clause.
FAM-011.allies: House Cinderwell, House Ironside, The Mistwalkers
FAM-011.secrets: Edric signed the hidden Ashmere clause in a bold fit and without the Chancellor's counter-seal. Rowena lost 4,000 embers of the Bowmen's pay on a wager in 1103 and covered it from the arrow tax stores.
