FAM-012.y1105: Hereditary shield-bearers of the crown. Sir Owain captains the King's Guard and witnessed the hidden clause; his blind father keeps the Shield Yard through his daughter Bryony.
FAM-012.arms: a grey tower shield on black, sown with red embers
FAM-012.founder: Sir Tobin Cinderwell (940–999), first Captain of the King's Guard
FAM-012.power: The lordship of Kingsdale, a town of 3,300, and about 6,000 acres; the hereditary captaincy of the King's Guard; the 200 heavy shield-men of the Cinderwell Shield Guard; the Cinderwell Shield Yard, one of the 66 fighting schools, which trains every royal shield-bearer; the right to stand behind the throne at every crowning.
FAM-012.history: The Cinderwells were yeomen of the Cinder slopes. Mount Cinder buried their farm in 776, and they dug down through 4 m of ash to find their old well, which gave the family its name. Under the Ashwater Charter they cleared and kept 60 acres on the new ash. Tobin Cinderwell, born 940, was the first of them with the oak tendons: a stiff, slow boy who could carry a plough-ox yoke on his shoulders at 14 and never tore a sinew wrestling at the May Fair. He joined the royal guard as a spearman in 960. In April 976 the Hawkmarch lords reached the half-shut gate of Ashmere with 2,000 men. Tobin held the 3 m gateway from dawn to dusk with a shield and twelve guards, seven of whom died. At the Pardon of Harrowbrook in 977 King Cedric made him first Captain of the King's Guard and gave him Kingsdale. His son Sir Harwin Cinderwell (970–1036) captained Queen Elsbeth's shield guard in the Varenna–Ashmere War and covered her retreat when she chased too far at the Brightwash in 1014. Harwin's son Sir Edmer (1002–1062) carried Elsbeth's coffin in 1055 and kept the captaincy until his death. Edmer's son Tobias, born 1036, stood in the shield guard at Edric's crowning in 1055, was captain from 1062 to 1098 and has trained every royal shield-bearer for 40 years at the Shield Yard in Kingsdale. He married Aveline of Windvale, a yeoman's daughter, in 1058. Their eldest son Owain, born 1060, held the royal chapel door against Ashen rioters on Ash Night 1094 and became captain in 1098. Their younger son Tobin serves in the guard. Their daughter Bryony, born 1075, passed the gate test at 17 and joined the Shield Guard in 1096, the second woman ever to do so; since 1100 she has guarded Princess Rowena's door. In March 1104 Owain stood behind King Edric at Kingsmere when the hidden clause was signed, and swore on his sword to say nothing. Tobias is going blind, and since 1102 Bryony has judged the Shield Yard's tests in his name. The Cinderwells are proud of being yeomen who became lords by holding a gate, and they still marry the daughters of yeoman families of the guard. They insist that the 400 Cinderwell shield-men, and no Aldmark knights, must escort the princess at her wedding.
dead: Sir Tobin Cinderwell (940–999): Held the gate of Ashmere for a day in 976.
Sir Harwin Cinderwell (970–1036): Captain of Elsbeth's shield guard in the war with Varenna.
Sir Edmer Cinderwell (1002–1062): Captain of the guard; carried Elsbeth's coffin.
marriages: 1058, with Aveline of Windvale: Tobias married a yeoman's daughter of Windvale, as Cinderwells do.
FAM-012.rivals: House Hawkmarch, the Iron Guard of Aldmark
FAM-012.secrets: Owain witnessed the hidden Ashmere clause. Tobias is going blind, and Bryony judges the Shield Yard's tests in his name; in 1104 she failed a Hawkmarch lord's son out of spite.

FAM-013.y1105: Pass lords of the south, loyal in name, trading quietly with Varenna. Lord Ranulf has joined the River Party and smuggles war bows over his pass.
FAM-013.arms: a golden hawk over a white road on dark green
FAM-013.founder: Oswy Hawkmarch (about 710–780), warden of the pass road after the Solen governors fled
FAM-013.power: Harrowbrook, a castle town of 3,300 below the Hawkmarch Pass; half of the pass toll, restored in 977; about 800 men-at-arms and the pass garrisons; friendships among Varenna's border lords; a tenth of every smuggled load of war bows.
FAM-013.history: The Hawkmarchs were the Solen road-wardens' sergeants on the high pass over the Ash Range, and when the governors fled in 741 they kept the road and its toll. Aldred Ashford bought them in 772 with a copper share and the right to half the pass toll. In March 975 King Cedric doubled the toll and took their share in a bold fit. In April 976 the Hawkmarch lords rose with 2,000 men and broke on the gate that Tobin Cinderwell held. At Harrowbrook in 977 Cedric pardoned them, gave back their share and made them wardens of the road. In 980 King Edgar married Aelfgifu Hawkmarch, so Queen Elsbeth was half Hawkmarch, and the house has sworn loyalty to every king since. Ranulf Hawkmarch, born 1049, is the great-grandson of one of the rebels of 976. He inherited Harrowbrook in 1074, guided Ashmere's envoys over the pass to Varenna in the 1080s and made friends among Varenna's border lords, among them Lord Bertran Ardane. He joined Lady Isolde Varley's River Party in 1104 and will refuse to let an Aldmark escort pass through or garrison Harrowbrook. He takes a tenth of every load of war bows carried over his pass to Varenna, which is treason under Ashmere law. The Hawkmarchs remember that a Cinderwell broke their fathers at the gate, and that a Cinderwell daughter failed their heir at the Shield Yard in 1104.
dead: Oswy Hawkmarch (about 710–780): Kept the pass road after 741.
Aelfgifu Hawkmarch (958–1020): Queen of Edgar and mother of Elsbeth the Wakeful.
marriages: 980, with House Ashford: Aelfgifu Hawkmarch married King Edgar Ashford.
FAM-013.secrets: Ranulf takes a tenth of every load of war bows smuggled over the Hawkmarch Pass to Varenna, which is treason in Ashmere.

FAM-014.y1105: River merchants of Crowbrook and heads of the Bargemen. Lady Isolde leads the River Party and writes to Varenna about the wedding.
FAM-014.arms: a broken silver chain across a blue river, on ash grey
FAM-014.founder: Godwin Varley (about 725–790), river lord of Crowbrook
FAM-014.power: The barge quays of Crowbrook, a city of 23,200; the Crowbrook Bargemen, about 2,000 bargemen and 400 barges that carry most of Ashmere's goods to the sea; a Varennan loan of 10,000 suns at no interest; the ear of Varenna's court.
FAM-014.history: The Varleys stretched an iron chain across the Ashwater at Crowbrook about 760 and took a toll from every barge that passed. Aldred Ashford bought them in 772 with a copper share and the right to keep the chain. For 250 years the Crowbrook toll made them the richest house in Ashmere after the crown. The Varenna–Ashmere War ended that. Varenna fought for untaxed barges (WAR-27), and by the Peace of Dorium in 1016 the chain came down. The Varleys changed their arms to a broken chain and turned to carrying goods instead of taxing them. They built barges, bought quays and ran the Crowbrook Bargemen. Their fortune now rests on Varennan trade, and their politics follow it. Isolde Varley, born 1058, married a Varennan wine factor in 1077 and learned the Palella trade from him until he died of the Harbor Pox in 1078. She became head of the house in 1086 and of the Bargemen in 1092. Since March 1104 she has written to Varenna every month, giving King Roderic's court the wedding date, the escort's size and news of King Edric's silence, and a Varennan banking house has lent her 10,000 suns at no interest. Her bargewoman Nessa Dunmore copies every letter for the Chancellor. Isolde means to get the Yeomen's Moot to refuse the dowry tax and delay the match past Return Day.
dead: Godwin Varley (about 725–790): Stretched the first toll chain across the Ashwater.
marriages: 1077, with a Varennan wine house: Isolde married a Varennan wine factor, who died of the Harbor Pox in 1078.
FAM-014.secrets: Isolde's letters have given Varenna the wedding date and escort, and she has taken a Varennan loan of 10,000 suns without interest.

FAM-015.y1105: A yeoman family of Swanburg risen through the bows and the halls. Gudrun speaks for the Common Halls on the Privy Council; her brother Godwin is Warden of the Stag Downs.
FAM-015.arms: a green hall roof over a red arrow, on white
FAM-015.words: One to the Hall, One to the Bow
FAM-015.founder: Wat Ashdown (about 770–840), yeoman of the Ashwater Charter
FAM-015.power: About 600 acres of free ash land at Swanburg; the Wardenship of the Stag Downs with command of Stagley's garrison of about 1,800, half of them archers; the Speakership of the Common Halls, the voice of Ashmere's village halls on the Privy Council.
FAM-015.history: Wat Ashdown was one of the landless men who came up from the southern downs in 798 under the Ashwater Charter and cleared 40 acres of ash near Swanburg. His family kept the land free and kept a rule that is still their motto: one child to the hall, one to the bow. For 250 years the Ashdowns gave the village halls their singers and keepers and the King's Bowmen their sergeants. Wat Ashdown the Younger (1018–1080), a sergeant of the Bowmen, was the father of the two Ashdowns who matter in 1105. Gudrun, born 1050, became a hall-singer at 17 and a hall-keeper in 1080. When the Edict of the Halls came in 1089 she walked to every hall in the Crown Vale to warn them, and she was chosen Speaker of the Common Halls in 1096. She opposed the iron-ring rite for the royal wedding from the start and has written to Hall-Keeper Aelfric of Amberhurst that Ashmere's village halls will join the Free Halls of the north if the emperor claims them. Her brother Godwin, born 1055, joined the King's Bowmen at 17 and hunted Ashen cultists and Hael Hounds in the Stag Downs for twenty years. In 1099 he rode into the Ashlands to recover the bodies of two Varennan surveyors killed by Hael Hounds, and King Edric knighted him and made him Warden of the Stag Downs. He oversaw the new walls of Stagley in 1100 and took a bribe to pass cheap mortar. The Ashdowns are the yeomen's family at court: plain, proud, and suspicious of lords, Luminaries and emperors alike.
dead: Wat Ashdown (about 770–840): Charter settler who cleared the family's land at Swanburg.
Wat Ashdown the Younger (1018–1080): Sergeant of the King's Bowmen; father of Gudrun and Godwin.
FAM-015.secrets: Godwin took 300 embers to pass hollow walls at Stagley. Gudrun has promised that Ashmere's halls will join the Free Halls of the north, which the crown could call treason.

FAM-401.y1105: Ruling line of Sylvaran for 5,316 years, now down to two carriers: Queen Ithrien, about 586, and her half-elf grandson Thalion Halfleaf in Eldergrove, whom the law bars from the crown.
FAM-401.arms: a silver oak whose roots and branches touch all four edges, on deep green
FAM-401.words: We plant for those not yet born.
FAM-401.founder: Queen Aelinwe (4390–3805 BR), who planted the First Oak
FAM-401.power: The crown of about 780,000 people and the chair of the Moot of Leaves. The queen's own groves around Evenglade, about 1,200 km² of the Heartwood. Command of 10,000 standing rangers and archers and, with the Moot's consent, a levy of 40,000. The Keepers' store at Evenglade: about 3,000 dwarf crowns, the tithe of honey, wax and arrows, and the unspent 20,000 marks of Rinael, which the queen may spend only with the Moot.
FAM-401.branches: The crowned line at Evenglade (Queen Ithrien); The half-elf branch at Silverbough: Thalion Halfleaf, son of Prince Caelan (born 1019); About 30 non-carrier kin of the Heartwood groves who took other line names after the Keepers' test and cannot pass the trait on
FAM-401.history: The Oakborn are the descendants of Queen Aelinwe, the first elf known to age slowly. The Keepers noticed it in her 150th year. When she planted the First Oak in 4211 BR, aged about 179, she looked like an elf of 100. She ruled 406 years. Her daughter Elunwe had the same slow clock and lived 670 years, and in the first centuries of the Grove Count the Moot made the crown hereditary in the line. Eighteen Oakborn have ruled since: twelve queens and six kings. The line has never been large. An Oakborn bears a child only every two or three centuries, and only about half of those children carry the deep years. At its largest, around 2500 BR, the Leaf Records count 17 living carriers; in 1105 there are two. The family's history is a list of trees and of losses. Queen Mirwen planted the Second Oak after the First fell in 3140 BR, and every planting since has been an Oakborn duty: Ylinwe in 2058 BR, Aerande in 983 BR, Maerith in 94 AR. King Vaelion was killed by orc raiders in 1432 BR, and his sister Lirwen gave the Keepers leave to burn the southern wood in 1410 BR, a secret the family has kept for 2,500 years. Queen Aranwe the Hard shut the forest against the starving humans in 9 BR. Queen Maerith won the War of the Forest Edge and sent Nimrael away in 340. King Caerion ruled 321 years and was 406 when his only child Ithrien was born in 518. Ithrien married Aerlan of Fenali, born into House Fenali, in 790; he died in 1004. Their only child, Prince Caelan, was born in 830. He learned the bow from Aelar the Silent and the sword from Vaelor the Unhurried, and spent long seasons at Nimthil among the Eldergrove ship-houses. There he fathered Thalion on Merra of Nimthil, a human sail-maker's daughter, in 1019; they never married. Caelan was gored by a black aurochs bull near Lirthil in October 1036, aged 206, and buried under a sapling planted by Naeris Seedfall. Thalion is the only child born to the line in five centuries. He carries the deep years: at 86 he looks like a half-elf of 45. He was born and raised a citizen of Eldergrove, and Sylvaran's law does not count him, because a half-elf may not own land or sit in the Moot. The other living kin are about 30 non-carriers in the Heartwood groves, who took other line names after the Keepers' test. When Ithrien dies, the Oakborn crown ends unless the Moot changes the law.
dead: Queen Aelinwe (4390–3805 BR): Planted the First Oak and founded the Moot. *Ruler:* Queen Aelinwe (the Planter), Kingdom of Sylvaran, 4211–3805 BR (RUL-4001).
Queen Mirwen the Replanter (3575–2930 BR): Planted the Second Oak. *Ruler:* Mirwen the Oakborn (Queen Mirwen the Replanter), Kingdom of Sylvaran, 3245–2930 BR (RUL-4004).
King Vaelion the Unlucky (1806–1432 BR): Killed by orc raiders in the Old Edge Wars. *Ruler:* Vaelion the Oakborn (King Vaelion the Unlucky), Kingdom of Sylvaran, 1476–1432 BR (RUL-4010).

Queen Lirwen the Grey (1782–1150 BR): Allowed the Year of Ash Trees; made the Peace of the Grass Line. *Ruler:* Lirwen the Oakborn (Queen Lirwen the Grey), Kingdom of Sylvaran, 1432–1150 BR (RUL-4011).
Queen Aranwe the Hard (610 BR–66 AR): Closed the forest in the Dimming. *Ruler:* Aranwe the Oakborn (Queen Aranwe the Hard), Kingdom of Sylvaran, 250 BR–66 (RUL-4015).
Queen Maerith the Unbending (264 BR–391 AR): Won the War of the Forest Edge; planted the Fifth Oak. *Ruler:* Maerith the Oakborn (Queen Maerith the Unbending), Kingdom of Sylvaran, 66–391 (RUL-4016).
marriages: 790, with House Fenali: Ithrien married Aerlan of Fenali; their son Caelan was born in 830.
1019, with Merra of Nimthil (human, no house): Not a marriage: Prince Caelan and Merra never wed. Their son Thalion was born at Nimthil.
FAM-401.allies: The Quickened, House Fenali, House Brightleaf
FAM-401.secrets: Ithrien met Thalion secretly at Mirlas at Leaf Fall 1103 and gave him Caelan's green-stone ring. The line has hidden the Year of Ash Trees since 1410 BR, and since spring 1104 the queen has lost feeling in her left hand.

FAM-402.y1105: Masters of Sylvaran's sword school and the queen's close guard. About 50 living kin, 14 of them carriers.
FAM-402.arms: a silver needle-blade crossed by a falling leaf, on black
FAM-402.founder: Sethril the Unwounded (460–877), the first carrier
FAM-402.power: The School of the Quickened at Evenglade; the Swordmaster of the Moot's seat on the queen's council; command of the Queen's Quickened, 120 duelists, of whom 11 are carriers; two of the finest swords alive, Vaelor and Veyla.
FAM-402.branches: Maerwen's line at Evenglade (Vaelor, Veyla, Aeron); The Lirith cousins, bowyers and yew-cutters, most of them non-carriers
FAM-402.history: The Quickened began with Sethril, born in 460 to a family of yew-cutters at Lirith. As a child he caught falling acorns before they reached the ground, and the Keepers timed him with a dropped rod: a blink sooner than any other elf they had timed. He became the greatest duelist of the elves. In June 527 he killed the Solen knight Sir Marcus Ravel at the Oak Line in four passes, and he stayed unbeaten for 400 years. In October 877 his grandson Vaelor moved his last bout at Evenglade from the lamp-lit hall into the torch-lit court so the crowd could see. The flicker brought on a fit, Sethril fell against a stone stair, and he died five days later. The Keepers wrote the true cause in their death record, and the sword schools banned bouts by torchlight without saying why. Only about one child in three carries the trait, and it skips generations. Sethril's daughter Maerwen, born 590, bore Vaelor in 688 and Sael in 720. Sael did not carry it; her children Veyla, born 870, and Thandil, born 902, did. Veyla married Caeron of Lirith, a bowyer, and bore Aeron in 990. In the Lost March of April 1079 Veyla led twelve Quickened with Calithil's rangers; Thandil's son Serin had a fit in the light of a burning wagon and was cut down. She told the Moot a crossbow bolt killed him. The line guards the queen and the secret of its weakness in equal measure, and Veyla keeps every carrier off night patrols.
dead: Sethril the Unwounded (460–877): Unbeaten for 400 years; died after a torchlit bout.
Maerwen of the Quickened (590–1002): Sethril's daughter, mother of Vaelor.
Serin of the Quickened (1010–1079): Killed during a fit in the Lost March.
marriages: 985, with Caeron of Lirith (bowyer line): Veyla married the bowyer Caeron; their son Aeron was born in 990.
FAM-402.secrets: Serin died in a fit, not of a bolt (1079), and Aeron had a fit in August 1103. Vaelor believes he killed Sethril by moving the bout of 877 into torchlight.

FAM-403.y1105: Ranger line of the Eastern Edge. Its head, Calithil, is Ranger-Captain of Sylvaran, one of the deadliest fighters alive and the Deep Root's choice of heir.
FAM-403.arms: a green leaf falling past a silver branch, on grey
FAM-403.power: Command of the Rangers of the Edge (2,400) and the Lightfoot Scouts (600) from Rinael Hall; the signal fires and ranger stores of the Eastern Edge; leadership of the Edge Wardens in the Moot.
FAM-403.branches: Rinael Hall line (Calithil); The scout families of Rinael and Elwen, about 40 carriers who form the core of the Lightfoot Scouts
FAM-403.history: Faelas Leafstep was born at Rinael in 380, a slight child who climbed before he could talk. His bones were so light that he broke his arm three times before he was 100, and so sure-footed that he ran along branches as thin as a wrist. In August 501 a charcoal-burners' fire from the Calena woods crossed the Oak Line near Aeravel. Faelas ran the canopy 160 km to Evenglade in a day and a half, and the Keepers cut a firebreak in time. King Caerion made his kin the realm's couriers in 502, and the Lightfoot Scouts have carried the Moot's word since. Faelas fell from a storm-broken branch at 390, broke both legs and walked with sticks until he died in 790. His great-grandson Calithil was born at Rinael in 781, ran messages from 830 and has been Ranger-Captain since 1003. In May 1078 his watcher Rhovan Greyleaf reported Aldmark loggers across the line near Foxhurst. After three warnings Calithil led the night attack of 23 September 1078 that burned three camps and killed 140 loggers but spared the boys. In the Lost March of April 1079 his rangers killed about 400 Aldmark men and left no elven body behind. That winter, without the Moot's leave, he showed Aldmark's envoy the Solen sun seal on the secret seventh clause; that is why Aldmark paid at Rinael. The Lightfoot share Rinael with House Brightleaf and quarrel with it over every cart that crosses the edge. The line has never married into the Oakborn, but Arannel's Deep Root names Calithil as the pure-blood heir it wants, and he has not said yes.
dead: Faelas Leafstep (380–790): Ran 160 km to warn of the Aeravel fire; founder of the Scouts.
Aelwyn Lightfoot (650–1044): Calithil's father; carried word of Kingsmere's first army to Evenglade in 780.
marriages: 760, with Rinael ranger kin: Aelwyn Lightfoot married a ranger of Rinael; Calithil was born in 781.
FAM-403.rivals: The Quickened, House Brightleaf, The Honeyhands
FAM-403.secrets: Calithil showed Aldmark the seventh clause in 1079 without the Moot's leave. The line counts 23 carriers crippled and 9 killed by single blows since 502, a weakness it hides from every enemy.

FAM-404.y1105: Wardens of the Oak Line and keepers of the elven map of its 212 stones. Head Thalanor is Warden of the Oak Line and a cousin of the late Prince Caelan.
FAM-404.arms: twelve silver stones in a curved line under a green oak, on brown
FAM-404.founder: Faeral of Fenali (about 890–470 BR), first warden of the southern edge
FAM-404.power: Fenali, a grove city of 27,000 on the Clarora road; Fenali Watch, which sees the stones for 20 km; the southern ranger posts under Faelan Ashgrove, about 800 rangers; the office of Warden of the Oak Line; the elven copy of the map of the 212 stones.
FAM-404.branches: Fenali Watch line (Thalanor); The Aeravel branch, whose groves burned in 301 and 501; Aerlan's line, which married into the Oakborn in 790
FAM-404.history: House Fenali has watched the forest's southern edge for 1,600 years. About 600 BR human farmers reached the Palella and Clarora valleys. In 520 BR Queen Nimwen set a permanent watch on the hills above the Clarora, and the grove elder Faeral of Fenali took it. His kin built the tree platforms and timber hall of Fenali Watch and turned back woodcutters with painted trees, then with arrows. By the time of the Solen kingdom Fenali was the largest grove city of the south. The house's great age was the War of the Forest Edge. In October 296 the Solen marched 14,000 men up the Clarora to burn Fenali itself. Taeris of Fenali, then head of the house, held the hill groves with 600 archers for three days while Nimrael's rangers struck the column in the fog. In August 301 the Solen burned the edge from Fenali to Aeravel, and the house lost its eastern groves and 90 of its kin. On 22 September 302 Taeris stood below Fenali when Maximian II signed the Treaty of the Oak Line. The house drew and still keeps the elven copy of the map of the 212 stones, and the Moot has named a Fenali as Warden of the Oak Line more often than any other line. In 501 the Aeravel branch lost its groves a second time, to a charcoal fire from Calena. In 790 Aerlan of Fenali married Queen Ithrien, and their son Prince Caelan was born in 830; Aerlan died in 1004. Caelan's death in 1036 left the house with a half-elf grandson of Aerlan in Eldergrove and no place in the succession. Thalanor, born in 850 and grandson of Aerlan's brother, has led the house since 960 and has been Warden since 1040. In 1078 and 1079 he held the southern posts while Calithil struck in the east. In 1080 he walked the line with Aldmark's surveyors and set the new stones. The ground no longer matches the house's map: near Foxhurst nine stones now stand about 1.5 km south of their old places, taking in the stump field where Aldmark's loggers cut 300 oaks. Naeris Seedfall replanted that field with 300 acorns in 1081 at Thalanor's asking. The house backs the Edge Wardens. It has kept out of the heir quarrel in the Moot, though Thalion Halfleaf is Aerlan's grandson and Fenali blood. Each Leaf Fall Thalanor meets human envoys at the stone below Fenali, and he has refused every request from Varenna and Aldmark to walk the line again.
dead: Faeral of Fenali (about 890–470 BR): First warden of the southern edge.
Taeris of Fenali (about 150 BR–388 AR): Held Fenali in the Clarora Mist and stood at the signing of 302.
Aerlan of Fenali (536–1004): Consort of Queen Ithrien, father of Prince Caelan.
marriages: 790, with The Oakborn: Aerlan of Fenali married Queen Ithrien.
FAM-404.secrets: Thalanor moved nine Oak Line stones near Foxhurst about 1.5 km south in 1080; only the Fenali map shows the old line.

FAM-405.y1105: Grove elders of Rinael and leaders of the Open Leaf in the Moot, which wants the heir law changed so Thalion Halfleaf may inherit.
FAM-405.arms: a gold leaf edged in silver, on green
FAM-405.words: Open the door, keep the tree.
FAM-405.founder: Aelwen Brightleaf (about 480–60 BR), first grove elder of Rinael
FAM-405.power: Rinael's grove seat in the Moot; the edge-market rights at Rinael, where licensed human carters unload salt and iron; about 30 kin and elders who speak for the Eastern Edge groves.
FAM-405.branches: The elders' line of Rinael (Elowen); Rhun, Elowen's half-elf son (1013–1062), buried outside the Oak Line
FAM-405.history: The Brightleafs have been grove elders of Rinael since about 300 BR, when Aelwen Brightleaf planted the first gardens where the Eastern Edge meets the plains road. Rinael became the gate of the east. Dwarven carters from the Iron Mountains came there first, then human traders from Kingsmere after 780 and from Aldmark after 951. The house grew rich in honey and trade rights and learned human speech sooner than any other Moot family. In 1011 Elowen Brightleaf took a human lover, a licensed carpenter of the edge, and their half-elf son Rhun was born in 1013 without a birth tree. She became a grove elder in 1020. Rhun died of a fever in 1062 and was buried outside the Oak Line below Rinael, like a stranger; Naeris Seedfall planted a sapling on his grave when no Keeper would. Since Prince Caelan's death in 1036 Elowen has led the Open Leaf. In 1080 Aldmark paid its blood-price at Rinael, in sight of the house's gardens. Since 1102 Elowen has written in secret to Queen Saelith, promising that a Sylvaran under Thalion would call the Sea Covenant a true covenant. The Moot never gave her leave. The house and the Lightfoot share Rinael and little else: the Brightleafs want the edge opened to trade, the Lightfoot want it closed.
dead: Aelwen Brightleaf (about 480–60 BR): First grove elder of Rinael.
Rhun (1013–1062): Elowen's half-elf son, buried outside the Oak Line.
FAM-405.secrets: Elowen's letters to Queen Saelith since 1102 promise a new covenant that the Moot never approved.

FAM-406.y1105: Heads of the Wax Circle of Evenglade, the only body in Sylvaran that trades abroad in bulk; the house wants the edge opened to human carts.
FAM-406.arms: a gold bee on a brown comb, on green
FAM-406.founder: Linna Honeyhand (about 360–770), who first carried the Evenglade wax to the dwarven buyers
FAM-406.power: Leadership of the Wax Circle, which handles about 40,000 pounds of wax and 200,000 pounds of honey a year and sells about a fifth of it at the edge for salt, iron and dwarf crowns; a network of licensed human carters at Rinael and Foxhurst.
FAM-406.branches: The Evenglade hives (Caerwen); Aelis Farwander, Caerwen's daughter, who took her father's line name
FAM-406.history: The Honeyhands have kept bees in the Heartwood since the fourth century. About 410 Linna Honeyhand first carried the Evenglade wax tithe to the dwarven buyers at Rinael and brought back salt, and the Moot let her kin handle the edge trade under the Keepers' eye. The Wax Circle grew from that errand. It gathers the honey and wax that the groves pay as tithe and trades the surplus at the forest edge; the Keepers keep the rest in the store at Evenglade. When the Black Cough shut the edge from 916 to 925 the Circle's trade stopped, and the house nearly failed. Caerwen was born at Evenglade in 960 and became Head of the Wax Circle in 1071. She built the trade with dwarf buyers and in 1088 sent the first cart of Sylvaran wax through Kingsmere to the candlemakers of Solenne. In 1041 she bore her daughter Aelis to Taelen Farwander, a trader of the edge groves; Aelis took her father's line name. After the blood-price of 1080 Caerwen argued in vain that the 20,000 marks should buy salt. Since 1090 she has hidden about 400 dwarf crowns from the Keepers' chest in a money-changer's strongbox at Foxhurst, though elves may hold no private coin. Aelis wants an open market at Rinael on May Fair 1105 with Aldmark's Iron Road Company, and in 1103 she led two Aldmark traders down a hidden path to Rinael. One of them was a Ravenscar spy. The house is the Open Leaf's purse and the Edge Wardens' constant worry.
dead: Linna Honeyhand (about 360–770): First carried the wax tithe to the dwarven buyers.
marriages: 1035, with Taelen Farwander (edge-grove trader): Caerwen's union with Taelen; their daughter Aelis was born in 1041.
FAM-406.secrets: Caerwen's 400 hidden dwarf crowns at Foxhurst; Aelis showed a Ravenscar spy the hidden path to Rinael in 1103.

FAM-407.y1105: Ruling line of Eldergrove since 340: Queen Saelith and her heir Ilvara, captain of the Night Rangers. About 120 living kin, of whom about 60 carry the night sight.
FAM-407.arms: a grey veil drawn across a silver fir, on sea blue
FAM-407.words: We see what the dark hides.
FAM-407.founder: Nimrael the Grey Veil (about 200 BR–340 AR)
FAM-407.power: The crown of about 340,000 people and the chair of the Council of the Grey Veil; the queen's treasury at Silverbough; one voyage in ten from every ship-owner; the harbor fee of one part in twenty at Nimthil and Ithira; the Night Rangers of the Veil (400) and the Dusk School; the sealed copy of Serra's notebook in the Silverbough Archive.
FAM-407.branches: The queens' line at Silverbough (Saelith, Ilvara); The ranger kin of the Mistwood around Aerdor, who lead the Night Rangers of the Veil; Taeros's line, descendants of Nimrael's brother, now ship-captains of Nimthil
FAM-407.history: The Mistwalkers are the descendants of Nimrael the Grey Veil, born about 200 BR at Mirlas on Lake Silara with eyes that shone in lamplight. Her kin were night fishers of the lake, and their shining eyes fed the Silara Groves through the Dimming. Nimrael captained Sylvaran's night rangers in the War of the Forest Edge, won the Clarora Mist in 296 and led the elven envoys at the Treaty of the Oak Line in 302. Her brother Taeros sold 300 unmarked mast-oaks to the Solen fleet in 334–336, and in 340 the Moot asked her to leave rather than face judgment for it. Every carrier of the line went with her; no Mistwalker has lived in Sylvaran since. Nimrael founded Silverbough on Leaf Fall 340 and died that December. Six queens have taken the veil since, each named by her predecessor and confirmed by the council, and each a carrier: the family's lamp test, a lamp raised before the child's face at its naming, decides who may ever be named heir. Serewen built the first ships and made half-elves citizens; Aerdis founded Aerdor; Ilvara the Elder raised the Nimthil chain after the noon raid of 611, the day that taught the line it cannot fight in sunlight. Maelwen died without a carrier child in 910, and the veil passed to her niece Lithiel, daughter of Maelwen's sister Nesta and the captain Caladh Greywave. Lithiel drowned off Ithira in 1003. Her daughter Saelith, born 893, has ruled since. In 1005 Saelith married Elorin of Aelorn, a cousin of the yew wardens; their daughter Ilvara was born in 1010 and named for the old queen. Elorin died in 1088. Saelith took the orphaned Thalion Halfleaf into her household in 1036 and raised him beside Ilvara. In 1067 she received Serra's notebook and never answered his plea for refuge. Ilvara has been Heir of the Veil since 1060, captains the Night Rangers and masters the Dusk School. She and Thalion are secretly sworn to marry after Leaf Fall 1105, which would join the Mistwalkers and the Oakborn for the first time. The line's rulers have always been queens, and no one in Eldergrove thinks it odd. The family keeps two customs that outsiders notice. Every carrier wears a grey veil of fine gauze from dawn to dusk, and every queen is buried on a hill facing the sea, as Nimrael was. It also keeps one quarrel: the Eldest Keeper of Evenglade has held the Leaf Record of 340 for 765 years and has never let a Mistwalker envoy forget it.
dead: Nimrael the Grey Veil (about 200 BR–340 AR): Founder of Eldergrove; won the Clarora Mist. *Ruler:* Nimrael the Grey Veil (Queen Nimrael), Kingdom of Eldergrove, 340 (RUL-4021).
Taeros (about 170 BR–361 AR): Nimrael's brother, who sold the mast-oaks.
Queen Serewen the Builder (60 BR–388 AR): Built the Forty Ships; made half-elves citizens. *Ruler:* Serewen Mistwalker (Queen Serewen the Builder), Kingdom of Eldergrove, 340–388 (RUL-4022).
Queen Ilvara the Elder (330–742): Raised the Nimthil chain. *Ruler:* Ilvara Mistwalker (Queen Ilvara I the Elder), Kingdom of Eldergrove, 560–742 (RUL-4024).
Queen Lithiel the Drowned (660–1003): Beat the Black Cough at Nimthil; lost with the Silver Fir. *Ruler:* Lithiel Mistwalker (Queen Lithiel the Drowned), Kingdom of Eldergrove, 910–1003 (RUL-4026).
marriages: 650, with House Greywave: Nesta, sister of Maelwen, married Caladh Greywave; their daughter Lithiel took the veil in 910.
1005, with House Aelorn: Saelith married Elorin of Aelorn; their daughter Ilvara was born in 1010.
FAM-407.allies: House Greywave, House Aelorn, House Saltleaf
FAM-407.secrets: Saelith kept Serra's copy and ignored his plea for refuge. Ilvara and Thalion Halfleaf are secretly sworn to marry. The rulers know of Taeros's mast-oak sale.

FAM-408.y1105: Richest ship-house of Nimthil, owning about a quarter of Eldergrove's trading cogs. Its head Tavor is Fleet-Warden and owes House Lunetti of Ostra 30,000 suns.
FAM-408.arms: a grey wave breaking over a black keel, on white
FAM-408.founder: Tarael Greywave (about 60 BR–395 AR), master shipwright of the Forty Ships
FAM-408.power: About 17 of the realm's 70 trading cogs and four ship-houses at Nimthil; the office of Fleet-Warden since 1060, commanding 40 longships and the harbor watch; the right, since Queen Lithiel, to carry the queen's grain; Greywave pilots' hold on the lodestone needle. Against this, debts of 30,000 suns to House Lunetti, secured on nine cogs.
FAM-408.branches: The Nimthil ship-house line (Tavor); Loren Seabright, Tavor's unacknowledged half-elf son, born 1041; Caladh's line, which gave Eldergrove Queen Lithiel
FAM-408.history: House Greywave began with a shipwright. Tarael Greywave had built lake boats on Silara for Nimrael's night fishers, and in 340 he walked to the coast with her. With the fir of the new realm and the iron and rope bought by Taeros's silver, he taught 9,000 forest elves to build and in ten years launched the Forty Ships. The ship-house he built at Nimthil still stands on the same ground, rebuilt five times. His grandson Oren Greywave was the first captain buried under a fir whose wood became a keel: in 470 his crew asked for it, the Sea Keeper marked it, and Queen Aerdis allowed it. The Greywaves have sailed on their dead since, and Sylvaran has called it robbing graves since. In the centuries of the Solen mast trade the house grew rich carrying masts south. It lost six ships in the noon raid on Ithira in 611. In 650 Caladh Greywave married Nesta, sister of Queen Maelwen, and in 910 their daughter Lithiel took the veil. Lithiel gave her father's house the right to carry the queen's grain, and the Greywaves have been closer to the throne than any other house since. Tavor was born at Nimthil in 940 and became head of the house in 1031. In 1041 he fathered a son on Hild Seabright, a human sail-mender, and never owned him; the boy, Loren, took his mother's name, trained at the Dusk School and became the best blade in Eldergrove. Tavor has been Fleet-Warden since 1060. In 1098 three Greywave cogs were lost on the southern run near the waters where Old Ironjaw hunts. To cover the cargoes Tavor borrowed about 30,000 suns from Cosimo Lunetti's bank in Ostra, secured on nine cogs. In 1104 Loren quietly asked his father for a ship-share in return for keeping silent about his birth. The house opposes Corin Saltleaf's Open Sea, which would let humans hold ship-shares, and it guards the lodestone needle as Greywave pilot craft against the star-reader Istavel's wish to teach it to every captain. In 1105 Tavor wants the queen's sanction for Greywave cogs to carry Ostran grain straight to Nimthil from Sea Opening, cutting Saltleaf out of the grain trade. The house is the Veil's most loyal servant and its most expensive one, and a Lunetti note now sits under its keel. If the bank calls the note, nine cogs, a sixth of the realm's merchant fleet, pass to Ostran hands.
dead: Tarael Greywave (about 60 BR–395 AR): Built the Forty Ships.
Oren Greywave (about 130–470): First captain whose grave tree became a keel.
Caladh Greywave (about 560–950): Married Princess Nesta; father of Queen Lithiel.
marriages: 650, with The Mistwalkers: Caladh Greywave married Nesta, sister of Queen Maelwen.
1041, with Hild Seabright (human sail-mender, no house): Not a marriage: Tavor fathered Loren Seabright and never acknowledged him.
FAM-408.secrets: Tavor owes House Lunetti 30,000 suns on nine cogs, and Loren Seabright is his son. Several Greywave keels since 1088 were cut from nameless trees, not captains' graves.

FAM-409.y1105: Wardens of the yew groves on the southern ridges, rich from selling about 8,000 Keeper-marked staves a year to Ashmere under the Yew Compact.
FAM-409.arms: a dark yew on a silver ridge, on green
FAM-409.founder: Aelor of the Ridges (about 90 BR–420 AR), first warden of the Yew Ridges
FAM-409.power: The yew groves of the Yew Ridges, up to 2,800 m; the Yew Compact's 8,000 staves a year, worth about 16,000 suns in silver, grain and wine; Ashmere's debt of about 9,000 suns; the yew carts that go each summer to Ashmere's high forest country.
FAM-409.branches: The Aelorn ridge line (Maelis); Elorin's line, which married into the Mistwalkers in 1005
FAM-409.history: In 362 Queen Serewen gave the Yew Ridges to Aelor, a Keeper-trained forester, to guard the old yew groves on the southern heights. For four centuries the house grew yew for elven bows and nothing else. In 776 Queen Maelwen let it sell the first 1,000 staves to Aldred Ashford, first King of Ashmere, whose longbowmen needed wood his hills could not supply. Every Ashmere war since has raised the house's fortune. Maelis was born at Aelorn in 900 and became head of the house in 1010. In 1012, as Ashmere went to war with Varenna over the Palella trade, he negotiated the Yew Compact with Queen Elsbeth's envoys: about 8,000 staves a year, paid in silver, grain and wine, and no Ashmere ship may cut timber on the Elder Coast. In 1005 his cousin Elorin married Queen Saelith, and the heir Ilvara is half Aelorn. Ashmere pays a year late and owes about 9,000 suns at New Year 1105. In autumn 1104 Chancellor Edmund Hale told Maelis that 1,000 staves a year will pass from Ashmere to Aldmark as a wedding gift, and Maelis agreed to say nothing. The Sea Keeper Nerys means to refuse the Keeper's mark to the Yew Ridges this spring. If she does, the house loses its wealth and Eldergrove loses its only friend.
dead: Aelor of the Ridges (about 90 BR–420 AR): First warden of the Yew Ridges.
Elorin of Aelorn (842–1088): Consort of Queen Saelith, father of Ilvara.
marriages: 1005, with The Mistwalkers: Elorin of Aelorn married Queen Saelith.
FAM-409.secrets: Maelis knows 1,000 staves a year will go from Ashmere to Aldmark after the wedding of 21 June 1105, and has kept it from the council.

FAM-410.y1105: Half-elf merchant house of the North Fjords shipping herring and seal oil to Northreach and Greyhaven. Its head Corin is Harbor-Master of Nimthil and Half-Elf Speaker on the council.
FAM-410.arms: a silver herring on a green leaf, on sea blue
FAM-410.founder: Marra Saltleaf (958–1079), half-elf herring trader of Ithira
FAM-410.power: About 9 cogs; the northern run of herring and seal oil to Coldhaven and Greyhaven; the salt contracts that keep the Herring and Seal Hall of Ithira in debt; the harbor fee of one part in twenty at Nimthil, which Corin collects for the queen; the half-elf seat on the Council of the Grey Veil.
FAM-410.history: Marra Saltleaf was born at Ithira in 958 to a half-elf mother and a Grover fisher, a citizen under Serewen's law of 344 like every child of the Veil. She began as a salt buyer for the herring sheds and saw that the fjord towns paid human merchants twice over, once for salt and again for carriage. In 1002 she bought her first cog with ten years of salt profits and shipped herring straight to Northreach. By 1040 the house had six cogs, and Marra had a son, Corin, by an elven sealer of Ithira. She died in 1079 after a fall on the Ithira quay, and Corin took the house. He became Harbor-Master of Nimthil in 1085 and Half-Elf Speaker on the council in 1090, the first time a half-elf merchant had held both. When the herring shoals failed in 1101, the Herring and Seal Hall of Ithira went into debt to Saltleaf for salt, and its head Wenna Netmaker now wants to sell to Coldhaven without Saltleaf ships. Corin leads the Open Sea, which wants more ships, open harbors and ship-shares for human partners. In November 1104 he took 2,000 suns from Aldmark's Treasurer Wendel Marsh as an advance on 400 fir masts for the Cold Bay fleet, before the council had agreed to any sale. His new cogs are being built by Brannoc the Shipwright on smuggled West Strand fir. The house is proof that half-elves can rise in Eldergrove, and the Return to the Root's favourite target.
dead: Marra Saltleaf (958–1079): Founded the house with one cog in 1002.
FAM-410.secrets: Corin has taken 2,000 suns of Aldmark silver for masts the council has not approved, and two Saltleaf cogs have keels of unmarked fir.

FAM-021.y1105: Royal house of Northreach. King Eirik III rules with the Ring and keeps the Free Halls; his only son Bjorn is heir but lacks the frost blood, which is kept secret.
FAM-021.arms: a white wolf's head over three blue waves, on night blue
FAM-021.founder: Eirik Winterborn the Ice-Walker (784–851), first King of Northreach
FAM-021.power: The crown of Northreach: the tin toll, a third of the crown's income; royal estates around Wolfhaven; the Ship Levy of about 48 longships and 15 cogs with 3,000 seamen; 10,000 standing troops, the 600 axemen of the King's Hird and the 1,600 Ice Walkers; the Ring of jarls and the king's oath to the Free Halls.
FAM-021.branches: the royal line at Wolfhaven; the Stagflow Winterborns, descended from a younger son of Bjorn II, who supply royal brides
FAM-021.history: The Winterborns descend from Thane Ulfar of the Amber Capes, a sealer-chief of the Cold Coast. His son Eirik was born in January 784 in a sealers' camp on the sea ice; a blizzard blew the tents away, and mother and newborn lived through the night in a snow-hole. The camp called him the winter-born child, and the name became the house. In October 796 the Hafgrim thanes of Wolfhaven burned Ulfar's hall, and the family fled to Kingsmere. Eirik grew up at Osbert Fairrush's court and swore him a boy's oath. In January 812 he led about 340 men across the frozen bay and took Wolfhaven, and the thanes raised him king that May. At his first Thing in 815 he gave the jarls the Ring and the villages their own priests. He refused to renew his oath to Kingsmere in 838 and was burned in a ship on Wolfhaven harbor in 851. Ten Winterborns have reigned, father to son, without a break: Eirik I, Bjorn I the Shipwright, Eirik II the Tall, Torvald the Amber King, Bjorn II the Young, Ingvar the Silent, Arne the Tin-King, Sigvald the Lawful, Bjorn III the Frost-Handed and Eirik III. The house's frost blood needs two copies to show, so the Winterborns have married cousins for most of three centuries, chiefly from their Stagflow branch, descended from a younger son of Bjorn II. The price is paid in the nursery: about one Winterborn baby in ten dies of fits before two, and royal nurses feed every child every three hours, day and night. Bjorn II was a boy-king under the regent Hrafn Stagg after the Black Cough killed his father in 917, and he kept the Glenwash exiles and their truce record in 947. Arne sealed the Tin Compact and refused the Iron Reform. Bjorn III, crowned in 1057, showed the frost blood so plainly that the jarls called him the Frost-Handed. He went to Kingsmere in January 1090 to argue against the Edict of the Halls and was poisoned there by Lady Ysolde Ravenscar's cook. His son Eirik III, born 1060, had married his cousin Sigrid Winterborn of the Stagflow branch in 1085. Eirik won the Northreach Rising by fog and ice and ended it at Coldhaven, but only after a secret letter of silence. Their only son Bjorn, born 1088, carries one copy of the frost blood from his father and does not show it; in January 1103 he lost the tip of a finger to frostbite on a hunt meant to prove his blood. Only Queen Sigrid and the royal leech know. The Winterborns are sea-kings and winter fighters. They are crowned on Lantern Night, swear on the Oathfather's ring at the Sea King's stones and are burned in ships on Wolfhaven harbor.
dead: Eirik Winterborn the Ice-Walker (784–851): Crossed the frozen bay and founded Northreach. *Ruler:* Eirik Winterborn (Eirik I the Ice-Walker), Kingdom of Northreach, 812–851 (RUL-0060).
Bjorn I the Shipwright (813–872): Ship Levy of 856. *Ruler:* Bjorn Winterborn (Bjorn I the Shipwright), Kingdom of Northreach, 851–872 (RUL-0061).
Arne the Tin-King (955–1019): Tin Compact of 1002; refused the Iron Reform. *Ruler:* Arne Winterborn (Arne I the Tin-King), Kingdom of Northreach, 981–1019 (RUL-0066).
Bjorn III the Frost-Handed (1031–1090): Poisoned at Kingsmere; his death began the Rising. *Ruler:* Bjorn Winterborn (Bjorn III the Frost-Handed), Kingdom of Northreach, 1057–1090 (RUL-0068).
marriages: 1085, with House Winterborn: Eirik III married his cousin Sigrid Winterborn of the Stagflow branch.
1056, with House Winterborn: Bjorn III married his cousin Solveig Winterborn of the Stagflow branch; mother of Eirik III.
FAM-021.allies: House Stagg, The Stonefoot kin, The Skarfell line
FAM-021.secrets: Prince Bjorn does not have the frost blood. Eirik III signed a private letter in 1093 promising ten years of silence over his father's murder.

FAM-022.y1105: Forest jarls of the Stagflow, ruling from Saltbridge. Jarl Halvard leads Bjorn's Avengers and hunts King Bjorn's poisoner in Ostra.
FAM-022.arms: a brown stag leaping over a white river, on forest green
FAM-022.founder: Thane Ulf Stagg (about 780–850), first Jarl of the Stagflow
FAM-022.power: Saltbridge, at 22,500 the largest town of Northreach, and the forest farms of the Stagflow; the iron workings of the valley; a levy of about 3,000 and two longships; the Ski Yard of Saltbridge in their town; the border stones of 952 on their land.
FAM-022.history: The Staggs were forest thanes of the Stagflow who swore to Eirik in 812 and were named jarls in the first Ring of 815. They hold Saltbridge, the river town on the road from Aldmark, and so they have always been the first to meet any army from the south. Jarl Hrafn Stagg was regent for the boy-king Bjorn II from 917 to 922. He closed Wolfhaven to ships for 40 days when the Black Cough came and saved the eastern districts, and he gave the crown back on time, which the Winterborns have never forgotten. In 947 the Staggs took in the 200 Greymane exiles from the Glenwash, and in 952 the border stones of the Peace of the Stones were set on Stagg land. Halvard Stagg, born 1052, became jarl in 1079. On 26 May 1091 his house held the ambush line at the Stagflow fords in fog, and his sons Rane and Geir died leading the first rush on the Aldmark column. At the winter feast of 1093, after the Accord of Coldhaven gave Northreach back its faith but no justice for its king, he founded Bjorn's Avengers. Since 1102 his men have asked questions in Ostra, and in November 1104 his man Toke found a Kingsmere-born cook in the dyers' quarter. Halvard has told no one, not even the king. The Staggs are loyal to the Winterborns and do not forgive their enemies; Halvard calls Jarl Asta Coldwater the plains men's fishwife.
dead: Jarl Hrafn Stagg (880–944): Regent for Bjorn II during the Black Cough.
Rane and Geir Stagg (died 1091): Halvard's sons, killed in the first rush at the Stagflow.
FAM-022.secrets: Halvard's man has found a Kingsmere-born cook in Ostra who may be King Bjorn's poisoner, and Halvard is hiding it from the king.

FAM-023.y1105: Jarls of the Amber Capes and the richest house in Northreach after the crown. Jarl Asta leads the Amber Traders and wants peace and trade with Kingsmere.
FAM-023.arms: a golden lump of amber in a silver net, on sea blue
FAM-023.founder: Sven Coldwater (about 860–930), fisher-chief of Coldhaven made jarl by King Torvald
FAM-023.power: Coldhaven, a walled port of 21,200, and the Amber Capes; most of Northreach's amber and the whale-tusk trade sold south as unicorn horn; a partnership with the Coldhaven Amber and Fish Guild; a levy of about 2,000 and five longships; wealth nearly equal to the crown's.
FAM-023.history: The Coldwaters were fishers of Coldhaven when the autumn storm of 824 left its beaches thick with amber. They gathered it, sorted it and sold it south through Kingsmere, and by 900 they owned the best beaches of the capes. King Torvald the Amber King made Sven Coldwater jarl of the Amber Capes about 905. The house grew with every storm. In 1059 Northreach traders sold a Hrimfell whale tusk to the Emperor of Zanara as a unicorn horn, and the Coldwaters built that sale into a trade, buying tusks from the giants of the White Coast and keeping the source quiet. Asta Coldwater, born 1058, the only child of Jarl Sven the Younger, became jarl when he drowned in 1086. During the Rising she fed Eirik's army with stockfish and lost the herring season of 1091. She hosted the talks that ended the war, and the Accord of Coldhaven was signed in her hall on 8 March 1093. At those talks her son was promised to Ingrid Greymane, captain of Aldmark's Cold Bay marines. In autumn 1103 Asta met an envoy of Lady Ysolde Ravenscar at Coldhaven and promised to keep Coldhaven's ships out of any new war in return for free entry to Kingsmere's amber market. If King Eirik learns of it she will be called an oath-breaker and set adrift.
dead: Sven Coldwater (about 860–930): First Jarl of the Amber Capes.
Jarl Sven Coldwater the Younger (1030–1086): Asta's father; drowned off the capes.
marriages: 1093, with House Greymane: Asta's son secretly promised to Ingrid Greymane of Aldmark.
FAM-023.allies: The Tinmark Reeves, House Greymane, House Ravenscar
FAM-023.secrets: Asta has secretly promised Aldmark's spymistress to keep Coldhaven's ships out of any war, and her son is promised to an Aldmark captain.

FAM-024.y1105: The family that has run Northreach's tin trade for generations. Reeve Oddny Tinmark holds the office of Tin-Reeve of Wolfhaven and collects a third of the crown's income.
FAM-024.arms: a black tin bar stamped with a white mark, on grey
FAM-024.founder: Hallgrim Tinmark (about 830–890), tin factor of Wolfhaven
FAM-024.power: The office of Tin-Reeve: the crown's tenth on all tin carried to Kingsmere, about a third of the crown's income; the summer fleet of eight cogs to Skarfell; the great balance at the Skarfell fair; warehouses at Wolfhaven; the giants' trade-talk, which few other humans speak.
FAM-024.history: Hallgrim Tinmark was a Wolfhaven trader who sailed to Skarfell when Bjorn I reopened the old tin road about 860. He stamped every bar he bought with the family mark, and buyers at Kingsmere learned to trust it. For a century and a half the Tinmarks were one tin house among several. Then in 1002 King Arne sealed the Tin Compact of Skarfell, and the crown made the head of the Tinmarks its Tin-Reeve. The office has stayed in the family for six of eight reeveships since. The great balance the reeves carry to Skarfell each summer has a counterweight about one part in twenty too heavy, so the giants are paid for less tin than they hand over; the trick dates from the first reeves of the Compact and has been handed down with the office. Oddny Tinmark, born 1066, is the daughter of a Tin-Reeve who took her to the Skarfell fair every summer from the age of eight. She learned the giants' slow trade-talk from the tribute-folk and could chant tin prices by 1082. She was chosen head of the Tin Reeves in 1097. Since the Rising she has shipped tin to the Highland League each autumn to pay down the Silver of the Halls. In 1104 she learned that Master Tova Brand of Kingsmere had offered the giants rye for tin sold direct, and she plans to seize any Kingsmere cog found near the Frostholm coast.
dead: Hallgrim Tinmark (about 830–890): Reopened the tin trade and gave the family its mark.
FAM-024.secrets: The Tin Reeves' balance has cheated the giants of Frostholm by about one part in twenty since the Compact of 1002, and the giants' own headman's tallies could prove it.

FAM-611.y1105: Chieftains of Frostholm since 903. Skarvi the Younger faces Haugberg's challenge at the Thing of 1106 and has secretly broken the Tin Compact.
FAM-611.arms: a small black giant's hand, open, on slate grey
FAM-611.founder: Skarvi the Small (870 to 960), first chieftain of Frostholm
FAM-611.power: The chieftainship: the right to set the tin price with the Northreach Tin Reeves each summer and to speak for all the halls at the Skarfell Tin Fair. Skarfell Hall-land with 540 giants and about 3,000 tribute-folk; the Pair-Yard of Skarfell; the 40 Skarfell Runners. About 60 giants count themselves Skarfell, and 34 of them are small.
FAM-611.branches: Skarvi the Younger's household at Skarfell Hall (his wife Asa, his small son Arni the Quick, his daughter Hild); the Skarfell Runners: 20 small giants who scout, hunt and carry messages; the Lindholm watch household; the hidden Haugberg branch: the children of Signy of Skarfell, full-size but carrying the trait; her granddaughter Una (b. 1101) shows it
FAM-611.history: The Skarfell line is the family of Skarvi the Small, born at Skarfell Hall in 870, the first small giant the chant records. His father Hogni was a giant of ordinary size whose mother came from Ragvik. Skarvi grew no taller than a small giant, could run and turn, and spent his youth at the tin fair, where he could sit in the traders' houses and learn their speech. At the Thing of 903 the halls made him chieftain and sold all their tin through him. He married Aud of Torvik, and three of their five children were small. His daughter Halla the Quick (r. 966 to 999), his son Ottar's son Kol the Trader (r. 1001 to 1049), who made the Tin Compact of 1002, and Kol's daughter Sigrun Tin-Tongue (r. 1050 to 1077) ruled after him. Kol's son Hallbjorn, a small giant who led the Skarfell Runners, drowned in 1046 when a Northreach boat overturned under him at the fair, and so the chieftainship passed to his sister and then to his son. That son, Skarvi the Younger, was chosen in 1078. In 1071 he married his first cousin Asa, Sigrun's daughter, after Lore-Chanter Sva left their shared grandmother Thorunn out of the Skarfell chant. They have a son, Arni the Quick, born 1073, a small giant who ran the Skarfell Runners until 1100 and is one of only two who know about the tin loaded at Ragvik in 1104, and a daughter, Hild, born 1082. The line has always married close. A small Skarfell woman who carries a full-size giant's child often dies giving birth, so Skarfell women marry small Skarfell men, and the big halls say the Skarfells breed like humans and marry like dogs. One Skarfell woman did marry out: Signy of Skarfell married Bergthor of Haugberg in 1058 to end the old quarrel between the two halls, and died in 1080 bearing his second son. Her surviving son Orri is full-size, but his daughter Una, born 1101, is growing small. The line's power has always been its usefulness. Every Skarfell chieftain has raised the tin price or held it, and the halls have eaten better for it. Its weakness is that the other halls see small giants as a lesser people, and that it has only ever ruled by the Thing's consent, renewed every seven years.
dead: Skarvi the Small (870 to 960): First chieftain of Frostholm and first small giant. *Ruler:* Skarvi the Small, Frostholm, 903–960 (RUL-6021).
Halla the Quick (906 to 999): Second chieftain; held the tin price as Aldmark's demand grew. *Ruler:* Halla the Quick, Frostholm, 966–999 (RUL-6022).
Ottar the Runner (912 to 985): Skarvi's small son; first leader of the Skarfell Runners.
Kol the Trader (950 to 1049): Made the Tin Compact of Skarfell (1002). *Ruler:* Kol the Trader, Frostholm, 1001–1049 (RUL-6023).
Sigrun Tin-Tongue (985 to 1077): Fourth chieftain; spoke at the fair for 30 years before her election. *Ruler:* Sigrun Tin-Tongue, Frostholm, 1050–1077 (RUL-6024).
Hallbjorn of Skarfell (1000 to 1046): Skarvi the Younger's father; drowned at the fair.
marriages: 895, with The Hall of Torvik: Skarvi the Small married Aud of Torvik.
1058, with The Hall of Haugberg: Signy of Skarfell married Bergthor of Haugberg.
1071, with The Skarfell line: Skarvi the Younger married his first cousin Asa, Sigrun's daughter.
FAM-611.allies: The Hall of Torvik, The Hall of Helstad, House Winterborn
FAM-611.secrets: Sva left a mother out of the chant in 1071 so that Skarvi could marry Asa; if it comes out, Arni and Hild are unlawful. Skarvi broke the Tin Compact at Ragvik in August 1104.

FAM-612.y1105: The oldest hall of Frostholm and keeper of the richest tin streams; Eldest Hroa holds the swing vote at the Thing of 1106.
FAM-612.arms: a white walrus tusk on grey
FAM-612.founder: Torvi, first Mother of Torvik in the chant
FAM-612.power: The northern capes, the walrus beaches and the richest tin streams on the island (the Sigrud tin works); 820 giants and about 3,500 tribute-folk; the Stone Ring of Torvik. About a third of the island's tin, though one of its best streams gave only a third of its old yield in 1104.
FAM-612.branches: Hroa's household at Torvik Hall; the whale-watch on the northern capes; the lesser household of the Stone Ring
FAM-612.history: Torvik claims to be the oldest hall on Frostholm, and the chant agrees. It holds the northern capes, where the walrus haul out each summer and whales pass close inshore, and the northern tin streams where Hael's traders first found the black stone. Torvik and Skarfell let the first tin-diggers land about 650 BR, and Torvik's tribute villages, such as Bolgard, are the oldest on the island. The hall has always married its daughters to Skarfell; Skarvi the Small's wife Aud came from Torvik, and Torvik has backed the Skarfell chieftains at almost every Thing since 903. In 1019 a Torvik woman crossed the sea to marry into Valdhall in Hrimfell, so Torvik has kin on the White Coast. Its eldest since 1041 is Hroa, born in 985, the oldest giant alive and the most feared fighter among the giants, famous for the falling overhead maul blow the halls call the Mountain Breaker. She watched the Tin Compact sworn in 1002, threw the Thing's unmatched 34 m stone in 1064, and in 1070 split a walrus's skull and the sea ice under it with one blow. Her great-granddaughter Solvei counts the whales on the capes and found the dead Frost Leviathan of October 1104. Her pupil Vermund Farcast, born into a lesser household of the hall in 1055, is champion stone-thrower of the halls and has secretly promised his arm to Haugberg. The hall's tribute-folk pay most for its tin: eleven miners, two of them Colm Ashby's brothers, died in a Torvik pit collapse in 1071. In 1104 Torvik's richest stream gave a third of its old yield, and Hroa has hidden the loss by buying tin from Helstad with walrus ivory.
dead: Aud of Torvik (872 to 961): Wife of Skarvi the Small and mother of the Skarfell line.
Thorve of Torvik (988 to 1062): Crossed the sea to marry into Valdhall in 1019, the last giant to do so.
marriages: 895, with The Skarfell line: Aud of Torvik married Skarvi the Small.
1019, with The Hall of Valdhall: Thorve of Torvik married into Valdhall in Hrimfell.
FAM-612.allies: The Skarfell line, The Hall of Helstad
FAM-612.secrets: Torvik's best tin stream is failing and Hroa buys Helstad tin to hide it. Solvei keeps a Drevnan harpoon head from a dead Frost Leviathan, and Vermund has sold his throw to Haugberg.

FAM-613.y1105: Hall of the biggest giants and keepers of the mammoths; Eldest Bergthor leads the Big Halls against the Skarfell chieftainship.
FAM-613.founder: Hauga, first Mother of Haugberg in the chant
FAM-613.power: The island's 900 Thunder Mammoths, which haul all timber for the halls; the Brunberg tin works; 760 giants of the largest size and about 3,000 tribute-folk; leadership of the Big Halls faction.
FAM-613.branches: Bergthor's household at Haugberg; the mammoth-herding households of the north-west; Orri's household (Signy of Skarfell's son), where Una is hidden
FAM-613.history: Haugberg is the hall of the biggest giants on Frostholm; its men and women stand over 400 cm. It holds the island's north-west and the herds of Thunder Mammoths, which its households have kept since the mammoths shrank on the island after the Long Walk. Every great timber in every hall was hauled by Haugberg's teams, and Haugberg has always thought itself the island's backbone. It has never liked the Skarfell chieftains. At the Thing of 903 Haugberg alone voted against Skarvi the Small, and it has challenged the Skarfell line at four Things since. In 1058 Eldest Grimkel of Haugberg married his son Bergthor to Signy of Skarfell to end the quarrel. She bore Groa in 1066 and a son, Orri, in 1072, and died in 1080 giving birth to a third child who was too large for her. Bergthor became eldest in 1079 and has blamed the Skarfells for her death ever since. Northreach traders saw his mammoths in 1080 and were mocked at home. In 1085 he led the mammoth teams that hauled the timber for Skarfell Hall's new roof, and he has reminded the halls of it at every Thing. He lost to Skarvi by two halls in 1092 and by three in 1099, and he has sworn to challenge in 1106. He has promised Vermund Farcast a new hall and a Haugberg bride, and he has sent word to Kingsmere that Haugberg would sell tin direct on giant terms. He does not know that Groa has told the Northreach Tin Reeve everything said at his fire since 1102. He hides his granddaughter Una, Orri's child, born in 1101, because she is growing Skarfell-small: the trait came to Haugberg hidden in Signy's son and showed again in Signy's granddaughter.
dead: Grimkel of Haugberg (990 to 1079): Eldest who married his son to a Skarfell to end the quarrel.
Signy of Skarfell (1034 to 1080): Bergthor's wife; died in childbirth.
marriages: 1058, with The Skarfell line: Bergthor married Signy of Skarfell.
FAM-613.rivals: The Skarfell line, The Hall of Helstad
FAM-613.secrets: Bergthor's granddaughter Una carries the Skarfell trait. His daughter Groa spies for Northreach's Tin Reeve, and he has bought Vermund's throw at the Thing.

FAM-614.y1105: The hall of the Mothers' Chant and of the best fighting pairs; its vote and Sva's voice have carried the Skarfells since 1078.
FAM-614.founder: Hela, first Mother of Helstad in the chant
FAM-614.power: The western shore and fishing coves where about 5,000 tribute-folk live; 560 giants; the keeping of the Mothers' Chant, which judges every marriage at the Thing; the master of the Pair-Yard of Skarfell.
FAM-614.branches: Eldest Ketil's household at Helstad; the chant-keepers' household; the Haldvang watch households
FAM-614.history: Helstad holds the western shore of Frostholm, and more tribute-folk live under it than under any other hall. It is the hall of the chant. For as long as the chant goes back, the Keeper of the Mothers' Chant has most often been a Helstad giant; the Keeper recites every mother of every hall and judges who may marry whom at the Thing. Ingvild of Helstad kept the chant until 1057 and taught Sva the Long-Voiced, born at Helstad in 1019, who has kept it since the Thing of 1057. In 797 two pairs of Helstad giants broke the Cold Coast thanes' shield wall at Ragvik, and the hall has sent the best pair-fighters to Skarfell ever since. Thrand the Broad, born at Helstad in 1050, became master of the Pair-Yard of Skarfell in 1090. Helstad has always lived close to its humans. Hauk of Helstad, born 1075, was nursed through a fever by a tribute-woman, let a smuggler's boat carry four runaway families past the shore watch in 1102 and now sits at the Miners' Moot at night. Its eldest, Ketil, is old and cautious; he backs Skarvi but would cast Hauk out if he knew. Helstad's vote and Sva's voice have carried the Skarfells at every Thing since 1078. Sva's lie of 1071 makes Helstad's chant the most dangerous thing on the island, and her letter to Hrimfell's chant-keeper about marriages across the sea may become the most hopeful.
dead: Ingvild of Helstad (960 to 1061): Keeper of the Mothers' Chant before Sva.
Gerd of Helstad (1052 to 1099): Thrand's wife and pair-partner; died of fever.
marriages: 1080, with The Hall of Helstad: Thrand the Broad married Gerd of Helstad, his pair-partner.
FAM-614.allies: The Skarfell line, The Hall of Torvik
FAM-614.secrets: Sva left a mother out of the Skarfell chant in 1071. Thrand fights alone with a failing knee, and Hauk let runaways pass the shore watch in 1102.

FAM-411.y1105: Royal clan of Irondeep since 610. Queen Brynja, 184, rules; her son Korrin is heir and means to set her aside. About 70 living kin, 30 of them carriers.
FAM-411.arms: a red coal-glow eye inside a black anvil, on iron grey
FAM-411.words: The dark hides nothing from us.
FAM-411.founder: Asa the Coal-Eyed (480–670), mother of King Korrin and the first carrier
FAM-411.power: The crown of about 100,000 people and the chair of the Council of Masters; the Deepeye vault under the Deep Halls, holding the royal share of every forge tithe (about 40,000 hold-marks in metal) and the arms tallies of 896–911; the Iron Road Contract and its three forts; Korrin's wardenship of Dunheim and the lower gate.
FAM-411.branches: The crowned line of the Deep Halls (Brynja, Korrin, Brynja's younger daughter Sigvor, born 1015); The Deepeye factors, cousins who have kept the royal counting vault and the Kingsmere and Eagleburg trade since 780
FAM-411.history: Clan Deepeye was a small clan of deep miners in one of the fourteen Iron Mountain halls until Asa the Coal-Eyed was born in 480. She could read an ore seam by the glow of one coal at the end of a gallery where others needed a lamp, and she could not bear the sun. Her son Korrin, born 560, had her eyes and her patience. He spent eleven years sinking 60 test pits, found the great seam in 609 and in 610 united the halls into the Kingdom of Irondeep. The clan has ruled since: five rulers in 495 years, each the eldest living child of the last, each confirmed by the Council of Masters and the Law-Carvers. Korrin ruled 110 years and died in 720. His daughter Gunnhild opened Dunheim and its coal in 760 and began the night trade with Kingsmere. Her son Bodvar sold about 14,000 sets of lamellar to the Wind Empire from 896 to 911, swore to the Judgment of the First Hall in 904 and broke it for seven years; the tallies of every sale lie in the clan's vault. His son Arnulf sealed the Iron Road Contract with Harald Ironside by torchlight in 951 and refused Aldmark's iron rings after the Iron Reform of 1002. The Deepeye eyes have shaped every one of these deals. Carriers cannot stand in daylight, so the clan's iron trains move at night, its treaties are sealed after dusk, and Aldmark's envoys have learned to wait for sunset at Eagleburg. Arnulf's daughter Brynja was born in 920 and crowned in 1032. In 975 she married Orri Coalbrow, born into a cadet line of the mine-master clan of Dunheim, who died in 1058; their son Korrin was born in 982 and their daughter Sigvor in 1015. Brynja has renewed the Iron Road Contract three times and sold iron at half price in the hungry winter of 1088. Korrin, named for the founder, led the Tunnel Crews for twenty years and has been Warden of Dunheim since 1060. Since 1091 he has called at every Council for Aldmark's debt to be paid in full. In December 1104 Brynja secretly promised Emperor Aldwin 200 soldiers in the lower Iron Road fort for 6,000 bushels of grain. Korrin has carved a petition asking the Law-Carvers to declare her unfit. If she learns of it before the Founding, she may pass him over for Sigvor, and the clan that has never had a disputed succession will have one.
dead: Asa the Coal-Eyed (480–670): First carrier of the deep eyes; mother of Korrin.
King Korrin Deepeye (560–720): Founder of Irondeep. *Ruler:* Korrin Deepeye (King Korrin the Founder), Kingdom of Irondeep, 610–720 (RUL-4031).
King Bodvar the Open-Handed (725–938): Armed the Wind Empire in secret. *Ruler:* Bodvar Deepeye (King Bodvar the Open-Handed), Kingdom of Irondeep, 830–938 (RUL-4033).
King Arnulf the Contract-Keeper (812–1032): Sealed the Iron Road Contract. *Ruler:* Arnulf Deepeye (King Arnulf the Contract-Keeper), Kingdom of Irondeep, 938–1032 (RUL-4034).
marriages: 975, with Clan Coalbrow: Brynja married Orri Coalbrow of Dunheim; their son Korrin was born in 982.
FAM-411.secrets: The arms tallies of 896–911 in the Deepeye vault; Brynja's letter of December 1104 promising Aldmark the lower fort; Korrin's petition to declare his mother unfit.

FAM-412.y1105: Mine-masters of Dunheim who dig Irondeep's coal and run its pumps; head Dain is First Mine-Master and his daughter Vigdis commands the Tunnel Crews.
FAM-412.arms: a black coal-seam across a red furnace mouth, on grey
FAM-412.founder: Grim Coalbrow (about 650–845), who cut the lower hold of Dunheim
FAM-412.power: The Dunheim coal seams, the coke ovens and the great waterwheel pump of 1071; the office of First Mine-Master since 1058; command of the Tunnel Crews and the Sapper Hall of Dunheim; blood kin to the heir.
FAM-412.branches: The Dunheim line (Dain, Vigdis); Orri's line, which married into Clan Deepeye in 975 and gave the realm its heir
FAM-412.history: In 760 Queen Gunnhild gave Grim Coalbrow the right to cut a lower hold in the Dunheim valley, where coal lay near the surface. The clan has dug Irondeep's fire ever since. Its mine-masters learned to bake coal to coke in clay ovens and to pump the deep workings dry with waterwheels on the Dunheim streams. In 975 Orri Coalbrow, of a cadet line of the clan, married Queen Brynja, and the heir Korrin is half Coalbrow. Dain was born at Dunheim in 960 and cut his first coal at 30. He became head of the clan in 1030 and First Mine-Master in 1058. In 1071 he built the great waterwheel pump of Dunheim, which let the hold dig 200 m deeper. His daughter Vigdis, born 1001, joined the Tunnel Crews in 1031, flooded a thieves' tunnel from the carters' camp in 1066 and became Sapper-Master in 1079. The clan's luck turned in the autumn of 1104. In October Vigdis flooded an Aldmark prospecting shaft east of the Ore Shelf and three human miners drowned; she told her father it was a natural flood, but carved law says she owes blood-price or exile. In November the lower coal seam at Dunheim flooded, and Dain told the Council it was a small leak, though his pump-master Thyra Wheelwright has shown him it will take two years to clear. Coal output will fall by a third in 1105.
dead: Grim Coalbrow (about 650–845): Cut the lower hold of Dunheim.
Orri Coalbrow (870–1058): Consort of Queen Brynja, father of the heir.
marriages: 975, with Clan Deepeye: Orri Coalbrow married Brynja Deepeye.
FAM-412.secrets: Vigdis drowned three Aldmark prospectors in October 1104; Dain is hiding the size of the Dunheim flood.

FAM-413.y1105: Master-smiths who keep Irondeep's forge secrets and its three small secret blast furnaces; head Hella is First of the Master-Smiths.
FAM-413.arms: a silver anvil struck by a red hammer, on black
FAM-413.words: The fire keeps its own counsel.
FAM-413.founder: Sigmund Brightanvil (about 540–730), master-smith of Korrin's first forge
FAM-413.power: The main forges of the Deep Halls; the three small secret blast furnaces (988, 1030, 1068), whose fire only a handful of smiths know; leadership of the Council of Master-Smiths; about a quarter of the hold's finished mail and plate pieces.
FAM-413.branches: The Deep Halls forge line (Hella); The Coldforge branch, from Hella's daughter's marriage in 1040 (Eyvind Coldforge)
FAM-413.history: Sigmund Brightanvil lit the first forge of Korrin's great hall in 612, and his clan has led the smiths of Irondeep since. In 988 the clan built the hold's first small secret blast furnace, the only way to make iron in the amounts the Iron Road Contract demanded, and taught its fire to four smiths only. A second followed in 1030. Hella was born in 948, took her name-carving in 978 and became a master-smith in 1010 and First of the Master-Smiths in 1055. In 1068 she built the third furnace herself and again taught its fire to only four. In 1040 her daughter married into the smith family of Coldforge, and her grandson Eyvind was born in 1050 and apprenticed at the Brightanvil forges from 1070. In 1096 a drunken clerk of the Law-Carvers told Eyvind of the exiled smith Hodd Ashbeard, and he came to believe the holds' secrecy was a crime. In the summer of 1103 he went down the Iron Road disguised as a carter and showed a smith at Saltbridge in Northreach how to build a water-driven trip-hammer, for a pouch of amber. Hella knows and has not reported him. By the Deep Law she should have brought him before the Law-Carvers, and a leak of dwarven machinery is the crime for which names are ground out of the vaults. The clan wants no new mail sold to Aldmark until the debt is paid.
dead: Sigmund Brightanvil (about 540–730): Lit Korrin's first forge.
marriages: 1040, with Coldforge smith family: Hella's daughter married a Coldforge smith; their son Eyvind was born in 1050.
FAM-413.secrets: Eyvind's trip-hammer leak of 1103, hidden by his grandmother.

FAM-414.y1105: Gate clan of the Deep Halls; head Harrek is Gate-Warden, master of the Shield Gallery and one of the hold's best fighters.
FAM-414.arms: a cave bear's skull above a closed gate, on grey
FAM-414.founder: Hauk Stonejaw (about 520–705), who speared the cave bear of 612
FAM-414.power: Command of the 600 Deep Gate Wardens; the Shield Gallery of Irondeep, which trains every shield and spear wall of the hold; the Deep Gate itself, a double gate of iron-faced oak with murder holes.
FAM-414.branches: The Deep Gate line (Harrek, his granddaughter Ylva); Tofi, Harrek's stonebairn son (born 1075), who lives in the carters' camp outside the gates and is barred from the hold
FAM-414.history: In February 612 miners cutting a new gallery broke into a cave bear's winter den. The bear killed five of them before Hauk Stonejaw drove a boar-spear into its chest. Korrin set its skull above the Deep Gate and gave Hauk's clan the gate. The Stonejaws have held it for 490 years; no human army has passed it. They also train the hold's walls: the Shield Gallery of Irondeep has been theirs since 640. Harrek was born in 970 in the Deep Halls and served his thirty years in the Hold Guard. In 1041 he held the Deep Gate against 200 Pinewild outlaws who tried to rush the carters' gate. He became master of the Shield Gallery in 1060 and Gate-Warden in 1072. Since 1091 he has argued at every Council that the Iron Road forts must stay in dwarven hands. In 1075 a human carter woman of the camp outside the gates bore him a stonebairn son, Tofi, whom he has taught shield work in secret; teaching an outsider breaks the Judgment of the First Hall, and a stonebairn is barred from the holds. His granddaughter Ylva joined the Deep Gate Wardens in 1102 and has befriended Tofi without knowing whose son he is.
dead: Hauk Stonejaw (about 520–705): Speared the cave bear of 612.
FAM-414.secrets: Harrek's stonebairn son Tofi, taught shield work against the Judgment of 904.

FAM-415.y1105: The Carver family of Irondeep for 2,200 years; head Orsa is Law-Carver of Irondeep, judge of the hold and keeper of its exile rolls.
FAM-415.arms: a chisel crossing a carved stone tablet, on dark grey
FAM-415.founder: Thrand Flintmark (about 1250–1040 BR), first Carver of the Iron Mountain halls
FAM-415.power: The office of Law-Carver of Irondeep, without whom no ruler may change carved law; the exile rolls and genealogies; the right to confirm a new ruler; a secret slate of the arms tallies of 896–911.
FAM-415.history: The Flintmarks have carved law in the Iron Mountains since about 1100 BR, when Thrand Flintmark came from the First Hall of Stonehold to judge the scattered halls. His descendants carved the exile of Hodd Ashbeard about 1000 BR and sent his name to the First Hall. When Korrin founded Irondeep in 610, the Flintmarks copied the First Hall's law onto its walls. Orsa was born in 905, the year after the Judgment of the First Hall, and was raised on the story of the Open Forge dispute. She studied the carved law for a century and became Law-Carver of Irondeep in 1012. In 1032 she confirmed Brynja as queen. In 1060 she ground out of the ancestor vaults the name of a smith who sold furnace plans to Kingsmere. She knows that Irondeep sold 14,000 sets of lamellar to the Wind Empire, and she has carved the totals on a slate hidden in the Law-Carvers' hall; she holds it as a threat over the Deepeyes. She wants the gates closed in winter, Aldmark's garrison refused and sales cut by half, and she has agreed to hear Korrin's petition to declare his mother unfit at the Founding on 3 March 1105.
dead: Thrand Flintmark (about 1250–1040 BR): First Carver of the Iron Mountain halls.
FAM-415.secrets: Orsa's slate of the arms tallies and her promise to hear Korrin's petition.

FAM-501.y1105: Ruling line of the Horde. Vrag is war-chief, but his heart is failing, his sons are children, and his only grown kinsmen of the blood are a wrestler and a half-orc rebel whom Vrag does not know is his brother.
FAM-501.arms: a white lightning bolt over a running mare on a black hide, under a horsetail standard
FAM-501.power: The war-chief's hearth herd at Urgol, about 9,000 horses and 20,000 sheep; one horse in twenty from every clan each year, about 50,000 horses, most given back as gifts and feast herds; a share of all plunder; Gorath's Hearth Guard of 1,200 picked riders; the Urgol hay stores and the Graknak grain store (Ushkar's hay law of 1085); the name of the Son of the Storm, which the Drum Council still confirms. About 140 living people descend from Gorath, and about 60 of them carry the blood fury.
FAM-501.branches: The Urgol hearth: Durgash's line through Vrag and his three young children, Gorr (born 1095), Maz (1097) and Shaka (1100); Nurga's branch: the line of Gorath's youngest daughter, headed by Durk Ironarms; The Hazelhollow branch: Tarn Halfblood, Durgash's half-orc son by Maren of Hazelhollow (secret); The Vrakoth branch: children of Gorath's daughters by Drazka, married into the Vrakoth lake clans; The Skardush branch: grandchildren of Brakk, Gorath's eldest son, in the Skardush clans
FAM-501.history: The Line of Gorath is young. Its root is the small Urgol clan, whose winter camp at Urgol lay among holm-oak hills far from the Gordush. Gorath was born there in 998, son of Mother Hagra, the clan-mother, and Durr One-Ear, a Vrakoth-born rider who had married into her clan. Neither parent showed any fury.
