In August 1012 Durr was killed in the feud of the Krugak wells, and Gorath, 14, rode into the fight bare-armed, killed three riders and then fell shaking and white. The Urgol hide shows 'the boy with the storm in him'. Gorath married three times, each time to bind a clan. In 1016 he married Shaka of the Skardush clans; their sons were Brakk (1017–1051) and Gashnak (1021–1049). After he beat three allied clans at Vrakoth in 1028 he married Drazka, daughter of the beaten Vrakoth chief Hurzag, in 1029; their son was Durgash (1034–1074), and Uthar (1036–1067) and four daughters followed. In 1046 he married Yelsha of the Goroth clans, whose youngest child was Nurga (1052–1090). Of Gorath's 23 children, 11 grew up. All four sons who carried the fury died before 45: Gashnak at the Gordush Bend in 1049, Brakk at Hartgate in 1051, Uthar of a stroke in the White Death winter of 1067, and Durgash of heart failure at 40. Gorath was named war-chief at the Drum Stones in 1024, with a driven herd of wild horses playing the Storm-Father's Thunder Horse. He founded the Horde at Urgol in 1041 and died at the Great Ride of 1058, aged 60, the oldest of his line. The Grey Mothers chose Durgash the same day. Durgash married Ulza of the Salt Edge clans in 1052; their sons Hrakka the Red (1053–1070) and Uzgar (1056–1073) died in the Second Horde War, Hrakka in a blood-fury charge at the Gashmar Fords and Uzgar under an engine stone at Crossmarch. Their daughters Oska and Relka married into the Goroth and Salt Edge clans. Ulza died in the White Death, and in 1069 Durgash married Kazra of the Goroth clans, who bore Vrag in 1072. In the raids of 1072 Durgash also took Maren of Hazelhollow into his camp. She bore his son at Graknak in March 1073 and took him home in 1074 with Durgash's copper arm-ring. That son is Tarn Halfblood, a member of the line by birth, though only Maren, Mother Ugra and Tarn himself know it. When Durgash died in August 1074 the line lost the staff. Kazra died that winter, and Mother Yazra raised Vrag at the Grey Mothers' fire while Ushkar the Grey ruled. Nurga married Harg, a rider of the Hearth Guard, and bore Durk in 1071; Durk carries the fury and has won the Great Ride wrestling four times. In 1093 Vrag married Dushka of the Vrakoth clans. In 1098 the Grey Mothers gave the staff back to the line to stop the clans splitting. Vrag has fainted twice after the fury, and the line now faces the same question it faced in 1074: who holds the staff when the heart of Gorath's blood gives out.
dead: Gorath the Great (998–1058): Uniter of the clans and founder of the Horde; first carrier of the blood fury. *Ruler:* Gorath the Great, Horde of Gorath, 1024–1058 (RUL-5001).
Durgash Blood-Fist (1034–1074): War-chief 1058–1074; took the upper Gordush; father of Vrag and, in secret, of Tarn. *Ruler:* Durgash Blood-Fist, Horde of Gorath, 1058–1074 (RUL-5002).
Brakk (1017–1051): Gorath's eldest son; died leading the first wave at Hartgate.
Gashnak (1021–1049): Gorath's second son; died at the Gordush Bend.
Hrakka the Red (1053–1070): Durgash's eldest son; died in a blood-fury charge at the Gashmar Fords.
Mother Hagra (971–1026): Clan-mother of the Urgol clan and Gorath's mother; kept his herds while he fought.
marriages: 1016, with The Skardush clans: Gorath marries Shaka; mother of Brakk and Gashnak.
1029, with The Vrakoth lake clans: Gorath marries Drazka, daughter of the chief he beat at Vrakoth; mother of Durgash.
1046, with The Goroth clans: Gorath marries Yelsha; mother of Nurga.
1052, with The Salt Edge clans: Durgash marries Ulza; mother of Hrakka and Uzgar.
1069, with The Goroth clans: Durgash marries Kazra; mother of Vrag.
FAM-501.allies: The Grey Mothers, The Longwind line, The Stonehoof line
FAM-501.rivals: The Redhand line, Clan Ironhide, House Harrow, House Ironside
FAM-501.secrets: Vrag's heart is failing. Tarn Halfblood is Durgash's son. The Thunder Horse of 1024 was a driven herd.

FAM-502.y1105: Law-keepers of the Horde. Their council of 43 grey-braided women names war-chiefs, may overrule them on law and keeps the old hides of every sworn clan at Urgol, and with them most of the dangerous secrets of the Grass Sea.
FAM-502.arms: a grey braid coiled around a painted hide, on undyed felt
FAM-502.founder: Mother Hesh of the eastern clans (about 590–683)
FAM-502.power: The Grey Braid Law of 925: the right to speak the law at every Great Ride and to overrule any war-chief on law. With the Drum Council they name the war-chief. They keep about 1,400 winter-count hides of the sworn clans in eight hide-tents at Urgol. They judge blood-price (50 to 100 horses for a killing) and keep one horse in ten of it. Their clan-mothers hold about 30,000 horses. About 140 women and 110 men of the blood are alive; 43 of the women sit on the Grey Council.
FAM-502.branches: Yazra's line at Urgol: Mother Ugra and the children of her sister Varka; Hela's line: Mother Shura, Keeper of the Grass, and her niece Mother Ossa; The Goroth mothers: descendants of Urtha Grey-Braid's younger daughter, who stayed with the Long Flight clans; The Vrakoth mothers: lines of Shagra's younger daughters on the lake
FAM-502.history: The line began with Mother Hesh, born about 590 among the eastern clans around Goroth. Her own mother died at 41. Hesh outlived four husbands and all her sisters, rode to the Great Ride at 80, and died at Goroth in 683 at about 93. Her daughters did not go grey at 30, and neither did theirs. In 661 Hesh settled a feud over the Goroth springs by reciting which kin had watered there 50 winters before, and after that the eastern clans brought her their quarrels. By about 700 they called her daughters' line the Grey Mothers and gave them the hides. The line is always small, because its women bear only two or three children, and late. It is passed only through women. Its best-remembered mothers are Urtha Grey-Braid (821–901), who led 60,000 people on the Long Flight West from 876 rather than fight the Wind riders, and her granddaughter Old Mother Shagra (879–970), born on that road. Shagra's mother Sulka (852–936) kept the law between them. Shagra spoke the law at the return to the Drum Stones in 923 and in 925 won the Grey Braid Law, which made the Mothers a council with power over war-chiefs. Shagra's daughter Tuska (912–998) carried the law through the feuding years. Tuska's daughter Arga (951–1044) was 90 when Gorath founded the Horde at Urgol in 1041. She moved the Mothers' fire there and took into her tents the old hides of every sworn clan, the Redhand hide with Gorza's knife among them. Arga's daughter Yazra (1003–1090) was Elder from 1044 to 1090. Yazra chose Durgash in 1058 and Ushkar the Grey in 1074, raised the orphan Vrag at her own fire, and before she died told her daughter Ugra what the hide for 1073 meant. Mother Ugra, born at Urgol in 1042, has been Elder since 1090. Her son Horg died of lung fever in 1088; her sister Varka died in 1099. In 1086 she argued the Krugak wells case against the Redhands and won them 900 horses in blood-price, and their hatred. In 1098 she chose Vrag. Her cousin Shura, daughter of Yazra's sister Hela, keeps the grass. Shura's niece Ossa, daughter of Hela's elder daughter Tessa, sets bones and brews Vrag's foxglove. Only women born of the line may take the grey braid. Other kin send girls to learn the law as braid-girls, but they never sit on the council. In 1070 one braid-girl, Hulga, set to repaint the Urgol clan's hides, saw the small picture of the horse drive of 1024 and fled east; her daughter is Ashka Drumtongue of the Tusk Clans. In 1105 the Grey Mothers hold the hides that could shame the Redhands, strip the Line of Gorath of its holy name, prove Tarn's blood and show 40 years of Solen grain. They mean to name an heir to Vrag at the Great Ride of 1105.
dead: Mother Hesh (about 590–683): First of the line; lived to about 93.
Urtha Grey-Braid (821–901): Led the Long Flight West from 876.
Old Mother Shagra (879–970): Born on the Long Flight; won the Grey Braid Law of 925; lived to 91.
Mother Arga (951–1044): Elder when the Horde was founded; brought the clans' old hides to Urgol.
Mother Yazra (1003–1090): Elder 1044–1090; chose Durgash and Ushkar; raised Vrag.
marriages: 935, with The Wolf clans of the Urgash Hills: Shagra's daughter Tuska marries into the Wolf clans to bind the western clans to the Grey Braid Law.
1040, with The Urgol clan: Yazra marries a Hearth Guard captain of Gorath's clan; Ugra is born at Urgol in 1042.
1031, with The Goroth clans: Hela marries a Goroth herd-master; mother of Tessa and Shura.
FAM-502.allies: The Line of Gorath, The Longwind line, The Stonehoof line
FAM-502.secrets: They hold the proofs of SEC-16 (Gorza's knife), SEC-50 (the Thunder Horse), SEC-65 (Vrag's heart), SEC-66 (Tarn's father) and the western hides of SEC-07. The hide for 961 shows that the Longwind founder was the son of a Northfolk captive.

FAM-503.y1105: Messengers and scouts of the Horde. Brak Longwind sits on the war-chief's council, runs 300 runners and carries Vrag's most private words, including the offer to Aldmark of November 1104.
FAM-503.arms: three white running feet on a dun hide
FAM-503.founder: Orrak the Walker (961–1011); the name Longwind from Tukar (1018–1070) in 1046
FAM-503.power: About 700 descendants of Orrak, of whom about 340 carry the long wind; about 330 of them serve among the 600 Longwind Runners, with post runners of other kin, who carry word 100 km a day on foot; the Runners' Camp at Gashmar; a relay of 20 runner posts being built from Gashmar to the Drum Stones; the council seat of Master of Messengers. Their herds are small, about 2,500 horses; their wealth is the war-chief's trust.
FAM-503.branches: Brak's line at the Runners' Camp of Gashmar, with his sons Tukar the Younger (born 1080) and Orm (1084); Hessa's line: Tollo Quietfoot and his sisters; The Graknak runners: Longwinds settled on the upper Gordush since 1074
FAM-503.history: In August 954 about 800 Gashmar riders crossed the Glenwash, burned new Northfolk farms and took 140 captives. One was a farm girl named Hilde. She served seven winters as a herd-thrall and in 961 was adopted into the Gashmar kin of a rider called Varg Crow-Eye, whom she married. Her son Orrak was born that year. He was half human, and the Grey Mothers' hide for 961 shows 'the winter the pale thrall bore a son'. Orrak could walk a horse to death and still be standing. At 12 he ran down a wounded deer over 30 km; at 15 he carried word from Gashmar to the camps on the Gnarzag, about 170 km, in a day and a night. The Gashmar war-captains used him as a runner, and the clans called him the Walker and, behind his back, the pale one's son. He married Mother Gazra of Gashmar and died in 1011. Four of his nine children had his wind. His son Durn Farstep (984–1030) ran for Mogdur Stonehoof, war-chief of the Gashmar clans, and was with him at the border meeting of 1033 where Gunnar Harrow threw him. Durn's son Tukar (1018–1070) made the family's name. In July 1046, when Gunnar Harrow rode across the Glenwash to burn the summer camps, Tukar ran about 300 km in three days to warn them. After that he was Tukar Longwind, and Gorath made the Gashmar runners a band of their own. Tukar scouted Aldmark's march for Gorath and carried the terms between the camps at the Peace of the Glenwash in 1052. At the Gashmar Fords on 17 June 1070 he ran 80 km through Aldmark patrols to bring up the reserve and died of his wounds on arrival. Tukar married Yenna of the Rushrak kin of Gashmar in 1042. Their daughter Hessa (1044–1101) bore Tollo, now called Quietfoot, in 1074. Their son Brak, born in 1058, was 12 when his father died. Brak ran for Durgash and for Ushkar, became head of the line when Yenna died in 1085, and was made Master of Messengers when Vrag was chosen in 1098. He believes Garnak Stonehoof carried his dying father at the fords, and honors him for it. The line marries within the Gashmar clans and keeps its runners together at Gashmar. It has always been mocked as half-human, and in truth its founder was. The Longwinds say Orrak's mother was a Gashmar woman. Brak knows the truth. In the autumn of 1104 he gave the Tusk half-orc Uzka Twoblood 400 suns of Horde silver with Vrag's knowledge, and in November he carried Vrag's private offer over the Gordush to Emperor Aldwin.
dead: Orrak the Walker (961–1011): Founder and first carrier; son of the Northfolk captive Hilde.
Durn Farstep (984–1030): Runner for Mogdur Stonehoof of Gashmar.
Tukar Longwind (1018–1070): Ran 300 km in three days in 1046; died after bringing the reserve at the Gashmar Fords.
Hessa Longwind (1044–1101): Tukar's daughter; ran for Ushkar; mother of Tollo.
marriages: 961, with The Gashmar clans: The captive Hilde, adopted, marries Varg Crow-Eye; mother of Orrak.
1042, with The Rushrak kin of Gashmar: Tukar marries Yenna; mother of Hessa and Brak.
1079, with The Goroth clans: Brak marries a Goroth herd-master's daughter; mother of his two sons.
FAM-503.allies: The Line of Gorath, The Stonehoof line, The Grey Mothers
FAM-503.secrets: The founder Orrak was half human, son of the Northfolk captive Hilde (Grey Mothers' hide for 961). Brak paid Uzka Twoblood 400 suns and carried Vrag's secret offer to Emperor Aldwin in November 1104. Tollo's counts of Aldmark's army come from an elven watcher of the Evenwood.

FAM-504.y1105: Chiefs of the Magak clans and leaders of the Old Clans. Skarn Redhand is First War-Captain of the Horde and means to take the war-chief's staff at the Great Ride of 1105.
FAM-504.arms: a red open hand on a black horse-hide
FAM-504.power: About 115,000 people of the Magak clans; the richest horse herds of the Horde, about 180,000 horses, grown from Gorza's 2,000 mares of 479; a war-band of 3,400 riders and about 9,000 at full levy; the first place in the relay line since 1036; about 600 horses sold to Aldmark's Millrun breeders since 1102 through Gorm the Trader.
FAM-504.branches: The Magak staff line: chiefs passing from uncle to sister's son since 440; The Ughgar camps: Redhand kin on the Ughgar river pastures granted in 1036; Urzag's sons' lines, long merged into the Vrakoth, Urga and Luguk clans
FAM-504.history: The line takes its name from Urzag Redhand, born in 421 in the clan whose winter camp was Drukak. At 13 he killed a bear with a knife and came home with red arms. His clan passed its leadership from a chief to his sister's son, an old custom of the foothill clans, and the Redhands keep it still. In 440, at 19, having married into the three largest clans, he was chosen war-chief of about 60 clans at the Drum Stones and founded the Old Horde (HPOL-07). He led it for 36 years, into the Grass Sea War of 470 and to his death at the Drum Stones on 21 June 476. His heir by custom was his sister Gashna's son Gorza, and Gorza had killed him. Gorza took 400 pounds of Solen silver and stabbed his uncle in the back in the fighting. Gashna, keeper of the clan hide, painted a small knife in its corner for that summer. Gorza was raised war-chief two days later, submitted at Vrakoth in February 478, led the Redhand kin to Magak in 479 and bought 2,000 mares with the silver. He died in 502. For six centuries the staff passed from uncle to nephew at Magak: Uldrak, who held the Magak grass against the Northward clans; Morzag (831–882), who knelt to Yargan the Hawk in 875 after Goroth and paid one horse in ten, and whose riders helped drive the March clans east in 887; Gorzak (987–1047), who swore to Gorath at Magak in 1036 for the Ughgar grass and the first place in the relay line; Durzag (1015–1062), who rode away from Durgash in 1058 and came back after the raid on Kyzai; and Ulzag (1041–1094), chief for 32 years, whose clans lost the feud of the Krugak wells and paid 900 horses in 1086. In 1041 the Redhand hides, with Gashna's knife, went into the Grey Mothers' tents with every other sworn clan's. Skarn, son of Ulzag's sister Rukka (1047–1101), was born at Magak in 1066, rode his first raid at 13 and led the Magak war-band from 1084. He took the staff in November 1094. He was passed over in 1098 and has led the Old Clans since, who want the staff back outside Gorath's line, as under Ushkar. He married Mother Olka of the Salt Edge clans in 1085. By Redhand custom his heir is his sister Zegga's son Ruzag, born in 1088. The Redhands sing Gorza as the heir who saved Urzag's kin. They have heard the Grey Mothers' claim about the knife and call it a lie of Gorath's women. If Mother Ugra shows the hide at the Great Ride and the Holy See's accounts are ever read, the proudest clans of the Horde lose their ancestor and Skarn loses his bid.
dead: Urzag Redhand (421–476): War-chief of the Old Horde 440–476. *Ruler:* Urzag Redhand, The Old Horde, 440–476 (RUL-5021).
Gorza (446–502): Urzag's sister's son and killer; last war-chief of the Old Horde; led the kin to Magak. *Ruler:* Gorza, The Old Horde, 476–478 (RUL-5022).
Morzag Redhand (831–882): Knelt to the Wind Khan's general in 875.
Gorzak Redhand (987–1047): Swore the Magak clans to Gorath in 1036.
Ulzag Redhand (1041–1094): Chief 1062–1094; paid the blood-price of the Krugak wells.
marriages: 439, with The Vrakoth lake clans, the Urga clans and the Luguk clans: Urzag's three marriages that made the Old Horde.
1062, with The Magak Ughgar camps: Ulzag's sister Rukka marries an Ughgar herd-master; mother of Skarn and Zegga.
1085, with The Salt Edge clans: Skarn marries Mother Olka.
FAM-504.allies: The Salt Edge clans, Horse-Traders of the Skardush road, Horse-Breeders of the Millrun
FAM-504.rivals: The Line of Gorath, The Grey Mothers, The Longwind line
FAM-504.secrets: SEC-16: Gorza knifed Urzag for 400 pounds of Solen silver, and the Magak herds grew from it. Since 1102 Skarn has sold about 600 Magak horses to Aldmark, and his captain paid Durk Ironarms to lose the Great Ride wrestling of 1102.

FAM-505.y1105: War-captains of the Gashmar clans and the family of Ushkar the Grey, the only war-chief not of Gorath's blood. Garnak Stonehoof faces Aldmark's 8,000 across the lower Gordush and wants to raid before May Fair.
FAM-505.arms: a grey hoof on green felt
FAM-505.power: Leadership of the Gashmar clans, about 125,000 people, and 3,600 riders on the lower Gordush and about 8,000 at full levy; the Gashmar fords; about 40,000 horses at Rushrak; the gratitude of the eastern clans that Ushkar fed in the killing winter of 1085.
FAM-505.branches: Ushkar's line: Garnak and his sons, the eldest of whom, Mogdur the Younger (born 1072), rides in the Gashmar war-band; Mogdur's line: the old war-captains of Gashmar, now herd-masters at Rushrak
FAM-505.history: Hagar Stonehoof broke a grey stallion with hooves so hard it never went lame, and led the Gashmar kin back to the Gordush after the Wind garrisons fell in 923. The Rushrak camp, a day's ride east of the Gashmar fords, has been the family's winter ground since 924. Hagar's grandsons led the Gashmar raids across the Glenwash, among them the raid of 954 that brought the captive Hilde to Gashmar. Mogdur Stonehoof (977–1036) was war-chief of the Gashmar clans for 30 years. In May 1033, aged 56, he rode to a border meeting near Crossmarch to talk, and Lord Gunnar Harrow pulled him from his horse and threw him. He never rode well again and died of a broken hip in 1036. The Gashmar clans swore to Gorath soon after. Mogdur's sister Burga (1001–1066) was clan-mother of the Stonehoof kin, and her son Ushkar, born in 1033, was Mogdur's heir. Ushkar rode for Gorath in the First Horde War and led the Gashmar wave at the Gordush Bend in 1049. In 1050 he married Harza of the Rushrak kin, and their son Garnak was born in 1052, the year of the Peace of the Glenwash. Durgash made Ushkar war-captain of the Gashmar clans in 1062. His hair went grey in the White Death winter of 1067, when he lost half his herds, and he was called the Grey from then on. At the Gashmar Fords in June 1070 Garnak, 18, ran when Conrad's heavy horse broke the line. His mother put it about that he had carried the dying Tukar Longwind from the field; Brak Longwind still honors him for it. Garnak won his name back on the ladders at Graknak in May 1072. When Durgash died in August 1074 the Grey Mothers chose Ushkar, 41, to hold the Horde until Vrag grew up. He ruled for 24 years without a war against Aldmark, settled the upper Gordush, fed the eastern clans in 1085, and with the Grey Mothers ended the Krugak feud in 1086. The Gashmar captaincy passed to his sister's son Varn, who drowned at the fords in 1092, and then to Garnak. Ushkar died at Urgol in the spring of 1098, aged 65. Harza had died in 1093. Garnak has faced Aldmark across the lower Gordush since the autumn of 1104. He wants to burn the stake stores at Crossmarch before May Fair, against Vrag's order, and he wants an adopted Aldmark soldier of his clan, who once garrisoned those fords, to guide his riders across.
dead: Hagar Stonehoof (about 885–941): Led the Gashmar kin back to the Gordush after 923.
Mogdur Stonehoof (977–1036): War-chief of the Gashmar clans; thrown by Gunnar Harrow in 1033.
Ushkar the Grey (1033–1098): War-Chief of the Horde 1074–1098. *Ruler:* Ushkar the Grey, Horde of Gorath, 1074–1098 (RUL-5003).
Mother Harza (1034–1093): Ushkar's wife; hid her son's flight at the Gashmar Fords.
marriages: 1050, with The Rushrak kin of Gashmar: Ushkar marries Harza; mother of Garnak.
1071, with The Goroth clans: Garnak marries Mother Yelka; mother of Mogdur the Younger.
FAM-505.allies: The Longwind line, The Grey Mothers, The Line of Gorath
FAM-505.secrets: At the Gashmar Fords in 1070 Garnak ran; his mother's story that he carried Tukar Longwind from the field is false.

FAM-601.y1105: Khans of the Nine Winds, first among nine equal tribes and not kings; once the imperial house of the Wind Empire. Khan Ozbek is nearly blind, Khatun Sorga governs in his name, and the heir Serik hides the same sickness.
FAM-601.arms: a lean grey wolf under a blue sky, on white felt
FAM-601.founder: Kharsa the Thin (about 765 to 829), a herder of the Blue Wind
FAM-601.power: The khan's tent-chest at Kharsa: the oil money (30 jars a year to Tessaria, paid in Tessarian silver), a tenth of every horse sold at the channel fairs (about 2,000 horses a year) and one horse in thirty from every tribe. Command of the Silver Tablet Guard (2,000 riders), the Keepers of the Seeps (1,000) and the Yam Riders (2,400). The Blue Wind's herds and the 33,400 people of the tent-city of Kharsa. The yams: about 400 stations on 12,000 km of track.
FAM-601.branches: Ozbek's hearth at Kharsa; the sons-in-tent: about 40 households of Kharsan daughters and their husbands at Kharsa and Ersgol, raised Kharsan under the Tent Law of 926; Toghrul's daughters' households at Ersgol; Temur's line (ended with his son Arik in 918)
FAM-601.history: House Kharsan began as a small clan of the Blue Wind, about 900 tents with good wells at Torkul. It is named for Kharsa the Thin, a herder who in the killing winter of 788 walked his family's last 40 sheep through the snow for three months on a strip of dried meat a day and came out lean but strong while his brothers died. His descendants found they, too, lost less in the hungry winters, and the clan took his name. Kharsa's grandson Tolun led the clan until the Yarbek chief poisoned him at a feast in 857. Tolun's son Ulagan grew up an exile in the salt marshes and married Saran, a salt-fisher's daughter, in 866. The White Death of 869 made him khan, and the Wind Empire (HPOL-04) made his house the greatest on the steppe. Saran, who never drew a war bow, was its mind. She counted the tribes for the Saddle Law, designed the yams, and in 912 hid her husband's death for 40 days so that her younger son Berek could take Kharsa. Her elder son Temur married Oyun of the Red Wind in 902; their only son Arik died of the Black Cough in 918, and Temur was murdered in 920. Berek, who paid for the murder, is the ancestor of every Kharsan alive. He married Nomin of the Grey Wind in 905 and began the house's habit of taking wives from that tribe. Berek feared a rival khan of his own blood more than any enemy, so in 926 he made the Tent Law: a Kharsan daughter's husband comes to live at Kharsa, and their children are raised Kharsan. The law still holds. Six khans followed Berek, father to son for five generations: Tokhai the Silent, Burun the Horse-Rich, Turgen the Swift, Tulgar and Toghrul, and then Toghrul's nephew. The same blood that let Ulagan outlast famine killed them in plenty. Burun went blind at 55; Turgen lost a foot and died of it; Toghrul's only son Aruq died of sugar sickness at 38 in 1076. Tulgar died at the Salt Shore in 1041, betrayed by two tribes he trusted. Toghrul, forced out after the caravan raid of 1079, was the first khan to lose his seat to the kurultai. His nephew Ozbek, son of Toghrul's brother Kerey, who was killed by Horde raiders in 1063, rebuilt the house's power by force of arms and by secrecy. He married Sorga of the Grey Wind in 1068 for 300 horses; she married into the house and has kept its tent-chest since 1079. She bore Serik in 1070 and the daughters Tana (1073) and Suren (1077), whose husbands live at Kharsa under the Tent Law. Serik married Naran of the Morning Wind in 1102. In 1105 the house is rich, feared and failing in body. Ozbek is nearly blind, Serik has the first signs of the same sickness, and Serik's lover Kulan of the Blue Wind is four months with his child, which under the Tent Law would be raised a Kharsan at Kharsa whether its mother is married or not.
dead: Kharsa the Thin (about 765 to 829): Clan founder; outlasted the killing winter of 788 and gave the house its name and its blood.
Ulagan Kharsan the Hungry (842 to 912): Founder of the Wind Empire. *Ruler:* Ulagan Kharsan (the Hungry), Wind Empire, 870–912 (RUL-6001).
Khatun Saran the Counter (848 to 916): Designed the Saddle Law census and the yams; hid Ulagan's death for 40 days.
Temur Kharsan (872 to 920): Rival khan of the west; murdered at Torkul. *Ruler:* Temur Kharsan, Wind Empire, 913–920 (RUL-6003).

Berek Kharsan the Patient (876 to 949): Won the War of Ulagan's Sons by his brother's murder; swore the Compact of 925. *Ruler:* Berek Kharsan (the Patient), Khanate of the Nine Winds, 925–949 (RUL-6011).
Burun the Horse-Rich (932 to 994): Richest khan in horses; died blind of sugar sickness. *Ruler:* Burun Kharsan (the Horse-Rich), Khanate of the Nine Winds, 968–994 (RUL-6013).
marriages: 866, with the salt-fishers of the south shore: Ulagan married Saran, daughter of the fisher who hid him.
902, with The Red Wind chiefs: Temur married Oyun, daughter of the Red Wind chief Arkan.
905, with The Grey Wind chiefs: Berek married Nomin of the Grey Wind.
1068, with The Grey Wind chiefs: Ozbek married Sorga, daughter of the Grey Wind chief Ergene, for 300 horses.
1102, with The Morning Wind chiefs: Serik married Naran, daughter of Altan of the Morning Wind, to hold that tribe's vote.
FAM-601.allies: The Grey Wind chiefs, The Keepers of the Kharsa Yam, The Morning Wind chiefs
FAM-601.rivals: The Red Wind chiefs, The Line of Gorath
FAM-601.secrets: The khan's tent-chest holds the cords of the Forty Silent Days and the Kyzai cords of 915, and the grave near Torkul holds Berek's tablet. Since 1103 the house sells fire-oil to Queen Livia; Ozbek's blindness, Serik's sickness and Kulan's child are all hidden.

FAM-602.y1105: Chiefs of the Grey Wind at Kyztai and the khan's in-laws; the heart of the Hearth Tribes. Chief Bars is Khatun Sorga's brother.
FAM-602.arms: a grey arrow across a white well-mouth
FAM-602.founder: Toghan Swift-Arrow (391 to 447), chief of the Grey Wind and khan of six tribes in the Wind War
FAM-602.power: About 170,000 people and the winter camp of Kyztai (13,000); the Ring Hunt of Kyztai, which drills thousands of riders; most of the 1,000 Keepers of the Seeps and many of the Silver Tablet Guard; one vote in the kurultai and the khatun's ear.
FAM-602.branches: the chief's household at Kyztai; Galla's line, the chief's kin who keep the tribe's tallies
FAM-602.history: The chiefs of the Grey Wind are the oldest chiefly line on the Salt Steppe and the only one with an ancestor in Solen records. Their songs begin with Toghan Swift-Arrow, who led six tribes in the Wind War (WAR-09). He burned the Solen barges at Kyzai with fire-oil in 425, destroyed a Solen army at the Dry Wells near Kyztai in 428 and made the Treaty of Torkul. His son Arslan married the Solen princess Galla in 432, and every Grey Wind chief since counts her among his mothers. Galla learned the Rider tongue and ran the salt trade for 30 years, and the Grey Wind's habit of keeping tallies begins with her. The tribe winters around Kyztai, and its land holds the Field of the Dry Wells. It backed Ulagan in 870 and Berek in 913, and in 905 its chief gave Berek his daughter Nomin. Since then the Grey Wind has given the Kharsan more wives than any other tribe, and the khans call it the Mother Wind. Its riders fill the Silver Tablet Guard and the Keepers of the Seeps, and it hosts the winter Ring Hunt of Kyztai, which drills thousands of riders to move as one. Ergene of the Grey Wind, chief from 1062 to 1089, gave his daughter Sorga to Ozbek in 1068 for 300 horses; she has kept the khan's tent-chest since 1079. Ergene's son Bars, Sorga's brother, has been chief since 1089 and votes with his sister in the kurultai. The Grey Wind stands or falls with Serik's raising in 1105.
dead: Toghan Swift-Arrow (391 to 447): Beat Solen at the Dry Wells and burned the Kyzai barges.
Galla of Torkul (about 412 to 470): Solen princess married to Toghan's son; ran the salt trade for 30 years.
Nomin of the Grey Wind (about 885 to 950): Wife of Berek Kharsan and mother of Khan Tokhai.
Ergene of the Grey Wind (1020 to 1089): Chief who gave Sorga to Ozbek.
marriages: 432, with the Solen imperial house: Arslan married Princess Galla to seal the Treaty of Torkul.
905, with House Kharsan: Nomin married Berek Kharsan.
1068, with House Kharsan: Sorga married Ozbek Kharsan.
FAM-602.allies: House Kharsan, The Keepers of the Kharsa Yam
FAM-602.secrets: The Grey Wind's own tally-keepers know that Khatun Sorga has governed in Ozbek's name since the summer of 1104, and they have told no one.

FAM-603.y1105: Chiefs of the Red Wind at Torkul and leaders of the four western tribes. Yesun means to prove the Kharsan khanship stolen at the Horse Feast of 1105.
FAM-603.arms: a red horse on salt white
FAM-603.founder: Bayar of the Red Wind (about 690 to 760), who moved his herds into the empty Solen salt forts at Torkul
FAM-603.power: About 175,000 people; the south-shore salt pans and the old Solen salt forts of Torkul; a toll on salt, caviar and fish passing Torkul; Jarak of the Red Wind and the tribe's riders; the lead of the four western votes in the kurultai.
FAM-603.branches: the chief's household at Torkul; the salt-fort households of the south shore
FAM-603.history: The Red Wind chiefs have held the south shore of the Salt Sea since about 720, when Bayar of the Red Wind moved his herds into the empty Solen salt forts at Torkul, which the Treaty of Torkul had given the empire in 431. The salt pans made the family rich, and the Red Wind has taken a toll on salt and fish at Torkul ever since. The family's grievance begins with the Kharsan. The Kharsan clan's old wells lay near Torkul, and Ulagan destroyed the Yarbek there in 871. In 902 chief Arkan of the Red Wind gave his daughter Oyun to Temur Kharsan, Ulagan's eldest son, and at the Broken Kurultai of 913 the Red Wind led the four western tribes for Temur. Temur kept his winter camp at Torkul among his wife's people. There his son Arik died of the Black Cough in 918, and there, on 9 January 920, his own guard captain killed him. Oyun made the song 'The Captain's Herd' in her widowhood, and it hints that Berek bought the killing. In the Compact of 925 Berek gave the Red Wind Torkul and the salt forts to buy its oath, and the family has kept both. It has never received any of the oil money. Kutlu of the Red Wind, chief from 1066 to 1093, did more than complain. In 1079 he paid Sartak of the Black Wind and six other raiders to take two fire-oil caravans to shame Khan Toghrul, and the chiefs forced Toghrul out. His son Yesun learned of it in 1095 and still pays Sartak to keep quiet. Yesun, chief since 1093, speaks for the four western tribes. His mother's sister married into the yam keepers of Kharsa, and her son Chagan told Yesun at a wedding in 1104 where the cords of 912 are kept. Yesun's champion Jarak, a salt-worker's son sworn to the family, found the guard captain's grave in November 1104.
dead: Bayar of the Red Wind (about 690 to 760): Took the Solen salt forts at Torkul.
Arkan of the Red Wind (about 855 to 931): Gave his daughter to Temur and led the western tribes for him in 913.
Oyun of the Red Wind (about 885 to 958): Temur's widow; made the song 'The Captain's Herd'.
Kutlu of the Red Wind (1030 to 1093): Paid the raiders of 1079 and so toppled Khan Toghrul.
marriages: 902, with House Kharsan: Oyun married Temur Kharsan.
1058, with The Keepers of the Kharsa Yam: A Red Wind daughter, sister of Yesun's mother, married Tabin the Keeper of the Kharsa yam; their son is Chagan.
FAM-603.rivals: House Kharsan, The Reed Wind chiefs, The Grey Wind chiefs
FAM-603.secrets: Yesun's father paid for the caravan raid of 1079 that toppled Toghrul, and Yesun pays Sartak to keep silent. Jarak alone knows where the guard captain's grave lies.

FAM-604.y1105: Chiefs of the Reed Wind at Kultau, rich from caviar, and secret grazing clients of the Horde since 1041.
FAM-604.arms: a silver sturgeon among blue reeds
FAM-604.founder: Nokai of the Reed Wind (about 770 to 840), who built the first sturgeon smokehouses at Kultau
FAM-604.power: About 160,000 people; Kultau, a city of 22,900 with the Salt Sea's sturgeon grounds and caviar cellars; a share of Old Bora's caviar trade; winter grazing north of Kultau by the Horde's leave; one western vote in the kurultai.
FAM-604.branches: the chief's household at Kultau; the herd-camps north of Kultau that winter on Horde grass
FAM-604.history: The chiefs of the Reed Wind hold Kultau, the second city of the steppe, and the reed beds and sturgeon grounds of the Salt Sea's north shore. The family grew rich on fish before it grew great in war. Kultau has twice seen khans made: Ulagan was raised there in 870, and the Broken Kurultai met there in 913, when the Reed Wind voted for Temur with the other western tribes. After 925 the family turned to trade. Its fishers landed Old Whiskers in 1001, and Kultau caviar reached Ostra within a generation. The family's secret dates from August 1041. Mergen of the Reed Wind, chief from 1029 to 1062, met Gorath's envoys at Kultau with the chief of the Morning Wind, knotted a treaty cord and held his riders back from the Battle of the Salt Shore. Gorath kept his word, and the Reed Wind's herds have wintered on the grass north of Kultau ever since. The cord is kept by the tribe's shaman and shown to no one. Mergen's son Bukha, chief from 1062, told his own son Tolui the truth on his deathbed in 1085, when Tolui became chief. Since 1090 the Horde clan-mother Shura has asked for horses each autumn, and Tolui pays about 150 as a grass price. He guards Old Bora's caviar boats and takes a share, and he shares the burden and the secret with the Morning Wind's chief. He is counted among the western tribes, but he is Yesun's enemy, because Yesun's hunt for old cords could find his.
dead: Mergen of the Reed Wind (1001 to 1062): Held the Reed Wind back from the Salt Shore for Horde grass.
Bukha of the Reed Wind (1027 to 1085): Told his son the truth of 1041 on his deathbed.
marriages: 1050, with The Morning Wind chiefs: Bukha married a daughter of the Morning Wind chief Tegin, binding the two tribes that share the secret of 1041.
FAM-604.secrets: The knotted cord of 1041 is in the keeping of the Reed Wind's shaman at Kultau; Tolui pays the Horde about 150 horses a year for grass.

FAM-605.y1105: Chiefs of the Morning Wind at Ozlun and the heir's in-laws; one of the two tribes that held back at the Salt Shore.
FAM-605.arms: a gold sun rising from grey water
FAM-605.founder: Bori of the Morning Wind (about 830 to 895), boat-chief of the channel shore
FAM-605.power: About 150,000 people; the northern channel shore, the Kularyk saltworks and the droving of horses to the khan's fair at Yarbek; winter grazing for 30,000 sheep and 4,000 horses north of Kultau; one Hearth Tribe vote.
FAM-605.branches: the chief's household at Ozlun; the drovers' households of Yarbek
FAM-605.history: The Morning Wind is the easternmost tribe, on the channel shore around Ozlun, and takes its name from the sunrise over the Grey Channel. Its chiefs have always traded with ships. In 882 Morning Wind boatwrights built the Khan's 300 channel boats at Yarbek, which Osric the Diver burned, and in 884 its herders helped load 70,000 horses onto Greyhaven cogs. After the Compact of 925 the Morning Wind's pastures took in the old Yarbek lands, though the khan kept the Yarbek horse fair as his own, and the family grew rich driving horses to it. It voted for Berek in 913 and has been counted among the Hearth Tribes ever since. That is why its secret would be so bitter. In August 1041 Tegin of the Morning Wind knotted the treaty cord with the Reed Wind's chief and Gorath's envoys at Kultau and held his riders back from the Salt Shore. Every November since, the Morning Wind's spare herds, about 30,000 sheep and 4,000 horses, are driven west to winter north of Kultau under Reed Wind herders, and the two chiefs split the grass price. Tegin's grandson Altan, chief since 1088, gave his daughter Naran to Serik Kharsan in 1102, so the heir's wife is the great-granddaughter of a man who helped get a khan killed. Altan's vote is one of the five Serik needs at the Horse Feast of 1105.
dead: Tegin of the Morning Wind (998 to 1070): Held the Morning Wind back from the Salt Shore in 1041.
marriages: 1050, with The Reed Wind chiefs: Tegin's daughter married Bukha of the Reed Wind.
1102, with House Kharsan: Naran married Serik Kharsan.
FAM-605.allies: The Reed Wind chiefs, House Kharsan
FAM-605.secrets: The Morning Wind is the second tribe of the knotted cord of 1041; if it comes out, the heir's own in-laws will be named traitors.

FAM-606.y1105: Chiefs of the Sea Wind at Erkent and leaders of the Well Riders; their two votes decide Serik's raising.
FAM-606.arms: a white horse's head over green waves
FAM-606.founder: Qorin of the Sea Wind (about 850 to 920), who ran the ferry landings at Erkent
FAM-606.power: About 165,000 people; the southern channel shore and the landings at Erkent; horse and felt trade with Sunland merchants; about 600 untaxed horses a year sent to Santora; the Well Riders' two votes.
FAM-606.branches: the chief's household at Erkent; the Bay kin of Morhaven through Idris's aunt
FAM-606.history: The Sea Wind holds the southern channel shore around Erkent, where the Narrows are about 50 km wide. In May 884 the Wind Empire's riders crossed from Erkent in Greyhaven ships, and the family grew rich running the landings for the next 30 years. After 925 it sold horses and felt to Sunland merchants on the shore. In 978 its chief Nasr of the Sea Wind took the Path of the Well from Qadiri horse buyers and gave a Well-Keeper a tent at Erkent. The Sea Wind was the first of the Nine Winds to leave the Eternal Blue, and the Dust Wind followed. The chiefs have kept close to the Sunlands since. In 1058 a daughter of the house married into the Bay family of Morhaven horse dealers, and her son Oskan Bay is Idris's cousin. Hamid of the Sea Wind sheltered a Qadiri Well-Keeper who taught his son Idris the Path, and when Hamid died of fever in 1090 Idris became chief. Idris leads the Well Riders in the kurultai. In 1096 he asked for a Well-Keeper at the Horse Feast and lost six to three. Since 1100 he has sent about 600 horses a year to Oskan Bay at Santora without paying the khan's tenth, and the silver has built a new Well shrine at Erkent. Yesun has promised the Well a seat for his vote; Serik has offered nothing yet.
dead: Nasr of the Sea Wind (940 to 1011): First chief of the Nine Winds to take the Path of the Well.
Hamid of the Sea Wind (1030 to 1090): Sheltered a Qadiri Well-Keeper; father of Idris.
marriages: 1058, with the Bay family of Morhaven: Hamid's sister married a Santora horse dealer; their son is Oskan Bay.
FAM-606.secrets: About 600 horses a year go south through Oskan Bay without the khan's tenth; the silver built the Well shrine at Erkent.

FAM-607.y1105: Hereditary keepers of the main yam station at Kharsa and heads of the Yam Keepers; they hold the memory of the Forty Silent Days.
FAM-607.arms: a silver tablet on a blue cord
FAM-607.founder: Bayan the Keeper (848 to 919), first keeper of the Kharsa yam station
FAM-607.power: The Kharsa yam station and the yam horse rolls for about 400 stations; the Head of the Yam Keepers' silver tablet; the training of keeper families; the monthly tallies brought to the khatun.
FAM-607.branches: the Kharsa station household; the keepers of the Kyztai station, trained from Kharsa
FAM-607.history: The keepers of the Kharsa yam are the first family of the post roads. When Khatun Saran set up the first post-stations in April 873, she gave the station at Kharsa to Bayan, a herder's son who had learned to knot tally cords from the two Morhaven scribes she had captured. Every rider who changed horses at Kharsa was knotted into Bayan's cords with the day and the road. His son Ordu kept the station in 912. On Saran's order he sent mourning riders to the hearth tribes on 27 January, 39 days before the khan's death was announced, and he knotted them into the cord as he knotted every rider. Those cords are in the khan's tent-chest, and the story of the Forty Silent Days has passed from father to son in the family ever since. In 915 the Black Cough rode the yam roads; the family lost eleven of its people and nearly all its horses, and its Kyzai cords show where the sickness began. The family has kept the Kharsa station for eight generations. It trains the keeper families of other stations, holds the yam horse rolls and gives the khan his Head of the Yam Keepers. Its men marry Blue Wind and Red Wind women. Tabin the Keeper, head until 1084, married a Red Wind woman in 1058 whose sister was the mother of Yesun of the Red Wind. Their son Chagan rode as a courier from 1073, kept the station at Kyztai from 1084 and became Head of the Yam Keepers in 1093. He has rebuilt 14 stations. In the autumn of 1104, drunk at a wedding at Torkul, he told his cousin Yesun that the cords of 912 are still in the chest.
dead: Bayan the Keeper (848 to 919): First keeper of the Kharsa yam.
Ordu the Keeper (875 to 941): Knotted the mourning riders of January 912 into the cords.
Tabin the Keeper (1025 to 1084): Chagan's father; married into the Red Wind.
marriages: 1058, with The Red Wind chiefs: Tabin married a Red Wind woman; her sister's son is Yesun.
FAM-607.allies: House Kharsan, The Grey Wind chiefs
FAM-607.secrets: The family knows the Forty Silent Days by heart, and Chagan has let the secret of where the cords lie slip to Yesun.

FAM-031.y1105: Leading family of Highcastle. Helga Stonefoot is First Speaker of the League; her daughter Ada runs the Ridge School and guards the high valleys where the Snow Drakes nest.
FAM-031.arms: a white foot on a grey stone under three white peaks, on sky blue
FAM-031.power: The First Speakership since 1099; the summer pastures of the Highcastle valley; the 200 Stonefoot Cliff Runners who guard the high valleys; the Ridge School of Redford, one of the 66 schools; the wall-run champions hired by other valleys; guardianship of the two closed valleys above Highcastle.
FAM-031.branches: the Highcastle kin; the herders of the two closed valleys above Highcastle
FAM-031.history: Orm Stonefoot was a cragsman of Highcastle who gathered eagle eggs and wild honey from cliffs no one else would climb. The herders said his feet were stone on the rock, and the name stuck to his family. His daughter Hild, born 680, climbed Mount Roktar in July 702, the first person known to stand on the Crown Range's highest peak. Two years later a Stonefoot hunter shot a Snow Drake taking lambs, and the League hung its hide in Highcastle's hall as the last of its kind. The kin knew better. A few drakes still nested in two high valleys above the town, and the Stonefoot herders decided to guard them and call them eagles. Hild was elected First Speaker in 719, settled the 30,000 refugees of the Upland Flight in the mines, and founded the Cliff Runners, scouts who run ridges and wall tops. She died in 741 and passed the secret of the drakes to her daughter. Three more Stonefoots have been First Speaker before Helga: Siv (874–883), who closed the high valleys to Wind Empire scouts and outside hunters; Idony (979–990); and Ylva (1052–1069), who signed the first contract for Irondeep dwarf crews in 1060. Ylva's daughter Asny kept the secret of the valleys until her death in 1097. Helga Stonefoot, born 1051, Asny's daughter, climbed 60 m of cliff at Redford in May 1063 to bring down a four-year-old boy from a Crown Eagle's ledge. She married Bard Cairnhold, a herder of Amberhurst who took the Stonefoot name, and their daughter Ada was born in 1075; Bard died in an avalanche in 1088. Helga served 20 years on the Highcastle valley council and was elected First Speaker by one vote in July 1099. Ada runs the Ridge School at Redford and keeps every hunter and buyer out of the closed valleys. The kin are proud, close and plain. They wear no rank, settle valley quarrels by the wall-run on Highcastle's walls, which their champions almost never lose, and cannot cross a lake without collapsing.
dead: Orm Stonefoot (about 652–720): Cragsman; first known carrier of the Stonefoot balance.
Hild Stonefoot (680–741): Climbed Mount Roktar; First Speaker 719–741. *Ruler:* Hild Stonefoot (First Speaker of Roktar), Highland, 719–741 (RUL-0127).
Ylva Stonefoot (1005–1069): First Speaker; brought the dwarf crews to Amberhurst. *Ruler:* Ylva Stonefoot (First Speaker), Highland, 1052–1069 (RUL-0152).
marriages: 1073, with Clan Cairnhold: Helga married Bard Cairnhold, who took the Stonefoot name.
FAM-031.allies: House Greycloak, Clan Silvervein, House Winterborn
FAM-031.secrets: About 15 Snow Drakes still nest in two valleys above Highcastle, and the kin have lied to the Council for 400 years that the white shapes are eagles.

FAM-032.y1105: Heirs of the League's founder and masters of its hired crossbows. Captain-General Ulric Greycloak commands the pass garrisons and wants the Aldmark contract.
FAM-032.arms: a grey cloak over a black crossbow, on sky blue
FAM-032.founder: Bran Greycloak (297–368), first Speaker of the Highland League
FAM-032.power: The Captain-Generalcy of the League; the 8,000 heavy crossbowmen of the Greycloak Companies, half abroad at any time; the Highcastle Crossbow Yard, one of the 66 schools; the hire-captains of Roseham; contracts worth tens of thousands of highland silver a year, a fifth of which goes to the Silver Chest.
FAM-032.history: Bran Greycloak, a herder of Roseham, led about 800 highlanders against the Solen weigh-house at Amberhurst in May 330 and trapped a Solen column in the gorge below Highcastle in July 331. He sealed the Charter of Highcastle with Aldric III in 336 and was the League's first Speaker until he died in 368. His grey herding cloak became the house's name and its soldiers' coat. Eight more Greycloaks have been First Speaker, among them Alda the Pike-Mother, who led 4,000 highlanders at Amberhurst in 471, Varin, who sent the Wind Khan's envoys home in 884, and Asa (952–968), who made the crossbow companies a League office with a Captain-General and a fifth of every contract for the Chest. The Greycloaks learned the crossbow from the Solen legions and made Roseham its workshop. Their companies won the Millrun fords for Kingsmere in 913 and held the stakes at Hartgate in 1051. Ulric Greycloak, born 1055, grew up among the hire-captains of Roseham. At 18 he served as a hired crossbowman in Aldmark's garrison of Crossmarch during the Horde siege of 1073 and watched the counterweight engines break it. He led companies for Ostra and Varenna in the 1080s, became Captain-General in 1095 and backed Helga Stonefoot for First Speaker in 1099. In November 1104 he signed a private promise with Aldmark's agents and took 20,000 highland silver in advance before the Council had voted. The Greycloaks say that a soldier who is paid and keeps his contract is as honest as a hall-priest.
dead: Bran Greycloak (297–368): Won the Crown Pass War and sealed the Charter. *Ruler:* Bran Greycloak (First Speaker the Gorge-Maker), Highland, 336–368 (RUL-0100).
Alda Greycloak the Pike-Mother (428–489): Led the highlanders at Amberhurst in 471. *Ruler:* Alda Greycloak (First Speaker the Pike-Mother), Highland, 470–489 (RUL-0110).
Asa Greycloak (905–968): Made the crossbow companies a League office. *Ruler:* Asa Greycloak (First Speaker), Highland, 952–968 (RUL-0144).
FAM-032.secrets: Ulric took 20,000 highland silver from Aldmark before the Council's vote.

FAM-033.y1105: Cattle lords of the Redford valley who led the League for 30 years until 1099. Speaker Tomas Redford wants the First Speakership back.
FAM-033.arms: a red ford-stone under a white tower, on green
FAM-033.founder: Hrodny Redford (about 360–430), elder of the Redford valley
FAM-033.power: The Redford valley, the League's richest in cattle, with about 40,000 head; Redford Tower and its beacon; the valley's seat on the Council; the Redford Men faction, which needs one-third of the Council to force a new election; a new silver vein under the valley, not yet known to them.
FAM-033.history: The Redfords are the elders of the valley that guards the foot of the Skardush road, and they have paid for it. Orc riders burned Redford in 455, in 470 and in 799. After the last raid the Redfords raised a 22 m stone tower with a beacon over the valley road in 800, and they have claimed the first place on the Council ever since. Seven Redfords have been First Speaker, from Edda (447–458) to Dagny, who refused the Holy See's claim to the tribute in 761, and Svein, who led the refusal of the Iron Reform in 1003. Hugo Redford (1017–1099) was elected in 1069 and led the League for 30 years, selling crossbowmen to anyone who paid and lending Northreach the Silver of the Halls in 1091. His son Tomas, born 1064, grew up hearing of Helga Stonefoot's climb to the eagle's ledge at Redford in 1063 and became Speaker of Redford when his father fell ill in 1097. When Hugo died in July 1099 the Council chose Helga over him by one vote. Tomas has worked since to win back the seat. He took 800 highland silver from Aldmark's agent to vote for the crossbow contract and pays the smuggler Col Eyrie, the boy Helga saved, to find what the Stonefoots hide in the high valleys. The Redfords are rich, proud and sure that the League's first seat belongs to the valley that lights the beacon.
dead: Edda Redford (395–458): First Redford First Speaker. *Ruler:* Edda Redford (First Speaker), Highland, 447–458 (RUL-0108).
Svein Redford (940–1003): Led the refusal of the Iron Reform. *Ruler:* Svein Redford (First Speaker), Highland, 990–1003 (RUL-0147).
Hugo Redford (1017–1099): First Speaker for 30 years. *Ruler:* Hugo Redford (First Speaker), Highland, 1069–1099 (RUL-0153).
FAM-033.secrets: Tomas took 800 highland silver from Aldmark's agent for his vote and pays a smuggler to find the Stonefoots' secret.

FAM-034.y1105: The silver clan of Amberhurst and keepers of the League's treasury. Mine-Warden Gerda Silvervein keeps the Silver Chest and heads the clan.
FAM-034.arms: a silver vein through black rock under a white pick, on sky blue
FAM-034.founder: Arn Silvervein (about 270–340), gang-master of the Amberhurst silver galleries
FAM-034.power: Shares in the Amberhurst silver galleries; the elected Wardenship of the Silver Chest, which takes a tenth of every mine, a fifth of every hire contract and the mule tolls; the League's loan to Northreach of 40,000 highland silver; no debts.
FAM-034.branches: the Amberhurst galleries; the Highcastle branch that has given the Silver Chest most of its wardens
FAM-034.history: The Silverveins were gang-masters of the Amberhurst galleries when Solen engineers first worked the silver with clan labor. They kept the tallies, and when the Solen tax-men took a third instead of a fifth in 326, it was Silvervein counts that proved it; the clan marched with Bran Greycloak to the weigh-house in 330. Seven Silverveins have been First Speaker. Garth kept the tribute of 756 in the Silver Chest, and it was never paid again. Torstein made the Warden of the Silver Chest an elected office in the 830s, and the clan's Highcastle branch has filled it more often than any other. When the Irondeep dwarf crews came in 1060, the Silverveins lost their place in the deep galleries but kept the count. Gerda Silvervein, born 1049 at Highcastle, learned figures from the dwarf crews' tallies as a girl, became a mine-clerk at Amberhurst in 1070 and Warden of the Silver Chest in 1088. In 1091 she arranged the Silver of the Halls for Northreach, and on her own word sent 46,000 instead of the 40,000 the Council approved. She has kept the League free of debt through three bad harvests since and suspects the dwarf crews of hiding silver. She will vote against the Aldmark contract so as not to anger the League's debtor.
dead: Garth Silvervein (690–758): Stopped the Solen tribute in 756. *Ruler:* Garth Silvervein (First Speaker), Highland, 741–758 (RUL-0128).
Torstein Silvervein (780–846): Made the Wardenship of the Silver Chest an elected office. *Ruler:* Torstein Silvervein (First Speaker), Highland, 833–846 (RUL-0134).
FAM-034.allies: The Stonefoot kin, The Tinmark Reeves
FAM-034.secrets: Gerda sent Northreach 6,000 highland silver more than the Council approved in 1091, and it appears in no roll of the Chest.

FAM-311.y1105: Kings of Greyhaven since 761. The king is deaf, the heir's ring dive was secretly helped, the king's elder sister is Empress of Aldmark, and the dragon year has begun.
FAM-311.arms: a silver diver with a knife in his teeth over a grey wave, on sea green
FAM-311.founder: Wenna Tidewell (688–752), chain-diver of the Solen channel fleet at Greyhaven
FAM-311.power: The crown and its royal domain around Greyhaven and the Smokewell March; the Toll-House, about 350,000 tides a year after Velgrad's half; 58 war galleys and about 140 cogs that can be pressed, with 9,000 seamen and marines; the Chain Guard (3,000), the Tide Divers (240) and the Rift Watch (1,600); a standing army of 60,000; the alliance with Aldmark.
FAM-311.branches: The royal line (King Osric IV, Prince Tristan, Lady Linnet); The line of Prince Aldred (Diver-Master Ness); Elswyth, Empress of Aldmark, married out in 1076; The hall-lords of Harold's line, died out in 1002
FAM-311.history: The Tidewells were divers before they were kings. In the 7th century the Solen fleet station at Greyhaven paid a Northfolk family to clear its harbor chain, fouled anchors and wrecks under water. In 719 the diver Wenna Tidewell freed the sunk harbor chain from a wreck in 30 m of water, going down eleven times in a day, and the admiral made her family the station's chain-keepers. Her son Cedric, born in 716, started as a diver's boy, commanded a galley by 30 and was admiral of the western squadron from 750. When Solenne fell, he swore himself king in the Oath Hall on New Year's Day 761, kept the 40 galleys with two years of withheld imperial tolls, and fixed the channel toll in 764. The house has held the crown for 344 years, father to son with two exceptions. In 851 Edric I died leaving an infant, and his brother Leofric took the crown. In 915 Osric the Diver's eldest son Harold could not dive, and the Tide Council chose the second son Edric, who made the Ring Law of 916. Since then every heir has dived for a silver ring at seven before the whole harbor. Osric the Diver is the house's hero. He cut the Khan's harbor chain at Yarbek in 882 and saved the Rift Coast. He is also the house's great secret, because by the Treaty of the Narrows he ferried the Wind armies into the Free Marches for silver. Every Tidewell king tells his heir, and in 1104 Osric IV told Tristan. Tidewell daughters marry abroad to buy alliances; Tidewell sons marry the great houses at home. In 1055 Osric III married Aldith Redley, so the present king is first cousin to Lord Godric Redley, the richest lender in the realm. In 1076 Princess Elswyth married Aldwin of Aldmark. She is Empress of Aldmark in 1105 and has sent Greyhaven pearls to the Horde's war-chief on her own account. Diving has cost the house its ears and sometimes its lives. Osric the Diver was deaf for his last 20 years. Osric III died in 1084 of a lung fever after a winter dive to free the harbor chain, and Osric IV was deaf at 26. He rules by divers' hand-signs, read aloud by his daughter Linnet, who is 19 and sometimes changes his words. His son and heir Tristan made the ring dive in 1090, but blacked out halfway down, and his cousin Ness, daughter of the king's late brother Prince Aldred (1035–1092), pressed the ring into his hand. By the Ring Law Tristan can never be crowned. Ness became Diver-Master in 1099 and leads the Tide Divers. In 1105 the king plans to marry Linnet to Prince Yaromir of Drevna, Tristan wants command of the galleys on the feared day, and the whole house waits to see whether the Black Dragon rises.
dead: Wenna Tidewell (688–752): Chain-diver who freed the sunk harbor chain in 719; the first known carrier of the deep lungs.
Cedric the Admiral (716–779): Last Solen channel admiral and first King of Greyhaven. *Ruler:* Cedric Tidewell (Cedric I the Admiral), Kingdom of Greyhaven, 761–779 (RUL-3101).
Osric the Diver (851–915): Cut the Khan's chain at Yarbek; secretly ferried the Wind armies. *Ruler:* Osric the Diver (Osric I), Kingdom of Greyhaven, 878–915 (RUL-3107).
Edric II the Ring-Giver (880–941): Made the Ring Law and the Horse Road Compact. *Ruler:* Edric Tidewell (Edric II the Ring-Giver), Kingdom of Greyhaven, 915–941 (RUL-3108).
Edmund the Toll-Doubler (966–1031): Doubled the toll and fought the War of the Channel. *Ruler:* Edmund Tidewell (the Toll-Doubler), Kingdom of Greyhaven, 998–1031 (RUL-3111).
Osric III (1029–1084): Died of a lung fever after a winter dive to free the harbor chain. *Ruler:* Osric Tidewell (Osric III), Kingdom of Greyhaven, 1060–1084 (RUL-3113).
marriages: 1055, with House Redley: Osric III weds Aldith Redley; mother of Osric IV and Elswyth.
1076, with House Ironside: Elswyth weds Crown Prince Aldwin; mutual defense pact.
1082, with House Wren: Osric IV weds Lady Maud Wren (died 1086), mother of Tristan and Linnet.
FAM-311.allies: House Redley, House Wren, House Ironside
FAM-311.secrets: The Diver's Ferry of 883; Tristan's ring dive was helped by Ness in 1090, which by the Ring Law bars him from the crown; Linnet changes her father's words in council and he has seen it.

FAM-312.y1105: The richest house in Greyhaven, lords of its largest city and lender to the crown. They want a seat in the Toll-House, lower tolls and peace with Velgrad.
FAM-312.arms: three golden sheaves on a red field, with a black harbor light
FAM-312.founder: Harold Redley (732–796), grain lord of the plain who first swore to Cedric
FAM-312.power: The city of Redley (48,900 people) and its harbor light; the Redley Plain, Greyhaven's best grain land, worked mostly by bound tenants; a levy of about 12,000; 30,000 tides owed by the crown on the loan of 1096; grain sales abroad in hungry years.
FAM-312.branches: The lords of Redley (main line); The Redleys of Easterstone, grain factors
FAM-312.history: House Redley has fed Greyhaven since before it was a kingdom. Its lords held the grain plain west of the Rift Heights and sold to the Solen fleet station for three centuries. When the empire fell and Cedric Tidewell swore himself king in 761, Harold Redley was the first plain lord to kneel, in return for a share of the new channel toll and the right to ship grain toll-free. His grain fed the 40 galleys through the first winters. In 812, when King Wystan drowned and the boy Godwin was crowned at 15, Lord Oswy Redley sat at the head of the Tide Council for three years. Since then a Redley has sat on the council in most reigns. The Redleys have always been the peace party. Their grain goes out by sea, so high tolls and channel wars hurt them first. In 1006 Lord Edwin Redley argued against King Edmund's doubled toll and lost, and the War of the Channel cost the house two grain fleets. When the Horse Road Compact of 925 began trading Greyhaven grain for steppe horses, it was mostly Redley grain, and the house grew rich on it. In 1055 Aldith Redley married the future Osric III, so the present king's mother was a Redley. Lord Godric Redley, born in 1047, became head of the house in 1075. In Tamar's hungry year of 1088 he sold Redley grain to Tamar's buyers at three times the price and doubled the house's silver. In 1096 he lent the crown 60,000 tides to rebuild the galley fleet, and only half has been repaid. He holds his tenants hard: in 1097 his stewards hanged a serf at Redley's gate for striking a steward, and that serf's brother, Ned Thornby, now leads 40 outlaws in the Wrendale forest and plans to free 200 more of the house's serfs at the Spring Equinox. Since 1103 Godric has written in secret to Borek Marten of Velgrad's Fur Staple about cutting the channel tolls on grain and furs behind the king's back. In 1105 he wants the crown to borrow 40,000 more tides from him in exchange for a seat and a fifth share in the Toll-House. If toll income falls in the dragon year, the king may have to accept, and the house that has always fed the crown would own part of its treasure.
dead: Harold Redley (732–796): First plain lord to swear to Cedric; fed the fleet.
Oswy Redley (768–829): Led the Tide Council for the boy king Godwin.
Aldith Redley (1034–1071): Queen of Osric III and mother of Osric IV and Empress Elswyth.
marriages: 1055, with House Tidewell: Aldith Redley weds the future Osric III.
FAM-312.secrets: Godric Redley's letters to Borek Marten of Velgrad (since 1103) could see him tried for treason.

FAM-313.y1105: Forest lords of Wrendale and masters of the Timber Guild, rich from selling oak to Aldmark and, in secret, to Velgrad.
FAM-313.arms: a brown wren on an oak bough, on a field of green
FAM-313.founder: Aelric Wren (752–818), forester who supplied oak for King Aldred's galleys
FAM-313.power: The city of Wrendale (29,000) and its harbor; the Wrendale forests of oak and chestnut; the Timber Guild of Wrendale, the richest guild after the Toll-House; contracts with Aldmark's Cold Bay yards.
FAM-313.history: House Wren rose on oak. When King Aldred built the chain towers and a larger fleet after 772, a forester named Aelric Wren supplied the timber, and in 790 the king made him lord of Wrendale. For three centuries the Wrens sold ship oak and chestnut to the channel yards at Brookhurst and to any foreign buyer the crown allowed. In 1082 Lady Maud Wren married Prince Osric, the future Osric IV; she died in 1086, so the heir Tristan and Lady Linnet are half Wren by blood. Elinor Wren became head of the house in 1079, when her brother died of a fall. In 1080, after the elves refused Aldmark any Evenwood timber in the Border War (WAR-42), she signed the first contract to sell Wrendale oak to Aldmark's yards. By 1095 she had made the Timber Guild the richest guild in Greyhaven after the Toll-House. Since 1102 she has also sold oak through an agent at Sevany to Velgrad's galley yards, the same yards that are now fitting fire rafts against Greyhaven. The outlaw Ned Thornby holds a letter that proves it. She is the late queen's cousin, the heir's kin, and a traitor if the letter is read.
dead: Aelric Wren (752–818): Supplied the oak for King Aldred's fleet and founded the house.
Maud Wren (1061–1086): Queen of Osric IV, mother of Tristan and Linnet.
marriages: 1082, with House Tidewell: Maud Wren weds Prince Osric, the future Osric IV.
FAM-313.rivals: House Redley, The Keels of Brookhurst
FAM-313.secrets: Since 1102 Elinor Wren has sold oak to Velgrad's galley yards through an agent at Sevany; Ned Thornby holds the letter that proves it.

FAM-314.y1105: The leading shipwright family of Greyhaven. One brother heads the Brookhurst yards; the other keeps the share-book of the Blackreef pirates.
FAM-314.arms: a black keel and rudder on a field of oak brown
FAM-314.founder: Ansel Keel (988–1058), master shipwright who hung the first sternpost rudder
FAM-314.power: The largest yard at Brookhurst and the headship of the Shipwrights of Brookhurst, who build and repair Greyhaven's galleys and cogs; 12,000 tides owed by the crown for galleys built since 1100; a copy of a page of Blackreef's share-book.
FAM-314.branches: The Brookhurst yard (Hamo Keel); Jonas Keel at Blackreef
FAM-314.history: The Keels are shipwrights who became too useful to ignore. Ansel Keel set up his own yard at Brookhurst after the War of the Channel ended in 1010, when the crown needed galleys faster than the old yards could build them. In 1035 he and his sons hung a single rudder on the stern of a cog in place of a steering oar, and Greyhaven cogs began to hold their course in the channel tides. His grandson Hamo Keel, born in 1056, built his first galley in 1080, rebuilt the fleet after the losses off Wolfhaven in 1092, and became head of the Shipwrights of Brookhurst in 1097. In September 1104 he sold three old cogs to a Sevany merchant for good silver, and they are now among the fire rafts below Mount Dobava. His younger brother Jonas ran away to sea at 14 in 1072, was taken by Blackreef corsairs in 1074 and signed their Articles because he could read. He has kept the Brotherhood's share-book since 1092. In 1100 he sent Hamo a sealed copy of the page that records Lucerna's secret fifth of the dragon toll, 'in case I drown'. The brothers have not spoken in years, but that page sits in the Brookhurst yard, and it could set Lucerna against every channel power.
dead: Ansel Keel (988–1058): Hung the first sternpost rudder on a cog in 1035.
FAM-314.secrets: Hamo sold three cogs that became Velgrad's fire rafts, and he holds Jonas's copy of the Blackreef share-book page on Lucerna's fifth.

FAM-315.y1105: Hereditary keepers of the Sea King's Hall at Greyhaven and leaders of the Dragon Watch. The present keeper preaches a rising he no longer believes in.
FAM-315.arms: a grey wave under an iron ring on a black field
FAM-315.founder: Ealdor Grey (about 390–455), first hall-priest of the Sea King's Hall at the Solen fleet station
FAM-315.power: The Sea King's Hall, the kingdom's Oath Hall; 40 priests and the widows' dole of 300; the iron ring on which marriages and oaths are sworn and the silver ring of the royal dive; the yearly Dragon rite and a seat on the Tide Council.
FAM-315.history: The Greys have kept the Sea King's Hall at Greyhaven since the Solen fleet station was built in 424. Hall-priests of the Seven Halls may marry, and the office passed from father to son or nephew. In 761 Hall-Keeper Wulfhere Grey held the iron ring on which Cedric Tidewell swore himself king, and since 916 the Hall-Keeper has thrown the silver ring into the harbor for every royal dive. In 1037 a Hall-Keeper wrote a smoke-serpent off Smokewell into the hall-roll. In 1071 young Wulfric Grey stood on the harbor wall when the black serpent rose, found that entry, and led the first rite to keep the dragon asleep. He became Keeper in 1080 and made the rite the heart of the hall. Since 1090, when the sulfur digger Hob Yellowhand showed him how Smokewell throws up dark columns of smoke, he has doubted the dragon. He pays Hob to keep quiet and keeps preaching, because the rite pays for 40 priests and feeds 300 widows. In 1105 he wants the harbor closed for nine days around the feared day, which would cost the Toll-House more than the dragon ever did.
dead: Ealdor Grey (about 390–455): First keeper of the Sea King's Hall at the fleet station.
Wulfhere Grey (712–781): Held the iron ring when Cedric swore himself king.
FAM-315.rivals: The Toll-House party of Beatrix Hollin, Diver-Master Ness Tidewell's party
FAM-315.secrets: The Hall-Keeper has known since 1090 that Smokewell's smoke made the dragon of 1071, and pays Hob Yellowhand to stay silent.

FAM-201.y1105: Royal house of Morhaven since 1012. King Aurelio II rules; his heir Prince Tancred lacks the Falcone eyes and has no son, so the crown may one day pass to Aurelio's Valdane grandson.
FAM-201.arms: a black falcon with spread wings over a white tower, on sky blue
FAM-201.founder: Piero Falcone the Falcon (921–989), a charcoal-burner's son who became a lookout of the Castina tower in 935
FAM-201.power: The crown of Morhaven: crown lands on the Heights and in the Castina foothills; the Horse Road toll on about 4,000 horses a year; harbor dues of Morhaven; 38,000 standing troops, 24 war galleys and about 40 cogs; the 1,400 lookouts of the Tower Watch, led by Falcone kin; about 60 suns a jar on 30 jars a year of secret fire-oil; against this a debt of about 350,000 suns to House Lunetti.
FAM-201.branches: The royal line of the Heights: King Aurelio II and Prince Tancred; The line of Prince Leone (1048–1079): Dame Serena, Master of the Tower of Far Eyes; The Tower Falcones of Felano, descended from Ugo Falcone (985–1051), who captain about a dozen Tower Watch companies; The Varennan branch through Queen Bianca, born Falcone, and her son Prince Galen Valdane
FAM-201.history: The Falcones were not born noble. In 898 Tancred the Steadfast's Tower Edict put a paid lookout in a stone tower every 10 km along the coast and the steppe edge. Piero, a charcoal-burner's son from the Castina hills born in 921, climbed the Castina tower at 14 in 935. He read the flags of the next tower at 3 km when the older lookouts saw a smudge, and he called raiders on the steppe edge an hour before anyone else. The watch called him Piero the Falcon, and the nickname became the family name. His son Bruno Falcone (950–1004) had the same eyes and rose to captain the Felano tower and its coast galley. Bruno's sons Aurelio (born 982) and Ugo (born 985) had them too. Aurelio took his father's command in 1004. In May 1011 he followed a flock of sea drakes out to sea, saw 42 corsair sails at 30 km and raced home in time for the harbor chain to rise. King Ottone ran, and on Return Day 1012 the Temple crowned the lookout's son. The council's price was a marriage: in 1013 Aurelio wed Costanza Rovani, Ottone's niece and a great-great-granddaughter of Tancred the Steadfast. So every Falcone king since carries the blood of the Lucani and the Rovani, and the house took their names, Tancred and Leone. Aurelio made the Tower Watch a royal corps and put his brother Ugo over the Felano companies; Ugo's descendants, the Tower Falcones, still captain most of them. Aurelio died in 1049 after weeks of headaches in a dark room. His son Leone II (1015–1079) married Giulia Castor of the chancellors' house in 1041 and ruled 30 careful years. Leone's sons both had the eyes. The younger, Prince Leone (1048–1079), married Nerina, a tower knight's daughter of Lucina, in 1073. She died of the Harbor Pox in 1077, and he died on the upper Tirana on 28 August 1079, when the Red Widow came out of the setting sun. His daughter Serena was raised at court and now runs the Tower of Far Eyes. The elder son, Aurelio II, was crowned in 1079. He married Maddalena Arcieri, a Varennan lady, in 1066; she bore Bianca in 1068 and Tancred in 1070 and died of the Harbor Pox in 1077. Bianca has the eyes. Tancred does not, and he has felt it all his life. He married Vittoria, daughter of a Temple knight of Pertena, in 1095; she died in childbirth in 1097 with a stillborn son, and he has not married again. Bianca married Roderic III of Varenna in 1090 and bore Prince Galen in 1092; Galen did not inherit the eyes. The house is small: three living carriers of the eyes, one heir without them, and one heir of the next generation who is a Valdane. Under the Pertena Judgment of 918, if Tancred dies without a son, Galen inherits Morhaven. That is why the Sun Party whispers that a Falcone without the eyes is only half a Falcone, and why Tancred wants a new wife as much as he wants towers.
dead: Piero Falcone the Falcon (921–989): First carrier of the eyes; lookout of the Castina tower from 935. His nickname became the family name.
Bruno Falcone (950–1004): Captain of the Felano tower and its coast galley; father of the first Falcone king.
Aurelio Falcone the Far-Eyed (982–1049): Spotted the corsair fleet at 30 km in 1011; king 1012–1049. *Ruler:* Aurelio Falcone the Far-Eyed (Aurelio I), Kingdom of Morhaven, 1012–1049 (RUL-2012).
Ugo Falcone (985–1051): Brother of Aurelio I; first captain of the Felano Tower Watch companies and founder of the Tower Falcones.
Costanza Rovani (994–1061): Queen of Aurelio I; brought the blood of the Lucani and Rovani kings into the house.
Leone II the Careful (1015–1079): King 1049–1079; kept Morhaven out of the Corsair War and saved silver. *Ruler:* Leone Falcone (Leone II the Careful), Kingdom of Morhaven, 1049–1079 (RUL-2013).
marriages: 1013, with House Rovani: Aurelio I weds Costanza Rovani, niece of the fled king, joining the old royal blood to the new house.
1041, with House Castor: Leone II weds Giulia Castor, granddaughter of Chancellor Piero Castor.
1095, with A Temple knight's family of Pertena: Prince Tancred weds Vittoria of Pertena; she dies in childbirth in 1097 with a stillborn son.
1066, with House Arcieri of Varenna: Aurelio II weds Maddalena Arcieri (1047–1077), mother of Bianca and Tancred.
1090, with House Valdane: Bianca Falcone weds Roderic III of Varenna under the Falcone marriage pact; 2,000 men promised each way.
FAM-201.allies: House Castor, House Sabine, House Valdane
FAM-201.secrets: King Aurelio II takes about 60 suns a jar on steppe fire-oil passing to Queen Livia, and the chancery holds the carrion roll of 897 that unmakes the Miracle of Morhaven. Prince Tancred has secretly warned Prince Nikos Tessaran that the Felano 'lamps' are meant for Coreria.

FAM-202.y1105: Extinct in the male line since King Roderic died of the Black Cough in 918. Its blood runs on in House Falcone through Queen Costanza Rovani.
FAM-202.arms: a grey wolf standing on a white wall, on dark red
FAM-202.founder: Lucan the Grey (714–788), general of the Morhaven legion and first King of Morhaven
FAM-202.power: None in 1105. In its time: the crown of Morhaven, the Morhaven legion's veterans settled on Pertena and Lucina land, and the Deep Walls.
FAM-202.branches: The royal line (760–918); The female line through Isotta Lucani into House Rovani and so into House Falcone
FAM-202.history: Lucan the Grey was the son of a centurion of the Morhaven legion, born at Pertena in 714. The name Lucani, 'Lucan's own', was first the name of his soldiers and then of his house. He led the unpaid legion to Solenne in 756, broke the emperor's sally at Clarente in 757 and was crowned by High Luminary Benedict on 22 September 760. He swore that the Temple would crown every King of Morhaven, and the oath still binds the Falcones. His son Marius the Mason built the Deep Walls with their listening galleries (792–806). Lucan II granted the Santora March to House Sabine in 824. Corrado the Quiet and Silvano the Pious kept 51 years of peace. Tancred the Steadfast (852–911) held the city against Khan Ulagan in 895–897 and fouled the Khan's water. At 42 he married Isolde Valdane, daughter of Roderic the Lionheart, in 894. She bore Roderic, called the Siege-Born, inside the besieged city in 896, and Isotta in 898. Isolde ruled for her son after 911 and for her grandson after 918, and died in 941. Roderic died of the Black Cough at 22 in 918, and the male line ended. The Pertena Judgment gave the crown to Isotta's son by Guido Rovani. The Lucani kings lie in the crypt of the Sun Temple of Morhaven, except Tancred, who asked to lie among his soldiers in the siege cemetery below the walls.
dead: Lucan the Grey (714–788): First King of Morhaven. *Ruler:* Lucan the Grey (Lucan I), Kingdom of Morhaven, 760–788 (RUL-2001).
Marius the Mason (745–811): Built the Deep Walls. *Ruler:* Marius Lucani (Marius I the Mason), Kingdom of Morhaven, 788–811 (RUL-2002).
Tancred the Steadfast (852–911): Held Morhaven against the Khan in 895–897. *Ruler:* Tancred the Steadfast (Tancred I), Kingdom of Morhaven, 884–911 (RUL-2006).
Isolde Valdane (870–941): Queen of Tancred, daughter of Roderic the Lionheart; regent for her son and grandson.
Roderic the Siege-Born (896–918): Last Lucani king; died of the Black Cough. *Ruler:* Roderic Lucani (Roderic I the Siege-Born), Kingdom of Morhaven, 911–918 (RUL-2007).
marriages: 894, with House Valdane: Tancred the Steadfast weds Isolde, daughter of Roderic the Lionheart; the dowry pays 400 knights for a year.
914, with House Rovani: Isotta Lucani weds Guido Rovani of Pertena; their son becomes king in 918.
FAM-202.secrets: The Pertena Judgment of 918 that ended the Lucani claim was not old Solen law at all but a bargain between the Rovani and the Temple.

FAM-203.y1105: Extinct in the male line since King Ottone the Fled died at Lucerna in 1026. Its blood runs on in House Falcone through Queen Costanza Rovani.
FAM-203.arms: a golden wheat sheaf bound with a red cord, on green
FAM-203.founder: Ascanio Rovani (655–721), a Pertena grain lord who armed his tenants after the Wind Rider raid of 693
FAM-203.power: None in 1105. Its Pertena grain estates passed to the crown in 1026; about a third of them went to the Temple in the settlement of 1012.
FAM-203.branches: The royal line (918–1011); The Pertena line of Ottone's younger brother Corrado (died 1010), which ended with Costanza
FAM-203.history: The Rovani were grain lords of the Pertena valleys north of Morhaven. When about 1,500 Wind Riders burned the Felano harvest in 693 and the empire's legion did nothing, Ascanio Rovani armed 300 of his tenants, and the family has been a military house ever since. They backed Lucan the Grey in 756 and grew rich on the grain that fed Morhaven through the siege of 895–897. In 914 Guido Rovani married Isotta, daughter of Tancred the Steadfast. When her brother King Roderic died in 918, the Rovani held the council's grain in a plague year, and the Pertena Judgment made their two-year-old son King Tancred II. Tancred II reigned 52 years and signed the first Horse Road compact in 930. His son Leone I and grandson Guido the Hunter spent the horse money on palaces at Pertena and borrowed from Lucerna. Ottone, crowned in 1003, inherited 90,000 suns of debt, seized Temple land at Lucina in 1007 and ran from the city when the hired corsairs came in May 1011. He was declared fled and died at Lucerna in 1026 without sons. His niece Costanza married the new king, Aurelio Falcone, in 1013, and through her the Rovani blood sits on the throne again.
dead: Guido Rovani (890–940): Husband of Isotta Lucani and regent for his son Tancred II until 932.
Tancred II the Cradle King (916–970): Crowned at two; reigned 52 years. *Ruler:* Tancred Rovani (Tancred II the Cradle King), Kingdom of Morhaven, 918–970 (RUL-2008).
Ottone the Fled (984–1026): Ran from the corsairs in 1011; died in exile at Lucerna. *Ruler:* Ottone Rovani (Ottone I the Fled), Kingdom of Morhaven, 1003–1011 (RUL-2011).
