Costanza Rovani (994–1061): Last of the Rovani blood; queen of Aurelio I Falcone.
marriages: 914, with House Lucani: Guido Rovani weds Isotta Lucani, daughter of Tancred the Steadfast.
1013, with House Falcone: Costanza Rovani weds King Aurelio Falcone.
FAM-203.secrets: Ottone's seizure of 1007 was of land the Temple had truly bought with Schism Tax money in 741; the Rovani chancery kept the proof, which passed to the Castor chancellors in 1011.

FAM-204.y1105: Hereditary chancellors of Morhaven since 760 and owners of the Castina iron. Lord Emilio Castor keeps the chancery and the carrion roll and owes the Temple 25,000 suns.
FAM-204.arms: a black hammer and a silver key crossed, on iron grey
FAM-204.founder: Decimo Castor (551–619), imperial procurator of the Castina iron
FAM-204.power: The Castina hills around Castina; the Dorica and Pisona iron workings, about 300 tonnes of bloom iron a year; the timber rights of the Castina beech and oak woods; the ground of the Mine Hall of Castina; the chancery of Morhaven and all its rolls; about 800 men-at-arms; a Temple debt of 25,000 suns.
FAM-204.branches: The chancellors' line at Castina; The mine-reeves of Dorica and Pisona, cousins who run the iron workings
FAM-204.history: The Castors are the oldest house in Morhaven. In 588 the Solen Empire named Decimo Castor procurator of the Castina iron, and his descendants have dug it ever since. They served whoever held the coast: Octavian in 616, Maximus in the 650s and Theodoric after 668. When the empire cut the Morhaven legion in 690 and the Wind Riders burned Felano's harvest in 693, the Castors armed their miners. Marco Castor (722–795) was quartermaster of Lucan the Grey's legion; he fed the army that besieged Solenne and was named the first Chancellor of Morhaven in 760. The office has passed from father to son since, and with it the chancery rolls, which the Castors copy, keep and sometimes read too closely. Castina miners built Marius the Mason's Deep Walls (792–806). In November 895 Arrigo Castor (861–925) led them through the listening galleries into the Khan's tunnel under the landward gate and fired it: the Night of the Mines. In 898 the house opened the Mine Hall of Castina on its own ground to train counter-miners, and it still owns the ground and pays the Hall's winter wages. In 1011, when King Ottone fled, Chancellor Piero Castor (968–1037) governed with the Luminary for a year and chose to back the lookout Aurelio Falcone. The Rovani chancery rolls, with the proof of what the Temple paid for its Lucina land, passed into Castor hands. Piero's granddaughter Giulia married Leone Falcone, the future Leone II, in 1041, and the house has stood closest to the throne since. Emilio Castor, born in 1050, became Lord Chancellor when Aurelio II was crowned in 1079. The wet winter of 1098 flooded the Castina pits. That same autumn Emilio found the garrison roll of 897 that pays the 'carrion carriers' and showed it to the king. In 1099 he let a clerk of the Holy See's Treasurer, Crispin Dorn, read it in return for a Temple loan of 25,000 suns to drain the pits. So the Temple knows the crown holds its shame, and the king does not know it knows. The Castors set the price of Castina timber, which sets them against the shipwrights of Felano, and Emilio will not draft the charter Felano wants. He means to break Luminary Cresta's Sun Party in 1105 by showing him the roll in private. Castor men-at-arms guard the iron road from the pits down to Felano, and a Castor cousin has been mine-reeve of Dorica for as long as the rolls go back.
dead: Decimo Castor (551–619): Imperial procurator of the Castina iron; founder.
Marco Castor (722–795): Quartermaster of Lucan the Grey; first Chancellor of Morhaven.
Arrigo Castor (861–925): Led the Castina miners on the Night of the Mines, November 895.
Piero Castor (968–1037): Chancellor who governed in the interregnum of 1011–1012 and backed Aurelio Falcone.
Giulia Castor (1019–1072): Queen of Leone II and mother of Aurelio II.
marriages: 1041, with House Falcone: Giulia Castor weds Leone Falcone, later Leone II.
FAM-204.secrets: Emilio Castor let the Holy See's Treasurer's clerk read the carrion roll of 897 in 1099 for a 25,000-sun loan, without telling the king. The chancery also holds Rovani proof that the Temple bought its Lucina farms with Schism Tax money.

FAM-205.y1105: Horse-lords of the Santora March and hereditary Masters of Horse. Lord Arnaut Sabine weighs the king's oil silver and skims it; his sister Dame Oriana commands the Santora Riders and means to catch the oil caravans.
FAM-205.arms: a white horse running on steppe gold, a blue cloth tied to its bridle
FAM-205.founder: Baldo Sabine (795–861), knight of Lucan II, first Lord of the Santora March
FAM-205.power: The Santora March, about 9,000 km² of steppe-edge grazing and terraced highland fields; Santora Keep, the last fort on the Horse Road; about 12,000 horses on Sabine runs; the office of Master of Horse, which collects the Horse Road toll for the crown and keeps a twentieth by old right; command of the 3,000 Santora Riders through Dame Oriana.
FAM-205.branches: The lords of Santora Keep; The steppe cousins: descendants of Sabine sons who married into the Sea Wind tribe and live on both sides of the Horse Road
FAM-205.history: Baldo Sabine was a knight of Lucan II. In 823 he took 300 horses from raiders on the steppe edge, and on May Fair 824 the king granted him the country around Santora to hold. Within a year he married the daughter of a Wind Rider horse trader, and the Sabines have married steppe women every other generation since. They wear felt coats over mail, drink mare's milk and tie blue cloth to the hill cairns, and the lords of the coast call them half-steppe. They built Santora Keep in the 830s and held it through the Wind Empire's years. During the siege of 895–897 Ottavio Sabine (858–920) kept Santora and sent riders by night to burn the grass of the Castina hills where the Khan's 100,000 horses grazed, which helped starve the siege. The Black Cough emptied the steppe edge after 916, and the Sabines turned the dead farms into horse runs. In 930 Rinaldo Sabine (889–952) rode to the new Nine Winds and swore the first Horse Road compact at the Santora Horse Fair. Since then the Master of Horse has been a Sabine in all but a few years, buying the crown's horses, tolling every herd and keeping a twentieth. Galvano Sabine (1030–1082) raised his children on horseback; he died in a fall at the Horse Fair of 1082. His son Arnaut, born in 1056, rode with the Santora Riders from 1072 and with the embassy that renewed the compact in 1080. He became head of the house in 1082 and, once the old deputy who held the office after Galvano died, Master of Horse in 1086. His sister Oriana, born in 1063, was the first woman to command a company of the Riders in 1088. In August 1097 she lost 120 riders chasing Horde raiders into an ambush and blamed a tower lookout, who lost an eye for her mistake. Prince Tancred made her Captain of the Santora Riders in 1099. Since 1103 Arnaut has met the oil caravans at Santora and weighed the king's cut, keeping one part in six in the strongroom of Santora Keep. He plans to sell 400 Morhaven-bred horses to Prince Andros's Dawn Lances this spring, against his king's promise to Queen Livia. Oriana plans to ride the Horse Road in March with 600 riders to catch the night caravans. The two Sabines are about to meet on the same road from opposite sides. The Santora Horse Fair each May is Sabine ground, and the house judges its archery; in 1099 a Nine Winds archer, Dorin Swiftarrow, beat Oriana there before her own riders.
dead: Baldo Sabine (795–861): First Lord of the Santora March.
Ottavio Sabine (858–920): Burned the grass of the Castina hills under the Khan's herds in 896–897.
Rinaldo Sabine (889–952): Swore the first Horse Road compact with the Nine Winds in 930; first hereditary Master of Horse.
Galvano Sabine (1030–1082): Father of Arnaut and Oriana; died in a fall at the Horse Fair.
marriages: 825, with Sea Wind horse-traders of the steppe: Baldo Sabine weds a Wind Rider trader's daughter; the first of many steppe brides.
1054, with Sea Wind tribe of the Nine Winds: Galvano Sabine weds a Sea Wind chief's niece, mother of Arnaut and Oriana.
FAM-205.secrets: Arnaut Sabine skims one part in six of the king's oil silver and hides it at Santora Keep. Oriana Sabine's report of 1097 blamed an innocent lookout for her own mistake.

FAM-206.y1105: Merchants of Felano raised to nobility in 1080. Mistress Adela Corso is Harbor-Mistress of Felano, sits on the Crown Council and keeps duplicate bills that prove the oil trade.
FAM-206.arms: a silver harbor key over three blue waves, on white
FAM-206.founder: Tomas Corso (962–1031), a Felano salt-fish buyer who bought his first two boats in 990
FAM-206.power: Eleven cogs and a salt-fish fleet of about 30 boats; warehouses on Felano's Salt Quay; the office of Harbor-Mistress of Felano and its harbor dues; the leadership of the Felano Merchants; bills of exchange handled by House Lunetti.
FAM-206.branches: The Salt Quay house at Felano
FAM-206.history: Tomas Corso bought his first two salt-fish boats at Felano in 990 and sold dried fish to the Heights and to the Holy Coast. His grandsons added cogs after the earthquake of 1039, when the rebuilt quays were cheap to rent. The house grew rich selling grain to both Tessarian camps after 1061. Adela Corso was born in 1059. The Harbor Pox of 1076–1078 killed her husband, the ship-master Matteo Venn, and both her brothers, and at 18 she took over the ships with an infant son. In the dry summer of 1080 her cogs brought Qadiri grain to Morhaven at the old price, and King Aurelio II raised the house to the nobility; the crown quietly paid the difference. She became Harbor-Mistress of Felano in 1087. Felano is bigger and richer than the capital, and Adela leads its merchants in asking for a charter of self-rule and a seat on the Crown Council. Since 1103 her clerks have signed the bills of lading for the 'lamp oil' that passes to Tessar. She kept a duplicate of every bill, with the royal clerk's seal, in the strongroom of her Salt Quay warehouse. That is her lever on the king. Her son, born in 1076, sails the family's cogs.
dead: Tomas Corso (962–1031): Founder of the salt-fish trade.
Matteo Venn (1051–1077): Ship-master, husband of Adela Corso; died of the Harbor Pox.
marriages: 1075, with Venn ship-masters of Felano: Adela Corso weds Matteo Venn, who takes the Corso name for the ships.
FAM-206.secrets: Adela Corso holds duplicate sealed bills of lading for every 'lamp oil' jar that has passed Felano since 1103.

FAM-211.y1105: The greatest bank of the Middle Sea and the ruling house of Ostra since 1047. First Banker Cosimo Lunetti leads the Twelve and hosts the secret Tessarian talks; his daughter Beatrice keeps the ledgers and shares his memory.
FAM-211.arms: a purple crescent moon over an open black ledger, on silver
FAM-211.founder: Benedetto Lunetti (806–871), a money-changer who took one of the first benches of the Exchange Hall in 849
FAM-211.power: About 4 million suns in coin and loans; the vault and strong-room on Ledger Street; the Temple's coin under the banking compact of 981 (renewed 1091); debts owed by Varenna (about 1.1 million suns), Queen Livia (about 700,000), Morhaven (about 350,000) and half the towns of the Free Marches; the First Banker's chair and a working majority of the Twelve; the Money-Changers' Bench and the Ledger School; the pay of the Purple Company (4,000) and the Exchange Guard (800); and four secrets in its keeping: the lead bars, the front-house ledgers, Jory Flint's map and the Neck drafts.
FAM-211.branches: The Ledger Street line: First Banker Cosimo and his daughter Beatrice; The Aventi-Lunetti of Calora, descended from the marriage of 931, who farm the old Aventi olive estates; Wards of the Ledger Contract: children of Lunetti daughters who showed the memory at five and were raised in the house
FAM-211.history: Benedetto Lunetti was a money-changer on the harbor steps who took one of the 24 benches of the new Exchange Hall in 849. His daughter Ilaria, born in 842, was the first of the house with the family memory. She kept his bench at 12, earned the name 'the Ledger' with her first great loan, and in 889 became the first woman and first Lunetti elected First Banker. She lent Morhaven 60,000 silver in 895 while buying captives from the Khan's governors, and in 909 she read the Wind Empire's end in its own ledgers and called in its loans. She married a Sabena ship-master who took her name, and her will of 911 bound her descendants by the Ledger Contract. Her son Marco, who lacked the memory, ruled eight years and died of the Black Cough in 919. His daughter Nora had the memory and drowned herself in the harbor below Ledger Street in 934 at 29, the first of two Lunetti to do so. Nora's brother Benedetto married Camilla, heiress of the last Aventi First Banker, in 931, and in 936 the Aventi bench and estates came to the Lunetti. Their son Andrea the Tally (938–1001) had the memory, made the house the Temple's banker in 981 and lent to Emperor Nikandros. His son Stefano (966–1030) did not have it, but his granddaughter Isabetta, born in 1001, did. Isabetta kept the record of the Gold Pledge in 1027. She married a Lucernan grain factor, Tullio Brandi, who took the Lunetti name. In 1044 she remembered the weight of every gold bar Tessar had sent, cut open the light new ones, found lead and broke an empire. She held the first seat from 1047 to 1080. Her younger son Ugo had the memory and walked into the sea in 1071 at 31. Her elder son Lorenzo (1025–1091) did not have it; he ruled patiently through the best clerks in the city and put down the Sabena riots of 1083. Lorenzo's son Cosimo, born in 1053, was found at six to have the memory. At 11 he read Olivar Mentis's letters in the chests of lead bars. He married Isotta Ferrante of a Sabena shipping house in 1077; she bore Beatrice in 1079 and died in 1085. Cosimo was elected First Banker on 1 July 1091. He bought Jory Flint's map in 1098 and has hosted the envoys of both Tessarian claimants since 1102. That same spring he walked into the harbor in a black mood and was pulled out by his physician, Elthas Moonwell, who has told no one. Beatrice recited all 1,300 entries of the Temple's debt roll before the Twelve in 1100 and became Keeper of the Ledgers in 1102. She sleeps about three hours a night. In 1105 the house has two living members with the memory and no third in sight: Beatrice is unmarried, and the Ledger Contract makes every marriage she might make a matter for the whole house.
dead: Ilaria Lunetti the Ledger (842–911): First carrier of the memory; First Banker 889–911. *Ruler:* Ilaria Lunetti the Ledger, Ostra, 889–911 (RUL-2108).
Nora Lunetti (905–934): Had the memory and drowned herself in the harbor below Ledger Street.
Andrea Lunetti the Tally (938–1001): First Banker 979–1001; made the house the Temple's banker. *Ruler:* Andrea Lunetti (the Tally), Ostra, 979–1001 (RUL-2113).
Isabetta Lunetti (1001–1080): Found the lead bars and called in the Tessarian loans in 1044; First Banker 1047–1080. *Ruler:* Isabetta Lunetti (the Breaker of Empires), Ostra, 1047–1080 (RUL-2116).
Ugo Lunetti (1040–1071): Isabetta's younger son; had the memory and walked into the sea.
Lorenzo Lunetti the Patient (1025–1091): First Banker 1080–1091; built the Sabena Citadel. *Ruler:* Lorenzo Lunetti (the Patient), Ostra, 1080–1091 (RUL-2117).
marriages: 931, with House Aventi: Benedetto Lunetti weds Camilla Aventi, heiress of the last Aventi First Banker; the Aventi bench passes to the Lunetti in 936.
1020, with Brandi grain factors of Lucerna: Isabetta Lunetti weds Tullio Brandi, who takes the Lunetti name under the Ledger Contract.
1077, with Ferrante shipping house of Sabena: Cosimo Lunetti weds Isotta Ferrante, mother of Beatrice; she dies in 1085.
FAM-211.allies: House Pell, House Sarto, House Doravelli, House Vanni
FAM-211.rivals: House Carrano, The Hold Bank of Stonehold
FAM-211.secrets: The lead bars of 1043, the front-house ledgers of Lucerna's toll share, Jory Flint's map and the two Neck drafts all lie on Ledger Street. The First Banker tried to drown himself in 1102, and Ilaria's second book shows the house traded in Marchfolk captives.

FAM-212.y1105: Failed in 1083 and lost its seat on the Twelve. Ser Adriano Carrano lives on Sabena rents, leads the Carrano Creditors and works to break House Lunetti.
FAM-212.arms: three gold coins on a black bench, on red
FAM-212.founder: Ruggero Carrano (781–846), a Sabena grain broker who began lending against harvests in 812
FAM-212.power: Rents from about 60 houses and warehouses in Sabena; a paper claim of 400,000 marks on Queen Livia's crown; the Carrano Creditors, about 40 ruined lenders and their lawyers; a paid clerk inside the Lunetti strong-room; Enzo Sarto's promised vote if Cosimo Lunetti falls.
FAM-212.branches: The Sabena line of Ser Adriano
FAM-212.history: Ruggero Carrano was a grain broker of Sabena who began lending to farmers against their harvests in 812. His son Giacomo (794–864) made the house rich shipping Tamari grain, paid for the Exchange Hall and its painted ceiling of every coin, and in 849 became the first head of Ostra styled First Banker. He married Livia Aventi, joining the two oldest fortunes of the city. The Carranos have always been Sabena's bank: they lend to dockers, dyers and ship-masters as well as to kings, and Sabena's poor both need and hate them. Lapo Carrano was First Banker from 958 to 979. When Tessaria struck the Leontine in 927, the Carrano bench became its market in Ostra, and the house held more Tessarian paper than any other. Bernardo Carrano the Weigher held the first seat from 1001 to 1029. His weighers found within a year that Nikandros had cut the silver in the Leontine in 1005, and the bench hoarded the old full-weight coin at a fine profit. His son Guido held the seat from 1029. In 1044 Guido argued against calling in the Tessarian loans, because his own bench would lose most by it. When the empire fell in 1047, the Twelve used the old rule that a First Banker whose bench stops paying must stand again, and Guido lost the seat to Isabetta Lunetti. He died in 1058, and the house has blamed the Lunetti ever since. To win back what it lost, House Carrano lent heavily to Queen Livia from 1062 against the Neck road tolls. Adriano Carrano, born in 1056, became head in 1080 and lent more. In September 1083 Livia's mint cut the Leontine to two parts silver in five. House Carrano failed with 400,000 marks of Tessarian debt. Its bench was broken in the Exchange square, its seat on the Twelve passed by vote to the shipping house of Ferrante, and Adriano spent 1084 and 1085 in the Debtors' Tower. He has lived on Sabena rents since, in the same black banker's cap. In 1099 he bought the Lunetti strong-room clerk, Fausto Renn, for less than a year's wage, and he knows what lies in the chests of lead bars. He has secretly given Mora Purplehand 300 suns and 200 cudgels for her march at the Purple Fair, and his gambling debtor Rico Ambro gave him the guard rota for the Lunetti vault in November 1104.
dead: Giacomo Carrano the Builder (794–864): Paid for the Exchange Hall; first First Banker. *Ruler:* Giacomo Carrano (the Builder), Ostra, 849–864 (RUL-2106).
Bernardo Carrano the Weigher (952–1029): First Banker 1001–1029; his weighers found the debased Leontine. *Ruler:* Bernardo Carrano (the Weigher), Ostra, 1001–1029 (RUL-2114).
Guido Carrano (980–1058): Lost the first seat to Isabetta Lunetti in 1047. *Ruler:* Guido Carrano, Ostra, 1029–1047 (RUL-2115).
marriages: 832, with House Aventi: Giacomo Carrano weds Livia Aventi.
FAM-212.secrets: Adriano Carrano pays the Lunetti strong-room clerk for copies of the papers beside the lead bars and secretly funds the Sabena Commons' June march.

FAM-213.y1105: Wine lords of the Isle of Vines and one of the Twelve since 758. Lord Enzo Sarto has never lost a vote and is quietly counting votes with Carrano in case Cosimo Lunetti falls.
FAM-213.arms: a purple grape cluster over a silver cup, on green
FAM-213.founder: Bartolo Sarto (690–751), a wine shipper who bought the first Calente vineyards on the Isle of Vines
FAM-213.power: The Isle of Vines, about 19,600 km², ruled from Calente; about 40,000 casks of wine a year; the Vintners of the Isle and the wine tax farm; a seat on the Twelve; untolled passage past Blackreef since 1090 in return for wine and grain.
FAM-213.branches: The lords of Calente on the Isle of Vines
FAM-213.history: Bartolo Sarto bought the first terraced vineyards above Calente on the Isle of Vines in 720 and shipped the wine to Solenne. His son Piero was one of the twelve who paid Lucan the Grey in 758 and swore the Charter of the Twelve, and the Sartos have sat on the council ever since. Piero Sarto was First of the Twelve from 772 to 787. On Sea Closing 796 his son Matteo's wine house sent the Ostran Letter, the oldest surviving bill of exchange, and Matteo held the first seat from 806 to 826. Tommaso Sarto was the last of the house to hold it, from 936 to 958. After him the Sartos stopped standing and started counting: since 979 they have voted with the winning side in every election of the Twelve. The Harbor Pox of 1076–1078 made land cheap, and Enzo Sarto, head of the house since 1075, doubled the vineyards. Since 1090 his ships have passed the Strait of Hael without paying the dragon toll, because the Coyle kin of Blackreef wave them through for Isle wine and grain each autumn. In 1091 Enzo voted against Cosimo Lunetti in the first count and for him in the second. In 1105 he wants to sell 3,000 casks to both Tessarian armies, and he is counting votes with Adriano Carrano, just in case.
dead: Piero Sarto the Vintner (724–787): One of the twelve of 758; First of the Twelve 772–787. *Ruler:* Piero Sarto (the Vintner), Ostra, 772–787 (RUL-2102).
Matteo Sarto the Letter-Writer (758–826): His house sent the Ostran Letter of 796. *Ruler:* Matteo Sarto (the Letter-Writer), Ostra, 806–826 (RUL-2104).
Tommaso Sarto (885–958): Last Sarto First Banker. *Ruler:* Tommaso Sarto, Ostra, 936–958 (RUL-2111).
marriages: 790, with House Aventi: Matteo Sarto weds an Aventi daughter; the two founding houses share the first seat for 60 years.
FAM-213.secrets: Since 1090 Sarto ships have passed the Strait without paying the dragon toll, by a private deal with the Coyle kin that cheats the Brotherhood's share-out.

FAM-214.y1105: Murex dyers raised to the Twelve in 1062. Master Oddo Pell heads the Murex Dyers' Guild, whose purple pays for half the city, and faces the Sabena Commons.
FAM-214.arms: a murex shell over three white waves, on purple
FAM-214.founder: Ubaldo Pell the Purplehand (880–944), dye-master of Felena
FAM-214.power: The murex beds and boiling vats of Felena and Miressa; the Murex Dyers' Guild of about 6,000 dyers and shell-gatherers; the purple cloth trade, which pays about half of Ostra's taxes through the purple tax; a seat on the Twelve.
FAM-214.branches: The dye-masters of Felena; The Miressa vat-houses
FAM-214.history: The murex beds of the Ostran Coast have made purple since Solen times, when only emperors and their priests could wear it. Ubaldo Pell was the dye-master of Felena who, in 910, bought the vats of three failing houses and set every boiling shed on the shore to one recipe. The Pells gave their name to the Murex Dyers' Guild and their hands to the vats: a Pell works the dye from the age of eight, and a Pell's hands are purple for life. The purple tax on dyed cloth grew into about half of Ostra's income, and the Twelve let only themselves and Temple envoys wear the color. In 1062 the shipping house of Fosco failed when the Neck road closed, and the Twelve gave its seat to Ubaldo's great-great-grandson, also named Ubaldo; the Lunetti wanted a vote they could count on, and the Pells owed them 30,000 suns. Oddo Pell, born at Felena in 1048, became head in 1079. In 1083 his guild paid its Sabena dyers in the dying Leontine while selling their cloth for Ostran suns, and that, more than the coin crash, started the Sabena riots. A dyer called Purplehand was hanged at the Sabena gate; his daughter Mora leads the Sabena Commons in 1105. Oddo helped pay for the Sabena Citadel. He votes with Cosimo Lunetti on everything but taxes and wants Gerolt Marr's crossbows ready for the Purple Fair.
dead: Ubaldo Pell the Purplehand (880–944): Joined the Felena dye sheds under one recipe and one guild.
Ubaldo Pell the Younger (1010–1079): Won the house its seat on the Twelve in 1062.
FAM-214.secrets: In 1083 the guild under Oddo Pell paid its dyers in debased Leontines and kept the difference, which started the Sabena riot.

FAM-215.y1105: Extinct since Vittorio Aventi died without sons in 936. Its bench, ships and Calora olive estates passed to House Lunetti through his daughter Camilla.
FAM-215.founder: Lucio Aventi (660–731), shipowner who led the rebuilding of Ostra's harbor mole after the earthquake of 697
FAM-215.power: None in 1105. In its time: the largest fleet of Ostra, the harbor mole, and five terms in the first seat.
FAM-215.branches: Its blood survives in the Aventi-Lunetti of Calora
FAM-215.history: When the earthquake of 9 February 697 threw down Ostra's harbor mole, the emperor sent 5,000 suns and nothing more. Lucio Aventi, the city's largest shipowner, and seven other houses paid to rebuild it and called themselves the Harbor Wardens. They were the first government Ostra made for itself. Lucio's grandson Aldo Aventi the Ransomer led the declaration of freedom on Sea Opening Day 758, paid the biggest share of the 80,000 silver suns given to Lucan the Grey and was chosen First of the Twelve. The Aventi held the first seat five times: Aldo (758–772), Bruno (787–806), Carlo (826–849), Ottavio (864–889) and Vittorio (919–936). They married with the Sartos and the Carranos, and when the Exchange Hall opened in 849 they took a bench and became bankers. The Black Cough of 916–925 killed both of Vittorio's sons. His daughter Camilla married Benedetto Lunetti in 931, and when Vittorio died in 936 the house ended and its fortune passed to the Lunetti. Ostra still calls the harbor mole the Aventi Wall, and the golden anchor still hangs over the first bench of the Exchange Hall, which the Lunetti keep.
dead: Lucio Aventi (660–731): Rebuilt the harbor mole after 697; first of the Harbor Wardens.
Aldo Aventi the Ransomer (709–772): Bought Ostra's freedom in 758; first First of the Twelve. *Ruler:* Aldo Aventi (the Ransomer), Ostra, 758–772 (RUL-2101).
Vittorio Aventi the Last (872–936): Last Aventi First Banker. *Ruler:* Vittorio Aventi (the Last Aventi), Ostra, 919–936 (RUL-2110).
Camilla Aventi (910–979): Heiress who brought the Aventi fortune to House Lunetti.
marriages: 790, with House Sarto: An Aventi daughter weds Matteo Sarto.
832, with House Carrano: Livia Aventi weds Giacomo Carrano.
931, with House Lunetti: Camilla Aventi weds Benedetto Lunetti.
FAM-215.secrets: The Aventi paid the largest share of the ransom of 758 with money borrowed from Lucerna, and the loan was never repaid.

FAM-701.y1105: Ruling house of Qadir. The Sultan is bedridden with stones, his brother the Grand Admiral wants war with Sabra, and the heir wants peace and hides his own stones.
FAM-701.arms: a white water jar on green, above three wavy blue bars
FAM-701.words: Half the water, all the road.
FAM-701.founder: Zahir the Thirstless, first Sultan of Qadir (760–815)
FAM-701.power: The crown gardens of Yasesh and the water rights of the Saman valley that turn the mills; the water-tax of a tenth; a tenth of the mill families' cash; 28,000 standing troops with the Guard of the Water Jar (1,200); 34 war galleys; the gold qadr mint. The treasury owes about 180,000 suns to the Water Endowment, about 200,000 to House Hassani and about 90,000 to the Gold Houses of Zanara.
FAM-701.branches: The Sultan's line: Zahir IV and Crown Prince Samir; The Admiral's line: Jalal Zahiri and his sons; The Cousins of Yasesh, from Sultan Rashad's younger son, who supply wives to the main line
FAM-701.history: House Zahiri is a branch of House Idrisi, the emirs of Qadir from 644 to 790. Its founder Zahir was born in 760, the son of Nadim, elder son of Emir Marwan Idrisi. Nadim died in 770 and Marwan in 771, and Zahir's uncle took the emirate from the 11-year-old boy as Kamil II. In 778 Kamil exiled him. Zahir spent 12 years at Tamar as a guest of the Tamaren kings, married Ahset, daughter of a royal scribe, in 783, and learned that his body was different: he could ride a day on the edge of the Burning Waste on half a water-skin. In January 790 he crossed the Burning Waste with 600 camel riders, bought a Rider guide's route with a sealed water-contract, and on Well Day took Qadira without a battle. The Well-Keepers named him Sultan and Guardian of the Water, and the house took his name. He paid for the blood too. He passed his first stone at 19 and died of kidney failure in the Dry Month of 815. His son Samir I made the house law of 815: the sultan names his heir from the sons of the house before the Keepers, and Zahiri daughters marry Zahiri cousins. From then each Zahiri son rides two days in the Sabun heat on half a water-skin at 15, and those who come back strong are 'of the Jar'. Of 14 sultans, 11 carried the blood, and most died in their fifties. The house built as well as ruled. Samir I finished the Great Cistern of Qadira (824). Idris I took the Bahesh mouth (848). Jalal I built the first fleet and drowned with six galleys in 874. Rashad, who did not carry the blood and lived to 59, chartered the paper mills about 880, the house's greatest gift to the realm. Idris II was the only sultan unmade by the Keepers: in 973 they declared his law selling believers into the galleys against the Book, and he gave the throne to his son rather than fight. Zahir II lost Sabra and the fleet in 1020–1025, the house's worst defeat. His son Jalal II rode out of the Sabun Pass ambush of 1022 on half a water-skin while his men died of thirst, a story the house tells with pride and the West March tells with bitterness. In 1105 the house has three men of note. Zahir IV lies sick and drinks only from a 'unicorn horn' cup bought from Emperor Mosi III, which is a whale's tooth. His brother Jalal leads the Bahesh Party. Crown Prince Samir, 23, was taught by Keeper Yusuf Alami and wants the sea lanes, not the Bahesh. Zahir IV's wife, Amina, is one of the Cousins of Yasesh, as the house law requires.
dead: Zahir the Thirstless (760–815): Crossed the Burning Waste and founded the sultanate; first carrier of the Thirstless blood. *Ruler:* Sultan Zahir the Thirstless (Zahir I), Sultanate of Qadir, 790–815 (RUL-7101).
Samir I the Cistern-Builder (784–838): Made the house law of 815 and the Great Cistern. *Ruler:* Samir Zahiri (Samir I the Cistern-Builder), Sultanate of Qadir, 815–838 (RUL-7102).
Rashad the Papermaker (853–912): Chartered the paper mills about 880. *Ruler:* Rashad Zahiri (the Papermaker), Sultanate of Qadir, 874–912 (RUL-7105).
Idris II the Gilded (921–978): Struck the first gold qadr; unmade by the Keepers in 973. *Ruler:* Idris Zahiri the Gilded (Idris II), Sultanate of Qadir, 951–973 (RUL-7108).
Zahir II the Fleetless (969–1031): Lost Sabra and the fleet. *Ruler:* Zahir Zahiri the Fleetless (Zahir II), Sultanate of Qadir, 996–1031 (RUL-7110).
Jalal II the Wall-Builder (993–1049): Survived the Sabun ambush of 1022; walled Mirad. *Ruler:* Jalal Zahiri the Wall-Builder (Jalal II), Sultanate of Qadir, 1031–1049 (RUL-7111).
marriages: 783, with a royal scribe family of Tamar: Zahir married Ahset, daughter of King Teti's chief scribe, in exile; mother of Samir I.
931, with House Hassani: Sultan Nizar married a Hassani shipowner's daughter; the first tie between the crown and the Miruma fleet.
1031, with House Qasimi: Jalal II married Samira Qasimi of the copper lords of Basim.
1080, with House Zahiri: Zahir IV married his cousin Amina of the Cousins of Yasesh, mother of Crown Prince Samir.
FAM-701.allies: House Hassani, House Warraqi, House Tarsi
FAM-701.secrets: The founder was guided across the Burning Waste by a Bahar Rider who sold him the route, not by the Giver, and Clan Bahar holds the sealed contract. Crown Prince Samir has hidden his stones since 1101, and the Sultan's unsent letter offering to recognize the Emir of Sabra lies in Omar the Patient's chest.

FAM-703.y1105: The first family of the Well-Keepers and the only living kin of the prophet Samar. Yusuf Alami is Keeper of the House of Water and head of the Water Endowment.
FAM-703.arms: a digger's spade crossed with a reed pen, black on sand-yellow
FAM-703.founder: Yahya son of Alam the Digger (about 544–606), who married Mira of the Wells in 568
FAM-703.power: Little land beyond the well-yards of Saman. Their power is office and name: the Keepership of the House of Water, held by an Alami for 212 of the last 500 years; the books of the Water Endowment, about 1 million suns in wells, inns and loans; four of the forty judges of the House of Water; and the right of the House to declare a sultan's order against the Book.
FAM-703.branches: The Keepers' line at the House of Water in Qadira; The Diggers of Saman, who still dig and clean the realm's deep wells and cisterns
FAM-703.history: House Alami descends from Samar the Water-Finder twice over. Its name comes from Samar's younger brother Alam the Digger (about 516–590), who dug the nine wells of the Well Road beside him in 566. In 568 Alam's son Yahya married Samar's daughter Mira of the Wells at the Well of Samar, and every Alami since descends from both brothers. Mira led the Wells from 581 and was the first Keeper of the House of Water from 604 until her death in 620; her grave by the House is still washed every Well Day. The family split early into two lines. The Diggers of Saman kept the family trade and still dig and clean the realm's deep wells, including the Great Cistern of Qadira. The Keepers' line entered the House of Water. An Alami, Zaki Alami (918–990), read the judgment against Sultan Idris II in 973 that made him give up the throne, and the family has been the sultans' conscience and their worry ever since. The family's words come from a saying of Samar that the Keepers dropped from the Book in 633: 'I did not make the water; I cleared the way.' The Alami kept it in their own teaching, and they know better than anyone that the Well was an old well cleared. Yusuf Alami was born in 1036 at Saman into the Diggers' line; his father was the first of that line to become a judge. Yusuf became Keeper in 1084 and read the House's sealed copy of the contract of Zahir that year. Since 1090 he has paid Clan Bahar from the Endowment to keep it hidden, and in 1105 he means to use the House's oldest power and declare the admiral's war against the Book.
dead: Samar the Water-Finder (512–581): Prophet of the Path of the Well; ancestor through Mira. *Ruler:* Samar the Water-Finder, The First Wells, 541–581 (RUL-7061).
Alam the Digger (about 516–590): Samar's brother; dug the nine wells of the Well Road.
Mira of the Wells (545–620): Led the Wells; first Keeper of the House of Water. *Ruler:* Mira of the Wells, The First Wells, 581–604 (RUL-7062).
Zaki Alami (918–990): Keeper who unmade Idris II's galley law in 973.
marriages: 568, with the line of Samar: Yahya son of Alam married Mira, Samar's daughter.
652, with House Idrisi: An Alami daughter married Ghalib Idrisi, heir of the emirate.
1062, with House Warraqi: Yusuf's sister married into the Warraqi mill family.
FAM-703.secrets: Yusuf pays Clan Bahar 2,000 suns a year from the Endowment, booked as well repairs on the pilgrim road, to keep the contract of Zahir hidden. The family has always taught the saying dropped in 633, and it knows the Well of Samar was an older well cleared.

FAM-704.y1105: Qadir's richest shipowners, with 40 merchant ships. Nadira Hassani is Keeper of the Purse, has lent the crown about 200,000 suns for the fleet, and leads the Sea Traders against the war.
FAM-704.arms: a white lateen sail on sea blue
FAM-704.power: 40 merchant ships; the Hassani yard at Miruma; the Lucerna counting-house; loans to the crown of about 200,000 suns, including the rowers' pay.
FAM-704.branches: The Miruma house, which owns the ships; The Lucerna counting-house, which sells paper, dates and copper in the north
FAM-704.history: Hassan the Boatwright built fishing boats at Miruma and bought his first three cargo ships in 902 with paper money from the mills: he carried Qadiri paper to Lucerna, where no one else could sell it. His sons carried dates, copper and paper north and Tamari wheat and Holy Coast timber home. In 931 a Hassani daughter married Sultan Nizar, and the house has lent to the crown ever since. The war of 1020–1025 nearly broke it: five Hassani ships hired as transports burned with the galleys at Sabra in 1024, and the house learned to fear the war party. Nadira's father Ziyad Hassani died of the Harbor Pox at Lucerna in 1077. Her uncle ran the house until she married Tamim, a Miruma captain who took the Hassani name, in 1080. When Tamim drowned off the Holy Coast in 1095, Nadira took the house herself, as Qadiri widows may. Zahir IV made her Keeper of the Purse in 1097. She lends the crown the money for the fleet because she would rather hold its debt than face its admiral, and she plans to hold back the rowers' March pay until the Divan votes the war down. Since 1100 two Hassani ships have also carried Sabran pearls to Lucerna under false Qadiri papers, bought from Jamila Sabrani's agents.
dead: Hassan the Boatwright (about 870–944): Founder; first to sell Qadiri paper in Lucerna.
Ziyad Hassani (1030–1077): Nadira's father; died of the Harbor Pox at Lucerna.
Tamim Hassani (1055–1095): Nadira's husband, a captain who took the Hassani name; drowned off the Holy Coast.
marriages: 931, with House Zahiri: A Hassani daughter married Sultan Nizar.
1080, with a captain's family of Miruma: Nadira married Tamim, who took the Hassani name.
FAM-704.allies: House Warraqi, House Alami, House Qasimi
FAM-704.secrets: Two Hassani ships carry Sabran pearls from Azara to Lucerna under false Qadiri papers, which is trade with the rebel emirate Nadira's own treasury is arming against.

FAM-705.y1105: Wardens of the West March since 1025. Emir Bashir signs as Emir of Basir, owes the Water Endowment 25,000 suns and presses for war; his son Nabil holds the Sabun Pass.
FAM-705.arms: a black tower above a green date palm on white
FAM-705.founder: Ghazi Tarsi, captain of Sultan Idris I (812–869)
FAM-705.power: The walled town of Mirad and about 40 West March villages; about 4,000 levy men; the Wardens of the Sabun (1,600) under Nabil; a debt of 25,000 suns to the Water Endowment against Basir fields the house does not hold.
FAM-705.branches: The Mirad line (Bashir and Nabil); The Wardens' Yard, where younger Tarsi sons train as pass fighters
FAM-705.history: Ghazi Tarsi led Sultan Idris I's soldiers when they took the Bahesh mouth in 848, and Idris gave him the irrigated Basir fields on the lower Bahesh. For 177 years the Tarsi were the richest date lords of the realm and signed as Emirs of Basir. They lost everything in the war of 1020–1025. In 1022 their riders were in the column ambushed in the Sabun Pass. In 1024 House Hazimi, their neighbors in the Sabran uplands, changed sides and let Sabran riders through to Basir, and Emir Anas Tarsi's eldest son died defending the date gardens. In 1025 Anas led about 3,000 people east to Mirad. His son Fadil Tarsi walled Mirad with Jalal II's silver in 1032–1036 and made his own son Bashir swear at 12, in 1060, never to sign any title but Emir of Basir. Bashir has led the West March since Fadil died in 1071, and his son Nabil has held the Sabun Pass since 1096. The house has gambled its future on the war. Bashir spent a secret Endowment loan of 25,000 suns (1102) on walls and on gifts to the Bahesh Party, and Nabil takes one mule-load in ten from the Qasimi copper trains going to Sabra.
dead: Ghazi Tarsi (812–869): Took the Bahesh mouth for Idris I; first Emir of Basir.
Anas Tarsi (975–1041): Lost Basir in 1025 and led the house to Mirad.
Fadil Tarsi (1010–1071): Walled Mirad and bound his son to the Basir oath.
marriages: 1045, with a Mirad date family: Fadil Tarsi married within the West March; the house has made no great match since 1025.
FAM-705.rivals: House Qasimi, House Hazimi, House Sabrani
FAM-705.secrets: Bashir's 1102 loan from the Endowment is pledged against Basir fields Sabra holds; the Keeper who lent it is the man trying to stop the war. Nabil's tenth of the Qasimi copper trains is unreported to the Divan.

FAM-706.y1105: Copper, lead and olive lords of the Basim Hills. Emir Idris votes for peace in the Divan and sells copper to Sabra over the Sabun Pass.
FAM-706.arms: a copper-red hammer on olive green
FAM-706.founder: Qasim of Basim, copper-master, made Emir of Basim by Samir I (about 790–850)
FAM-706.power: Five Sunwall mines (copper at Basan, Ashaya and Rashin; lead at Basifa and Zarin), the olive terraces of the Basim Hills, a train of about 400 mules and about 3,000 levy men.
FAM-706.branches: The Basim line; The mine-captains of Rashin and Basan, cousins who run the pits
FAM-706.history: Qasim was a copper-master of the Basim hills who reopened the old Solen lead-silver pits after the emirate had let them flood. In 821 Sultan Samir I made him Emir of Basim in return for a share of the metal. The house has lived on copper ever since: Qadiri copper pans boil sugar in Tamar and dye in Lucerna, and Qadiri lead roofs the House of Water. The hills around Basim are where Prince Idris lost to the Solen in 253, and the Qasimi keep the old battlefield as a grazing common. In 1031 Samira Qasimi married Sultan Jalal II, and the house has been part of the royal kin ever since. Idris Qasimi, the only son of an Emir who opened three new mines, took the house in 1084. When the Sultan's copper price fell in 1088 he began selling to Sabran brokers over the Sabun Pass. Since 1101 he has paid Nabil Tarsi one load in ten to let the trains cross, and since 1102 his mule drivers have carried sealed letters for a Sabran broker without asking what was in them. The letters are the Sultan's nurse's reports to the Emir of Sabra, and the copper becomes the boiling pans of the oil sheds at Zariya.
dead: Qasim of Basim (about 790–850): Reopened the Solen pits; first Emir of Basim.
Samira Qasimi (1012–1060): Wife of Sultan Jalal II; grandmother of Zahir III.
marriages: 1031, with House Zahiri: Samira Qasimi married Sultan Jalal II.
FAM-706.secrets: Qasimi copper becomes the boiling pans of Sabra's fire-oil sheds, and Qasimi mule trains carry the nurse Dalia Sharif's reports on the Sultan to the Emir of Sabra.

FAM-707.y1105: First of the 32 mill families of Qadira. Hamid the Papermaker is Master of the Mills and speaks for the guild in the Divan; two Warraqi journeymen, his grandnephews, vanished in September 1104.
FAM-707.arms: a white sheet over a blue mill wheel
FAM-707.founder: Latif Warraqi, the fuller of Saman who made the first rag paper (848–911)
FAM-707.power: Four paper mills on the Saman streams; the mastership of the Guild of the Mills, whose families pay a tenth of the Sultan's cash income; the watermark molds for the Sultan's gift paper.
FAM-707.branches: The Saman mill line, which owns four of the 32 mills; The Qadira line, which sells ink and paper by the harbor
FAM-707.history: Latif Warraqi was a fuller in the Saman valley whose mill beat wool cloth with water-driven hammers. The Well-Keepers wanted a writing sheet cheaper than Tamari papyrus, and about 880, after three years of trying, Latif beat old linen into pulp, lifted it on a wire screen and dried the first rag paper. Sultan Rashad gave the Warraqi and their neighbors a mill charter, and the mill families swore never to teach the craft to outsiders; a worker who takes it abroad is outlawed and his family fined 500 silver qadr. The Warraqi gave the guild its first masters and still hold four mills. Like the other mill families they marry cousins to keep the craft inside, and they wear the small brass stamp of a master on a cord. Hamid was stirring pulp at 9, became master of his family's mill in 1078 and Master of the Mills in 1090. He brought the mill families into the Sea Traders, because war closes the sea lanes that carry paper north, and in 1100 he began selling straight to the Temple scriptoria through Ostra. In 1096 his nephew Yasin vanished; the family was told he had fled abroad. In August 1104 Hamid refused Yasin's sons Adil and Hakim their master's stamps to keep his own son ahead of them, and in September they left Qadira hidden in rag bales.
dead: Latif Warraqi (848–911): Made the first rag paper about 880.
Yasin Warraqi (1060–1096): Journeyman who 'fled abroad' in 1096; father of the two missing journeymen.
marriages: 1062, with House Alami: Hamid's brother married the sister of Yusuf Alami.
FAM-707.secrets: Yasin Warraqi did not flee in 1096: the Master of Doors had him drowned off Miruma for trying to sell mill drawings to a Lucernan. His sons, the missing journeymen, are hidden at Janiya and bound for Marira and a Ranpuri buyer.

FAM-731.y1105: Royal house of Tamar. The king's crown rests on the re-cut flood mark of 1089; the house has one heir, aged 8, who hides a weak eye.
FAM-731.arms: a gold sun-boat on blue-green above a black band of river silt
FAM-731.power: The crown's farmland, about a third of the valley beside the temple's third; the royal granaries (claimed four months' bread, truly three); a month of dyke work from every man; 44,000 standing troops, 16 river galleys and about 300 barges; tolls on the spice barges. But the flood-priests set the grain tax, and the crown owes Lucerna's grain factors about 300,000 suns.
FAM-731.branches: The king's line (Amenhar V and Crown Prince Khaset); Princess Tiye's line (Tiye and Queen Nefret); The exiled princes of Talim, ended 966 except through Neferu
FAM-731.history: House Tamaren was founded by Nefira of the Delta, daughter of the Sethepi lord of Marira, who was crowned at the Flood Stairs on 15 August 640 and took the name Tamaren, 'of Tamar'. She was the first of the house with the fever-proof blood: she walked the delta marshes unharmed while fever killed her brothers, and her delta men beat the Solen landing at Marira in 642 while fever killed a third of the invaders. She had eleven children and outlived four. Her daughter Meret married Emperor Theodoric I in 664 and bore Emperor Justin V; Meret had nearly died of fever as a girl, and the blood did not pass to the Solen emperors. Nefira's son Kheti I followed her in 688. From his time the house married cousins to keep the temple lands and the blood together, and the blood sickness followed: Kheti II's two sons died of it, and his daughter Wenet reigned and made the law of the eldest healthy son in 740. Teti the Canal-Digger dug the canal of Akayn and sheltered the Qadiri exile Zahir; his son Wenis paid for Zahir's crossing in 790. For two centuries the house ruled a rich and quiet valley. It fell in 942, when Tessaria took Tamar and sent Kheti III and 30 kin to Talim as temple wards. Kheti died there in 958, his elder son of fever in 961, and his younger son Khaset was beheaded by the Exarch in 966; Khaset's daughter Neferu was born a month later, the last of Nefira's blood. In 981 the Talim priests of House Senmut proclaimed Amenhar, a Senmut priest's son, as Kheti's grandson. In 989 they married him to Neferu and made the law that only a king's son by a Tamaren wife may reign. Every king since descends from Neferu and carries Nefira's blood through her. The Amenhars married cousins again. Amenhar III fathered Amenhar IV and Princess Tiye; Amenhar IV's son, Amenhar V, married Tiye's daughter Nefret in 1088. Both carry the blood, and their first son died of the blood sickness in 1101 at 11. In 1105 the house has four living members of note: the king, who knows his crown rests on the re-cut mark of 1089; Queen Nefret, who suspects it; Tiye, Overseer of the Granaries, who sold a month's grain in secret in 1103 to pay the Lucernan interest; and Crown Prince Khaset, 8, who hides a weak eye since a fall in October 1104.
dead: Queen Nefira of the Delta (612–688): Founder; first carrier of the fever-proof blood. *Ruler:* Queen Nefira of the Delta, Kingdom of Tamar, 640–688 (RUL-7021).
Meret Tamaren (641–699): Nefira's daughter; wife of Emperor Theodoric I and mother of Emperor Justin V.
Queen Wenet the Steady (685–748): Made the law of the eldest healthy son. *Ruler:* Wenet Tamaren (Queen Wenet the Steady), Kingdom of Tamar, 719–748 (RUL-7024).
Kheti III the Exile (896–958): Lost Tamar to Tessaria and died a temple ward at Talim. *Ruler:* Kheti Tamaren the Exile (Kheti III), Kingdom of Tamar, 921–942 (RUL-7033).
Queen Neferu the Last Daughter (966–1031): Last of Nefira's blood; wife of Amenhar I.
Amenhar I the Freer (950–1017): Freed Tamar; by blood a son of House Senmut. *Ruler:* Amenhar I the Freer, Kingdom of Tamar, 989–1017 (RUL-7034).
marriages: 664, with the Solen imperial house: Meret married Emperor Theodoric I by the Treaty of the Flood Stairs.
989, with House Senmut: Neferu married Amenhar I, whom the priests called her cousin; by SEC-49 he was a son of House Senmut.
1088, with House Tamaren: Crown Prince Amenhar married his cousin Nefret, Tiye's daughter.
FAM-731.allies: The Measurers of the Stair, House Kadari
FAM-731.secrets: The flood mark of 1089 was re-cut to save the king. The founder of the present line was a Senmut priest's son, and the house's claim to Nefira's blood rests on Queen Neferu. Crown Prince Khaset cannot see well from his left eye.

FAM-733.y1105: Chief Flood-Priests of Talim and rivals of the Tamar temple. Djedi Senmut keeps the true birth roll of Amenhar I and the sealed Kadah order, and his niece nurses the Crown Prince.
FAM-733.arms: a white ibis standing on a black stair, on blue-green
FAM-733.founder: Senmut the Reader, first Chief Flood-Priest of Talim of the house (about 770–840)
FAM-733.power: The Flood Temple and temple fort of Talim near the Neck border, with its own river stair and about 800 temple guards; Talim's temple estates in the Upper Nome; the vault holding the true birth roll of Amenhar I and the Kadah order.
FAM-733.branches: The chief priests' line at Talim (Djedi); Djedi's younger brother's line (Tuya)
FAM-733.history: House Senmut has served the Flood Temple of Talim, the upper valley's temple fort near the Neck border, since its founder Senmut the Reader became Chief Flood-Priest there about 800. Talim reads its own river stair, and the Senmut have always said their reading is as true as Tamar's. In 942 the Tessarians sent Kheti III and 30 royal kin to Talim as temple wards. The Senmut kept them alive, hid the royal records and watched the male line die: Kheti in 958, his sons in 961 and 966. Only a girl, Neferu, was left, and they raised her as a priest's foundling. In 981 the house made a king. Its chief priest proclaimed Amenhar, 31, son of the flood-priest Ipi Senmut, as Kheti III's grandson, forged his birth roll and raised Talim against its garrison. The true roll lies in a sealed jar in the Talim vault and passes from each chief priest to the next. After the massacre of 985 the house also took charge of the captured Kadah order sealed by Emperor Nikandros. For a generation after 989 the Senmut were the king's priests, and their blood sat on the throne. But the stair-measurers of the Tamar temple won back the High Flood-Priesthood by about 1030, and the two temples have been rivals since. Djedi Senmut's father showed him the birth roll and the Kadah order in 1070. Djedi became Chief Flood-Priest in 1084 and read the third low flood of 1089 on Talim's own stair; he has never believed the Tamar mark. His niece Tuya has nursed Crown Prince Khaset since 1101 and reports to him weekly. In December 1104 the dying mason Ahmose asked for a Talim priest, and the house may soon hold proof against the king as well as against his ancestor.
dead: Senmut the Reader (about 770–840): Founder; first Chief Flood-Priest of Talim of the house.
Ipi Senmut (922–987): Talim flood-priest; true father of Amenhar I.
marriages: 989, with House Tamaren: Ipi Senmut's son, crowned Amenhar I, married Neferu Tamaren.
FAM-733.rivals: The Measurers of the Stair, House Tamaren
FAM-733.secrets: The royal house began with a Senmut priest's son, and the Talim vault holds the Kadah order. Tuya knows the Crown Prince's eye is weak.

FAM-734.y1105: The stair-reading family of the Flood Temple at Tamar. Menna the Measurer is High Flood-Priest, sets the realm's grain tax, and re-cut the flood mark in 1089.
FAM-734.arms: a black measuring rod on gold, crossed by a blue wavy line
FAM-734.founder: Hekaib, High Flood-Priest of Tamar, who opened the river gate to the Solen (about 160–231)
FAM-734.power: The High Flood-Priesthood; the reading of the Flood Stairs, which sets every year's grain tax; the temple estates of a third of the valley; the temple watch; the archive under the Stairs with the bronze plate of 210.
FAM-734.branches: The readers of the Stairs; The keepers of the tax rolls and the library under the Stairs
FAM-734.history: The Measurers are the family of stair-readers of the Flood Temple at Tamar, and they hold its oldest secret. They descend from Hekaib, the High Flood-Priest who in April 210 opened Tamar's river gate to the Solen in return for a promise that the temple lands would never be touched. A bronze plate of the pact, sealed by Aldric II and Hekaib, lies in the archive under the Flood Stairs, and each head of the family is shown it. The family has read the Stairs, trained the stair-masons and kept the tax rolls ever since, and it has held the High Flood-Priesthood more often than any other. Under the Tessarians it obeyed: in 943 it handed the tax rolls to the Exarch's clerks, which the Senmut of Talim never forgave. After 989 the Senmut had the king's ear, but the Measurers' skill at the Stairs won the High Flood-Priesthood back by about 1030. Menna, born in 1038 into the family, read his first flood at 20 and became High Flood-Priest in 1079. In 1089 he had the true mark of the third low flood plastered over and a new one cut, saving the king and the temple's power together. In December 1104 he ordered the 1089 tax roll burned and sent his watch captain to Talim to see that the dying mason Ahmose speaks to no one.
dead: Hekaib (about 160–231): Opened the river gate to the Solen in 210 for the temple's lands.
marriages: 1060, with a scribe family of Tamar: The Measurers marry among temple scribes; Menna's mother was a royal scribe's daughter.
FAM-734.secrets: The bronze plate of 210 and the re-cut mark of 1089: the family has sold one king and saved another.

FAM-735.y1105: Lords of the Kadah nome and the realm's soldiers. Rahotep Kadari is General of the River and has secretly offered Prince Andros galleys for blood-price for Kadah.
FAM-735.arms: a red spear over a burning tower, on black
FAM-735.founder: Senbi Kadari, made lord of the Kadah nome by Kheti I (about 630–700)
FAM-735.power: The Kadah nome's rift-shoulder fields and pastures; the rebuilt Kadah Wall; about 6,000 levy men; the generalship of the River, with command of the 44,000 standing troops, 16 river galleys and the Crocodile Boats.
FAM-735.branches: The lords of Kadah; Kadari captains of the river fleet
FAM-735.history: House Kadari has held land at Kadah on the rift shoulder since the Solen held the town. When Emperor Theodoric gave Kadah back to Tamar in 664, King Kheti I made Senbi Kadari lord of the Kadah nome in 670, and the house has led the realm's soldiers since. Kadari captains led the 2,000 Tamari archers who broke Maximus's line at Felano in 667. In 942 the house fought Cassian Reed and lost its lands; in 981 it rose with Talim. In April 985 Tessarian hired soldiers burned Kadah and killed about 2,000 townsfolk on Emperor Nikandros's sealed order. The head of the house, Iuny Kadari, died in the fire, and his five-year-old son Wenamun was carried out of it. Amenhar I gave the nome back to the house in 989 and paid for the new Kadah Wall. Wenamun lived to 92, married three times and fathered Rahotep at 72; he raised him on the story of the fire and died in 1072 still asking for blood-price. Rahotep fought on the Neck border from 1070, became head of the house in 1072 and General of the River in 1086. In the Hungry Year of 1088 he broke dykes to flood out grain thieves and held the valley together. He wants the Kadah order out of the Talim vault, and in December 1104 he offered Prince Andros ten river galleys and a copy of the order in return for blood-price when Andros takes Tessar.
dead: Senbi Kadari (about 630–700): Founder; first lord of the Kadah nome.
Iuny Kadari (932–985): Head of the house; died in the burning of Kadah.
Wenamun Kadari (980–1072): Carried out of the fire at five; Rahotep's father.
marriages: 1051, with a boatman family of Kadah: Wenamun's third wife, Rahotep's mother, was a river captain's daughter.
FAM-735.secrets: Rahotep's letter of December 1104 to Prince Andros, carried by Nakht the Oar; his spy Henut Ankhesi at Queen Livia's court has a Tessarian husband he knows nothing of.

FAM-736.y1105: Grain and rag brokers of Marira and the first family of the Delta Wells. Yunus Marari is Harbor-Master and leads the Delta Wells' claim to temple land and office.
FAM-736.arms: a white well-mouth above a sheaf of wheat, on green
FAM-736.founder: Marar the Factor, grain broker of Marira (about 870–940)
FAM-736.power: Warehouses and grain barges at Marira; the Harbor-Mastership of Marira; brokerage between the Lucernan factors and Tamari growers and between Tamari weavers and Qadiri rag-buyers; the trust of the delta's believers, about a sixth of the delta.
FAM-736.branches: The Marira brokers; The Qadira counting-house, which sells rags to the mills
FAM-736.history: House Marari are grain and rag brokers of Marira and the first family of the Delta Wells. Their founder Marar the Factor took the Path of the Well from Qadiri merchants about 905, in the first years of the Well missions to the delta. The family grew rich between two faiths. It sells Tamari wheat to the Lucernan factors who hold first right to it under the contract of 645, and Tamari linen rags to the Qadiri mills. Delta Wells believers may hold royal office but never temple office, and the Marari have pushed at that line for a century. Yunus Marari, born in 1054, became Harbor-Master of Marira in 1085, the highest believer in royal service, and has led the Delta Wells since 1090. In the Hungry Year of 1088 the flood-priests said the Mother was angry at the Delta Wells, and a mob burned two Marari warehouses. In 1091 Yunus sealed the Rag Compact with Rasha the Ragwoman and Nofret the Weaver. He kept his own harbor tallies of the 1089 harvest, which show it was a third short of a fair year, and he has begun to suspect the flood mark. He means to petition the king on 1 March 1105 for the right of believers to hold temple land, while the preacher Faruq the Lamp plans a march the same day.
dead: Marar the Factor (about 870–940): Founder; one of the first Delta Wells.
marriages: 1078, with a Well merchant family of Qadira: Yunus married the daughter of a Qadiri paper trader, which opened the rag trade.
FAM-736.secrets: Yunus's harbor tallies prove the 1089 harvest was a third short; with Merit's hidden tax roll they could prove the mark was false.

FAM-721.y1105: The chief's line of Clan Bahar and the Speakers of the Sand Clans since 1001. It holds the Speakership, the salt-fee chests, the Well-Mother's register, the Noon Lances, the oldest Book of Wells and the contract of Zahir.
FAM-721.arms: a white oryx on rust red
FAM-721.founder: Ghanim Bahar, who swore the Riders' Oath beside Hazir (about 540–612)
FAM-721.power: The Speakership; the salt-fee chests of Zarak, which keep a fifth of every fee paid at Mirah; the Well-Mother's knotted register; the Noon Lances (1,600); the oldest copy of the Book of Wells; the sealed contract of Zahir and 2,000 suns a year from Qadir for keeping it quiet; about 110,000 clan herders who follow the chief.
FAM-721.branches: The House of Rashid: the sand-eyed Speakers' line (Tariq, Mansur); The Well-Mother's line (Salma and her son Hamza); Cousin lines of the older chiefs, without the sand-eyes
FAM-721.history: Clan Bahar was one of the eleven clans that swore the Riders' Oath to Hazir on 1 September 581, and this family is its chief's line. Its founder Ghanim Bahar rode with Hazir to the Sabun Pass in 593. In 645 the family walled the salt wells of Zarak into a market and took a fee on every camel-load; Zarak made it rich, and Salih Bahar became the first Bahar Speaker in 651. About 690 the Riders gave the family their copy of the Book of Wells to keep, the copy that still holds the saying 'I did not make the water; I cleared the way'. In January 790 the chief Hamdan Bahar sold the exiled Qadiri prince Zahir the Burning Waste route and three hidden cisterns, and took from him a water-contract sealed with Zahir's ring. He told the council only that Qadir had sworn to keep its soldiers from the Well. Imad Bahar, Speaker 846–866, set the council's fifth of the salt fee. The family changed with Rashid, born in 960, the first with the sand-eyes. He won the feud with Clan Talun on the plain of Sarad in 1000 with the first noon charge and was acclaimed Speaker in 1001. His wife Layla the Knotter was Well-Mother, and the register has stayed in Bahar tents since. Four Bahar have been Speaker in a row: Rashid (1001–1030), his son Yazid (1030–1052), Yazid's son Malik (1052–1087) and Malik's nephew Tariq (since 1087). Malik led the Salt War; his brother Bakr was killed on the Hazir River in 1062 on a moonless night he could not see through. Malik's sister Salma became Well-Mother in 1070, and her son Hamza is Salt-Master. Tariq, Bakr's son, won the Speakership in 1087 on a promise to the south that he has not kept. In 1088 he opened the contract chest, and since 1090 Qadir's Keeper has paid him to keep it closed. The family holds too much, and every member knows it. Hamza skims the gold with a second tally cord, Salma hides a new well from the other clans, and Mansur, Tariq's son by his Hazari wife, has sold a third of the salt fee to the south in secret to win the next acclaim.
dead: Hamdan Bahar (about 745–812): Chief who sold Zahir the Burning Waste route in 790 and kept the contract.
Rashid Bahar the Far-Seer (960–1030): First carrier of the sand-eyes; Speaker from 1001. *Ruler:* Rashid Bahar the Far-Seer (Speaker), Confederacy of the Sand Clans, 1001–1030 (RUL-7222).
Layla the Knotter (966–1049): Rashid's wife and Well-Mother; taught the register to her granddaughter Salma.
Malik Bahar (1022–1087): Speaker through the Salt War. *Ruler:* Malik Bahar (Speaker), Confederacy of the Sand Clans, 1052–1087 (RUL-7224).
Bakr Bahar (1026–1062): Tariq's father; killed on the Hazir River on a moonless night.
marriages: 734, with Clan Hazari: A Bahar chief's son married a Hazari daughter at the peace that ended the three empty years.
1070, with Clan Hazari: Tariq married Nour Hazari, a cousin of Umar Hazari; mother of Mansur.
FAM-721.secrets: The family holds the sealed contract of Zahir and takes 2,000 suns a year from Qadir's Endowment to keep it hidden. Hamza keeps a second tally cord; Salma has hidden the Red Hollow well; Mansur has promised Harith Sayf a third of the salt fee behind his father's back.

FAM-722.y1105: Heirs of Hazir the Rider and hereditary guards of the Well of Samar. Umar Hazari leads Hazir's Heirs and wants Qadiri Well-Keepers out of the desert; his cousin Jabir is the finest camel lancer of the clans.
FAM-722.arms: a black ring with a lance across it, on white
FAM-722.founder: Hazir the Rider, first leader of the Riders (530–603)
FAM-722.power: Guardianship of the Well of Samar and its cisterns for 5,000 pilgrims; the Riders of the Well (1,000 camel lancers); the water fee at the pilgrim-road cisterns; the School of the Long Ride; the honor of Hazir's blood, which no Rider will insult.
FAM-722.branches: The chief's line at the Well (Umar); The School line at Zarak (Jabir)
FAM-722.history: Clan Hazari is Hazir the Rider's own clan, and this is his line. Hazir led it and ten other clans out of the towns' faith in 581, rode to the Sabun Pass in 593 and died in the siege camp before Qadira in 603. His son Nabhan was the second Speaker (603–629) and made the clan the hereditary guards of the Well and its cisterns. Three later Hazari were Speakers: Habib (734–755), who ended the three empty years; Khalil (829–846), who rebuilt the Well-court cisterns for 5,000 pilgrims; and Shakir (941–962), the last. Hazir's saddle and lance hang in the Well-court and are carried round the Well each Well Day. The family has kept the Riders' way purer than any other: no Well-Keeper courts, no fee for a drink at the Well itself, and no Qadiri judge in the desert. Umar Hazari, born at the Well in 1051, rode the pilgrim road at 12, heard Hazir the Blind recite at Zarak in 1063, became chief in 1082 and backed Tariq Bahar in 1087. His cousin Jabir, born at the Well in 1047, has been master of the School of the Long Ride since 1085; in 1101, after a bad year for his herds, he taught the Desert Night March to two Zanaran riders for 200 gold weights. Since the summer of 1104 Umar's eldest son has preached that the Well-Finder is coming back, and since November Umar has let the prophets of the Last Well camp at the Well's cisterns.
dead: Hazir the Rider (530–603): Led the Riders from 581; won the Sabun Pass in 593. *Ruler:* Hazir the Rider (First Rider), Confederacy of the Sand Clans, 581–603 (RUL-7201).
Nabhan Hazari (565–629): Second Speaker; made the clan guards of the Well. *Ruler:* Nabhan Hazari (Speaker), Confederacy of the Sand Clans, 603–629 (RUL-7202).
Habib Hazari (690–755): Speaker who ended the three empty years (734). *Ruler:* Habib Hazari (Speaker), Confederacy of the Sand Clans, 734–755 (RUL-7208).
marriages: 734, with Clan Bahar: A Hazari daughter married into the Bahar chief's line.
1070, with Clan Bahar: Nour Hazari married Tariq Bahar.
FAM-722.secrets: Umar lets the prophets of the Last Well camp at the Well, and his own son preaches among them. Jabir sold a sworn fighting secret of the School to Zanara in 1101.

FAM-723.y1105: Chief's line of the largest southern clan and holders of Mirah and its Zanaran market. Harith Sayf leads the Southern Clans and threatens to close the Salt Road; he secretly pays the outlaw Zayd Blackveil, born of his own line.
FAM-723.arms: a curved sword over a red hill, on sand
FAM-723.founder: Sayf the Hill-Rider, who brought the southern hill herders into the Riders (about 572–640)
FAM-723.power: The walled hill town of Mirah (22,400 people) and its Zanaran market; the last wells of the Salt Road before the Golden Plains; about 95,000 clan herders and the lead of the seven Southern Clans; debts of about 40,000 suns shared with the south.
FAM-723.branches: The chief's line at Mirah (Harith); The line of Harith's great-uncle, from which Zayd Blackveil was born and cast out
FAM-723.history: Sayf the Hill-Rider brought the herders of the Southern Hills into the Riders about 600, and his line has led Clan Sayf ever since. The family gave the council two Speakers: Bishr Sayf (690–712), the first southern Speaker, and Fahd Sayf (880–903), who took the hill town of Mirah about 885 from headmen who paid tribute to the Kingdom of the Tedana and made it the clan's winter seat. The Sayf are the one clan that lives behind walls all winter. In April 1060 Muhsin Sayf held Mirah against 18,000 Zanarans for five months, and his son Harith was born in the town during the siege. After 1063 the Zanaran market at Mirah made the family rich, but the salt gold passed through Mirah on its way to Zarak. Harith rode in the southern levy at 16, became chief in 1084 and gave his clan's acclaim to Tariq Bahar in 1087 for a promise that was never paid in full. The family also bred Zayd, born at Mirah in 1072, whose grandfather was the younger brother of Harith's grandfather. Zayd was a camel thief of renown by 16. In 1098 he killed his cousin's killer at the well of Marir, within sight of the water, and Harith sent him into the desert without water to keep Clan Marir in the southern bloc. Since autumn 1104 Harith has paid Zayd 50 gold weights a month to burn Zanara's east-road camps.
dead: Sayf the Hill-Rider (about 572–640): Founder; brought the southern herders into the Riders.
Fahd Sayf (840–903): Speaker; took Mirah about 885. *Ruler:* Fahd Sayf (Speaker), Confederacy of the Sand Clans, 880–903 (RUL-7216).
Muhsin Sayf (1025–1084): Held Mirah against Zanara in 1060; Harith's father.
marriages: 1082, with Clan Birayn: Harith married a Birayn chief's daughter to bind the cattle clan below Mirah to the Sayf.
FAM-723.secrets: Harith pays Zayd Blackveil, whom he exiled, to raid Zanara's east road; Clan Marir would leave the southern bloc if it knew. Mansur Bahar has promised Harith a third of the salt fee.

FAM-724.y1105: Chief's line of the coast clan of Yasira and Janiya, the clans' only sailors and smugglers. Rami Yasiri hides the two runaway paper journeymen of Qadira under water law.
FAM-724.words: The sea gives water to no one; we do.
FAM-724.founder: Munqidh the Netmaker, chief of the Sunwall coast fishers (about 668–735)
FAM-724.power: The harbors of Yasira and Janiya; about 40 fishing and coasting boats; the smuggling trade in paper, dates, salt and people past Qadir's customs; paid friendships with the pilots of Miruma.
FAM-724.branches: The Yasira line (the chief); The Janiya boatbuilders
FAM-724.history: The fishers of the Sunwall coast east of Qadir lived beyond Qadir's reach and beyond the Riders' notice until about 700, when their chief Munqidh the Netmaker took the Riders' Oath and brought them into the council. The Yasiri have smuggled ever since: dates and paper out of Qadir without the duty of one part in ten, salt shavings from the cutters, and in bad years people. In 1020–1025 Yasiri boats carried Sabran messages along the coast, and Qadir has watched the clan since. Rami Yasiri, born at Yasira in 1064, is the son of a chief who ran paper and dates past Qadir's customs. He took his first smuggling boat out at 14 and became chief in 1095, and since then he has grown the clan's boats from 25 to 40. Since 1101 he has paid the pilots of Miruma to keep their harbor lamps dark on certain nights. In October 1104 the smuggler Kamal the Eel brought two frightened young men to Janiya, and Rami offered them water before he knew they were the missing paper journeymen of Qadira. By clan law they are his guests, and he must protect them even from the Speaker. In December 1104 he lent Tahir Sabrani's fire-boat captains two boats to scout Miruma harbor.
dead: Munqidh the Netmaker (about 668–735): Founder; brought the coast fishers into the Riders.
marriages: 1085, with Clan Musuz: Rami's sister married a Musuz salt cutter, which is how the slab shavings reach Yasiri boats.
FAM-724.secrets: The two paper journeymen of Qadira are hidden at Janiya, bound for Marira and a Ranpuri buyer when the sea opens. Rami lent Sabra the boats that scouted Miruma.

FAM-801.y1105: Imperial house of Zanara. Emperor Mosi III, 41, reigns with a hand that has already gone numb once; his heir Tano is 16 and his cousin Juma commands the army.
FAM-801.arms: a black running man beneath a black baobab on gold
FAM-801.founder: Dembe Kanemba (824–873), first hereditary Master Runner of the Tedana kings
FAM-801.power: The throne of an empire of 11 million; the gold store on the Ancestor Hill and every nugget in the empire by law; a standing army of 140,000 and a levy of 560,000; the 2,400 Runner Guard, of whom about 140 are Runner kin; the relay posts of the House of Runners on every road.
FAM-801.branches: the imperial line (sons of senior wives); the Marshal's line (sons of Prince Sundu, now Juma Kanemba); the Runner kin (lines of junior wives' sons, about 300 people, who run the House of Runners)
FAM-801.bloodline: House Kanemba (the Runner's blood): Runner's blood
FAM-801.history: The Kanemba were runners before they were emperors. The family came from Anumba, a cattle town on the Lotapa 200 km east of Zanara, and carried messages for the Tedana kings from at least the 820s. Its gift was first noticed in Dembe Kanemba. In March 851 he ran 206 km from Zanara to Anumba in two days and a night to raise the Anumba spearmen against an Omamba raid, and King Tumo III made him Master Runner and the office hereditary. Dembe trained his children and nephews, and the family saw that about half of each brood could run as he did and half could not. Dembe fell dead at the Tetamo ford at the end of a run in 873, at 49: the first Kanemba stroke on record. His son Jabali (850–901) married Princess Nandi Tedani, sister of King Obasi, in 876. Their son Mosi, born 878, was the king's nephew and the best runner at court. In May 903 Mosi took the crown from the old king with 3,000 spearmen at his back, made himself Emperor in September and spent 27 years conquering the plains (WAR-21). Then he turned his family into an institution. The Law of the Sung Line binds every child of the emperor's blood to the Kanemba line and no other, and the Law of the Runners made the House of Runners, run by Kanemba kin, the one relay of the empire. Mosi's son Tano I began the Senior Wife Rule when he married his cousin Ama Kanemba in 930: every emperor since has taken a Kanemba senior wife, so that the heir has the Runner's blood from both parents. The rule keeps the blood in the house, but it also doubles it in some children, and doubled blood clots worst. Five emperors in a row died of strokes between 44 and 49: Tano I (959), Obi the Quiet (980), Tano II the Drummer (1004), Kofi the Lion (1025) and Tano III the Gentle (1046). Only Mosi the Runner (70) and Mosi II (68) grew old, and Mosi II never had the blood at all; at his crowning in 1046 he could barely finish the Runner's Round. Sons of junior wives are Kanemba but cannot inherit. Their lines form the Runner kin, about 300 people in 1105, who run the House of Runners, hold about 140 places in the Runner Guard, and marry among themselves or bring husbands into the Kanemba compound. Sefu the Runner, master of the House of Runners and the eighth-deadliest fighter alive, is a grandson of Prince Juma Kanemba, a junior-wife son of Tano II. The house paid heavily in the Salt War: at Mirah in 1060 Prince Kofi, 15, eldest son of the emperor's brother Sundu, died running water to the lines. Sundu himself died of a stroke in 1072 at 44 and left his younger son Juma, then six. Mosi II married his cousin Adisa Kanemba of the Runner kin as senior wife in 1060, and from her Mosi III has the blood his father lacked. Mosi III married Zola Kanemba in 1085, and she bore Tano in 1088. In 1105 the house stands on three men. The emperor is 41 with a numb hand. The heir is 16 and has secretly sworn the Well oath. The Marshal is 38, commands the field army from Atani, and wants the regency.
dead: Dembe Kanemba (824–873): First Master Runner; ran Zanara to Anumba in 851; first Kanemba stroke.
Jabali Kanemba (850–901): Master Runner who married Princess Nandi Tedani; father of Mosi.
Mosi the Runner (878–948): Took the Tedana crown and founded the empire. *Ruler:* Mosi the Runner (Mosi I), Empire of Zanara, 903–948 (RUL-8001).
Tano I the Builder (910–959): Walled the Ancestor Hill; began the Senior Wife Rule. *Ruler:* Tano I Kanemba (the Builder), Empire of Zanara, 948–959 (RUL-8002).
Kofi the Lion (979–1025): Founded the Elephant Corps; lost at the Matazi Ford. *Ruler:* Kofi Kanemba (Kofi I the Lion), Empire of Zanara, 1004–1025 (RUL-8005).
Mosi II Kanemba (1026–1094): The emperor without the blood; fought the Salt War. *Ruler:* Mosi II Kanemba, Empire of Zanara, 1046–1094 (RUL-8007).
marriages: 876, with House Tedani: Jabali Kanemba married Princess Nandi Tedani, sister of King Obasi; mother of Mosi the Runner.
930, with House Kanemba: Tano I married his cousin Ama Kanemba, the first senior wife taken from the Runner kin.
1060, with House Kanemba: Mosi II married Adisa Kanemba of the Runner kin as senior wife; mother of Mosi III.
1085, with House Kanemba: Mosi III married Zola Kanemba of the Runner kin as senior wife; mother of Crown Prince Tano.
FAM-801.rivals: House Tedani, House Asfari, Clan Bahar
FAM-801.secrets: Mosi III's left hand went numb in November 1104, and only Sefu the Runner knows. In 1104 Juma Kanemba secretly sent 8,000 suns of his own gold to Lord Mesfin Mandari of Abara to raise horse for the exiled Prince Tekle.

FAM-802.y1105: Vassal kings of the Tedana at Tandi. King Kato withholds his 1105 tribute and his Rememberers refuse to sing the Kanemba line; his nephew Baraka has sold him to the Marshal.
FAM-802.arms: a gold fist over three blue wavy bars (the Tedana and two tributaries)
FAM-802.founder: Tedan the Gold-Fist (562–631), chief of Kimba and first King of the Tedana
FAM-802.power: The Tedana gravels, panned for the emperor under royal wardens; the city of Tandi (17,900); about 6,000 spearmen drilled by night since 1102; the Spear School of Tandi; the Tedana Rememberers; a secret pit of nuggets worth about 80,000 suns.
FAM-802.branches: the vassal kings of Tandi (Kato's line); the Spear School line (Baraka, son of Kato's dead younger brother)
FAM-802.history: House Tedani takes its name from the river its first king ruled. Tedan the Gold-Fist, chief of Kimba on the Tatendi, made himself king in 600 by taxing the salt that came east from the Well Road, and his line ruled the Kingdom of the Tedana (HPOL-09) for 13 generations. Sundu I founded the salt market of Zanara in 668. Bomani the Lawgiver made the Nugget Law in 702. Kasimu the Mover took the court to Zanara in 781 and buried six kings on the Ancestor Hill. The eastern towns of Kimba and Tandi became the seats of kings' sons. The house lost the crown in May 903, when the old King Obasi gave it to his sister's son Mosi Kanemba. Obasi's sons fled to Tandi, where the eldest, Sefu the Stubborn, ruled the lower Mosawa as King of Tandi for 18 years. He beat Mosi at Nuzeko in 916, but the Salt and Gold Pact of 918 starved Tandi of salt, and the city fell in October 921 after seven months. Sefu died on the palace roof with a thrown spear in him. Mosi buried him on the Ancestor Hill and made his son Kato, then 24, vassal King of the Tedana at Tandi on oath and tribute. Kato's heirs have held the title since. They pan the Tedana gravels for the emperor, pay tribute in gold, cattle and captives, and are sung at Tandi by their own Rememberers in Old Tedani, who count Sefu as the fourteenth king. For 180 years the vassal kings were quiet. The present king's father paid every year and died a vassal in 1080. Kato Tedani took a spear in the thigh fighting Sand Clan raiders in 1071 and has paid tribute every year since 1080. But for ten years he has kept back Tedana nuggets, about 80,000 suns' worth, in a pit under his ancestor house, against the law his own ancestor made. In 1102 he asked his nephew Baraka, master of the Spear School of Tandi, to drill Tedana spearmen by night, and the same year the Tedana Rememberers stopped singing the Kanemba line at Tandi.
