In 1103 he began buying spearheads from Dauda the Smith, paid in Tedana gold dust. He means to withhold the tribute of 1105. The house is split inside. Baraka, son of Kato's younger brother who died of fever in 1071, taught the spear to Crown Prince Tano in 1100 and 1101, and in 1103 he told Marshal Juma Kanemba the size of the night drills. Juma has promised to make him King of the Tedana if Kato rebels and falls. Baraka says he does it to keep Tandi from burning again as it burned in 921.
dead: Tedan the Gold-Fist (562–631): First King of the Tedana. *Ruler:* Tedan the Gold-Fist, Kingdom of the Tedana, 600–631 (RUL-8021).
Sundu I the Salt-Master (622–684): Founded the salt market of Zanara in 668. *Ruler:* Sundu I Tedani (the Salt-Master), Kingdom of the Tedana, 655–684 (RUL-8023).
Bomani the Lawgiver (648–713): Made the Nugget Law in 702. *Ruler:* Bomani Tedani (the Lawgiver), Kingdom of the Tedana, 684–713 (RUL-8024).
Kasimu the Mover (741–796): Moved the court to Zanara and founded the Ancestor Hill. *Ruler:* Kasimu Tedani (the Mover), Kingdom of the Tedana, 760–796 (RUL-8028).
Obasi the Old (836–904): Last Tedana king; gave the crown to Mosi. *Ruler:* Obasi Tedani (the Old), Kingdom of the Tedana, 871–903 (RUL-8033).
Sefu the Stubborn (866–921): King of Tandi 903–921; Mosi's great rival.
marriages: 876, with House Kanemba: Princess Nandi Tedani married Jabali Kanemba, the Master Runner; mother of Mosi the Runner.
FAM-802.allies: the Society of Smiths of Zanara, the Tedana Rememberers of Tandi
FAM-802.secrets: Kato hides about 80,000 suns of nuggets in a pit under his ancestor house. Baraka Tedani has told Marshal Juma of the night drills for the promise of his uncle's crown.

FAM-803.y1105: First of the five Gold Houses; its head Kwame Sorondo is Master of the Scales and creditor of the emperor, King Yonas's court and the Marshal.
FAM-803.arms: a pair of gold scales on black
FAM-803.founder: Kwasi Sorondo (861–930), gold-weigher of the Zanara salt market
FAM-803.power: A fortune guessed at 1.5 million suns; the standard gold weights of the Scale Pact; first place among the five Gold Houses; loans of 100,000 suns to Mosi III, 60,000 to King Yonas's court (with the other Gold Houses) and 20,000 to Marshal Juma; Sabra's caravan advances and the southern Sand Clans' debts.
FAM-803.branches: the main house on the Scale Street of Zanara; the Qadira and Sabra counting houses
FAM-803.history: House Sorondo began as a family of gold-weighers in the Zanara salt market. Kwasi Sorondo bought dust from panners and sold it to the Qadiri buyers of the Well merchants, and in 921 he lent the young Emperor Mosi the gold that paid for the seven-month Siege of Tandi, taking the salt tax of Zanara's east gate as security. When Tano I gave the Charter of the Scales in 951, licensing five Gold Houses to weigh and buy all gold dust sold in Zanara and to keep the standard weights, House Sorondo was named first of the five. Its head has been Master of the Scales ever since. The other four Gold Houses are smaller and follow the Sorondo scales. The house grew with the Gold Road. After Sabra broke from Qadir in 1025, both ports bid for Zanari gold, and the Gold Houses set the price for both. During the Debt War of 1044 to 1047 the banks of Ostra and Lucerna called in the Tessarian loans and wanted metal, and the gold price at Zanara rose by about a quarter; Sorondo bought at the old price, sold at the new and doubled its fortune. It lent to the court in the Salt War and was paid back out of the salt peace. Adoma Sorondo, head of the house from 1049, sent his eldest son Kwame to Qadira with the house scales in 1068. Kwame wrote most of the Scale Pact of 1071, which made the Sorondo weights the standard for gold at Sabra and Qadira. On the day it was sealed the house had the standard weight shaved by one part in fifty. Every buyer at Sabra and Qadira has been short-weighted by the house for 33 years, and nobody has yet tested the Zanari standard against an honest Solen weight. Kwame became head and Master of the Scales in 1085. In 1074 a Sorondo cousin married Amara Kabale; he died in 1086, and Kwame still buys the Kabale gold. In 1103 Kwame lent Mosi III 100,000 suns for the east road, and in 1104 the Gold Houses lent King Yonas's court the last of its 60,000. The house needs the road built, because its loans are tied to the road, and it needs no war with Abara, because a war would make Yonas's debt worthless. Kwame has no son; his heir is a nephew at the Qadira counting house, and the other four Gold Houses watch the Sorondo ledgers for the first sign of weakness.
dead: Kwasi Sorondo (861–930): Founder; financed the Siege of Tandi.
Adoma Sorondo (1020–1085): Head of the house through the Salt War; Kwame's father.
marriages: 1074, with House Kabale: A Sorondo cousin married Amara Kabale; he died in 1086.
FAM-803.secrets: Since the Scale Pact of 1071 the Zanari standard gold weight kept by the house has been one part in fifty light.

FAM-804.y1105: Mine-lords of the Southern Hills under Lady Amara Kabale, who hides a dying vein and 172 dead and wants a war for captives.
FAM-804.arms: a red lamp over a black shaft mouth on grey
FAM-804.founder: Chief Mbaku Kabale (882–951), who swore to Mosi the Runner on the Ancestor Hill
FAM-804.power: The deep gold mines of the Southern Hills around Kabale (18,300); about 9,000 slaves and one guard for every 20; the Kabale mine forts; gold sold through House Sorondo.
FAM-804.history: The Kabale are the mine-lords of the Southern Hills, where gold lies in quartz veins rather than river gravel. Before the empire, the Kabale chiefs held the shafts around Kabale and paid the Tedana kings only when an army came. They were among the western chiefs who still held out against Mosi the Runner after 925. After the Battle of Bandi in April 927, Chief Mbaku Kabale submitted, and on 20 March 930 he swore on the Ancestor Hill in return for keeping his shafts as the emperor's vassal. The house has dug for the emperor ever since, with slaves: war captives, debtors and their children. The shafts are deep and the work kills. In 1049 the slaves of the deep shafts rose. Lady Nala Kabale, Amara's grandmother, held the mine forts with 300 guards until the Golden Horse came from Zanara, and 400 slaves were hanged at the pit mouths. Amara, only daughter of the last lord, was married at 16 in 1074 to a Sorondo cousin who died in 1086. She took the house in 1087 over two uncles, with Mosi II's leave. After a gallery fire in 1092 she rebuilt the forts and doubled the slave pens. In August 1103 the deep south shaft collapsed and killed 212 slaves; she reported 40 to the emperor. The south vein now yields a third of what it did, which she hides from the Gold Houses. She wants a war with Abara to bring her 3,000 new captives and presses Marshal Juma to march before the rains. Her hired Well Quarter surveyors have found a new vein west of Kabale, on land that King Kato Tedani holds. Her lamp-master Sadiki, a freed slave, is hiding wedges and oil for a rising on the Night of Masks.
dead: Mbaku Kabale (882–951): Chief who swore to Mosi in 930 and kept the mines.
Nala Kabale (1004–1071): Put down the slave rising of 1049.
marriages: 1074, with House Sorondo: Amara Kabale married a Sorondo cousin, who died in 1086.
FAM-804.secrets: The collapse of August 1103 killed 212 slaves, not 40, and the south vein is failing.

FAM-805.y1105: Leading Well house of Zanara; Bakari Kante is Speaker of the Well Quarter and sits on the emperor's council.
FAM-805.arms: a blue well-mouth over a gold camel on white
FAM-805.founder: Sidi Kante (951–1019), gold carrier and first Kante of the Well Quarter
FAM-805.power: Caravans on the Gold Road north through Sabra and Qadira; the Speakership of the Well Quarter; a seat on the imperial council; a grandnephew who tutors the Crown Prince in letters.
FAM-805.branches: the Zanara house; the Kante agents at Qadira and Sabra
FAM-805.history: The Kante are gold carriers of Zanara's Well Quarter. Sidi Kante ran donkey strings of dust to the Qadiri buyers in the salt market, and when Tano II gave the Charter of the Well Quarter in 988 the family moved into the new quarter and began running its own camel caravans north through the Red Waste. For a century the Kante kept the ancestors, as most Zanari do. Bakari's father took the Path of the Well at Qadira in 1049 and made the Kante a Well house, although the family still keeps its ancestors' names on its household altar, as most of the Well Quarter does. Bakari, born in 1052, crossed the waste with his father's caravans eight times between 1068 and 1080, learned the Well Speech and Qadiri letters, and was chosen Speaker of the Well Quarter in 1089. He has sat on the emperor's council since 1094. The house's wealth is the northern trade: every weight of gold it carries to Sabra and Qadira. The east road would send that gold east instead, down the Monuti. In October 1104 Bakari sent 5,000 suns in gold dust to Marshal Gebre Tsega of Abara to stiffen King Yared against the road. His grandnephew tutors Crown Prince Tano in letters, and in 1104 Tano swore the Well oath beside him. It is the house's greatest success and its greatest danger: if the High Rememberer learns of it, the Well Quarter may lose its place at court.
dead: Sidi Kante (951–1019): Moved the family into the Well Quarter in 988.
Musa Kante (1024–1088): Bakari's father; took the Path of the Well at Qadira in 1049.
FAM-805.allies: the Well merchants of Qadira and Sabra, House Tsega
FAM-805.secrets: Bakari paid Gebre Tsega 5,000 suns in 1104 to block the east road. Crown Prince Tano swore the Well oath beside a Kante tutor.

FAM-806.y1105: Scribes of the Ancestor Hill whose two daughters hold the empire's two roads to the sea: Nia builds the east road, Imani seeks a track to Monuro.
FAM-806.arms: a white reed pen crossed with a measuring cord on indigo
FAM-806.founder: Oyo Tembo (962–1031), first letter-scribe of the High Rememberer
FAM-806.power: The written tallies of the Ancestor Hill's offerings and gold store; the Road-Mastership and 11,000 road laborers at Atani; Imani's knowledge of the Deep Green.
FAM-806.history: The Tembo are a family of scribes to the Rememberers of the Ancestor Hill. Rememberers keep their songs by heart, but after the Charter of the Well Quarter of 988 brought letters to Zanara, the High Rememberer began to keep written tallies of offerings, land given to the ancestor houses and the weights in the gold store, and from 990 the Tembo wrote them. Four generations kept the tallies and learned numbers from Well Quarter clerks. Nia Tembo, born in 1070, daughter of a Rememberer's scribe, measured the Mosawa lands for the grain tax from 1090 to 1098, surveyed a route east from Tandi through Atani to the Abari border in 1102 and was made Road-Master in 1103. Her survey hides 80 km and about 150,000 suns of true cost. Her younger sister Imani, born 1076, went to Kesh in 1093 with an ivory caravan and learned the Deep Green from the Keshi explorer who came home in 1070. She has made four journeys to the Leaf People and now seeks a track from the Mosawa lands to Monuro for House Monuri, a route that would carry Zanari gold to the sea without Abara and would rival her sister's road. The family is not rich. In 1105 its daughters hold two of the three ways Zanari gold might reach the sea.
dead: Oyo Tembo (962–1031): First letter-scribe of the High Rememberer.
FAM-806.allies: House Kanemba, House Sorondo, House Monuri
FAM-806.secrets: Nia's survey of 1102 hides that the road is 80 km longer and about 150,000 suns dearer than she told the emperor.

FAM-821.y1105: Princes of Kesh since 1068. Prince Amani rules with an empty treasury and pawned harbor dues; the infant heir carries the Keshari blood and may carry the Maruang storm-sense from his mother.
FAM-821.arms: a red rope tied in a slip-knot on dark green
FAM-821.founder: Pili Keshari (968–1041), rigger, festival climber and founder of the Rope Hall of Kesh
FAM-821.power: The princedom: command of the League's 45 fighting ships and the 1,000 Pepper Guard; the Keeper of Keys and his thieves; the Rope Hall of Kesh and its 400 boarding climbers; the love of the harbor lanes. Almost no money of its own.
FAM-821.branches: the princely line (Amani and the infant Nuru); the Keeper's line (Faraji, son of Nuru by Taji of the Rope Hall); the unacknowledged line (Kito the Gecko, son of Nuru by the rope-walker Dalila)
FAM-821.history: The Keshari were nobody in particular for most of their history. The name means only 'of Kesh'. The family were mast-riggers, rope-makers and festival climbers of the harbor lanes, the people who race up masts at the Harvest Home while the merchant houses watch. Sauti Keshari, born 945, could fold her thumb flat against her wrist and did it at fairs for coppers. Her son Pili, born 968, first made the family's loose joints pay. He won the Harvest Home climb on the Pepper Hall roof in 985 by wedging his hands into gaps no other climber could use, and that winter he slipped his wrists out of the harbor stocks and was gone by morning. In 1004 he founded the Rope Hall of Kesh to teach climbing, rope-walking and slipping bonds, and its masters have been Keshari or Keshari-trained ever since. His son Kombo (1004–1058) was the best roof thief of his day and died when a knee gave way on a warehouse roof. Kombo's son Nuru, born 1035, grew up in the Rope Hall. In May 1068, with the Monuri prince dead and the League paying the Amber harbor tax, Nuru climbed into the Amber harbor-house at Kesh, put his own shoulder out of joint to slip through a window 20 cm wide while the boy Tumaini held the rope, and came out with the ledgers that proved the Amber tax-men had cheated Keshi ships. The council made him Prince on 19 May 1068. He led the League through the Spice War (WAR-39), burned 12 Amber ships in Amberport in June 1069 and escaped capture through a drain, and saw the Treaty of Madamo signed in 1072. He ruled 24 years and fell from the Pepper Hall roof at the Harvest Home climb of 1092 when his shoulder gave way. Nuru married Subira, a pepper-gardener's daughter of Kioya, in 1058; she bore Amani in 1060 and died of fever in 1066. In 1070 he married Taji, an acrobat of the Rope Hall, who bore Faraji in 1072. In 1080 a festival rope-walker named Dalila bore him a son, Kito, whom he never acknowledged; Faraji knows and keeps Kito close. The council elected Amani in 1092. He made peace with the Amber Isles and in 1101 married Laila Maruang, Sultan Iskandar's sister, who came into the house by marriage and keeps her Well faith. Their son Nuru was born in 1103. House Keshari rules but is not rich. It owns no great ships and few gardens; the Prince's treasury is empty, the harbor dues of 1105 are pawned to an Amber house, and the League owes Amber merchants 200,000 suns. Faraji, Keeper of Keys since 1093, is the League's spymaster and its thief. The house holds the princedom because the council fears the Monuri, and because in the harbor lanes a Keshari prince is one of their own.
dead: Pili Keshari (968–1041): First climber of the blood; founded the Rope Hall.
Kombo Keshari (1004–1058): Roof thief; died when a knee gave way.
Nuru Keshari the Boneless (1035–1092): Stole the Amber ledgers; Prince 1068–1092. *Ruler:* Nuru Keshari the Boneless, Kesh, 1068–1092 (RUL-8212).
marriages: 1058, with pepper gardeners of Kioya: Nuru married Subira, mother of Amani; she died in 1066.
1070, with the Rope Hall acrobats: Nuru married Taji, mother of Faraji.
1101, with House Maruang: Amani married Laila Maruang, Sultan Iskandar's sister.
FAM-821.allies: House Maruang, the Rope Hall of Kesh
FAM-821.secrets: Kito the Gecko is Nuru the Boneless's unacknowledged son. Faraji pays a palace cook in the infant heir's kitchen. The harbor dues of 1105 are pawned.

FAM-822.y1105: Oldest ship-owning house of the League and its princes for most of 919–1068; Hamisi Monuri leads the Old Houses and plots with Amberport for the next election.
FAM-822.arms: a white galley under a gold sun on sea blue
FAM-822.power: About a third of the League's 150 merchant ships; the Harbor-Lordship of Monuro and its shipyards; the cinnamon forests bought from the Madami; command of the 20-ship Pearl Squadron through Baruti.
FAM-822.branches: the Harbor-Lords of Monuro (Hamisi's line); the war-galley line (Baruti, son of Hamisi's brother Salum)
FAM-822.history: House Monuri is the oldest merchant house of the League. Mwamba Monuri, a ship-owner of Monuro, launched his first coasting ship in 812, and his family has owned ships in Monuro ever since. When the four towns swore the League in 880, the Monuri gave six of the first shared galleys, and in 919 the council made Chande Monuri the Galley-Maker Prince of Kesh. Chande built the League's first 12 war galleys in his own yards, walled the yards and founded the Sea School of Monuro. For 150 years the Monuri held the princedom more often than any house: Chande (919–938), Shabani (967–984), Kassim (996–1017), Rashidi (1046–1061) and Idrisa (1061–1068). They rebuilt the Monuro sea wall after the cyclone of 1033, and they rose highest after the Tessar default of 1046 ruined House Madami, buying the Madami cinnamon forests at a third of their worth. Idrisa died of fever in February 1068, and the council met to choose his brother Saidi. It chose Nuru Keshari instead, and Saidi's son Hamisi, 17, watched it happen. The Monuri lost two ships in the last year of the Spice War and have forgiven neither the Amber Isles nor the Keshari. Hamisi took his father's seat and ships in 1079, became Harbor-Lord of Monuro in 1090 and has led the Old Houses on the council since Nuru's death in 1092. The house owns about a third of the League's 150 merchant ships and buys Rehema's merchant hulls, and its ships carry the smuggler Omari's pepper past the Pepper Hall scales. In November 1104 Hamisi wrote to Grand Vizier Rahim Sulong of the Amber Isles, offering Monuro's ships for the Isle of Pearls if Amberport will back a Monuri prince at the next election. He also pays the Zanari explorer Imani Tembo to find a track from the Mosawa lands to Monuro, which would bring Zanari gold to Monuri ships and make Monuro, not Kesh, the League's richest port. His nephew Baruti, son of his younger brother Salum, learned ramming at the Sea School, burned a pirate galley off Madamo in 1094 and commands the 20-ship Pearl Squadron. In December 1104 Baruti told Faraji Keshari about the Vizier letter in return for that command. Hamisi does not know. The house is patient, rich and divided against itself at the moment it most needs to be one.
dead: Mwamba Monuri (781–850): Founder; first Monuri ship.
Chande Monuri the Galley-Maker (870–938): Built the League's first war galleys. *Ruler:* Chande Monuri (the Galley-Maker), Kesh, 919–938 (RUL-8203).
Idrisa Monuri (1022–1068): Last Monuri prince. *Ruler:* Idrisa Monuri, Kesh, 1061–1068 (RUL-8211).
Saidi Monuri (1026–1079): Lost the election of 1068 to Nuru; Hamisi's father.
marriages: 1047, with House Madami: Saidi Monuri married a Madami daughter when the Monuri bought the Madami forests.
FAM-822.allies: The Tembo, the Shipwrights of Monuro
FAM-822.secrets: Hamisi has offered Monuro's ships to the Amber Grand Vizier for a Monuri prince; Baruti has betrayed the letter to Faraji Keshari.

FAM-823.y1105: Pepper growers of the Kioya hills who keep the Pepper Hall; Zawadi Kioyani withholds the Prince's fees to stop the Pearl Venture.
FAM-823.arms: a green pepper vine with red berries on white
FAM-823.founder: Kitwana Kioyani (840–902), pepper grower of the Kioya hills
FAM-823.power: The largest pepper and cardamom gardens of the Kioya hills; the Mistress-ship of the Pepper Hall, which weighs and taxes all League spice; the weighing fees the Prince's treasury depends on; the Hall watch's pay.
FAM-823.history: The Kioyani are the pepper growers of the Kioya hills, the wettest gardens on the coast. Kitwana Kioyani held the largest pepper and cardamom gardens around Kioya when the League was sworn in 880 and pushed for the Pepper Hall, so that hill growers would be paid by one honest weight and not cheated by each port. The house gave the League two princes: Makame Kioyani (938–951), who won the Neck charter of 944 from Emperor Leontius I, and Tatu Kioyani the Weigher (984–996), the only woman prince, who reformed the Hall's weights in 990. Since then a Kioyani has usually held the Pepper Hall. Because Kioya lies high in the hills, the house kept its sea fleet at Kioya Water, its landing on the Spice Coast below the hills, and on 15 August 1068 the Amber fleet burned 22 of its ships there. Zawadi's father died aboard one; she was five. She learned the weighing floor from her mother, became head of the house in 1090 and Mistress of the Pepper Hall in 1097. She speaks for the growers, sets the weighing fees and hates the Amber Isles. Yet in 1104 she quietly sold 40 tonnes of Keshi pepper to the Grand Vizier's spice monopoly at Amberport, because Ranpur's Nagora pepper had driven prices down in the north. In 1105 she withholds the Prince's weighing fees to stop the Pearl Venture and has barred the Rope Hall's climbers from the Hall roof.
dead: Kitwana Kioyani (840–902): Pushed for the Pepper Hall.
Tatu Kioyani the Weigher (930–996): Only woman prince; reformed the weights. *Ruler:* Tatu Kioyani (the Weigher), Kesh, 984–996 (RUL-8207).
Jumbe Kioyani (1035–1068): Zawadi's father; burned with the fleet at Kioya Water.
FAM-823.allies: the Pepper Hall growers, the Pepper Guard
FAM-823.rivals: House Keshari, House Monuri, House Maruang
FAM-823.secrets: Zawadi sold 40 tonnes of pepper to Amberport in 1104 while leading the fight against the Amber alliance.

FAM-824.y1105: Fallen. The first princely house of the League was ruined by the Tessar default of 1046; its members are clerks and weighers.
FAM-824.arms: a brown cinnamon branch on gold
FAM-824.founder: Seif Madami the Founder (838–901), first Prince of Kesh
FAM-824.power: None left but the old Madami hall at Madamo, where the treaty of 1072 was signed, and a few weighers' places at the Pepper Hall.
FAM-824.history: House Madami were the cinnamon lords of the Madamo hills, whose bark forests give the League its cinnamon-like bark. Seif Madami was chosen first Prince of Kesh when the League was sworn in 880 and built the Pepper Hall in 884. The Madami held the princedom three more times: Kombo (901–919), Hamadi (951–967) and Mbaraka the Lender (1017–1046). They sold cinnamon north through the Neck after the charter of 944 and became the League's lenders to Tessar, selling spice on credit to Tessarian buyers. That was their ruin. When the Tessarian Empire's loans were called in during the Debt War (WAR-31), the buyers of Tessar defaulted on about 90,000 suns in 1046, most of it owed to the Madami. The council deposed Mbaraka, and the house sold its cinnamon forests to the Monuri and Kioyani at a third of their worth; a Madami daughter married Saidi Monuri in 1047 as part of the sale. By 1105 the Madami are clerks. The weigher at the Pepper Hall whom the smuggler Omari pays is a Madami, and Madamo gave its name to the Treaty of Madamo of 1072, signed in the old Madami hall.
dead: Seif Madami the Founder (838–901): First Prince; built the Pepper Hall. *Ruler:* Seif Madami (the Founder), Kesh, 880–901 (RUL-8201).
Mbaraka Madami the Lender (975–1052): Deposed after the Tessar default. *Ruler:* Mbaraka Madami (the Lender), Kesh, 1017–1046 (RUL-8209).
marriages: 1047, with House Monuri: A Madami daughter married Saidi Monuri as part of the forest sale.
FAM-824.secrets: A Madami weigher at the Pepper Hall takes the smuggler Omari's money.

FAM-811.y1105: Royal house of Abara under the twin kings Yared (reigning 1105) and Yonas. Neither has a twin son, and the exiled Prince Tekle holds the hidden better claim.
FAM-811.arms: two white spears crossed over a banner cut green and blue
FAM-811.founder: Asfar Asfari (986–1049), elder of the twin kings; before 1012 the family were the lords of Nusalo
FAM-811.power: The crown of 6.5 million people; two courts at Abara and Nusalo with about 35,000 household troops each and the Green and Blue Twin Guards of 2,000; a tenth of grain and cattle; Tamar's river gift in the reigning king's year; the royal ancestor houses' gold, whose key the Queen Mother holds.
FAM-811.branches: the line of Kaleb (the twin kings); the line of Kiros (Prince Tekle, in exile); the Cord Branch (children of Asfari daughters in Houses Tsega, Mandari and Mekonen, tied onto the royal cords)
FAM-811.history: Before it was royal, House Asfari was the house of the lords of Nusalo, vassals of the Kimoni kings. Its women were known for twins. Lady Tsehay of Nusalo, a daughter of the house who married her cousin, bore three pairs of twins between 921 and 932, and her daughters bore twins after her. The lords paid the Rememberers a soul-price of 100 cattle for each pair, so that they could keep both children instead of giving the younger away as village custom demands. In the 950s Lord Asrat of Nusalo married Princess Werknesh, sister of King Dagne the Steadfast. Their son Berhanu married his cousin Genet, Tsehay's granddaughter, and in 986 Genet bore twin sons, Asfar and Asmar. Berhanu died in 1004. When King Anbesa II died without sons in November 1011, his nearest male kin were Berhanu's twins, and the Rememberers, who could not choose between two men born in one hour, crowned both at dawn on 1 January 1012. The house took the elder twin's name. The twin kings ruled one court together for 37 years. In 1016 they beat Emperor Kofi of Zanara at the Matazi Ford. In 1022 they made the Cord Law: Asfari daughters marry only Asfari men or the lords of the three cord houses, and every child of such a marriage is tied onto the royal cords. Asfar's wife Rahel, a Nusalo cousin, died bearing Kaleb and Kiros in 1029; the knotted cord tied at her bedside shows Kiros first. Asmar had four daughters and no sons. He married Lulit to Lord Tesfaye Mandari in 1041 and Tigist to Lord Workneh Tsega in 1049, and Asfar's daughter Hanna married Tefera Mekonen, brother of the Keeper of the Source, in 1034. Asfar and Asmar died nine days apart in the spotted fever of March 1049. Kaleb and Kiros each crowned himself, and the Twin War (WAR-33) followed until the Compact of 1 November 1053 gave Kaleb the odd years and Kiros the even. The Compact made the house two households. Kiros married Senait Mandari, Lulit's daughter, in 1060; she died in 1062 bearing a single son, Tekle, and Kiros never married again. Kaleb's first wife, Etenesh Mekonen, Hanna's daughter, lost two pairs of twins and died in 1063. In 1068 he married Saba, Tigist's daughter, born a Tsega, and in 1070 she nearly died bearing Yared and Yonas. Saba also raised the motherless Tekle from the age of six. Both kings died in 1089. Yared and Yonas were crowned on 1 January 1090, and Tekle, single-born, was shut out and then banished in May for demanding to see the cord. He serves Queen Livia of Tessaria as a hired captain and ranks among the 15 deadliest fighters alive. Yared married his Tsega cord cousin Mahlet in 1093; she has borne one daughter, in 1096. Yonas's wife Bezawit, a Mekonen cord daughter, died in 1099 bearing twins who did not live. Neither king has a twin son, and under the Compact, if none is born, the Rememberers must choose among twin-born kin. In 1105 the house has two kings who distrust each other, a Queen Mother both obey, and an exile with the better claim.
dead: Tsehay of Nusalo (902–960): First known carrier of the twin-bearing blood; bore three pairs of twins.
Asfar Asfari (986–1049): Elder twin king; held the Matazi Ford; made the Cord Law. *Ruler:* Asfar Asfari, Kingdom of Abara, 1012–1049 (RUL-8140).
Asmar Asfari (986–1049): Younger twin king; led the horse at the Matazi Ford. *Ruler:* Asmar Asfari, Kingdom of Abara, 1012–1049 (RUL-8141).
Rahel of Nusalo (1007–1029): Asfar's wife; died bearing Kaleb and Kiros.
Kaleb Asfari (1029–1089): King in odd years 1053–1089; father of Yared and Yonas. *Ruler:* Kaleb Asfari, Kingdom of Abara, 1049–1089 (RUL-8142).
Kiros Asfari (1029–1089): King in even years; firstborn by the knotted cord. *Ruler:* Kiros Asfari, Kingdom of Abara, 1049–1089 (RUL-8143).
marriages: 1034, with House Mekonen: Asfar's daughter Hanna married Tefera Mekonen; mother of Etenesh.
1041, with House Mandari: Asmar's daughter Lulit married Lord Tesfaye Mandari; mother of Senait.
1049, with House Tsega: Asmar's daughter Tigist married Lord Workneh Tsega; mother of Saba.
1056, with House Mekonen: Kaleb married Etenesh Mekonen, who died in 1063.
1060, with House Mandari: Kiros married Senait Mandari, who died in 1062 bearing Tekle.
FAM-811.allies: House Tsega, House Mekonen, House Teferi
FAM-811.secrets: The birth-cord of 1029 shows Kiros born first, so Tekle's line is the elder. Queen Mother Saba has taken 9,000 suns from the ancestor houses' gold to pay Yonas's interest.

FAM-812.y1105: Extinct in the male line since 638. Its 27 kings, two of them unsung, lie in the oldest royal ancestor houses at Abara, and every later king claims descent from them through daughters.
FAM-812.founder: Abar the Cattle-Lord (238 BR–168 BR), first King of Abara
FAM-812.power: None in 1105; its ancestor houses at Abara are the second holiest site of the Thousand Ancestors.
FAM-812.history: The Line of Abar ruled Abara for 837 years, from the founding in 200 BR to the famine of 637. Abar the Cattle-Lord won the grazing war of the upper Monuti and built the first ancestor houses; the Abari say he climbed down a baobab tree from the sky, which is why the line's badge is a baobab although none grows on the Highveld. His son Zeray I began the Source rite with the priest Mekonen in about 150 BR. The line's greatest test was the Dimming. Mulat the Grey kept the kingdom alive through the Grey Grass years and ordered the first terraces at Zutati. His heirs rebuilt the herds, bound the smith clans to the crown, bought horses from the delta towns and kept Solen out of the Highveld for 428 years with the Koyako Tribute of Habte the Wary. Bekele the Builder raised the Walls of Abara. The line bred its own disasters: the royal cousin Gashaw murdered Ayele I in 490 and was put to death in 493, and the last king, Negash II the Hungry, kept the granaries shut through the famine of 636 to 638 until the lords deposed him. Both are unsung. The line continued through Negash II's daughter Hiwot, wife of Tesfa of Kimoni, so House Kimoni and, through Princess Werknesh, House Asfari both descend from Abar.
dead: Abar the Cattle-Lord (238 BR–168 BR): Founder of the kingdom. *Ruler:* Abar (the Cattle-Lord), Kingdom of Abara, 200–168 BR (RUL-8101).
Zeray I the Source-Keeper (196 BR–133 BR): Began the Source rite. *Ruler:* Zeray I (the Source-Keeper), Kingdom of Abara, 168–133 BR (RUL-8102).
Mulat the Grey (45 BR–14 AR): King of the Dimming; first terraces. *Ruler:* Mulat (the Grey), Kingdom of Abara, 19 BR–14 (RUL-8107).
Habte the Wary (151–219): Made the Koyako Tribute. *Ruler:* Habte (the Wary), Kingdom of Abara, 172–219 (RUL-8113).
Bekele the Builder (322–384): Built the Walls of Abara. *Ruler:* Bekele (the Builder), Kingdom of Abara, 350–384 (RUL-8118).
Negash II the Hungry (577–638): Deposed in the famine; unsung. *Ruler:* Negash II (the Hungry), Kingdom of Abara, 606–637 (RUL-8127).
marriages: 95 BR, with a Tamari temple-lord's house: Tesfa I married a Tamari temple-lord's daughter to open the river trade.
624, with House Kimoni: Negash II's daughter Hiwot married Tesfa, lord of Kimoni.
FAM-812.secrets: The Rememberers who unsung Negash II had been fed from his shut granaries through the famine.

FAM-813.y1105: Extinct in the male line since 1011. Its blood runs in House Asfari through Princess Werknesh, and its ancestor houses at Kimoni still receive offerings.
FAM-813.founder: Tesfa II Kimoni the Rain-Bringer (601–668), lord of Kimoni
FAM-813.history: House Kimoni were lords of Kimoni, east of Abara, before they were kings. Tesfa of Kimoni married Hiwot, daughter of King Negash II, and when the lords deposed Negash in the famine of 637 they crowned his son-in-law. The rains returned in 639 and the song called Tesfa the Rain-Bringer. He stopped the Koyako Tribute in 641 when Tamar broke free of Solen. His grandson Kasa II the Rider took the Monundi valleys, and the Mandari swore to him in 712. The house nearly ended in 781, when Hawaz the Red of Zutati killed Seyum II; the Tsega restored Seyum III in 786. Girma II outlived all his sons, and his daughter Hirut the Keeper ruled in her own name from 872 and made the Knot Decree of 874. Her great-grandson Dagne the Steadfast, crowned at 14 in 940, faced the Tessarian Empire: he refused its tribute in 943, refused its silver to dam the Monuti in 986 and made the River Gift Pact with free Tamar in 989. His son Anbesa II died in November 1011 without sons. Dagne's sister Werknesh had married Lord Asrat of Nusalo, and her twin grandsons Asfar and Asmar took the crown in 1012.
dead: Tesfa II the Rain-Bringer (601–668): First Kimoni king; ended the Koyako Tribute. *Ruler:* Tesfa II Kimoni (the Rain-Bringer), Kingdom of Abara, 637–668 (RUL-8128).
Kasa II the Rider (658–729): Took the Monundi valleys. *Ruler:* Kasa II Kimoni (the Rider), Kingdom of Abara, 695–729 (RUL-8130).
Hirut the Keeper (848–897): Only ruling queen; made the Knot Decree. *Ruler:* Hirut Kimoni (the Keeper), Kingdom of Abara, 872–897 (RUL-8136).
Dagne the Steadfast (926–991): Refused the Tessarian dam; made the River Gift Pact. *Ruler:* Dagne Kimoni (the Steadfast), Kingdom of Abara, 940–991 (RUL-8138).
Anbesa II the Last (965–1011): Died without sons. *Ruler:* Anbesa II Kimoni (the Last), Kingdom of Abara, 991–1011 (RUL-8139).
marriages: 624, with The Line of Abar: Tesfa of Kimoni married Hiwot, daughter of Negash II.
952, with House Asfari: Princess Werknesh, Dagne's sister, married Lord Asrat of Nusalo; grandmother of the twin kings.
FAM-813.secrets: Anbesa II fathered a son by a Kimoni serving woman in 1008; the Rememberers never sang the boy, whose descendants still farm near Kimoni.

FAM-814.y1105: Lords of the Zutati highlands and backbone of King Yared's court; Gebre Tsega commands the Northern Host and holds Tamowa against the Zanari road.
FAM-814.arms: a white pike over green terraces
FAM-814.founder: Tsega the Spear (749–812), who killed Hawaz the Red
FAM-814.power: Zutati (21,000) and the northern wheat and cattle highlands; the Spear Yard of Zutati and 12,000 drilled pikemen; command of the Northern Host (about 35,000 of King Yared's household troops and levies); 8,000 men at Tamowa; northern cattle lent to Yared's court.
FAM-814.branches: the Zutati lords (Gebre's line); the cord daughters (Saba and Mahlet, counted on the Asfari cords)
FAM-814.history: The Tsega were spearmen of Zutati under the lords of that town. When Hawaz the Red, lord of Zutati, killed King Seyum II in 781 and took the crown, the Tsega spearmen refused him. In 786 Tsega the Spear led 600 of them into the royal hall at Abara, killed Hawaz and set the dead king's son on the throne. Seyum III gave Zutati to the Tsega, and they have held it since. They founded the Spear Yard of Zutati in 790 to drill the northern levies in the pike hedge, the defense of the terraces that has turned back every raider from the south. Under House Asfari the Tsega became a cord house by the Cord Law of 1022. Lord Workneh Tsega married Princess Tigist, King Asmar's daughter, in 1049, just before the Twin War. In that war the Tsega were Kaleb's hammer. At Zutati in February 1051 Abebe Tsega, Workneh's younger brother, led the Tsega pikes that broke Kiros's center and turned the Mandari charge. The court songs credit the deed to Tsega, and Abebe's son Gebre has let the songs mean him. Workneh's daughter Saba, born 1052, married King Kaleb in 1068 and bore the twin kings. Workneh's only son died of fever in 1079, so when Workneh died in 1085 the house passed to his nephew Gebre, 27. Yared made Gebre Marshal of the Northern Host in 1090, and that May Gebre ordered Tekle Asfari seized on the Zutati road; Kebede the Pike, master of the Tsega Spear Yard, let the prince pass. In 1093 Yared married Gebre's cousin Mahlet, a cord daughter. Gebre has hunted the Monundi raiders since 1102 and buys copies of every letter between Mesfin Mandari and Tekle from the pedlar Desta. In October 1104 he took 5,000 suns in gold dust from Bakari Kante of Zanara's Well Quarter to stiffen Yared against the Zanari road. In 1105 he means to collect Tamar's river gift in silver by 1 March, hold Tamowa with 8,000 men, and, if Yared asks, keep the Green Guard in the capital at the next New Year's dawn. The Tsega are the Asfari's closest kin and their sharpest knife. Their wealth is northern wheat and cattle from the terraces around Zutati, and in the Upland War of 1014 to 1017 Tsega pikes held the Loati fords while the twin kings fought at the Matazi. Gebre is unmarried at 46 and his heir is a cousin's son of 12, so the house's future, like the crown's, hangs on one man.
dead: Tsega the Spear (749–812): Killed Hawaz the Red and restored Seyum III.
Workneh Tsega (1026–1085): Married Princess Tigist; father of Queen Mother Saba.
Abebe Tsega (1030–1080): Led the Tsega pikes for Kaleb at Zutati in 1051; Gebre's father.
marriages: 1049, with House Asfari: Lord Workneh Tsega married Princess Tigist, King Asmar's daughter.
1068, with House Asfari: Workneh's daughter Saba married King Kaleb.
1093, with House Asfari: Gebre's cousin Mahlet, a cord daughter, married King Yared.
FAM-814.rivals: House Mandari, House Mekonen, House Kanemba
FAM-814.secrets: Gebre took 5,000 suns from the Well Quarter of Zanara in 1104. He has bought copies of the Mandari letters to Tekle since 1100.

FAM-815.y1105: Cavalry lords of the Monundi valleys who fought for Kiros and now lead Kiros's Men; Lord Mesfin is raising 6,000 horse for Prince Tekle's return.
FAM-815.arms: a white horse running on blue over a red river
FAM-815.founder: Mandar the Horse-Lord (668–731), who swore to Kasa II the Rider
FAM-815.power: Mandi (19,800) and the Monundi valleys, the kingdom's horse country; the 6,000 Horsemen of the Monundi; the Horse School of Mandi; the horse fairs of Mandi and Basazi; about 8,000 suns of Zanari gold in 1104.
FAM-815.branches: the lords of Mandi (Mesfin's line); the Horse School line (Yohannes, son of Mesfin's uncle)
FAM-815.history: The Mandari were horse-lords of the Monundi valleys, 300 km south of Abara, where the horses Asrat the Horse-Buyer brought to the Highveld in about 80 AR had bred best. They kept their own lords and sang their own lines until Kasa II the Rider brought his army south, and in 712 Mandar the Horse-Lord swore to him at Mandi in return for keeping his horse fairs and his own judges. The house has been the kingdom's cavalry ever since and has never forgotten that it chose to join. The Cord Law of 1022 made it a cord house. Lord Tesfaye Mandari married Princess Lulit, King Asmar's daughter, in 1041; she bore their daughter Senait in 1044 and died in 1047 bearing twins. Tesfaye married again, a Mandari cousin, and his son Mesfin was born in 1055. In the Twin War Tesfaye led the southern horse for Kiros. At Zutati in 1051 his charge broke on the Tsega pikes, a disaster the Horse School still teaches its riders to avoid, and in 1052 his riders starved with Kiros before the walls of Abara. After the Compact, the Mandari were Kiros's court. In 1060 Kiros married Senait, Tesfaye's daughter, and she died in 1062 bearing Tekle. Mesfin is therefore Tekle's half-uncle, and he grew up at Kiros's even-year court and rode in his guard from 1072. He became Lord of Mandi in 1086. Since Tekle's banishment in May 1090 he has written to him every season by pedlars; the pedlar Desta sells copies to Gebre Tsega. In 1104 Mesfin took 8,000 suns from an agent of Marshal Juma of Zanara to raise horse for Tekle. His cousin Yohannes, master of the Horse School of Mandi since 1096, keeps 300 picked riders ready for the Monundi fords, and has quietly sold about 200 highland horses a year since 1101 to Zanara's Golden Horse through a dealer at Tamowa. The horses a Zanari army would ride into Abara were bred at Mandi. The valleys also shelter the cattle raiders who lift Tsega herds from the Zutati pastures; Meron the Red Cow, daughter of a Mandari horseman killed raiding in 1091, leads 40 of them, and Yohannes sometimes rides with her. King Yared's plan to take a tenth in silver at the Mandi horse fairs would strike the house's purse directly, and the Mandari have answered every northern tax since 712 by riding to the next claimant.
dead: Mandar the Horse-Lord (668–731): Swore to Kasa II in 712.
Tesfaye Mandari (1019–1086): Led the southern horse for Kiros; father of Senait and Mesfin.
Senait Mandari (1044–1062): Kiros's wife and Tekle's mother.
marriages: 1041, with House Asfari: Lord Tesfaye Mandari married Princess Lulit, King Asmar's daughter.
1060, with House Asfari: Tesfaye's daughter Senait married King Kiros; mother of Tekle.
FAM-815.secrets: Mesfin took 8,000 suns of Zanari gold in 1104. Yohannes sells Mandi horses to the Golden Horse of Zanara.

FAM-816.y1105: Keepers of the Source and receivers of Tamar's river gift. Dawit Mekonen threatens to postpone the May rite; his daughter Tsion commands King Yonas's Blue Host.
FAM-816.arms: a white spring rising from a blue hill
FAM-816.founder: Mekonen of Mazezi (about 190 BR–130 BR), Source-priest of King Zeray I
FAM-816.power: The Source shrine and the Monuti terraces around Mazezi; receipt of Tamar's river gift at Koyako (20,000 bushels of wheat, 300 bolts of linen and 2,000 sheets of papyrus a year); the Loati channel; command of the Blue Host (about 35,000) through Tsion.
FAM-816.branches: the Keepers of the Source (Dawit's line); the Tefera line (cord members through Princess Hanna)
FAM-816.history: House Mekonen is older than any royal line in Abara except the first. In about 150 BR the priest Mekonen of Mazezi led King Zeray I to the spring where the Monuti rises and taught him to pour milk into it before the rains. His descendants have kept the Source for every dynasty since, and the Rememberers sing their line back to him. The Keeper performs the Source rite each May; the Tamari believe the flood depends on it. When Solen took Tamar the Mekonen made the rite a point of pride, and when the Tessarian engineers came in 986 with silver to dam the upper Monuti, it was the Keeper who told King Dagne that the Source would curse whoever blocked it, and Dagne sent them home. The River Gift Pact of 989 made the Keeper of the Source the man who receives Tamar's gift at Koyako each year, and the house has grown rich and proud on it. The Cord Law of 1022 made the Mekonen a cord house. Princess Hanna, Asfar's daughter, married Tefera Mekonen, the Keeper's brother, in 1034; their daughter Etenesh was King Kaleb's first queen and died in 1063, and a granddaughter, Bezawit, married King Yonas and died in 1099 bearing twins who did not live. Dawit Mekonen, of the Keeper's line and not of the cord, became Keeper in 1079. When Tamar's flood failed in 1087 and 1088 and Tamari envoys came to accuse the terraces, he sent them home with Source water and no apology. In 1098 he had his engineer Fikru cut a channel from a Loati headwater stream to the Mekonen terraces. It takes about a twentieth of the stream's water in the dry months, and under the pact of 989 Tamar could call it a dam. His daughter Tsion, born 1072, served in Yonas's household troops from 1090 and was made Marshal of the Blue Host in 1101. In December 1104 she met Marshal Juma of Zanara secretly at the border stream below Atani. In 1105 Dawit says he will postpone the May rite if Tamar's gift is not paid by 1 March, which Tamar's flood-priests would call a curse on the flood. The house's strength is that no king can do without it: the river gift, the rite and the Mekonen terraces of Mazezi all pass through its hands. Its weakness is the same: if Tamar ever measures the Loati channel, the Mekonen will be blamed for every low flood since 1098.
dead: Mekonen of Mazezi (about 190 BR–130 BR): First Keeper of the Source.
Tefera Mekonen (1010–1068): Married Princess Hanna; made the house a cord house.
Etenesh Mekonen (1040–1063): King Kaleb's first queen; died in childbirth.
marriages: 1034, with House Asfari: Tefera Mekonen married Princess Hanna, King Asfar's daughter.
1056, with House Asfari: Etenesh Mekonen married Kaleb; died in 1063.
1095, with House Asfari: Bezawit Mekonen, a cord daughter, married King Yonas; died in 1099.
FAM-816.rivals: House Tsega, the flood-priests of Tamar
FAM-816.secrets: The Loati channel of 1098 takes a twentieth of the stream in the dry months. Tsion has a private agreement with Marshal Juma of Zanara.

FAM-817.y1105: Royal tally-keepers; Almaz Teferi is Keeper of the Salt Bars for both courts and keeps two sets of books.
FAM-817.arms: a white salt bar crossed with a knotted cord on brown
FAM-817.founder: Teferi the Tally-Keeper (840–905), first Keeper of the Salt Bars under Queen Hirut
FAM-817.power: The office of Keeper of the Salt Bars; the books of both courts; 12,000 suns in a temple deposit at Tamar in Almaz's name.
FAM-817.history: House Teferi began with Queen Hirut's reforms. The same year she made the Knot Decree, she made her tally-keeper Teferi Keeper of the Salt Bars, the treasurer who counts the crown's tenth of grain and cattle and its store of salt bars, the everyday money of Abara. His descendants have kept the office, or trained whoever kept it, for 230 years. They kept the tallies in knotted cords until the River Gift Pact of 989 brought 2,000 sheets of Tamari papyrus a year up the Monuti, and then learned Tamari letters. Under the Compact of 1053 the Keeper had to split the treasury between two courts, and the Teferi began to keep two sets of books. Almaz Teferi, born 1064, daughter of a royal tally-keeper, learned letters from the bone-diggers' clerks and became Keeper in 1090, the year the twins were crowned. In 1103 she moved 12,000 suns of the shared treasury into a temple deposit at Tamar in her own name, as insurance if the courts go to war, and Seti the Scribe of Tamar keeps it quiet. In 1104 she signed the loan papers of Yonas's court with the Gold Houses of Zanara. She insists that Tamar's gift be paid in wheat, linen and papyrus as the pact of 989 says, and split between the courts, against Gebre Tsega and King Yared.
dead: Teferi the Tally-Keeper (840–905): First Keeper of the Salt Bars.
FAM-817.secrets: Almaz holds 12,000 suns of the shared treasury in a Tamar temple deposit in her own name.

FAM-621.y1105: Royal line of Hrimfell since 993. King Hraldr cannot stand, and the Thing of Midsummer 1105 must choose between his son Ulfar and a king who can walk.
FAM-621.arms: a white whale's tail rising from a black sea under a grey sky
FAM-621.founder: Jora, first Mother of Jotunhall in the old chant (about 250 BR); as a royal line, Grom the Mountain (950 to 1035)
FAM-621.power: The crown and the Mother's sole right to name candidates for it; Jotunhall hall-land with 850 giants and about 3,000 human hunters; the largest ivory store in the kingdom; the Hall Pairs of Jotunhall (48 giants); a share of every tusk and carved piece at Jotunhall.
FAM-621.branches: the Mothers' line: the eldest women, of whom Asta is the 52nd; the king's household at Jotunhall; Orm's children at Jotunhall, of ordinary size; the Ulfdal Mothers, grafted into the chant in 1000
FAM-621.bloodline: The Jotunhall line: Giants among giants
FAM-621.history: The Jotunhall line is the royal house of Hrimfell, counted through the Mothers of Jotunhall, the eldest women of the hall's eldest household. Jotunhall's own chant begins with Jora, a Mother of about 250 BR, and for most of its history the hall was one among several. It grew when the Warm Winters of 762 to 768 emptied the hall of Ulfdal, whose last giants moved into Jotunhall by 790 and brought their Mothers' chant with them. Jotunhall gave Hrimfell its fourth war-king, Hallvard the Trader (r. 818 to 857), who made the Ivory Peace with the Northreach and Eastfolk traders in 821. The line's greatness begins with Grom the Mountain, born in 950 to Alfhild, a woman of an ordinary Jotunhall household. He grew larger than any giant in any chant. He married Hervor, heir to the Mothers, in 975. In the Famine Winter he dragged a frozen whale 20 km across the ice to feed three halls, and the Thing of 993 made him king. At the Thing of 1000 he had the halls swear the Law of the Mothers: Hrimfell would always have a king, from the eldest line, named by its living Mother. The chant-keeper of Jotunhall then sang Jotunhall's Mothers as that eldest line, with 18 Mothers of dead Ulfdal at its head; the old chant, which Grani the Rememberer still knows, put Valdhall's and Torholm's Mothers first. Grom's size passed to all his daughters and none of his sons. His elder daughter Gudrun became the 51st Mother in 1041; her son Hrolf the Heavy (r. 1035 to 1049) had the great size, and her son Orm the Walker (r. 1049 to 1077) did not. Grom's younger daughter Gunnhild married Arnbjorn of Valdgard and bore Hraldr in 1040. Gudrun's daughter Asta became the 52nd Mother in 1074 and named her cousin Hraldr king in 1077. Hraldr married Hrolf's daughter Ragnhild, a carrier, so that their sons would have the size; their son Ulfar was born in 1068, and Ragnhild died in 1090. The line has always paid for its size. Grom ruled 30 years from a seat of whale vertebrae; Hrolf broke his hip in a fall on the ice and died of it; Hraldr has commanded from a sledge since the Hrimfell Raids; Ulfar has walked on crutches since 1102. One giant of the line eats more than a whole household, and in the hungry winter of 1103 Jotunhall ran short while Valdhall's pits were full. In 1105 the line faces its hardest Thing: its king privately wants a successor who can walk, its Mother will name only Ulfar, and its heir does not want the crown.
dead: Hallvard the Trader (770 to 857): War-king who made the Ivory Peace of 821. *Ruler:* Hallvard of Jotunhall (the Trader), Kingdom of Hrimfell, 818–857 (RUL-6034).
Grom the Mountain (950 to 1035): First permanent king; made the Law of the Mothers. *Ruler:* Grom the Mountain, Kingdom of Hrimfell, 993–1035 (RUL-6035).
Hervor, the 50th Mother (951 to 1041): Grom's wife; named Hrolf king in 1035.
Gudrun, the 51st Mother (978 to 1074): Grom's elder daughter; mother of Hrolf, Orm and Asta.
Hrolf the Heavy (1003 to 1049): King; died of a fall on the ice. *Ruler:* Hrolf of Jotunhall (the Heavy), Kingdom of Hrimfell, 1035–1049 (RUL-6036).
Orm the Walker (1011 to 1077): King without the size; walked every hall-land. *Ruler:* Orm of Jotunhall (the Walker), Kingdom of Hrimfell, 1049–1077 (RUL-6037).
marriages: 975, with The Jotunhall line: Grom married Hervor, heir to the Jotunhall Mothers.
1035, with The Hall of Valdgard: Grom's daughter Gunnhild married Arnbjorn of Valdgard; their son is Hraldr.
1062, with The Jotunhall line: Hraldr married his cousin Ragnhild, Hrolf's daughter, to double the blood.
FAM-621.rivals: The Hall of Torholm, The Hall of Valdhall
FAM-621.secrets: The Jotunhall Mothers' chant was changed in 1000: 18 of the 52 Mothers are Ulfdal's, and Grani knows the old order. Hraldr privately wants a king who can walk, Ulfar does not want the crown, and Asta will name only Ulfar.

FAM-622.y1105: The richest hall in grain and the seat of the ivory and unicorn-horn trade; Eldest Brenna leads the Grain Party at the Thing of 1105.
FAM-622.arms: a white walrus on barley gold
FAM-622.founder: Valda, first Mother of Valdhall in the old chant
FAM-622.power: The walrus beaches of the far west and the summer landing of the Northreach and Lakeland traders; the whale-tusk ('unicorn horn') trade, worth up to 3,000 suns a horn in the south; two years of grain in its pits; 590 giants and about 1,800 humans.
FAM-622.branches: Brenna's household at Valdhall; Skuli's hunting household on the walrus beaches; the Lindnes watch household; Ragnfrid Gatebreaker, in exile in the Free Marches
FAM-622.history: Valdhall is the far western hall of the White Coast, on the tundra by the walrus beaches, and the hall of Hrimfell's first king. In the Dimming its eldest, Hrimr the Wide (r. 9 BR to 26 AR), argued for taking in the starving Eastfolk hunters, and the Thing of 9 BR raised him king to do it; the land still bears his name. In the old chant that Grani knows, Valdhall's Mothers come first of all. In 821 Hallvard the Trader made the Ivory Peace at Valdhall, and since then the summer traders of Northreach and the Lakeland have landed there to weigh walrus ivory against grain, ale and iron. Valdhall has been the richest hall in grain ever since. In 1019 Thorve of Torvik crossed the sea from Frostholm in the hold of a Northreach cog to marry into Valdhall, and Brenna is her granddaughter. From 1059 the hall took the trade in the spiral tusks of the White Coast's small whales, which Northreach traders sell in the south as unicorn horn. Brenna's mother ran that trade until 1080 and Brenna after her, and Brenna became eldest in 1090. During the Hrimfell Raids she kept Valdhall's pairs at home and sold ivory all four summers, and in February 1098 she argued hardest for the Truce of Dobin. Her cousin Ragnfrid Gatebreaker, born at Valdhall in 1045, did fight; she burned a Drevnan fishing hamlet near Yarov in 1097, was named for punishment in the truce and fled into exile in the Free Marches. Brenna's younger brother Skuli leads the hall's walrus hunters and in 1104 showed a Drevnan trader the bay where the tusk-whales calve. Valdhall holds two years of grain in its pits and is buying the small halls' votes with it.
dead: Hrimr the Wide (72 BR to 26 AR): First war-king; took in the Eastfolk hunters. *Ruler:* Hrimr of Valdhall (the Wide), Kingdom of Hrimfell, 9 BR–26 (RUL-6031).
Thorve of Torvik (988 to 1062): Frostholm bride of 1019; Brenna's grandmother.
marriages: 1019, with The Hall of Torvik: Thorve of Torvik crossed from Frostholm to marry into Valdhall.
FAM-622.allies: House Coldwater, The Hall of Torvik
FAM-622.rivals: The Hall of Torholm, The Jotunhall line
FAM-622.secrets: Valdhall hides two years of grain to buy votes; Skuli has shown a Drevnan trader the tusk-whale calving bay; Ragnfrid is wanted by Drevna under the truce.

FAM-623.y1105: The shore hall on Whale Sound and the leader of the Walking Halls, who want a king who can walk and no peace with whalers.
FAM-623.arms: a grey stone club over white surf
FAM-623.founder: Tora, second Mother in the old chant
FAM-623.power: The southern shore on Whale Sound nearest the Drevnan whalers, a stone-walled boat harbor and the farming villages around Hrimborg; 480 giants and about 1,600 humans; the strongest pairs in the kingdom after Jotunhall's.
FAM-623.branches: Torvald's household of 14 at Torholm; the Skarhamar watch household
FAM-623.history: Torholm is the southern shore hall on Whale Sound, the closest to the Lakeland and to Drevna's whalers, and in the old chant its Mothers stand second only to Valdhall's. Its humans farm as well as hunt; the villages around Hrimborg grow barley and keep pigs. Torholm gave Hrimfell its second war-king. In the spring of 412 its own hunters rose after the hall had taken their whole winter catch, and the Thing raised its eldest, Bolverk the Hard (r. 412 to 441), to break the rising. He did it in two winters and then made the Hunters' Law, whose blood-price and sea-giving still stand. Torholm resented the Law of the Mothers of 1000, which shut it out of the crown, and it has voted against the Jotunhall line's candidates at every Thing where it dared. The present household of 14 is ruled by Torvald, eldest since 1086. When Drevna settled the Whale Coast after 1085 and its whalers began to kill Frost Leviathans, Torholm suffered first. Torvald's son Hakki was one of two giants killed by Drevnan crossbows at the Torholm shore in July 1096, and in August 1097 Torvald and his pair-partner Brodd, born into the household in 1062, broke the harbor gate of Dobin. Torvald spoke against the Truce of Dobin and lost. He now leads the Walking Halls, who want a king who can walk to the shore. Brodd binds Torvald's own failing knee each morning before the hall wakes, and Ulfar has secretly offered Torvald the war-leadership of the pairs in return for his vote.
dead: Bolverk the Hard (355 to 441): War-king who broke the Hunters' Rising and made the Hunters' Law. *Ruler:* Bolverk of Torholm (the Hard), Kingdom of Hrimfell, 412–441 (RUL-6032).
Hakki of Torholm (1077 to 1096): Torvald's son; killed at the Torholm shore.
FAM-623.rivals: The Jotunhall line, The Hall of Valdgard
FAM-623.secrets: Torvald's left knee is failing and Brodd hides it; Brodd kept a silver ring taken from a dead whaler at Dobin in breach of the truce.

FAM-624.y1105: The timber hall and school of the kingdom's fighting pairs; kin of the king and loyal to the Old Blood.
FAM-624.arms: two grey giants back to back under a green spruce
FAM-624.founder: Sigvald the Woodwright (790 to 880), who led Jotunhall households to the southern forest edge
FAM-624.power: The southern forest edge, the Eyheim Wood and the kingdom's richest farm villages (Hjalvik, Isahall, Thundset); 445 giants and about 2,200 humans; the Pair Hall of Valdgard, where every young giant of Hrimfell learns to fight.
FAM-624.branches: Eldest Hallgrim's household; the Pair Hall of Valdgard
FAM-624.history: Valdgard is the youngest of the great halls of Hrimfell. Its first households came from Jotunhall in 834 under Sigvald the Woodwright, to cut timber on the southern forest edge for the halls and for the stone border halls King Hallvard the Trader was building on the fells. The human tribute-folk who followed them herd reindeer and farm the villages of Hjalvik, Isahall and Thundset, the richest farmland in the kingdom. Because its timber and its fields make it rich, Valdgard has always kept close to Jotunhall. In 1035 Arnbjorn of Valdgard married Gunnhild, Grom's younger daughter, and their son is King Hraldr; Valdgard has backed the Jotunhall line at every Thing since. Valdgard is also where Hrimfell's young giants learn to fight. The Pair Hall of Valdgard teaches back-to-back pair fighting and stone throwing, and Ulfar trained there from 1093 beside Ragna, born at Valdgard in 1058. Ragna fought through the Hrimfell Raids, lost an ear at Yarov and lost her partner Hallgerd at the Torholm shore in 1096, a death she has always told wrongly. She has been master of the Pair Hall since 1099 and wants to be named war-leader of the pairs so that no new raid on Drevna can be made. Valdgard's eldest, Hallgrim, follows the king.
dead: Sigvald the Woodwright (790 to 880): Founded Valdgard.
Arnbjorn of Valdgard (995 to 1066): King Hraldr's father.
Hallgerd of Valdgard (1060 to 1096): Ragna's pair-partner; killed at the Torholm shore.
marriages: 1035, with The Jotunhall line: Arnbjorn of Valdgard married Gunnhild, Grom's daughter.
FAM-624.secrets: Ragna broke from her pair to chase a crossbowman at the Torholm shore, and Hallgerd died alone; she has said Hallgerd fell first.

FAM-625.y1105: Extinct as a hall since about 790; its blood runs in Jotunhall, and 18 of its Mothers are sung as Jotunhall's.
FAM-625.arms: a grey wolf on white ice
FAM-625.founder: Ulfa, first Mother of Ulfdal in the chant
FAM-625.power: None in 1105. Its name survives in the Ulfdal stones and in the first 18 Mothers of the Jotunhall chant, which underpin the Law of the Mothers.
FAM-625.history: Ulfdal was one of the nine halls that reached the White Coast at the end of the Long Walk North, and its ring of standing stones still stands a day's walk from Jotunhall. Its Mothers' chant was the longest on the coast. Ulfdal hunted the far ice, out where the sea froze thickest, and its giants were known as ice-walkers. When the sea ice failed in the Warm Winters of 762 to 768, the Thing raised Ulfdal's eldest, Thorgrim Icewalker (r. 762 to 769), as war-king to lead the halls on long hunts to the far ice. He kept the halls alive for seven winters and died on the ice in 769 with his pair-partner when a floe broke under them. The Warm Winters killed most of Ulfdal's households. By 790 its last giants had moved into Jotunhall and married there, and they brought the chant of the Ulfdal Mothers with them. At the Thing of 1000, when Grom the Mountain made the Law of the Mothers, the chant-keeper of Jotunhall sang 18 of those Ulfdal Mothers as the first Mothers of Jotunhall, which made Jotunhall the eldest line on the coast. Grani the Rememberer is the last giant who can sing the older chant, in which Ulfdal's Mothers are Ulfdal's and Valdhall's and Torholm's come first. Ulfdal itself is gone, but its blood runs in Jotunhall and its Mothers are chanted at every Thing.
dead: Thorgrim Icewalker (698 to 769): War-king of the Warm Winters; died on the ice. *Ruler:* Thorgrim of Ulfdal (Icewalker), Kingdom of Hrimfell, 762–769 (RUL-6033).
marriages: 790, with The Jotunhall line: The last Ulfdal giants married into Jotunhall.
FAM-625.secrets: The Jotunhall chant's first 18 Mothers are Ulfdal's; if Grani sings the old chant at the Thing of 1105, the Law of the Mothers loses its ground.

FAM-711.y1105: Ruling house of Sabra since 1025. Emir Karim holds the oil secret and a chest of about 800,000 suns; his sister holds the pearl fleet; his son holds the fire-boats and wants to strike first.
FAM-711.arms: an orange flame above a white pearl on black
FAM-711.founder: Bakr Sabrani, pearl merchant and governor of Sabra (935–1009)
FAM-711.power: The Emir's private chest of about 800,000 suns from fire-oil; the water-tax of a tenth; the best pearl of every boat each week; a third of the gulf's pearling boats (Jamila); the Camel Guard (2,000), 17,000 standing troops, 14 galleys and 30 fire-boats.
FAM-711.branches: The Emir's line (Karim and Tahir); The Azara line (Jamila and the pearl boats)
FAM-711.history: The Sabrani were pearl merchants of Sabra when it was a Qadiri governorship. In 971 Bakr Sabrani lent Sultan Idris II money for galleys, and Idris made him governor. Bakr was the first of the house with the Salt-skin: as a boy he sweated through his shirt in winter, licked salt from the drying racks and cramped on the boats, and his mother learned to feed him salted water. In 981 Sultan Munir let Bakr's son hold the office after him. Tahir Sabrani, governor from 1009, took Lucerna's offer in 1019 and refused the water-tax in October 1020. His son Farid led the camel riders who broke the Qadiri column in the Sabun Pass in 1022 and the fire-boats that burned 19 galleys on the Night of Fire, 19 August 1024. Tahir became Emir by the Peace of the Bahesh in 1025, and Farid married Nura Hazimi that year to bind the upland house. Farid ruled 1034–1060 and made the house what it is. He built the Oil Fort and the token law, kept the oil out of council and in the Emir's own chest, blackened the harbor towers, raised the Camel Guard and in 1051 sold Mag Brine the fire behind the Dragon of Blackreef. In 1035 he made the house law that every child of a Sabrani parent, son or daughter, takes the Sabrani name and grows up in the Emir's household at Sabra; the husbands of Sabrani daughters live there too. He fought at noon in August with a servant beside him carrying salted water, and the city called him 'the Dry' because it never saw him drink. His son Nasir, Emir 1060–1086, built the slave-dived pearl trade with House Zarani and died after the Dry Month of 1086, having fasted without salt as a pious Emir was expected to. Karim, Emir since 2 October 1086, learned the oil secret on his first night and has doubled the chest. His sister Jamila is Pearl-Master and the second fortune of the realm; his son Tahir, named for the founder, commands the fire-boats. The house is rich, young and exposed. Its power rests on a trade that three foreign powers would go to war over, and its members cannot keep the Dry Month fast in public without risking their lives. Karim's palace by the harbor towers holds about 40 Sabrani of the blood with their husbands and wives, all under the Emir's eye as the house law requires, and every one of them eats salt at every meal. Tahir, the heir, has his great-grandfather's taste for noon drills.
dead: Bakr Sabrani (935–1009): First governor of the house and first carrier of the Salt-skin.
Tahir Sabrani the Founder (962–1034): Led the revolt and became first Emir. *Ruler:* Tahir Sabrani (Emir Tahir the Founder), Emirate of Sabra, 1025–1034 (RUL-7151).
Farid Sabrani the Dry (990–1060): Burned the Qadiri fleet; built the oil state. *Ruler:* Emir Farid Sabrani the Dry, Emirate of Sabra, 1034–1060 (RUL-7152).
Nasir Sabrani the Pearl-Emir (1027–1086): Built the slave-dived pearl trade; died after the fast. *Ruler:* Nasir Sabrani (Emir Nasir the Pearl-Emir), Emirate of Sabra, 1060–1086 (RUL-7153).
marriages: 1025, with House Hazimi: Farid married Nura Hazimi, mother of Nasir, to bind the upland house to the emirate.
1053, with a pearl master family of Azara: Nasir married Rania of Azara, who ran two pearling boats; mother of Karim and Jamila.
1076, with a pearl master family of Azara: Karim married Huda, a pearl master's daughter; mother of Tahir.
FAM-711.secrets: The house sells fire-oil to Lucerna and supplies the Dragon of Blackreef; the Oil-Master's tally sticks in the Emir's treasury prove both. Farid 'the Dry' drank salted water every hour of every fight.

FAM-712.y1105: Hereditary oil-masters of Sabra. Qasim Nafari runs the seeps and boiling-sheds and keeps the tally sticks of every jar sold to Blackreef and Lucerna.
FAM-712.arms: a black jar with an orange tongue of flame, on sand
FAM-712.words: The fire keeps its own count.
FAM-712.power: The Oil-Master's office; sole right to enter the boiling-sheds; the craft of boiling fire-oil, taught only to Nafari sons; about 200 slave and free oil-workers; the store caves of the Oil Fort.
FAM-712.branches: The Boilers of Zariya, who work the sheds; The Tally line, which keeps the jar counts in the Emir's treasury
FAM-712.history: Nafar the Pitch-Boiler boiled seep pitch in pots on the shore at Zariya about 870 and sold it to gulf boatmen for caulking and lamps. His family kept the trade for three generations. About 958 Wafiq Nafari found that the thin oil that boils off first burns on water, and the governor of Sabra told the family to show no one. The Nafari boiled the oil for Tahir Sabrani's revolt and for the boats of the Night of Fire in 1024. When Farid built the Oil Fort in 1036, he made the Nafari hereditary oil-masters and gave them sole entry to the boiling-sheds. The craft is taught only to Nafari sons, at 12; Nafari daughters marry out and never learn it. The family counts every jar on notched tally sticks kept in the Emir's treasury, a habit that began as honesty and is now the proof that could start a war. Qasim, taught at 12 by his father, became Oil-Master in 1080 under Emir Nasir and swore to keep the tallies for Karim in 1086. The house is proud and narrow: it refuses to let Saad the Burnt's Oil Yard boil its own oil, and it treats the oil slaves as tools. In November 1104 a slave boiler burned a shed at Zariya so that three men could flee, and Qasim has hidden the cause from the Emir while he hunts them.
dead: Nafar the Pitch-Boiler (about 840–905): Founder; boiled seep pitch for caulking.
Wafiq Nafari (925–990): Found the light oil that burns on water, about 958.
marriages: 1040, with House Sabrani: A Nafari daughter married a Sabrani cousin in Farid's household; she never learned the craft.
FAM-712.secrets: Qasim's tally sticks record every jar sold to Blackreef and Lucerna. He has hidden that the November 1104 fire was set by a slave, and one of the three runaways knows the way to the seeps.

FAM-713.y1105: Upland lords of the date gardens and camel pastures of Hazim, holding the road north toward Qadir. Walid Hazimi leads the Old Allegiance and has secretly offered to bring Sabra back under the Sultan; his nephew Nuri trains the Emir's camel riders.
FAM-713.arms: a white camel on a red hill, on sand
FAM-713.words: We ride where the road goes.
FAM-713.founder: Idris of Hazim, camel lord of the uplands (about 850–915)
FAM-713.power: Hazim Castle and town, the upland date gardens and camel pastures; about 2,400 camel riders; the Camel School of Hazim, which trains the Emir's Camel Guard; the tolls of the Sabun road on the Sabran side.
FAM-713.branches: The lords of Hazim Castle (Walid); The Camel School line (Nuri)
FAM-713.history: The Hazimi are camel lords of the uplands above the gulf, named for their town. They served the Qadiri governors as road guards from the 880s and rode for Sultan Zahir II in 1022. In the Sabun Pass that October about 300 Hazimi riders died of thirst on the way down after the Sabrans took the column's water camels, while Prince Jalal rode home on half a water-skin. In 1024 the house changed sides and let Sabran riders into the Basir fields, in return for its own grazing and the Sabun road tolls. In 1025 Nura Hazimi married Farid Sabrani, and her son Nasir became Emir. Some of the house never forgot where it came from. Walid Hazimi fought camel raiders on the Sabun road as a young man and took a lance in the hip in 1075; he became Lord of Hazim in 1080 and stood at Karim's crowning in 1086. His younger brother died of heat-stroke chasing raiders in 1088, and Walid raised the boy, Nuri, who became master of the Camel School in 1100. Walid believes the oil trade will bring a northern war that Sabra cannot win. In November 1104 he wrote to Qadir's Grand Vizier offering to bring Sabra back under the Sultan as a vassal if Qadir's fleet stays in port, and Nuri saw the courier leave.
dead: Idris of Hazim (about 850–915): Founder; camel lord and road guard for the Qadiri governors.
Nura Hazimi (1004–1066): Wife of Farid the Dry and mother of Emir Nasir.
marriages: 1025, with House Sabrani: Nura Hazimi married Farid Sabrani.
FAM-713.secrets: Walid's letter of November 1104 offers Sabra to Qadir as a vassal. Nuri knows and has told no one.

FAM-714.y1105: Lords of the South March and the slave-takers of Sabra. Musa Zarani supplies most of the gulf's slave divers and sold Sandfolk children in 1103.
FAM-714.arms: a black rope coiled on a white field
FAM-714.founder: Jafar Zarani, caravan captain, made Lord of the South March by Farid (998–1063)
FAM-714.power: Zaran and the South March villages; about 600 slave-riders; the slave pens of Zaran; a share in Jamila Sabrani's pearl boats.
FAM-714.branches: The lords of Zaran; The slave-riders who raid the Western Veld
FAM-714.history: Jafar Zarani was a caravan captain whom Emir Farid made Lord of the South March in 1041 to hold the frontier toward the Western Veld against raiders. The house grew rich when Emir Nasir wanted more pearls. From 1062 Zarani riders raided Veld villages for young divers and sold them at Zaran. Musa Zarani, born in 1060, rode on his first slave raid at 17 and became Lord of the South March in 1089. In 1094 his riders took about 200 young divers in the Veld, among them the boy now called Bilal Nine-Fathom. The house and Jamila Sabrani's pearl masters stand together as the Pearl Masters faction against Mahmud the Just, whose rulings free converted divers. In 1103 Zarani captains brought in 30 children from the Sand Clan border camps at Marad and swore they were Veld-born. A Sandfolk may never be enslaved by clan law or by the Book, and Clan Marad has begun to ask where its children went. Musa's riders work with Veld headmen who sell their neighbors' children for iron, cloth and salt. His pens at Zaran hold 300 to 500 captives before each pearling season, and the free divers of Azara call the house 'the Rope'. Mahmud the Just has twice been refused entry to the pens.
dead: Jafar Zarani (998–1063): Founder; first Lord of the South March.
marriages: 1082, with a pearl master family of Azara: Musa married into the Azara pearl masters, tying the slave pens to the boats.
FAM-714.secrets: Thirty of the captives sold at Zaran in 1103 were Sandfolk children from the Marad camps. If the Sand Clans prove it, Sabra's Gold Road guides could walk away.

FAM-321.y1105: Kings of Velgrad since 736. The king is a head taller than other men, going blind in his headaches and 33; his heir is five, and the regency is already being fought over.
FAM-321.arms: a black bear standing upright under a red lamp-flame on a field of white
FAM-321.founder: Borislav Sevrin (700–758), commander of the Eastern March and first King of Velgrad
FAM-321.power: The crown lands around Velgrad, about a fifth of the realm's people; half the channel through-toll and a tenth of every river cargo; a standing army of 50,000, the Bear Guard (600) and the channel squadron of 38 galleys and 22 cogs; the three Neck road stations held from Andros; the crowning bond with the Patriarch of Dawn.
FAM-321.branches: The royal line at the Bear Keep; Princess Vesna's line, married into House Tessaran; Monastery princes of the Tvernik and Malova houses (no heirs)
FAM-321.history: The Sevrins were Eastfolk officers of the Solen legions, from the channel town of Sevina. Borislav Sevrin, born in 700, stood a head over other men at 18 and carried the black bear standard of the Eastern March legion; by 728 he commanded the March. In 733 he made his bargain with Luminary Bogumil, in 735 he took 7,000 soldiers and 22 galleys over to the Dawn Church, and on Dawn Feast 736 Bogumil crowned him first King of Velgrad. The bear standard became the royal arms, and the red lamp-flame of the Dawn was set above it. Fifteen kings have followed father to son, without a break, for 369 years. The house has had two kinds of king: ordinary men who lived long, and bear-blood giants who did not. Velimir grew huge and died at 42 in 866. Radoslav the Bear, a head taller than his guards, beat Tessaria at Lake Ostec in 957, made the Code of Radoslav in 962 and lived to 56, the only giant of the line to pass 50. Miroslav, 208 cm, lost the Lakeland War and 5,000 men (WAR-30) and died at 47 in 1041. His son Dobrin, crowned at eight under the regency of his mother Anka Tolmir, grew to ordinary height and ruled 57 years. Since Vladan III the house has measured every Sevrin boy against a notched doorpost in the Bear Keep each Midwinter. A prince who stops growing early is quietly sent to a monastery: Prince Kazimir Sevrin (1000–1069), Miroslav's younger brother, was sent to the Dawn house at Tvernik at 14 and outlived both his brothers by decades. Sevrin princes are named for great kings and never for one who died young. The house marries the great lords of its own realm and sends its daughters abroad to buy armies. In 1075 Dobrin's eldest daughter Vesna married Prince Andros of Tessaria; she has been her brother's eyes at Andros's court since 1098 and sends copies of his council papers to the Keeper of the Seal. Her son Nikos grew to ordinary height. Dobrin's only son Stanislav stood a head over other men at 17. In 1097 he married Zora Koren, daughter of the Lord Marshal; she was born a Koren and belongs to this house by marriage. Their son Radoslav was born in 1099 and named for the Bear; a second child died at birth in 1102. Stanislav was crowned on 2 July 1098. In November 1104 he went blind for a moment in the practice yard, and in December he signed a sealed letter naming Zora regent if he dies. The house that was founded by a general's bargain with a priest now depends on a queen's sealed letter and a five-year-old's growth.
dead: Borislav Sevrin (700–758): Commander of the Eastern March and first King of Velgrad. *Ruler:* Borislav Sevrin (Borislav I the Founder), Kingdom of Velgrad, 736–758 (RUL-3201).
Velimir Sevrin (824–866): Bear-blood king who died at 42. *Ruler:* Velimir Sevrin, Kingdom of Velgrad, 846–866 (RUL-3206).
Lubomir the Fur-King (849–901): Chartered the Fur Staple. *Ruler:* Lubomir Sevrin (the Fur-King), Kingdom of Velgrad, 866–901 (RUL-3207).
Radoslav the Bear (925–981): 211 cm; victor of Lake Ostec and maker of the Code. *Ruler:* Radoslav the Bear, Kingdom of Velgrad, 955–981 (RUL-3210).
Miroslav Sevrin (994–1041): Lost the Lakeland War; died of heart failure at 47. *Ruler:* Miroslav Sevrin, Kingdom of Velgrad, 1024–1041 (RUL-3213).
Kazimir Sevrin (1000–1069): Sent to a monastery at 14 when he stopped growing; outlived his brothers.
marriages: 1032, with House Tolmir: Miroslav weds Anka Tolmir, later regent for their son Dobrin.
1075, with House Tessaran: Princess Vesna weds Prince Andros by the Compact of the Dawn Wedding.
1097, with House Koren: Prince Stanislav weds Zora Koren.
FAM-321.allies: House Koren, House Volan, House Tessaran
FAM-321.rivals: House Tidewell, House Dravic, The Holy See
FAM-321.secrets: The founding bargain of 733; the staged rising; the king's blind moments and the sealed regency letter; the heir's false notch on the doorpost.

FAM-322.y1105: Hereditary Channel-Masters of Velgrad since 1010, hungry for all the channel tolls and preparing the fire rafts of the staged rising.
FAM-322.arms: a black galley on a red sea under a white star
FAM-322.founder: Captain Jaros Volan (701–766), who brought his galley over to Borislav in 735
FAM-322.power: The Channel-Mastership: the Sevany toll fort and chain towers, 38 war galleys and 22 armed cogs, about 7,000 rowers and sailors; the Sevany Hooks (1,600); a share of the toll chest; the eight hulls below Mount Dobava.
FAM-322.branches: The Volans of Sevany; The Volans of Sevina, nearly wiped out in 1009
FAM-322.history: The Volans have been sailors of the east shore for as long as the shore has had galleys. Captain Jaros Volan commanded one of the 22 galleys of the Solen channel squadron at Sevany, and in 735 he was the first captain to bring his ship over to Borislav Sevrin and the Dawn. The kings rewarded the family with land on the channel shore between Sevany and Sevina, and for 270 years the Volans captained the royal galleys without ever holding the command. The War of the Channel (WAR-26) made them. When King Edmund of Greyhaven doubled the toll in 1006, King Bogdan ordered toll forts built at Sevany and Sevina, and Kazimir Volan (975–1040) built them. Off Beaconstone in July 1008 he held the Velgradan line in the tide race when the royal admiral was killed. In 1009 Greyhaven galleys burned 60 fishing boats and the toll fort at Sevina; Kazimir's brother and two sons died there, with most of the Sevina branch of the house. When the Treaty of the Two Shores was signed in 1010, Bogdan made Kazimir the first Channel-Master of Velgrad, and the office has passed in the family since. Every Volan heir is taken to the burned stones of the old Sevina fort at 12 and told who burned it. Under the Volans the squadron grew from 22 galleys in 1010 to 38 in 1105, and the Sevany yards learned to build armed cogs. The Volans also keep the chain towers of the Sevany toll fort and the debt-rowers: men sentenced for debt row the toll galleys under Volan captains, a few hundred each season. Radek Volan, born in 1058, watched the smoke of the Black Dragon rise from the channel off the Sevina shore in July 1071, aged 13. He became Channel-Master in 1094. In 1099 he began to suspect that Greyhaven's Toll-House was shaving Velgrad's half of the through-toll, and he has paid for stolen copies of its ledgers ever since, to prove a cheat that would justify war.
