In the autumn of 1104 he bought eight condemned hulls at Sevany, three of them built at Greyhaven's own Brookhurst yards, and began fitting them with pitch and Smokewell sulfur in a creek below Mount Dobava. He means to loose them on a July dusk, 34 years after 1071, and take all the tolls in the panic. It is the revenge his house has waited 95 years for, and if it fails it will bring Greyhaven and Aldmark down on Sevany.
dead: Jaros Volan (701–766): First captain to bring his galley over to the Dawn in 735.
Kazimir Volan (975–1040): Built the toll forts, held the line off Beaconstone, first Channel-Master.
FAM-322.secrets: The staged rising and the stolen copies of Greyhaven's toll ledgers.

FAM-323.y1105: Marcher lords of the Ostec March and the richest lenders in Velgrad. The head is Lord Marshal and the queen's father; his son commands the volunteers in the Neck; he expects to rule as regent.
FAM-323.arms: a silver lance across a black marsh reed on a field of green
FAM-323.founder: Ostoja Koren (921–985), captain who held the marsh flank at Lake Ostec
FAM-323.power: The Ostec March with Yarec (22,400) and the Ostmir road; the Ostec Lances (2,400); the office of Lord Marshal and command of the royal army of 50,000; debts owed by House Ordane (40,000 marks, half of Calossa pledged), by other northern Tessarian barons, by a Temple-faith baron of Livia's south (20,000 marks) and by the Veskovs of Ostmir; the captaincy of the Bear Guard through Varin Strak.
FAM-323.branches: The lords of Yarec (main line); Koren vassal houses of the Ostec March, among them the Straks
FAM-323.history: House Koren was made on the shore of Lake Ostec. In September 957 Ostoja Koren, a captain of Radoslav the Bear, held the marsh flank of the narrow neck of land where Velgrad's 8,000 broke Cassian Reed's 10,000. After the Treaty of Novgrad in 958 Radoslav gave him the march lands around Yarec and the duty of guarding the southern border. The Korens built the Ostec Lances, the only Velgradan knights who fight in the open, and for a century they watched the Tessarian border from Yarec and the Ostmir Gate. When the Tessarian governors fled the Free Marches in 1045 and 1047, the lands south of the gate fell lordless, and the Korens turned from guarding the border to lending across it. Northern Tessarian lords needed silver after the empire fell, and the Korens had it from their march tolls. Lord Zoran Koren inherited at 22 in 1072, led the Ostec Lances to the Neck under the Compact of the Dawn Wedding in 1075, and from 1080 lent to Andros's barons. House Ordane alone owes him 40,000 marks with half the Calossa lands as security. King Dobrin made him Lord Marshal in 1092. In 1097 Zoran married his daughter Zora to Prince Stanislav, and in 1098 she was crowned queen beside him. His son Anton, born in 1074, went south with the volunteers in 1096, led the storm of Doria in 1103 and holds the left of Andros's line at Coreria. In 1103 Zoran also lent 20,000 marks, through an Ostran middleman, to a Temple-faith baron of Queen Livia's south, so that House Koren holds debts on both sides of the Neck whoever wins. The house also holds the Ostmir lands in all but name. Lord Pavo Veskov of Ostmir died in 1101 deep in debt to Koren, and the Korens say a second will pledged his lands to them; his widow Dana produced only the first will and refuses to send her lances south. The Korens are marcher folk by habit. They speak the Marchfolk speech of the border as well as Eastfolk, hire half-orc axemen like Rurik Greytusk's company for the Neck, and will not grant march land to them. He has placed his vassal Varin Strak as captain of the Bear Guard, and Varin sends him a weekly report on the king's health. He wants the Lords' Bench to name him regent-in-waiting for his grandson. He does not know that the king has already named his daughter instead, and that his son draws the pay of 300 dead volunteers.
dead: Ostoja Koren (921–985): Held the marsh flank at Lake Ostec and founded the house.
marriages: 1097, with House Sevrin: Zora Koren weds Prince Stanislav.
FAM-323.rivals: House Tolmir, The Veskovs of Ostmir
FAM-323.secrets: Zoran Koren holds Tessarian debts on both sides of the war and spies on the king through the Bear Guard; Anton Koren draws pay for about 300 dead volunteers.

FAM-324.y1105: Fur and river lords of the Tolek Vale and keepers of the royal purse. Their head is Lord Treasurer and leads the Purse Bench against the war money.
FAM-324.arms: a gold sable on a blue river between two silver barges
FAM-324.founder: Lord Bratko Tolmir (835–898), first warden of the Fur Staple on the Tolek
FAM-324.power: The Tolek Vale with Koritsa (22,000); the river barges of the Fur Road and the king's tenth on river cargo; the office of Lord Treasurer, with the channel toll chest, the fur-tax and the money sent to Andros; a cousin in Ostra who reads the bankers' secrets.
FAM-324.branches: The Tolmirs of Koritsa (main line); The Mareks, poor cousins of the house, fur factors at Ostra
FAM-324.history: House Tolmir rose with the fur trade. When King Lubomir chartered the Fur Staple in 870, he made Bratko Tolmir, lord of the river landings around Koritsa, warden of the staple on the Tolek, and every barge of pelts and wax from the Lakeland has paid the Tolmirs' clerks ever since. The house grew rich on the Fur Road (TR-10) and lost much of it in the Black Cough of 917, when the Tolek villages emptied. It learned to count, and it learned to keep its own books: the Tolmir tally-rolls of the Fur Road, kept at Koritsa since 870, are the oldest trade records in the kingdom, and the Lord Treasurer still checks the crown's fur-tax against them. In 1032 Anka Tolmir married King Miroslav, and when he died in 1041 the Lords' Bench named her regent for their eight-year-old son Dobrin. She ruled with the Bench for eight years, paid the debts of the Lakeland War out of fur-staple money, and handed Dobrin a full treasury in 1049. Since then a Tolmir has usually kept the king's purse. The house has always wanted peace with Drevna, because the Lakeland's furs and silk come down the Tolek, and peace with Greyhaven, because the pelts go out by the channel. The Tolek Vale lies on the Drevnan border, and every time Velgrad and Drevna quarrel the barges stop. The Tolmirs opposed Miroslav's war in 1033 and lost two sons in it all the same, both killed at Kraina in 1034. When Drevna raised the silk toll at Lubany in 1100, the house argued against closing the Tolek, since a closed river hurts Koritsa first, and it keeps quiet dealings with House Lubec of Lubany, which holds Drevna's silk staple. Mirek Tolmir, born in 1061 at Koritsa, grew rich on the barges and became Lord Treasurer in 1098, the year Stanislav was crowned. In 1099, when the money sent to Andros passed 100,000 marks, he founded the Purse Bench to stop it. His poor cousin Lidia Marek, a fur merchant's widow at Ostra, sells harbor gossip to the Keeper of the Seal and sends the same news to him. In November 1104 her letter told him that Andros's and Livia's envoys are talking peace at Ostra. He has hidden it from the king, because a peace would end the war payments he hates, and if the king learns it from someone else, the Treasurer will be the first man the Lamp Party calls a traitor.
dead: Bratko Tolmir (835–898): First warden of the Fur Staple on the Tolek.
Anka Tolmir (1012–1063): Queen of Miroslav and regent for Dobrin, 1041–1049.
marriages: 1032, with House Sevrin: Anka Tolmir weds King Miroslav.
FAM-324.secrets: Mirek Tolmir has hidden the Ostran peace talks from the king.

FAM-325.y1105: Lords of the Redcrown Heights, its sulfur pits and its pilgrim road. Their head is Keeper of the Seal and runs the king's couriers and informers.
FAM-325.arms: a red mountain with a gold flame on a field of black
FAM-325.founder: Lord Dragan Belak (731–795), warden of the Redcrown pilgrim road
FAM-325.power: Belansk (23,400) and the Redcrown Heights; the sulfur pits at Yarnik and Yasov; a fee from every pilgrim to Redcrown; the Keeper's seal and a web of couriers and informers from Ostra to Lubany.
FAM-325.history: When the Dawn Cathedral was consecrated on Dawn Feast 772, King Branimir gave the road to Redcrown, whose glow the Dawn calls the Lamp's embers, to Dragan Belak, a captain of the Bear Guard, to guard the pilgrims and keep a fee from each. The Belaks found that the volcano's slopes were rich in sulfur, and their pits at Yarnik and Yasov have sold sulfur for pitch-pots, medicines and dyes ever since. Every August, when pilgrims camp below Redcrown to watch its glow, the house takes its fee. Vera Belak inherited at 24 in 1090, when her brother died in a pit collapse. Stanislav made her Keeper of the Seal in 1098, and she built a web of couriers and paid informers from Ostra to Lubany; her agent Lidia Marek buys secrets from the servants of the Ostran banks. Her pits were to supply the sulfur for the fire rafts. In September 1104 a rockfall flooded the best of them, and she sent the Channel-Master only a third of what she promised, letting him think the carts were late. His buyers bought the rest across the channel at Smokewell, where Greyhaven's own diggers sold it.
dead: Dragan Belak (731–795): First warden of the Redcrown pilgrim road.
FAM-325.secrets: The Redcrown pits flooded in September 1104, and the house has hidden its failure to supply the fire-raft sulfur.

FAM-326.y1105: The largest fur house in Velgrad, heading the Fur Staple, and a quiet voice of the Purse Bench for peace and lower tolls.
FAM-326.arms: a black marten on a field of white fur
FAM-326.founder: Borek Marten (born 1049), son of a Solgrad trapper
FAM-326.power: The headship of the Fur Staple of Velgrad, through which every exported pelt must pass; warehouses at Velgrad, Solgrad and Koritsa; buyers on the Silk Road east of the Tusk toll camp; credit with fur buyers at Sevany and Greyhaven.
FAM-326.branches: The fur house of Velgrad; Buyers at Solgrad and Koritsa
FAM-326.history: House Marten is new money. Borek Marten was born in 1049 at Velgrad, the son of a trapper from the North Woods around Solgrad, and sold his first sable at 12. The house owns no land: only warehouses at Velgrad, Solgrad and Koritsa, run by Borek's two sons, and the debts of half the trappers of the North Woods. He opened his own fur house in 1072, bought pelts from the Solgrad trappers before the Tolmir clerks could, and by 1080 had the largest fur house in the kingdom. In 1088 the merchants of the Fur Staple, chartered by King Lubomir in 870, chose him as their head. Since 1099 he has sat with Mirek Tolmir's Purse Bench, because the war money and the channel tolls both eat his profits. From 1101 his buyers have used a quieter road east of the Tusk Clans' silk toll camp, guided by Anvar the Guide, and since 1103 he has written in secret to Lord Godric Redley of Greyhaven about a private pact to cut the channel tolls on grain and furs. If the staged rising starts a channel war, his trade stops; if his letters are found, he hangs.
FAM-326.secrets: Borek Marten writes secretly to Godric Redley of Greyhaven and dodges the Tusk silk toll on a hidden track.

FAM-331.y1105: Rulers of Drevna since 802. The queen and her heir have the Listener's ears; the heir collapses at drums, and the queen's husband leads the party that would set her aside for a son who is secretly married.
FAM-331.arms: a silver open ear above three blue wavy lines on a green field
FAM-331.founder: Dragomir Dravic (764–829), lord of Drevna town and first King of Drevna
FAM-331.power: The crown lands of the Crown Lakes, with the richest honey and wax estates; a standing army of 64,000, the Listener's Guard (400) and the Still Hall; the queen's listeners under the Queen's Ear; a tenth of every silk caravan at Lubany and the Dromir river tolls; the crowning bond with the Dawn Church.
FAM-331.branches: The line of Ludmila the Listener (the only line since 1010); The cadet line of Lord Vratislav, ended in 1010
FAM-331.history: The Dravic were lords of Drevna town before there was a kingdom, keepers of the ferries and fish-weirs of the Crown Lakes and leaders of the Lake Council that met each New Year's Day to reckon debts. When the lake lords broke from Velgrad in May 802, the council crowned Dragomir Dravic, and the house has held the crown for 303 years. For two centuries its kings were ordinary men. Radim I bought peace from the fleeing March orcs in 887 for 2,000 horses and set the Zorac wardens at Zorin. Svetozar II died of the Black Cough in 917. Radim II built the island citadel that became the Listening Tower. Ozren buried four of his five children, and his only living child, Ludmila, was born in 984 with ears no one in the family had had before her. Ludmila was crowned in 1010. Her cousin Lord Vratislav Dravic sent two men with knives on the night after her crowning; she heard them whisper behind the wall, and he was hanged within the month. The cadet line ended with him, and every Dravic since descends from Ludmila. In 1011 she married Lord Ostromir Lubec of Lubany. She won the Lakeland War by retreat, fire and ice (WAR-30), freed the levies who fought for her, and in 1048 wrote the Code that makes the eldest child heir, son or daughter. Her son Yaromir married Vesela Zorac of Zorin in 1043. Their sons Radim (1044–1064) and Svetozar (1047–1064) both had the ears, and both fell to the orc drums at Zorek and were killed. Their daughter Milena became heir at eight. Yaromir, afraid that she too would fall to the drums, had a clause slipped into the Code in 1066 that lets the Lake Council set aside an heir who cannot lead the army. Milena married Pavel Brodar of Brodava in 1079; he was born a Brodar and is counted with his own house, which he still heads. She was crowned in 1085 by Velgrad's Patriarch, not her own, turned the kingdom north to the Whale Coast, and made the Truce of Dobin with the giants in 1098. Her daughter Ludmila, born 1080 and named for the Listener, has the ears and has fainted at Tusk drums twice, at Sevmir in 1098 and at the Harvest Home feast of 1104, when her own father paid a thief to beat the drum. Her son Yaromir, born 1084, lacks the ears, and the Prince's Party wants him made heir. At dawn on 22 September 1104 he married Alena Birchwood, a free beekeeper's daughter of the Crown Lakes, on the lake shore before two witnesses, a lawful marriage by Drevnan custom that no one at court knows of, while his mother is arranging to marry him to Linnet Tidewell of Greyhaven at Sea Opening. The house that was saved by one woman's hearing is now divided by it.
dead: Dragomir Dravic (764–829): First King of Drevna. *Ruler:* Dragomir Dravic (Dragomir I the Lake-King), Kingdom of Drevna, 802–829 (RUL-3301).
Radim I the Toll-Taker (844–889): Let the March orcs pass in 887 and set the Zorac wardens. *Ruler:* Radim Dravic (Radim I the Toll-Taker), Kingdom of Drevna, 870–889 (RUL-3304).
Queen Ludmila the Listener (984–1052): First carrier of the Listener's ears; won the Lakeland War and gave the Code. *Ruler:* Queen Ludmila the Listener, Kingdom of Drevna, 1010–1052 (RUL-3309).
Yaromir Dravic (1014–1085): Lost the Tusk War and both sons; signed the rye tribute. *Ruler:* Yaromir Dravic, Kingdom of Drevna, 1052–1085 (RUL-3310).
Prince Radim Dravic (1044–1064): Elder son of Yaromir; fell at the drums at Zorek.
Prince Svetozar Dravic (1047–1064): Younger son of Yaromir; killed at Zorek.
marriages: 1011, with House Lubec: Ludmila weds Lord Ostromir Lubec; Lubany gets the silk staple.
1043, with House Zorac: Yaromir weds Vesela Zorac of Zorin, mother of Milena.
1079, with House Brodar: Milena weds Pavel Brodar of Brodava.
1104, with The Birchwoods, free beekeepers of the Crown Lakes: Prince Yaromir weds Alena Birchwood in secret at dawn on Harvest Home.
FAM-331.allies: House Lubec, House Lark, House Tidewell
FAM-331.rivals: House Sevrin, Clan Ironhide, The Jotunhall line
FAM-331.secrets: The succession clause of 1066 was added without a vote; the queen knows her husband paid for the drum at Harvest Home and has done nothing; Prince Yaromir is already married.

FAM-332.y1105: Wardens of the Steppe March and cousins of the queen. The head is Lord Marshal and is holding back the winter rye; his daughter doubts him.
FAM-332.arms: a grey stone wall with a black crossbow above it, on a field of steppe yellow
FAM-332.founder: Ratko Zorac (861–920), first warden of the steppe edge at Zorin
FAM-332.power: The Steppe March, with the walled town of Zorin, Sevmir and the Sevmir line; the Zorin Crossbows (3,000) and the Zorin Crossbow Yard; the office of Lord Marshal and command of the army of 64,000; the winter rye carts held at Sevmir.
FAM-332.history: House Zorac was set on the steppe edge to watch the orcs. When the March clans passed the Lakeland's southern rim in 887, King Radim I made Ratko Zorac, a lake lord's younger son, warden of the steppe edge at Zorin, and the Zoracs walled the town in stone over the next 30 years. For two centuries they kept the Steppe March with crossbows and wagon forts, trading with orc herders in peace and fighting their raiders in bad winters. In 1043 Vesela Zorac married Prince Yaromir, and she was the mother of Queen Milena; the present Lord Marshal is the queen's first cousin. In the spring of 1063 Zorin's walls turned back about 5,000 orcs of the Tusk Clans after three weeks. A year later, at Zorek, Vadim Zorac, 16, saw both princes, his cousins, fall at the war-drums. He broke and ran with the rout, and his father's men wrote him into the list of the last stand. He stood in the escort at the Treaty of Thardush in 1066 and swore he would one day end the rye. Milena made him Lord Marshal in 1086. In December 1104 he held the 2,000 bushels of winter rye at Sevmir, saying the roads were unsafe, and his party, the Rye Shame, wants the grazing line pushed back east. His daughter Mara, master of the Zorin Crossbow Yard since 1096, commanded the guard on the rye carts and wrote privately to Irina Lubec that the roads were safe. The house is split over the one thing it was made to do.
dead: Ratko Zorac (861–920): First warden of the steppe edge.
Vesela Zorac (1024–1070): Queen of Yaromir and mother of Queen Milena.
marriages: 1043, with House Dravic: Vesela Zorac weds Prince Yaromir.
FAM-332.secrets: Vadim Zorac ran at Zorek in 1064; his daughter has told the Silk Peace party that his reason for holding the rye is false.

FAM-333.y1105: Lake lords of Brodava and masters of the sleds and the lake fleet. The head is the queen's husband and leads the Prince's Party against his own daughter.
FAM-333.arms: a black sled on white ice under a silver star, on a field of blue
FAM-333.founder: Vasil Brodar (995–1061), sled master of Brodava, made lord of Brodava after the Lakeland War
FAM-333.power: The lake town and island fort of Brodava (23,300); the Sled Riders (1,200) and the winter sled roads; command of the lake fleet of about 300 lake and river boats; the Prince-Consort's seat on the council; the Prince's Party in the Lake Council.
FAM-333.history: House Brodar was made on the ice. Before 1035 the Brodars were fishers and ice-road keepers of Brodava, the lake town on the Western Lakes that marks the border with Velgrad. They knew every lake road and every weak patch of winter ice for 50 km around. In November 1035 King Miroslav of Velgrad besieged Brodava, and the town's granaries were empty by Midwinter. Vasil Brodar, the sled master, gathered about 600 sleds and drove them across the frozen lake by night with food from the eastern shore, week after week, while Velgradan sentries froze on the bank. Queen Ludmila rode on the first run herself. By April 1036 Velgrad had lifted the siege, and after the Peace of Polov in 1037 the queen made Vasil lord of Brodava and Master of the Sleds. The Sled Riders, the kingdom's winter raiders who cross the frozen lakes by night, were raised from his drivers, and a Brodar has commanded them ever since. They teach the Ice Crossing: sleds spaced 30 paces apart, horses shod with spiked shoes, and a man with an ice-staff walking ahead of the first team. Vasil's son Lord Oleksa Brodar (1024–1080) held Brodava through the Tusk War, when Velgrad stayed quiet, and kept the lake fleet. Vasil's grandson Pavel, born at Brodava in 1052, grew up on the ice. In 1079 he married Princess Milena, the heir since Zorek, and in 1085 he became Prince-Consort at her crowning. Since 1086 he has commanded the Sled Riders and the lake fleet. Pavel saw his daughter Ludmila faint at the Tusk drum at Sevmir in 1098, and he has believed since that she can never lead an army against the orcs. He leads the Prince's Party, which wants the Lake Council to set her aside and name their son Yaromir heir. At the Harvest Home feast of 1104 he paid the lake-market thief Lesko Reedpipe 30 bears to beat a war-drum under the hall window, and the princess collapsed in front of the lords. The thief kept the drum, which bears the brand of the Brodar sled house. In December Pavel offered the royal physician 500 bears to tell the council the heir's ears are failing. The queen knows what he did and has said nothing. If the drum is shown at the Lake Council, the house that saved Brodava will be the house that betrayed its own heir.
dead: Vasil Brodar (995–1061): Fed Brodava over the ice in 1035–1036 and founded the house.
Oleksa Brodar (1024–1080): Held Brodava and the lake fleet through the Tusk War years.
marriages: 1079, with House Dravic: Pavel Brodar weds Princess Milena.
FAM-333.allies: House Zorac, Stefan the Grey, lesser Patriarch of Drevna
FAM-333.secrets: Pavel Brodar paid for the drum at Harvest Home 1104 and has offered the royal physician a bribe.

FAM-334.y1105: Merchant lords of Lubany who hold the silk staple, lend to the crown and half the river towns, and lead the Silk Peace party.
FAM-334.arms: a gold bale of silk on a blue river, on a field of white
FAM-334.founder: Lord Ostromir Lubec (980–1049), husband of Queen Ludmila and first lord of the silk staple
FAM-334.power: The silk staple of Lubany, where every silk caravan pays a tenth; Lubany (26,100) and its granaries; loans of about 90,000 bears to the crown and more to the river towns; the office of Keeper of Wax and Furs, which runs the treasury; about 12,000 suns of Kraoth toll silver on deposit.
FAM-334.branches: The Lubecs of Lubany; Lubec factors at Polov and Korov
FAM-334.history: The Lubecs were river merchants of Lubany on the middle Dromir who traded fish, wax and pelts and, from the 950s, the first small silk caravans that came west across the Eastern Steppe. In 1011 Lord Ostromir Lubec married Queen Ludmila, and in 1012 she granted his house the silk staple: every silk caravan must stop at Lubany and pay a tenth to the crown, and the Lubecs keep the scales. King Yaromir was Ostromir's son, so the house is royal kin. After the Tusk Clans united in 1062 and their toll camps began to tax the Silk Road (TR-09), the Lubecs learned to deal with orc toll-keepers as well as with Drevnan lords. Irina Lubec, heiress of the staple, took over the house in 1089 and has lent the crown about 90,000 bears since. Milena made her Keeper of Wax and Furs in 1094. In February 1103 a Lubec silk caravan lost in a blizzard was saved by an orc herder named Brug, and Irina has argued for peace with the Tusk Clans ever since. Since 1099 the house has held about 12,000 suns of toll silver on deposit for Gurz the Toll-Keeper of the Tusk camp at Kraoth, and she has lent part of it to the Drevnan crown. She has offered to pay the withheld rye from her own granaries if the queen allows. The silk toll raised at Lubany in 1100 and 1103 fills the treasury and angers Velgrad, and if the Tusk Clans ride in spring, the staple and the house's loans go up in smoke together.
dead: Ostromir Lubec (980–1049): Husband of Queen Ludmila; first lord of the silk staple.
marriages: 1011, with House Dravic: Ostromir Lubec weds Queen Ludmila.
FAM-334.secrets: House Lubec holds Tusk toll silver for Gurz the Toll-Keeper and has lent some of it to the crown.

FAM-335.y1105: Whaling lords of Dobin on the Whale Coast, who lost their founder and 14 boats to the giants and lead the Whalers' Grievance against the Truce of Dobin.
FAM-335.arms: a white whale under a red harpoon, on a field of grey
FAM-335.founder: Stepan Kolin (1035–1095), who led burned-out Steppe March families to Dobin
FAM-335.power: The lordship of Dobin (21,700) and its harbor; about 50 whaling boats; the settler families of the Whale Coast, about 400 of whom are ready to move to Hrimfell's whaling grounds; whale oil sold south.
FAM-335.history: House Kolin is the youngest house of Drevna. Stepan Kolin held farms near Sevmir until the Tusk riders burned them in October 1062. In 1064, after Zorek, he led about 300 burned-out families of the Steppe March north to the old fishing town of Dobin on Whale Sound. His son Ivo was born there in 1065. When Queen Milena turned the kingdom north in 1086 and sent settlers and whalers to the Whale Coast, she made Stepan Lord of Dobin. The Kolins built the whaling stations, and their boats began to kill Frost Leviathans. On 12 June 1095 16 giants of Hrimfell burned the station at Yarov and killed 40 whalers, Stepan among them. Ivo fought at Dobin's harbor gate when the giants broke it in August 1097 and lost 14 boats. He has hated the Truce of Dobin since the day it was sealed, and he leads the Whalers' Grievance. In October 1104 two of his boats killed a Frost Leviathan off the Torvik capes and lost it when it drifted north; he paid the crews to say nothing. A harpoon head of Drevnan iron is now in that whale's back.
dead: Stepan Kolin (1035–1095): Led the settlers to Dobin; killed at Yarov.
FAM-335.secrets: Ivo Kolin's boats killed a Frost Leviathan in October 1104, breaking the Truce of Dobin.

FAM-336.y1105: Hereditary keepers of the queen's listeners. Its head is the Queen's Ear and holds the secret of who paid for the Harvest Home drum.
FAM-336.arms: a brown lark rising over an open ear, on a field of green
FAM-336.founder: Mila Lark (992–1071), the maid who ran for the guards on Queen Ludmila's crowning night
FAM-336.power: The office of the Queen's Ear and the network of listeners and informers in the Lake Council, the river towns and Velgrad's court; paid news from the Tusk envoy Dorn Twotongue; maids and servants placed in the great houses.
FAM-336.branches: The Larks of the Listening Tower
FAM-336.history: On the night after Queen Ludmila's crowning in 1010, a chamber maid named Mila slept across the queen's door. The queen heard men whispering behind the wall and woke her, and Mila ran barefoot through the Listening Tower for the guards, who caught the men with knives in the wall passage. Ludmila gave her a house on the island, a pension and the name Lark, for the bird that wakes first, and made her keeper of the royal chambers. The Larks have served the queen's household since, and when Ludmila built the Still Hall and the Listener's Guard after 1048, the Larks became her listeners in the town. Nadia Lark, Mila's granddaughter, born 1060, served as chamber maid to the young Milena from 1074, and Milena made her the Queen's Ear at her crowning in 1085. She runs the queen's informers, has paid the Tusk envoy Dorn Twotongue for news of the clan council since 1098, and has a niece serving as a maid in Pavel Brodar's household. Through that niece she learned that the Prince-Consort paid the drummer at Harvest Home 1104. The queen ordered silence. Nadia has kept the thief's name as a hold over the queen's husband.
dead: Mila Lark (992–1071): The maid who fetched the guards on Ludmila's crowning night.
FAM-336.secrets: Nadia Lark knows who beat the drum at Harvest Home and who paid him, against the queen's order of silence.

FAM-941.y1105: The leading herd-lord family of Skyhold, kin of two abbots. Since 1061 its men hold the captaincies of the Stair Guard and the Snowborn Guides, and its elder is trying to buy the next search.
FAM-941.arms: a white peak over a red herding tent, on sky blue
FAM-941.founder: Dondrub of Bellcrest (603-661), elder brother of Abbot Norden
FAM-941.power: Herds of about 9,000 yaks and 20,000 sheep and goats in the Bellcrest valleys; the Snowborn Guides (300), recruited from their herds; the captaincy of the Stair Guard (2,400); kinship with the Abbot; guide fees in silver and gold dust from Drevnan merchants, dwarves and pilgrims.
FAM-941.branches: the elder's household at Bellcrest (Pasang); the household of Karma Snowborn, Abbot Tashen's birth family; the guide households of the high camps (Jigme, Captain of the Guides; Tsering, Captain of the Stair Guard)
FAM-941.history: The Snowborn are a herding household of Bellcrest that a story made great. In 614 the search monks found a four-year-old boy of the household, Norden, as the fifth Abbot of the White Stair. In January 650 Norden led 12 monks over the Zardeep Pass in deep winter and brought 46 people out of a snowbound caravan. Lowlanders and dwarves said his monks had lungs no other men had. In truth every Skyfolk child raised in the high camps can work at 5,000 m; Norden's monks were herders' sons who had spent their boyhood summers there. But Stonehold granted Skyhold's salt caravans free passage in thanks, and Norden's elder brother Dondrub's household took the name Snowborn in 651 and began to sell the story. For four centuries they were the guides of the Roof, sending their boys to the highest camps at eight and hiring them to pilgrims, salt caravans and dwarven prospectors. Lowland writers came to speak of a Snowborn bloodline; the Skyfolk never did. The family's real rise came through the treasury. Lobsang Snowborn (1014-1090), a monk born to the house, kept the salt books for twenty years and was made Steward in 1049. When the 12th Abbot died in 1060, Lobsang's faction swapped in Tashen, the nine-year-old son of Lobsang's cousin Karma Snowborn, for the boy the searchers had found first. Tashen, born into the house in 1052, became the 13th Abbot, and the Snowborn have held the best posts in Skyhold since. Lobsang confessed the swap to Tashen on his deathbed in January 1090 and told nobody else. Pasang, born into the house in 1038, a famous guide who once carried a Drevnan merchant down from 5,400 m on his back, became elder in 1080. He does not know how Tashen was chosen, and in December 1104 he did the same thing on his own: he gave a young search monk of Sunfold gold dust and a list of three Snowborn households expecting children in 1105. His kinsmen command Skyhold's soldiers. Jigme, born at Bellcrest in 1058, captains the Snowborn Guides and has guided Emberdeep's hunters for dwarf silver since 1101, including the Dragon Watch crossbowmen who shot at the sky-kings above Kardeep in October 1104. Tsering, born to a Snowborn guide household in 1068, the son of Pasang's cousin, is Captain of the Stair Guard; one of the three brothers his mother married rides with the Red Stair. The house fears the day Tashen dies, when a new abbot found anywhere but Bellcrest could strip them of everything the 1061 search gave them.
dead: Abbot Norden of the White Stair (610-688): Fifth Abbot; led the winter crossing of 650. Born to the household. *Ruler:* Abbot Norden of the White Stair (5th Abbot the Winter-Walker), Skyhold, 614–688 (RUL-9205).
Dondrub of Bellcrest (603-661): Norden's elder brother; first to bear the Snowborn name.
Lobsang Snowborn (1014-1090): Steward 1049-1089 who swapped the boys in 1061.
Karma Snowborn (1025-1081): Herder of Bellcrest; father of Abbot Tashen.
marriages: 1048, with a herding household of Bellcrest: Karma Snowborn and his two brothers shared one wife, Tashen's mother, as Skyfolk brothers do.
1067, with The Snowborn of Bellcrest: Tsering's mother, Pasang's cousin, married three brothers of a Snowborn guide household; the youngest later joined the Red Stair.
FAM-941.allies: House Windmane, Steward Sonam and the White Stair faction
FAM-941.rivals: House Bluewater, the Red Stair, Abbess Dechen of Moonstair
FAM-941.secrets: Steward Lobsang Snowborn swapped Tashen for Norbu in 1061. Pasang has bribed a search monk to look in Snowborn tents again. Jigme guided Emberdeep's Dragon Watch against the sky-kings.

FAM-942.y1105: Herd-lords of Eaglespire who own more yaks than any family outside the monasteries and run the Salt Caravan Brotherhood. Dawa Windmane smuggles salt past the abbey toll.
FAM-942.arms: a black yak running before a white wind, on red
FAM-942.founder: Gyatso of Eaglespire (796-860), first lawful caravan master of the Eaglespire road
FAM-942.power: About 12,000 yaks; the Salt Caravan Brotherhood; the Salt Letters trade with Drevna each summer; about 300 smuggled yak loads of salt a year since 1096.
FAM-942.branches: the Eaglespire household of three brothers and one wife (Dawa is the eldest); the caravan masters of the Beaconrun road
FAM-942.history: The Windmane were herders of Eaglespire who drove salt down the Beaconrun valley to the Lakeland in secret until Abbot Rabten made the trade lawful in 831 and taxed it. Their founder Gyatso became the first lawful caravan master. In the Black Cough years Abbot Gendun shut the Eaglespire gate (916 to 921), and the family lost half its herd to hunger; it took the name Windmane in the 980s as its herds recovered. The Salt Letters of 1071, written by Dawa's fathers, gave Drevnan merchants the right to buy salt, borax and sky wool at Eaglespire each summer for a toll of one load in five. Dawa, born into the house in 1050, became its elder in 1086 and head of the Salt Caravan Brotherhood in 1090. From 1091 to 1101 the Highland guide Liss Cairnhold mapped the High Wastes paths for his trains. Since 1096 the house has driven about 300 yak loads a year down a herders' path east of Eaglespire tower and sold them at Lubov without paying the toll. Dawa wants the Council to lower the toll to one load in eight before the Drevnan buyers come in June.
dead: Gyatso of Eaglespire (796-860): First lawful caravan master of the Eaglespire road.
marriages: 1074, with a herding household of Redcrest: Dawa and his two brothers took one wife from Redcrest.
FAM-942.allies: The Snowborn of Bellcrest, House Bluewater, Drevnan salt buyers of Lubov
FAM-942.rivals: Norzin of Starspire and the salt treasury
FAM-942.secrets: House Windmane has smuggled about 300 yak loads of salt a year past the abbey toll since 1096, against the Brotherhood's own oath.

FAM-943.y1105: Keepers of the pilgrim inns and ferries of the Bluespire circuit. Lady Lhamo Bluewater funds the Quiet Doubters and pays the Red Stair in butter to spare her inns.
FAM-943.arms: a white ferry boat on a blue lake, under seven white steps
FAM-943.founder: Tsomo of Starspire (902-971), who built the first pilgrim inn on the Bluespire shore
FAM-943.power: Fourteen inns and about 30 ferry boats on the Bluespire circuit; 120 hired circuit wardens under Dorje Stonesling; pilgrims' silver and butter, down by a third in 1104.
FAM-943.branches: the Starspire household (Lhamo and her three husbands); the innkeepers of the twelve resting places of the circuit
FAM-943.history: In 930 a herder's widow of Starspire, Tsomo, built the first stone inn for pilgrims at the start of the Bluespire circuit that Abbot Samten had fixed in 470. Her children built more at the circuit's twelve resting places and bought ferry boats to carry pilgrims across the lake's arms, and the house took its name from the lake. The Bluewater grew rich in the long peace of the 12th Abbot, when Ranpuri and Drevnan pilgrims came in hundreds each summer. The split of 1062 nearly ruined them, and they paid both Stairs to swear the Truce of the Circuit in 1064. Lhamo, born at Starspire in 1057, married three brothers of the Bluewater herd in 1075, joining the house by marriage, and took over the inns when her mother-in-law died in 1089. She built a new ferry landing at Starspire in 1093. After Red Stair and White Stair herders fought with staves in her own courtyard in 1102 she joined the Quiet Doubters. Since 1101 she has paid Red Stair herders 40 loads of butter a year to spare her inns. In August 1104 her warden Dorje Stonesling killed a robber, and she had the body hidden under a cairn.
dead: Tsomo of Starspire (902-971): Built the first pilgrim inn of the circuit.
marriages: 1075, with the Starspire herding households: Lhamo of Starspire married three Bluewater brothers.
FAM-943.allies: House Windmane, Abbess Dechen and the Quiet Doubters
FAM-943.rivals: The Snowborn of Bellcrest, the Stair Guard
FAM-943.secrets: The house pays the Red Stair in butter that feeds Norbu's monasteries, and hides a robber's body under a cairn above Starspire.

FAM-416.y1105: Royal line of Stonehold for 3,445 years and 41 rulers. King Harvald is about 214 and losing his memory; his son Hrodgar must make the Crown Shelf climb, which he has already failed once in secret.
FAM-416.arms: a gold anvil on a white mountain peak, on deep grey
FAM-416.founder: King Brom Bardun (2520–2310 BR), who opened the First Hall
FAM-416.power: The crown of 300,000 people and the chair of the Hall Council; command of 6,000 standing troops and a levy of 18,000; the royal share of the Zardeep tolls and of the 1 in 20 of Nagora tolls; joint control with the Carvers of the Hold Bank's 600,000 dwarf crowns; the secret tenth of Tessarian gold.
FAM-416.branches: The crowned line of the First Hall (Harvald, Hrodgar); The Crown Shelf Guard kin: about 80 Bardun cousins and guides who fight on the ice above 6,000 m, led by Brom Bardun (born 1018), next in line after Hrodgar; Thrand's line, descendants of the mine-master killed by Dagna Hammerhand in 398, who keep the blood-claim against Emberdeep
FAM-416.history: House Bardun is the oldest ruling family in the Known World after the Oakborn. Brom Bardun, born about 2520 BR on the Roof, led about 3,000 dwarves of eleven clans down to the valley of the First Hall and opened it on 3 March 2340 BR. He had climbed above every other dwarf to the Crown Shelf on the great peak at about 7,000 m, and the peak has borne his name since. His daughter Halla the Carver finished the carved Law and carried his first ingot to the Crown Shelf, and every Bardun heir since has made that climb before the Eldest Carver cuts the new name. Forty-one Barduns have ruled: 26 kings and 15 queens. The climb is the house's law and its sieve. Only carriers of the deep breath can reach 7,000 m with an ingot, so only carriers wear the crown. Princess Hild died of cold at 6,800 m in 1792 BR; the son of Brom III turned back bleeding at 6,500 m in 1290 BR; both times a younger sibling climbed and ruled. The house has also paid in blood outside the halls. In 398 Thrand Bardun, mine-master and nephew of Hrodvar V, was killed by Dagna Hammerhand in a forge quarrel; her clan was exiled and founded Emberdeep, and the Bardun blood-claim for Thrand has never been paid. Orm III won the Zardeep tolls in the Worldspine Toll War (608–615). Queen Hallgerd paid for the Tessarian Revolt in 702. Hrodmar fought the Gold Road War (996–1004) and carved the secret tenth. In 880 Hrodmar married Sif Grimstone of Kelfast, a cousin of the later Eldest Carver Thora, and their son Harvald was born in 890. Harvald was 114 when he helped bargain the Treaty of the Tirana Heads and 121 when he took the crown in 1011. In 975 he married Gerd Silverthane of Dramhall, who died in 1062; their son Hrodgar was born in 986. Harvald lost the Nagora Pass in 1082–1085 and sent Hrodgar down to Tirpur, at 787 m, to seal the peace, because a Bardun who goes below 1,000 m sickens within weeks; Hrodgar was ill for a month after. Harvald has not left the First Hall since 1098, and since 1103 his memory has failed. Hrodgar commands the 2,400 Gate Wardens and wants no more wars with humans. In August 1101 he made a practice climb and turned back at 6,400 m with blood in his mouth; only his Crown Shelf Guard guide knows. Some thanes hope he fails again. If he does, the crown would pass to the next carrier of the line, Brom Bardun of the Crown Shelf Guard, a great-grandson of Hrodmar's brother.
dead: King Brom Bardun (2520–2310 BR): Opened the First Hall. *Ruler:* King Brom Bardun (King Brom I the Founder), Kingdom of Stonehold, 2340–2310 BR (RUL-4041).
Queen Halla the Carver (2450–2235 BR): Finished the Law; first climb to the Crown Shelf. *Ruler:* Halla Bardun (Queen Halla I the Carver), Kingdom of Stonehold, 2310–2235 BR (RUL-4042).
Princess Hild (about 1890–1792 BR): Died of cold at 6,800 m on the heir's climb.
Thrand Bardun (about 300–398): Killed by Dagna Hammerhand; his blood-claim is unpaid.
King Orm III the Toll-King (480–690): Won the Zardeep tolls. *Ruler:* Orm Bardun (King Orm III the Toll-King), Kingdom of Stonehold, 596–690 (RUL-4076).
Queen Hallgerd (575–772): Paid for the Tessarian Revolt. *Ruler:* Hallgerd Bardun (Queen Hallgerd), Kingdom of Stonehold, 690–772 (RUL-4077).
marriages: 880, with House Grimstone: Hrodmar married Sif Grimstone of Kelfast; their son Harvald was born in 890.
975, with Gerd Silverthane of Dramhall (no great house): Harvald's queen; mother of Hrodgar. Died 1062.
FAM-416.allies: House Grimstone, House Goldvein, The Stonelungs
FAM-416.secrets: Harvald's memory has failed since 1103 and he signs what Orrin Goldvein reads him; Hrodgar failed a practice climb in 1101; the house holds the unpaid blood-claim for Thrand against Emberdeep and the secret tenth.

FAM-417.y1105: Mine-masters' clan of Stonehold and Emberdeep. Head Grimbald is Thane of Morhall, war leader of the Hall Council and victor of Tiravi; his cousin Dagny heads the Emberdeep branch at Kardeep.
FAM-417.arms: two crossed picks under a grey cloud of dust, on black
FAM-417.founder: Old Hald Stonelung (720–930), the first carrier
FAM-417.power: Morhall Hold and the deep mines of the north-west; headship of the Mine-Masters' Guild of Stonehold since 1041 and of the Mine-Masters of Emberdeep since 1066; the Kardeep gold mines; Grimbald's command as war leader; about 90 kin, 45 of them carriers.
FAM-417.branches: The Morhall line (Grimbald); The Emberdeep branch at Kardeep (Dagny), from Hald's daughter Sigrid's marriage in 880
FAM-417.history: Hald Stonelung was born at Morhall in 720 into a family of tunnel-cutters. Most cutters of the deep galleries died of the miners' cough by 150; Hald cut rock in the dustiest headings for a century and never coughed. He also could smell almost nothing, and in 812 his work partner died in a pocket of bad air that Hald walked through without noticing. The Carvers wrote down both facts, and when two of his four children proved the same, the clan took the name Stonelung. Hald became head of the Mine-Masters' Guild, and in late 900, at 180, Queen Svala II sent him to Irondeep with Stonehold's Open Forge complaint. He died in 930. In 880 his daughter Sigrid married a gold miner of Kardeep in Emberdeep, and her descendants, the Emberdeep Stonelungs, run Kardeep's gold in 1105. Grimbald was born at Morhall in 962. He fought at the Thargard ambush in 996, in the Nagpur gorge in 999 and at the siege of Kelfast in 1002, where Stonelung counter-miners worked the dust of the breaking galleries for days. He became head of the Guild in 1041. In March 1079 the north gallery of Morhall fell, and his nephew was among the 14 Arn Holdfast dug out. In April 1083 he broke Ranpur's elephants at Tiravi. His cousin Dagny, born 990 at Kardeep, lost two brothers to a gas pocket in 1031 and has headed Emberdeep's mine-masters since 1066. In November 1104 she sent Grimbald a survey of gold gravels east of Moonstair without her queen's leave. Grimbald also keeps a secret: in 1085 a drunk Chanari smith told him that 'our dwarven teachers' still took a share of every blade, and he has never told the Carvers.
dead: Old Hald Stonelung (720–930): First carrier; carried the Open Forge complaint.
Sigrid Stonelung (about 790–990): Hald's daughter, founder of the Emberdeep branch.
marriages: 880, with A gold-mining clan of Kardeep (Emberdeep): Sigrid Stonelung's marriage founded the Emberdeep branch.
FAM-417.secrets: Grimbald knows Emberdeep still takes a share of Chanari's blades (1085) and has Dagny's gold survey of Emberdeep ground.

FAM-418.y1105: Gold-mine owners of Dramhall and Masters of the Hold Bank since 790. Head Orrin runs the largest gold reserve in the Known World and has secretly lent part of it to his own failing mines.
FAM-418.arms: a gold vein running through a black rock, on white
FAM-418.founder: Gerd Goldvein (about 2230–2020 BR), first mine-master of the Dramhall gold
FAM-418.power: The Mastership of the Hold Bank and its reserve of about 600,000 dwarf crowns; the gold, ruby and sapphire galleries of Dramhall; debts owed by Tessaria, Aldmark (about 100,000 suns), Ranpur (20,000 crowns), Captain Gerolt Marr of Ostra (12,000 suns) and Kiran Ranavir (30,000 lotus); the Debtors' Wall.
FAM-418.branches: The Dramhall line (Orrin); The bank's factors at Ostra and Tirpur, cousins who place the Hold Bank's loans among humans
FAM-418.history: House Goldvein has owned the gold of Dramhall since about 2150 BR, when Gerd Goldvein became first mine-master of the galleries King Hrodvar I opened under Mount Bardun. For 2,900 years it dug gold, rubies and sapphires and grew rich. Its second fortune began in 790. The Toll Vault, founded by Orm III in 615 to hold the Zardeep tolls under the Carvers' seal, had begun lending to the human kingdoms that rose from the Solen Empire, and King Brom V named Rorik Goldvein its first Master. The Vault became the Hold Bank, and the house has held the Mastership since: eleven Masters in 315 years. The Bank's rules are carved. It lends only against metal or land and never forgives a debt. It carves the names of unpaying debtors on the Debtors' Wall in the First Hall, and a debtor's heirs inherit the debt for 300 years. It lent the Tessarian kings silver after the revolt, the Kingdom of Kingsmere money for its wars, and after 1004 the Tessarian Empire silver against the upper Tirana gold. When the empire fell in 1047 the Wall gained three Tessarian emperors, Nikandros the Gilded and Anselm Six-Fingers among them. Orrin was born at Dramhall in 940. He counted the Tessarian gold claims during the Gold Road War and became Master in 1032. In 1072 he lent Ranpur 20,000 crowns to rebuild the delta dykes and kept collecting through the whole Nagora War. In the 1090s he lent Aldmark about 100,000 suns. He lends through agents in Ostra and Tirpur, and his clerk Ragnhild Tallystone, born to a family that has served the house for four generations, watches the debtors. The house's own fortune has turned. The Dramhall ruby seam failed in 1099, and Orrin lent 30,000 crowns from the Bank's reserve to House Goldvein's mines without the Carvers' leave; carved law forbids the Master to lend to himself. Ragnhild found the tally in 1103 and keeps a copy to claim the Mastership when Orrin dies or falls. Since 1103 King Harvald signs the Bank's reports as Orrin reads them, which gives Orrin more power than any Master before him. He leads the Gold Claim on the Hall Council: Stonehold must lead or share any fourth expedition to the upper Tirana gold, and Tessaria must swear again to the secret tenth before it gets another crown. If his own loan comes out, the Carvers can strip the house of the Mastership it has held since 790.
dead: Gerd Goldvein (about 2230–2020 BR): First mine-master of the Dramhall gold.
Rorik Goldvein (about 700–905): First Master of the Hold Bank (790).
FAM-418.secrets: Orrin's unlawful loan of 30,000 crowns to his own mines (1099), known to Ragnhild Tallystone; the king signs Bank reports he cannot remember.

FAM-419.y1105: Toll-keepers of Mormund and the Zardeep Pass for 490 years. Head Kettil leads the Old Toll and wants the Dwarf's Gate back; his sister Brenna masters the Pike Hall of Mormund.
FAM-419.arms: an iron bar across a mountain pass, on red
FAM-419.founder: Ketil Ironbrow (about 540–740), first Toll-Warden of Zardeep
FAM-419.power: The Zardeep tolls, one part in ten of goods; Stonehold's 1 in 20 share of Ranpur's Nagora tolls; Mormund Hold (9,900 people) at 4,863 m; the Pike Hall of Mormund; the Old Toll faction on the Hall Council.
FAM-419.branches: The Mormund toll line (Kettil); The Pike Hall line (Brenna)
FAM-419.history: Ketil Ironbrow kept the first toll gate on the Zardeep road for King Orm III in 615, after the Worldspine Toll War won Stonehold the right to tax every cargo. His house has kept the tolls from Mormund, at 4,863 m above the pass, for 490 years. The Ironbrows are hard folk of a hard post: the pass is open only from June to September, and every winter the house loses porters and mules to the snow. For centuries the tolls made it rich, because one part in ten of every load of pepper, cotton and steel that crossed the western Worldspine passed through its gate. Kettil was born at Mormund in 1001 and became Toll-Warden in 1060 when his father died. The Nagora road opened in 1081, and his income fell by a third. He pressed the Hall Council to raise the Dwarf's Gate across the Nagora road in 1082. His only son died at that gate in August 1084, behind the inner door that Shield Elder Eyvind Graywall ordered shut. Kettil's younger sister Brenna, born 1030, carried the order, and she has let him believe the Ranpuri killed the boy. Brenna led a pike block at Tiravi in 1083 and has mastered the Pike Hall of Mormund since 1087. Kettil leads the Old Toll, which calls the Treaty of Tirpur a shame carved in stone. He pays the elven scout Lirien Duskwater in dwarf crowns to report the route of Ostra's gold expedition and means to have her lead it into the Red Widow's dawn feeding ground.
dead: Ketil Ironbrow (about 540–740): First Toll-Warden of Zardeep.
Arnulf Ironbrow (1036–1084): Kettil's only son, shut out at the Dwarf's Gate.
FAM-419.secrets: Brenna carried the order that shut the door on Kettil's son; Kettil plans to lead an expedition of humans into the Red Widow's path.

FAM-420.y1105: The Carver family of Kelfast, which has given the Deep Law five Eldest Carvers. Head Thora is Eldest Carver of the First Hall and judge of all dwarves.
FAM-420.arms: a grey law-stone cut with runes, on black
FAM-420.founder: Asvor Grimstone (about 230–20 BR), first Carver of Kelfast
FAM-420.power: The office of Eldest Carver, chief judge of the Deep Law for all three holds; the exile rolls, the genealogies and the secret carved clauses of 702 and 1004; the veto of the Carvers over any change in carved law; the Law Halls of Kelfast.
FAM-420.branches: The Kelfast Carvers (Thora); Sif's line, which married into House Bardun in 880
FAM-420.history: Asvor Grimstone cut the first law-stones of Kelfast when King Brom IV opened the hold about 100 BR, and her descendants have carved law there since. The house has given the Deep Law five Eldest Carvers. Hroald Grimstone read the exile of Dagna Hammerhand's clan in 398 and set her exile-stone with its face to the wall. Olaf Grimstone sealed Queen Hallgerd's secret contract with Leo Tessaran in 702. Bera Grimstone gave the Judgment of the First Hall on Founding Day 904, and her granddaughter Thora, born at Kelfast in 870, cut it into the stone at 34. In 880 Thora's cousin Sif married Hrodmar Bardun, and King Harvald is Grimstone on his mother's side. In 1004 Thora carved the secret clause of the Treaty of the Tirana Heads. She became Eldest Carver in 1031 and read out the exile of the pump-wright Brokk Gravelbeard in 1040. Since 1031 she has known that Irondeep sold about 14,000 sets of lamellar to the Wind Empire, and she has let it lie. At the Kindling of 1104 she declared that Chanari's steel was too good to be human work and swore to find who taught it. She means to call the Carvers of Emberdeep to the First Hall at the Founding on 3 March 1105. Forge-Princess Asta of Emberdeep has sent her a sealed letter asking for a hearing, and her own assayer, Snorri Truemark, is sitting on a result that points to his mother's clan.
dead: Asvor Grimstone (about 230–20 BR): First Carver of Kelfast.
Hroald Grimstone (about 260–470): Eldest Carver who exiled Dagna's clan.
Bera Grimstone (about 760–960): Eldest Carver who gave the Judgment of 904.
marriages: 880, with House Bardun: Sif Grimstone married Hrodmar Bardun; mother of King Harvald.
FAM-420.rivals: Clan Ashgrave, Clan Emberhand, The Stonelungs
FAM-420.secrets: Thora has known of Irondeep's arms sales since 1031 and let them lie, which would make her judgment of Emberdeep look like one law for friends and another for rivals.

FAM-422.y1105: Royal clan of Emberdeep for 705 years and seven rulers. Forge-Queen Hilde rules; her daughter Asta is heir and wants to confess the clan's crimes; her nephew Rolf champions the Hammer Guard.
FAM-422.arms: a red hammer over a white plume of steam, on black
FAM-422.founder: Dagna Hammerhand (340–560), exile and first Forge-Queen
FAM-422.power: The Forge Crown of 220,000 people; the Council of Forge-Masters; the clan treasury and the two eggshells of 612 in its vault; command of 4,400 standing troops, the 400 Hammer Guard and the Kardeep Dragon Watch; the Ranpuri friendship and the 40,000-lotus Lotus Loan taken in the clan's name.
FAM-422.branches: The Forge-Queen's line (Hilde, Asta); Hauk's line (Rolf), from Hilde's younger brother Hauk (960–1071); The Hammer Guard kin, about 30 carriers of the full hammer arms among the clan's 140 members
FAM-422.history: Clan Hammerhand was a smith clan of Stonehold's First Hall that married cousins to keep its hammer arms. Dagna, born 340, had them in full. In 398 she struck the mine-master Thrand Bardun once with a forge hammer, meaning to break his arm, and broke his skull; the Carvers exiled the whole clan. She led about 2,000 dwarves 1,200 km east and founded Emberdeep in 400. She set her own 90 kg anvil in the Breath Halls and ruled that no child would inherit who could not lift it above the head at the Kindling, and seven Hammerhands have ruled by that test: five Forge-Queens and two Forge-Kings. Because the full hammer arms appear in only about one child in four of two carriers, the clan has always married other carriers, mostly cousins, and every ruler has had to wait to see which child could lift. Dagna died in 560. Her son Harl lost his heir Durek in 612, when Durek's party stole two dragon eggs and died on the Gundgard road; the clan has kept the eggshells and the survivor's account hidden since, and no child of Emberdeep is named Durek. Durek's sister Sif lifted the anvil in 615 and ruled 124 years. Her son Orvar tied the hold to Ranpur. Orvar's daughter Aslaug swore to the Judgment of 904 and then, in the hungry years around 950, let Clan Emberhand teach Chanari crucible steel, the act that Stonehold now means to try. Aslaug's daughter Ragna ruled 88 years and was killed by the steam burst of February 1050. Hilde was born in 944, lifted the anvil at her mother's burial and has ruled since. In 975 she married Kolr Ironfoot, a carrier cousin, who died in 1060; their daughter Asta was born in 1002 and lifted the anvil at the Kindling of 1035. Hilde's younger brother Hauk, also a carrier, fathered Rolf in 1040, and Rolf has the full arms; he won the Hammer Guard's champion's place in 1088 by breaking an iron-bound door with three blows. The clan's weakness is its heart. Dagna died of a failing heart, and twice in 1104 Rolf's heart stumbled and he fell at the Hall's anvil. Asta learned of the eggs of 612 and the compact of 950 on her 100th birthday in 1102 and founded the Clean Name to confess them. Hilde wants the hold's secrets kept until her escape road is finished. In 1105 mother and daughter want opposite things, and both are Forge-Queens by the anvil's law.
dead: Dagna Hammerhand (340–560): Exile and founder of Emberdeep. *Ruler:* Dagna Hammerhand (Forge-Queen Dagna the Exile), Kingdom of Emberdeep, 400–560 (RUL-4091).
Durek Hammerhand (551–612): Heir killed on the Gundgard road after stealing dragon eggs.
Forge-Queen Sif (575–772): Lifted the anvil after Durek's death; cut Balmund. *Ruler:* Sif Hammerhand (Forge-Queen Sif), Kingdom of Emberdeep, 648–772 (RUL-4093).
Forge-Queen Aslaug (765–962): Allowed the Chanari Compact. *Ruler:* Aslaug Hammerhand (Forge-Queen Aslaug), Kingdom of Emberdeep, 870–962 (RUL-4095).
Forge-Queen Ragna (850–1050): Killed by the steam burst of 1050. *Ruler:* Ragna Hammerhand (Forge-Queen Ragna), Kingdom of Emberdeep, 962–1050 (RUL-4096).
marriages: 975, with Kolr Ironfoot (carrier cousin, no great house): Hilde's consort; father of Asta. Died 1060.
FAM-422.secrets: The eggshells of 612, the unsung verse that names Thrand, the Chanari Compact of about 950, the heat readings and the escape road to Balmund. Rolf's heart is failing.

FAM-423.y1105: The crucible-steel clan of Emberdeep. Head Sigrun is First Forge-Master and keeper of the Chanari Compact; her mother Aud is the last living teacher of Chanari; Sigrun's cousin's son Snorri Truemark is Stonehold's Master Assayer.
FAM-423.arms: a red crucible over a black flame, on white
FAM-423.founder: Hrafn Emberhand (about 330–550), Dagna's forge-master on the exile road
FAM-423.power: The Breath Forges and the Guild of the Breath Forges; Emberdeep's crucible steel; the secret share of every Chanari blade, about one lotus in twenty, paid through House Varma at Tharmund; since 1101, about 400 ingots a year sold to Balforge, which gives Sigrun a hold over Stonehold's crucible guild.
FAM-423.branches: The Tharmund forge line (Sigrun, Aud); The Truemark branch at Stonehold's First Hall: Snorri, son of Aud's niece and a Stonehold assayer
FAM-423.history: Hrafn Emberhand carried the crucibles of Dagna's clan east on the exile road and lit the first crucible fire of Emberdeep in 400. His descendants have made the hold's steel since, at Tharmund and in the Breath Forges. Aud was born at Tharmund in 905 and learned the crucible from her father. In the hungry years around 950, aged about 45, she and two other Emberhand smiths went down to Chanari and taught its smiths crucible steel for rice, grain and a share of every blade. The first Chanari blade was forged in 952 under her eye; she kept it, with her own rune and the first Steel-Warden of House Varma's mark on the tang, wrapped in oilcloth under her bed. She bore Sigrun in 980 and handed her the forges in 1040. Sigrun became First Forge-Master in 1051, after the steam burst of 1050 killed the old master. She has met each new Steel-Warden of House Varma at Tharmund, most recently Devika Varma in 1090, and the clan's share still comes up the road. Since 1101 she has also sold about 400 ingots a year to Hela Brightforge of Stonehold, whose Balforge ore went brittle, and Hela sells them under her own mark. Aud's niece married a Stonehold assayer, and their son Snorri Truemark, born 1005 at the First Hall, is Master Assayer there; in December 1104 his assay matched Chanari steel to old Emberhand steel, and he has told no one. Aud wants to cross to Stonehold in June and confess; Sigrun wants the compact kept hidden.
dead: Hrafn Emberhand (about 330–550): Lit Emberdeep's first crucible fire.
marriages: 1000, with Truemark assayers of Stonehold: Aud's niece married a Stonehold assayer; their son Snorri was born in 1005.
FAM-423.secrets: The Chanari Compact and its share; the first Chanari blade under Aud's bed; Snorri's unreported assay; the ingots sold to Balforge.

FAM-424.y1105: The Carver clan of Emberdeep; head Bolli is Eldest Carver, judge of the hold and keeper of its genealogies and its worst secrets.
FAM-424.arms: a grey chisel over a black grave-mound, on red
FAM-424.words: We carve what the fire forgets.
FAM-424.founder: Thyri Ashgrave (about 310–520), first Law-Carver of the exiles
FAM-424.power: The office of Eldest Carver of Emberdeep, without whom the Forge-Queen may change no carved law; the confirmation of every heir at the anvil; the genealogies, the exile rolls and the heat tally stones; the faction of the Smith-Father's Breath.
FAM-424.history: Thyri Ashgrave was a young Carver of the First Hall who chose exile with Dagna's clan in 398 rather than carve its sentence. In 401 she cut the first law-stones of Emberdeep, copying the Law of the First Hall from memory, and her clan has judged the hold since. The Ashgraves keep the founding chant and its unsung verse, the survivor's account of 612 and the genealogies that prove which Hammerhands may lift for the crown. Bolli was born at Balmund in 930 and became Eldest Carver in 1025, when the Forge-Queen told him of the eggshells and the verse. He judged the dead of the steam burst of 1050 and confirmed Hilde at the anvil. He has read every heat tally since 1051 and has hated each one. In 1097 he read the exile of the bellows-wright Yrsa Windbellows and had her walled out in the winter snows. In 1103 he ordered two of Hakon Steamwright's sworn surveyors to cut the heat figures on the tally stones by three degrees, and carved the order himself. Since the Kindling of 1104 the captain of the works guard, Vigga Blackpick, has reported the Queen's tunnel to him. He leads the Smith-Father's Breath, which says that leaving the First Forge would be faithless, and he wants Hilde to swear at the next Kindling never to abandon it.
dead: Thyri Ashgrave (about 310–520): Chose exile and carved Emberdeep's first law.
FAM-424.secrets: Bolli falsified the heat tallies in 1103 and spies on the Queen's tunnel through Vigga Blackpick.

FAM-425.y1105: Road-wardens of Tharmund, keepers of Emberdeep's only road in from the south; head Orm runs the trade with Ranpur's merchants.
FAM-425.arms: a copper gate between two black mountains, on gold
FAM-425.founder: Bram Coppertooth (about 360–590), first gate-keeper of Tharmund
FAM-425.power: The office of Road-Warden of Tharmund and the gate fee on all human trade; the Tharmund Gate Shields (1,600); the road down to the Gundgard valleys; the Ranpuri cotton brokers and steel buyers who trade at the gate.
FAM-425.history: When Dagna cut Tharmund Gate about 430 on the one road up from the Gundgard valleys, she gave its keeping to Bram Coppertooth, whose copper-capped front tooth gave the clan its name. The Coppertooths have kept the gate since. Every load of steel, gems and gold that goes down to Ranpur and every sack of rice that comes up passes through their hands, and the gate fee on human trade has made them rich. They speak Ranpuri as well as Holdspeech, and Ranpuri traders have called the clan's heads uncle for generations. Orm was born at Tharmund in 1015 and served his five-year turns in the Tharmund Gate Shields from 1045. In 1079 the monsoon washed out the gorge road, and he rebuilt it in one season with Ranpuri labour; the Forge-Queen made him Road-Warden that year. In 1102 he carried the terms of the Lotus Loan between the temple banks of Ranpur and the Forge-Queen. Since then he has taken one gem in ten from the trains going down to Ranpur as a private fee, though those gems were pledged to the temple banks. He leads the Chanari Compact with Sigrun Emberhand and wants another 20,000 lotus from Ranpur for the Queen's tunnel, which puts him against Forge-Princess Asta, who wants the hold cut free of Ranpur.
dead: Bram Coppertooth (about 360–590): First gate-keeper of Tharmund.
FAM-425.secrets: Orm skims one gem in ten from the gems pledged under the Lotus Loan.

FAM-901.y1105: Royal house of Ranpur since 998. Only three men of the blood can inherit: Raja Indrajit, his sickly son Vikram, who secretly failed the arsenic test in 1102, and his cousin Kiran, who wants the crown.
FAM-901.arms: a silver cup turned upside down on hill green, under a gold lotus
FAM-901.founder: Bhim Ranavir, first lord of Devesh (846-912)
FAM-901.power: The crown of Ranpur: a sixth of the rice harvest on all land that is not temple land, the market tax of the ports, and the Nagora tolls (sold for 1105-1107 for 60,000 lotus). An army of 84,000 standing and 350,000 at full levy, the 1,000 blades of the Steel Guard, about 560 war elephants and 50 war galleys. The Devesh yellow-stone mines, the only lawful source of arsenic in the kingdom. Debts of about 20,000 dwarf crowns to the Hold Bank and the Nagora road loans to the temple banks.
FAM-901.branches: the Raja's line (Indrajit and Prince Vikram); the line of Arjun (Lord Kiran and his two sons, Arun and Dev, both passed the test); the Devesh cousins, who keep the yellow-stone mines and marry into the main line
FAM-901.history: The Ranavir were hill lords before they were kings. Their first known lord, Bhim Ranavir, held Devesh, a town at 1,740 m in the eastern hills, as a captain of the Sagar rajas from 871. Devesh sits on rock full of yellow stone, the arsenic ore that painters grind for gold and poisoners grind for murder. In the drought of 889 Bhim's household drank a whole dry season from a deep well cut through that rock. Nine servants and soldiers died with dark spots on their skin and numb feet, but Bhim and four of his seven children stayed well. Raja Jaidev III Sagar gave the family the yellow-stone mines, since they could work the ore without sickening. For a century the Ranavir sold arsenic to painters, physicians and, quietly, to anyone at court who could pay. Bhim's great-grandson Devendra (948-1001), son of the Sagar princess Lila, rose as a general of the Sagar and married his Devesh cousin Uma in 972. When Harsha died without a son in March 998, Devendra held the palace with 3,000 soldiers, gave the temples gold, and was proclaimed the worthiest man. In February 1001 he and six guests died after a feast, and his son Vikram, who ate the same dish, lived. Devendra had not inherited the blood; Uma had, and she passed it to Vikram, which taught the house that it runs through women as well as men. Vikram the Unpoisoned ruled 43 years and made the family's blood a legend. He also made it a rule: from 1003 every Ranavir child drinks a small, rising cup of arsenic at each Festival of Lamps from the age of five, and any who sicken are struck from the heirs. Daughters who pass the test may marry only Ranavir cousins, and daughters who fail may marry out. Because the test finds exactly who carries the blood, the trait has never left the house. It has cost the house its children. Two carriers who marry lose about one child in four in the womb, and Vikram, Devraj and Indrajit all married cousins. Of Vikram's eleven children only Devraj (1019-1090) and Arjun (1023-1079) lived to be men. Devraj married Padmini of the old Sagar blood in 1050 and had Indrajit in 1058; Arjun married Meena of the Devesh cousins and had Kiran in 1061 and Sita in 1065. Indrajit married his cousin Sita in 1083. She lost four children, bore Prince Vikram in 1093 and died in 1097 with a fifth. Devraj left the house a road and a debt: the Hold Bank loan of 1072 and the Nagora road, which Indrajit won in the Nagora War. In 1105 the house is three men. Indrajit (born 1058) is bold and proud. Prince Vikram (born 1093) is sickly and failed his test in 1102, which his nurse hid. Lord Kiran (born into the house in 1061, the son of Arjun) has two sons who passed the test, and he is buying the temples' favor with 30,000 lotus borrowed from the Hold Bank of Stonehold.
dead: Bhim Ranavir (846-912): Lord of Devesh; first known carrier of the blood; survived the bitter well of 889.
Devendra Ranavir (948-1001): General who took the throne in 998 and died of poison in 1001. *Ruler:* Devendra Ranavir (the General), Kingdom of Ranpur, 998–1001 (RUL-9058).
Raja Vikram the Unpoisoned (975-1044): Survived seven poisonings; made the arsenic test the law of the house. *Ruler:* Raja Vikram the Unpoisoned (Vikram I), Kingdom of Ranpur, 1001–1044 (RUL-9059).
Devraj Ranavir (1019-1090): Built the Nagora road and borrowed from the Hold Bank. *Ruler:* Devraj Ranavir (the Road-Builder), Kingdom of Ranpur, 1044–1090 (RUL-9060).
Arjun Ranavir (1023-1079): Younger son of Vikram; father of Kiran and of Rani Sita.
Rani Sita Ranavir (1065-1097): Indrajit's cousin and queen; mother of Prince Vikram; died bearing her fifth dead child.
marriages: 947, with House Sagar: Rudra Ranavir of Devesh married Lila Sagar, aunt of Raja Harsha IV; their son Devendra claimed the throne as the king's cousin.
972, with House Ranavir: Devendra married his Devesh cousin Uma, who carried the blood and passed it to Vikram.
1000, with House Ranavir: Vikram married Gauri of the Devesh cousins, a carrier; seven of their eleven children were stillborn.
1050, with House Sagar: Devraj married Padmini, a great-granddaughter of Raja Tej III Sagar.
1083, with House Ranavir: Indrajit married his cousin Sita, Kiran's sister.
FAM-901.allies: House Nagar, House Varma, Clan Emberhand, House Bhaskar
FAM-901.rivals: House Bardun, House Maruang, House Sethi
FAM-901.secrets: Three of Vikram's seven famous poisonings were staged by his ministers. Prince Vikram sickened at his 1102 test and may not carry the blood; Lord Kiran owes the Hold Bank 30,000 lotus.

FAM-902.y1105: The first royal house, deposed in 9 BR. Hereditary Keepers of the White Stable since 5 BR. Its head, Keeper Anand, leads the White Stable Circle and hides the false calf.
FAM-902.arms: a rising moon over three rice sheaves on indigo
FAM-902.founder: Surya Chandar the Dreamed (328 BR-271 BR), first Raja of Ranpur
FAM-902.power: The White Stable at Ranpur and the Pearl Herd, about 20 grey elephants of the white line kept at a temple estate near Nagita; three temple estates granted in the reign of Dev I Mitra; a voice in every crowning, because the white elephant must kneel. No troops.
FAM-902.branches: the Keepers of the White Stable at Ranpur; the herd-keepers of the Pearl Herd at the temple estate near Nagita
FAM-902.history: The Chandar ruled Ranpur for its first three centuries. Surya Chandar married Tara Mitra of Mitari in about 300 BR and became the first Raja. His heirs built the first dykes and the first brick Great Temple and took Tirpur. Thirteen Chandar kings ruled until the Sleeper's Dim, when the monsoon failed four years running after Mount Hael's eruption. In 9 BR the temples deposed Hemant Chandar and crowned Arun Mitra. The Mitra did not kill the old house. When the first white elephant came to Ranpur in 5 BR, Arun made Hemant's sons its keepers, a post that honored them and kept them in the temple's sight. The Chandar have kept every white elephant since. They breed the Pearl Herd, the grey cows and bulls of the white line, at a temple estate near Nagita, because a white calf is born only when both parents carry the pale blood, and about sixteen white elephants have come from that herd in eleven centuries. Moon-Pearl, born in 1046, is the last. The herd is old and inbred, and no white calf has been born since. Anand, born into the house in 1048 and given to the White Stable at 12, became Keeper in 1085. In 1101 he and three temple families bought a pale cow at Amberport and hid her near Nagita. For the Chandar the stakes are total: if the dream ends, the house that has knelt its elephants before five dynasties has nothing left to keep.
dead: Surya Chandar the Dreamed (328 BR-271 BR): First Raja of Ranpur. *Ruler:* Surya Chandar (Surya I the Dreamed), Kingdom of Ranpur, 300–271 BR (RUL-9001).
Karan Chandar the Northman (228 BR-171 BR): Took Tirpur and the upper Chanpur. *Ruler:* Karan Chandar (the Northman), Kingdom of Ranpur, 199–171 BR (RUL-9005).
Hemant Chandar the Dim King (40 BR-3 BR): Last Chandar Raja, deposed in the Sleeper's Dim. *Ruler:* Hemant Chandar (the Dim King), Kingdom of Ranpur, 21–9 BR (RUL-9013).
marriages: 300 BR, with House Mitra: Surya Chandar married Tara Mitra; the founding of the kingdom.
130 BR, with House Mitra: One of many Chandar-Mitra marriages; the Mitra claim to the throne rested on them.
FAM-902.secrets: Keeper Anand hid a bought pale cow near Nagita to pass off as Moon-Pearl's calf. The herd book of the Pearl Herd proves that no white calf has been born since 1046.

FAM-903.y1105: Extinct in the male line since 233, when Vasant Pratap had the last Mitra princes drowned in the Chanpur. Their shrine at Mitari is kept by the town.
FAM-903.arms: a white elephant kneeling under a rain cloud on green
FAM-903.founder: Tara Mitra of Mitari (310 BR-255 BR), wife of the first Raja
FAM-903.power: None in 1105. At its height: the eastern arm of the delta, the Jalari cotton lands and the Red Walls.
FAM-903.history: The Mitra were the lords of Mitari on the eastern arm of the delta and the other half of Ranpur's founding marriage. For three centuries they served the Chandar as first vassals and married their daughters. In 9 BR, in the fourth failed monsoon of the Sleeper's Dim, the temples crowned Arun Mitra. When the rains returned in 6 BR he was called the Rainbringer. He took the first white elephant as his sign and bought his crown from the temples with the Rain Compact of 5 BR, the law that still frees temple land from tax. The Mitra widened the kingdom: Ashok Mitra took the Kesita cotton lands in 72 and Vijay Mitra finished the Red Walls in 118. They also made debt labor on temple fields a law, and the Red Walls were built with it. Their court bred poison. Uday Mitra died after a feast in 181, and in 231 Kumar Mitra was poisoned by his queen's brother, Vasant Pratap. In 233 Vasant had the last three Mitra princes drowned. The Mitra left Ranpur its greatest compact and its oldest habit of murder.
dead: Arun Mitra the Rainbringer (38 BR-21 AR): Crowned in the Dim; swore the Rain Compact. *Ruler:* Arun Mitra (Arun II the Rainbringer), Kingdom of Ranpur, 9 BR–21 (RUL-9014).
Ashok Mitra the Cotton King (14-79): Took the Jalari cotton lands. *Ruler:* Ashok Mitra (Ashok I the Cotton King), Kingdom of Ranpur, 44–79 (RUL-9016).
Kumar Mitra the Poisoned (196-231): Poisoned by Vasant Pratap. *Ruler:* Kumar Mitra (the Poisoned), Kingdom of Ranpur, 219–231 (RUL-9024).
marriages: 300 BR, with House Chandar: Tara Mitra married Surya Chandar.
215, with House Pratap: Kumar Mitra married Leela Pratap of Ganara, whose brother poisoned him.
FAM-903.secrets: The Bhaskar temple records say the Mitra paid the temples 40,000 silver weights for Arun's crown in 9 BR, before the Rain Compact was sworn.

FAM-904.y1105: Extinct in the male line since the Drowning of 588. Its blood runs in the Sagar and, through them, in the Ranavir.
FAM-904.arms: a black hill with a gold cup on its peak, on red
FAM-904.founder: Vasant Pratap the Cupbearer (199-254), lord of Ganara
FAM-904.power: None in 1105. At its height: the eastern hills, Chanari's iron, the Pepper Hills and the first war elephants.
FAM-904.history: The Pratap were lords of Ganara, a hill town at 1,396 m, and they came to the throne by poison. Vasant Pratap married his sister Leela to Raja Kumar Mitra, poisoned Kumar at a feast in 231 and held the palace with his hillmen. Fifteen Pratap rajas ruled for 357 years. The greatest, Aditya the Hill-Taker, took Chanari, the Elephant Hills and the Pepper Hills in 338 and made the Mallik catchers his Masters of Elephants. Aditya II married his daughter Amala to the Solen emperor Lucian the Fair in 447, which opened the Nagora path to western silver; he struck the first lotus coins from it. The Pratap fought hill wars for two centuries and let the delta dykes decay. Rudra III built a river palace at Mitari on the lowest ground of the delta, because the hill kings liked the sea wind in the hot months. In September 588 a cyclone drove the sea up the delta, and Keshav III and his three sons drowned in the river palace at Mitari with about 30,000 people. The temples crowned Keshav's son-in-law, Jaidev Sagar, and the Pratap blood passed to the Sagar through his wife Padma.
dead: Vasant Pratap the Cupbearer (199-254): Took the throne by poison. *Ruler:* Vasant Pratap (Vasant I the Cupbearer), Kingdom of Ranpur, 231–254 (RUL-9025).
Aditya Pratap the Hill-Taker (300-352): Took the eastern hills in 338. *Ruler:* Aditya Pratap (Aditya I the Hill-Taker), Kingdom of Ranpur, 322–352 (RUL-9029).
Princess Amala Pratap (429-481): Married Emperor Lucian the Fair of the Solen Empire in 447.
Keshav Pratap the Drowned (536-588): Drowned at Mitari with his sons. *Ruler:* Keshav Pratap (Keshav III the Drowned), Kingdom of Ranpur, 563–588 (RUL-9039).
marriages: 447, with the Solen imperial house: Amala Pratap married Emperor Lucian the Fair at Solenne.
575, with House Sagar: Padma Pratap married Jaidev Sagar of Budanga, who became Raja after the Drowning.
FAM-904.secrets: The Solen marriage treaty of 447 promised Amala's sons a claim to the Pratap throne; she bore none, and the clause was forgotten.

FAM-905.y1105: Out of power since 998. The main line ended with Harsha IV; the blood survives through Sagar daughters married to the Ranavir and through the teak lords of Budanga.
FAM-905.arms: a gold galley on blue waves under a lotus
FAM-905.founder: Jaidev Sagar the Dyke-Raiser (555-611), lord of Budanga
FAM-905.power: In 1105 only the teak yards and pepper gardens of the Budanga cadet line. At its height: the fleet of Ranpur, the delta dykes and the Chanari Compact.
FAM-905.branches: the teak lords of Budanga (a cadet line, unprofiled)
FAM-905.history: The Sagar were the teak and ship lords of Budanga. Jaidev Sagar married Padma, daughter of Raja Keshav III Pratap, and when the Pratap drowned in 588 the temples crowned him. Eighteen Sagar rajas ruled for 410 years. They raised the dykes and kept them up, built the fleet, and made Ranpur a sea power when the Neck road closed: Mahendra II built Ranpur Light and 40 galleys in 706. They fought pirates and the Amber harbor chiefs for the cotton ships. They lost Raja Amar II to the Black Cough in 919. Their greatest king, Mahendra IV the Rice-Giver, fed Emberdeep in its hungry years and won the Chanari Compact of about 950, which made Chanari the only human city that knows crucible steel. Mahendra III made the Ranavir of Devesh hill captains, and Jaidev III gave them the yellow-stone mines, which raised the house that would replace them. Harsha IV lost three sons and died in March 998 with no heir, and his cousin Devendra Ranavir took the throne. Sagar daughters married into the Ranavir in 947 and 1050, so Raja Indrajit is a Sagar through his mother and his great-grandmother.
dead: Jaidev Sagar the Dyke-Raiser (555-611): First Sagar Raja. *Ruler:* Jaidev Sagar (Jaidev I the Dyke-Raiser), Kingdom of Ranpur, 588–611 (RUL-9040).
Mahendra Sagar the Seafarer (657-714): Built Ranpur Light and the fleet. *Ruler:* Mahendra Sagar (Mahendra II the Seafarer), Kingdom of Ranpur, 690–714 (RUL-9044).
Mahendra Sagar the Rice-Giver (918-962): Won the Chanari Compact. *Ruler:* Mahendra Sagar (Mahendra IV the Rice-Giver), Kingdom of Ranpur, 938–962 (RUL-9055).
Harsha Sagar the Childless (952-998): Last Sagar Raja. *Ruler:* Harsha Sagar (Harsha IV the Childless), Kingdom of Ranpur, 979–998 (RUL-9057).
marriages: 575, with House Pratap: Jaidev Sagar married Padma Pratap.
947, with House Ranavir: Lila Sagar married Rudra Ranavir of Devesh; mother of Devendra.
1050, with House Ranavir: Padmini Sagar of the Budanga line married Devraj Ranavir; mother of Raja Indrajit.
FAM-905.secrets: Budanga's teak lords keep a letter of Harsha IV naming his cousin Devendra Ranavir heir 'if no son of mine lives', which would have made the Ranavir claim lawful without the temples' gold; Devendra paid the temples anyway.

FAM-906.y1105: Hereditary Steel-Wardens of Chanari since about 950 and the only Ranpuri who speak with the Emberdeep smiths. Its last heir, Devika, is shortchanging the dwarves and hunting a dwarven exile.
FAM-906.arms: a red crucible between two crossed blades, on black
