FAM-906.founder: Ashok Varma, first Steel-Warden of Chanari (912-981)
FAM-906.power: The office of Steel-Warden: the walled smiths' quarter of Chanari, the steel tally of every blade made, the Smiths' Wall guard of about 600 men, and the right to sell Chanari blades (400 suns each in the Middle Sea). A seat on the Raja's council. The compact share owed to Clan Emberhand, one blade in twenty, passes through Varma hands.
FAM-906.branches: the Warden's line at Chanari (Devika, the only child of the last Warden); the Tharmund factors, a cousin line who keep the house's trading hall at Tharmund
FAM-906.history: Before 950 the Varma were iron merchants of Chanari, a hill town the Pratap had taken in 338. Their head, Ashok Varma, carried Raja Mahendra IV Sagar's rice up the Kesita valley to Tharmund in the dwarves' hungry years of 946 to 949, and he learned enough Holdspeech to bargain. In about 950 he was one of three men who swore the Chanari Compact with the elders of Clan Emberhand: twelve Chanari smiths would learn crucible steel, and Emberdeep would get rice in hungry years and one blade in twenty. It broke the dwarves' Judgment of 904, so it had to stay secret on both sides. Mahendra made Ashok Steel-Warden of Chanari and gave the office to his heirs. Ashok walled the smiths' quarter, set the rule that smiths teach only their sons under oath, and began the steel tally, a record of every blade forged, sold and paid to the dwarves. For a century and a half the Varma have been the only Ranpuri allowed to speak with the Emberhand smiths, and they meet them once a year at Tharmund. They served every raja. Kamala Varma, Warden from 1041 to 1072, sold the Ranavir the blades of the Steel Guard; her son, Devika's father, kept the smiths working through the Nagora War, when Chanari steel armed the Miners of Tirpur and the Raja's guard. Devika, born into the house in 1063 as her father's only child, learned the tallies from him and became Warden in 1090 at 27. She rebuilt the Smiths' Wall higher in 1096. After a bad rice year in 1100 she began paying Clan Emberhand one blade in thirty instead of one in twenty and writing off the rest as spoiled. In 1105 the house faces three dangers at once. Stonehold's Carvers want proof that Emberdeep taught Chanari, and the dwarven exile Yrsa Windbellows, who runs a hidden water-bellows mill above Chanari for the guild head Ravi Lohar, could give it to them. Ravi's hidden mill is making blades that never enter the Varma tally, including 40 for Steward Sonam of Skyhold. And Devika has no child. If she dies, the office has no heir of the blood, and the Raja would have to choose a new Warden who has never met a dwarf. The Emberhand smiths have said more than once that they swore their compact with the Varma, not with Ranpur.
dead: Ashok Varma (912-981): Swore the Chanari Compact and became the first Steel-Warden.
Kamala Varma (1016-1072): Warden who armed the first Steel Guard.
Harish Varma (1034-1090): Devika's father; kept Chanari forging through the Nagora War.
marriages: 1060, with the iron merchants of Jagkot: Harish Varma married a Jagkot iron merchant's daughter; Devika is their only child.
FAM-906.rivals: Ravi Lohar's Steel-Smiths guild, the Carvers of Stonehold
FAM-906.secrets: Since 1100 Devika has paid Clan Emberhand one blade in thirty, not one in twenty, and hidden the difference as spoiled blades. The house has always known the compact broke the Judgment of 904.

FAM-907.y1105: Lords of the Nagora March and keepers of its road forts. Its head, Rohan Nagar, commands Ranpur's army and secretly keeps two toll books.
FAM-907.arms: a white road climbing a black mountain, on saffron
FAM-907.power: Tirpur fort and the Nagora March; the 6,000 Nagora Road Wardens; a share of the Nagora tolls, plus about 9,000 lotus a year skimmed through a second book; the office of Warden, which commands the army.
FAM-907.branches: the Tirpur line (Rohan); the fort captains of the Nagora road, cousins who hold three of the road forts
FAM-907.history: The Nagar were soldiers of Tirpur. After Tessarian surveyors mapped the Nagora mule road in 969 and noted Ranpur's forts, Raja Tej III Sagar gave Tirpur fort to his captain Suresh Nagar in 971 and doubled its garrison, and the family has held it since. When the Ranavir took the throne in 998 the Nagar backed them early. In 1077 Raja Devraj gave them the building of the forts along the new Nagora cart road, and a share of its tolls for their trouble. Rohan Nagar, born into the house at Tirpur in 1055, led foot at Tiravi in 1083 and was hurt when the Dwarf's Gate tower fell in 1084. He stood at the signing of the Treaty of Tirpur in 1085 and became Warden of the Nagora March in 1092. Under him the house has grown rich and greedy. His clerks keep two books at Tirpur and pay Stonehold's 1 in 20 and the crown's share on the smaller one. Rohan leads the Northern Road party, which wants to push soldiers and caravans past Nagora into the Free Marches and join the race for the upper Tirana gold. In 1105 the Amberport merchants who bought the toll farm will send a toll farmer to Tirpur, and he will find both books.
dead: Suresh Nagar (938-1002): First Nagar captain of Tirpur.
Vasu Nagar (1030-1083): Rohan's father; built the Nagora road forts; killed at Tiravi.
marriages: 1076, with the cotton brokers of Jalari: Rohan married a broker's daughter; the match brought money for the road forts.
FAM-907.allies: House Ranavir, Ostran bankers of House Lunetti
FAM-907.rivals: House Mallik, Chief Minister Sanjay Dhar, the Old Toll of Stonehold
FAM-907.secrets: The second toll book at Tirpur hides about 9,000 lotus a year taken from the crown and from Stonehold's 1 in 20.

FAM-908.y1105: Elephant masters of the Elephant Hills. Hari heads the house and the royal elephants; his cousin Bala runs the Elephant School. Both carry secrets that touch the false calf.
FAM-908.arms: a grey elephant's head with a gold goad, on green
FAM-908.founder: Bala Mallik the Catcher (301-367), first Master of Elephants
FAM-908.power: The catching grounds of the Elephant Hills (about 60 wild elephants a year); the royal war elephants (about 560) and the Elephant Corps; the Elephant School of Nagita; sales of trained war elephants at 6,000 suns each.
FAM-908.branches: the senior line at Nagita (Hari); the junior line of the Elephant School (Bala)
FAM-908.history: The Mallik were catchers of wild elephants in the hills around Nagita long before those hills belonged to Ranpur. When Raja Aditya Pratap took the hills in 338, their chief Bala Mallik brought him 40 trained elephants, and Aditya made him Master of Elephants. The house has trained the kingdom's war elephants ever since. It is a house of two lines. The senior line catches and sells elephants. Hari, born into it at Nagita in 1050, caught his first wild elephant at 15, rode a howdah at Tiravi and became head of the house and Master of Elephants in 1088. The junior line runs the Elephant School; Bala, born into it in 1045, drove the lead elephant of the second wave at Tiravi and saw it fall into a staked pit. Both men warned Prince Indrajit against the charge at Tiravi, and both watched 40 drivers flogged for it. Bala rebuilt the School's training around noise, fire and hidden ground after 1086. The house has fallen into two secrets. Hari sold 30 war elephants through Amberport to the Spice Coast League in 1103, against the Raja's ban. Bala was paid by Keeper Anand in 1102 to train a pale cow to kneel, and has guessed why.
dead: Bala Mallik the Catcher (301-367): First Master of Elephants.
Gaja Mallik (1022-1088): Hari's father; Master of Elephants during the Nagora War.
marriages: 1074, with House Varma: A Mallik daughter married into the Varma's Tharmund factors, a trading tie, not a blood tie to the Warden's line.
FAM-908.secrets: Hari's 1103 sale of 30 war elephants to the Spice Coast is written in Amberport's market roll beside the pale calf's sale. Bala trained the false calf.

FAM-909.y1105: The oldest temple family of the Great Temple, which has given it most of its High Priests. Its head, Govind the Elder, crowns the Raja and runs the temple banks.
FAM-909.arms: a gold sun rising from a lotus, on white
FAM-909.founder: Bhaskar the Singer (about 430 BR-370 BR), keeper of the river shrine at Ranpur
FAM-909.power: The Great Temple of Ranpur and its estates; the largest of the temple banks, which lend to the crown and to Emberdeep at 12% (the Lotus Loan of 40,000 lotus); the temple courts; the right to crown the Raja under the Rain Compact.
FAM-909.branches: the High Priest's line at the Great Temple (Govind); the struck-off line of Govind's son Ravindra, who took the name Jalan (Meera Jalan)
FAM-909.history: The Bhaskar kept a shrine on a mound at the mouth of the Chanpur before Ranpur had kings. Their priests blessed the marriage of Surya Chandar and Tara Mitra in about 300 BR and drew the plan of the first Great Temple in 238 BR. In 9 BR they led the temple families that deposed the Chandar, and in 5 BR they wrote the Rain Compact and the hymn of the white elephant. Every dynasty since has been crowned by a Bhaskar or with Bhaskar consent, and each paid for it. The house keeps the oldest ledgers in Ranpur, including the one that records payments to "tasters who fell ill" in 1009, 1015 and 1026, the proof that Vikram's fame was partly staged. Govind, born into the house in 1036, became High Priest in 1078. He crowned Indrajit in 1090 and sealed the Lotus Loan with Emberdeep in 1102. His son Ravindra left the temple in 1077 to marry a cotton broker's daughter, was struck from the rolls and took his wife's name, Jalan. Ravindra's daughter Meera, born of the Bhaskar blood in 1078, now preaches the One Face against her grandfather's temple.
dead: Bhaskar the Singer (about 430 BR-370 BR): Founder of the shrine and the family.
Ravindra Jalan (1058-1096): Govind's son, struck from the rolls in 1077; died of fever.
marriages: 1077, with the Jalan cotton brokers: Ravindra Bhaskar married a Jalan and was struck from the temple rolls.
FAM-909.secrets: The house keeps the ledger of Vikram's staged poisonings. Govind does not know that the One Face preacher Meera Jalan is his granddaughter; his daughter secretly sends Meera news.

FAM-910.y1105: The richest cotton brokers of Ranpur. Its head, Amar Sethi, leads the Cotton Brokers and the One Face and holds a copy of the proof of the false calf.
FAM-910.arms: a bale of white cotton bound with blue cord, on gold
FAM-910.founder: Mohan Sethi, cotton broker of Jalari (1004-1071)
FAM-910.power: Warehouses at Ranpur and Jalari; the head of the Cotton Brokers of Ranpur; a factor's house at Amberport; money enough to fund the One Face preachers and, in secret, the debtor band of Dev the Unbound.
FAM-910.branches: the Ranpur house; the Amberport factor's house, which buys and ships cotton at Amberport
FAM-910.history: Mohan Sethi, a cotton broker of Jalari, moved his warehouses to Ranpur in 1031 and grew rich selling Jalari cotton by sea. When the Tessarian Empire collapsed in the Debt War, the Sethi lost about 20,000 lotus in Tessarian bills, and Mohan never trusted a king's paper again. His son traded with the Well merchants of Amberport, where one God and one set of scales ruled the market. Amar, born into the house in 1066, took it over in 1088 and became head of the Cotton Brokers in 1097. In 1098 a temple court seized a broker's warehouse for debt, and Amar began to preach the One Face: the thousand gods are one god, and temple courts and 12% loans are not holy. In 1103 his factor at Amberport copied the market roll entry for the pale calf, and Amar has held it since, waiting for Moon-Pearl to die. He funds the preacher Meera Jalan openly and the debtor rebel Dev the Unbound in secret. If the temples win the Raja, he has said, the brokers will move their money and their ships to Amberport, and the crown will lose its best customers for the market tax.
dead: Mohan Sethi (1004-1071): Founded the house at Ranpur; drowned in the cyclone of 1071.
marriages: 1090, with a Well-faith merchant family of Amberport: Amar married the daughter of an Amberport spice broker.
FAM-910.secrets: Amar holds a copy of the Amberport roll entry for the pale calf and pays Dev the Unbound's band to burn the temple ledgers.

FAM-301.y1105: Split between two crowned claimants at war since 1061: Queen Livia holds Tessar and the south under the Temple, Prince Andros holds the north under the Dawn Church. Five living people carry the blood, and the only one of the next generation is Prince Nikos.
FAM-301.arms: a white open hand with six fingers on a field split green and gold
FAM-301.founder: Kallias Tessaran (603–668), post-rider of the Imperial Post and first Master of the Neck Road
FAM-301.power: Divided. Livia: Tessar and the Crown Lands, Albina South, 12 galleys, a field army of about 14,000 with hired companies, the Queen's Six-Fingers (600), the Tessar mint and about 60 jars of fire-oil. Andros: Calossa North, Vitella, Lorino, Feleria and Doria, about 13,000 men at Coreria including 1,200 Dawn Lances and about 4,000 Velgradan volunteers, and a mint at Calossa. Each side collects the Neck road tolls on its own stretch.
FAM-301.branches: The line of Anselm: Queen Livia at Tessar; The line of Damian: Prince Andros and Prince Nikos at Calossa; The line of Lukas: Dame Helena at Tessar; The Tessarans of Feleria, cedar lords, ended in the male line in 1046; Anselm's natural son, Sir Petar Grell, unacknowledged
FAM-301.history: House Tessaran began on horseback. In the 7th century the family were post-riders of the Imperial Post at Tessar. The first of them anyone wrote down was Kallias Tessaran (603–668), born with a working sixth finger on each hand. In April 621 he carried the news of Emperor Octavian's death from Calora to Tessar in four days, and in 648 the governor of the Neck made him Master of the Neck Road, the man who farmed the road tolls and ran its post stations. His son Andronic (631–694) held the office after him, and then his grandson Leo. Leo led the Tessarian Revolt (WAR-15) and was crowned first King of Tessaria on Return Day 712. The price of the crown was a secret: Stonehold's silver and mail paid for the revolt, and the dwarves got a toll-free road. Every Tessaran king was told this at his crowning until 1047. Leo's son Theron I began the Double Crowning in 740 and made it law in 741, so that each king was anointed by both the Temple and the Dawn Church. Ten kings ruled the first kingdom (HPOL-06), father to son except once, when Leo II died of his weak heart in 781 and his brother Isidor took the crown. Leontius I, crowned king in 919, struck the Leontine in 927 and made himself Emperor in 930. His house ruled the Tessarian Empire (HPOL-05) for 117 years, and for a time it lost the hand. Leontius II, Nikandros the Gilded and Nikandros's son Crown Prince Leontius were all born with five fingers. The trait lived on in a cadet branch, the Tessarans of Feleria, founded by Leontius I's younger son Prince Isidor (920–988), who held the cedar hills around Feleria. In 995 Nikandros married his heir to Theodora of Feleria (975–1040), a six-fingered cousin, to bring the hand back to the crown. Their son Anselm was born in 998 with six working fingers on each hand, and Nikandros had it cried in the streets as a sign. The legend of the Tessaran hand dates from that birth, and so does the name Six-Fingers. Anselm was crowned at 22 in 1020, married Callista Asterio of Albina in 1021 and presided over the empire's collapse. His sons Kallias (1027–1031) and Leontius (1023–1043) died of the weak heart. His brother Damian (1002–1059) married Irena Ordane of Calossa in 1045 and had two sons, Andros and Lukas. The Feleria branch ended in the male line when its last lord, Kallias of Feleria, was killed at Calella in 1046. When Anselm died in 1061 the blood was held by his daughter Livia, his nephews Andros and Lukas, and one boy nobody counted: Petar Grell, Anselm's natural son by a Calossa laundress, born in 1057, whose sixth fingers a midwife cut off at birth. The house has been at war with itself since. Livia married Marcus Corvane of the Holy See in 1063; he died at Vitella in 1068, and their only son Leo died of the Harbor Pox in 1077. Andros married Vesna Sevrin of Velgrad in 1075; she belongs to House Sevrin by birth and to this house by marriage, and their son Nikos was born in 1077. Lukas, raised in Tessar as Anselm's ward, married Serena Asterio in 1066 and fought for Livia; he was killed by his brother's army at Felina in 1096. His daughter Helena commands the Queen's Six-Fingers. Each claimant shows the six-fingered hand to the people as proof of blood, and each calls the other's hand the cursed one. In 1105 there is one heir of the next generation, Nikos, and both claimants' readings of Leo's law point to him.
dead: Kallias Tessaran (603–668): Post-rider and first Master of the Neck Road; the first recorded six-fingered Tessaran.
Leo Tessaran the Free (671–740): Led the Tessarian Revolt and founded the kingdom. *Ruler:* Leo Tessaran the Free (Leo I), Kingdom of Tessaria (first), 712–740 (RUL-3001).
Leo II the Pale (750–781): Died of the weak heart after two years as king. *Ruler:* Leo Tessaran (Leo II the Pale), Kingdom of Tessaria (first), 779–781 (RUL-3004).
Zenon the Tollmaster (806–861): Wrote the Toll Book of 845. *Ruler:* Zenon Tessaran (the Tollmaster), Kingdom of Tessaria (first), 838–861 (RUL-3007).
Leontius I (889–961): Struck the Leontine and proclaimed the empire. *Ruler:* Leontius I (the Builder), Tessarian Empire, 930–961 (RUL-3011).
Nikandros the Gilded (943–1020): Lost Tamar, fought Stonehold and borrowed the empire into ruin. *Ruler:* Nikandros the Gilded, Tessarian Empire, 983–1020 (RUL-3013).
marriages: 995, with The Tessarans of Feleria (cadet branch): Crown Prince Leontius weds his six-fingered cousin Theodora to bring the hand back.
1021, with House Asterio: Anselm weds Callista Asterio; House Asterio becomes the empress's family.
1045, with House Ordane: Prince Damian weds Irena Ordane of Calossa; parents of Andros.
1063, with House Corvane: Livia weds Marcus Corvane in a Temple match; he dies at Vitella in 1068.
1066, with House Asterio: Lukas weds Serena Asterio; parents of Dame Helena.
FAM-301.allies: House Asterio, House Ordane, House Sevrin, House Corvane
FAM-301.rivals: House Bardun, House Lunetti, House Tamaren
FAM-301.secrets: The founding was bought with dwarven silver, Anselm took a fifth of the imperial loans and died without naming anyone. Sir Petar Grell is Anselm's natural son, and Queen Livia does not know he exists.

FAM-302.y1105: Queen Livia's mother's house and her firmest support. Its head commands her field army, its daughter's child commands her guard, and its copper secretly feeds the enemy's mint.
FAM-302.arms: a copper tower on a field of dry gold, with a green border
FAM-302.founder: Captain Justin Asterio (676–741), imperial officer who went over to Leo at Albina
FAM-302.power: The lordship of Albina and its copper hills, including the Melentia workings; Albina Fort, Castel Domano and Fort Pavella; about 2,400 southern levies; a fifth of all Albina copper; command of the queen's field army of about 14,000.
FAM-302.branches: The lords of Albina (main line); The Asterios of Castel Domano, keepers of the southern road
FAM-302.history: House Asterio began with a change of sides. Captain Justin Asterio commanded a cohort of the last imperial army in the Neck. At Albina in October 711, pinned against the coast by Leo Tessaran, he led about 3,000 unpaid men over to Leo. In 712 Leo gave him the lordship of Albina and its copper hills, and the Asterios have held Albina ever since. Their wealth is copper. The Melentia workings and the hill pits around Albina gave the kings copper for small coin and bronze fittings, and the Asterios kept a fifth. In the first kingdom they guarded the dry road south from Albina Fort, Castel Domano and Fort Pavella, and they stayed with the Temple when the north went over to the Dawn in 734. Under the empire they led the southern levies, first in the conquest of Tamar and later in the Gold Road War, where two Asterio sons died in the Nagpur gorge in 999. In 1021 Emperor Anselm married Callista Asterio (1004–1062), and the house became the family of the empress. Her brother Lord Andrian Asterio (1008–1061) held the south through the Debt War and kept Albina's copper flowing when the gold stopped. Andrian died in the first months of the civil war in 1061, and his son Corvin, 16, took up the command. Corvin is Queen Livia's first cousin through Callista. He defended Tessar in the siege of 1064 and 1065, took the queen's field army home after the disaster at Vitella in 1068, agreed the Truce of the Cedars with relief in 1087, and held the line at Coreria in 1104 only because of the Reef Crossbows. His sister Serena (1048–1089) married Lord Lukas Tessaran in 1066; her daughter Helena commands the Queen's Six-Fingers, so the queen's army and the queen's guard are both led by Asterio blood. The house is tired and poorer each year. Albina copper sells for less while the road is shut, the miners want Ostran silver instead of the queen's Leontines, and in 1095 they chose Irene Stoll as their Mistress. Since 1101 Corvin has sold Albina copper north through Hektor Wain's carters to Andros's mint at Calossa. He calls it keeping the mines alive. It also means that the enemy's coin is struck from the queen's own hills, and if it comes out, Livia loses the one house she never doubted.
dead: Justin Asterio (676–741): Brought 3,000 imperial soldiers over to Leo at Albina and founded the house.
Callista Asterio (1004–1062): Empress, wife of Anselm and mother of Queen Livia.
Andrian Asterio (1008–1061): Held the south through the Debt War; died as the civil war began.
Serena Asterio (1048–1089): Wife of Lukas Tessaran and mother of Dame Helena.
marriages: 1021, with House Tessaran: Callista Asterio weds Emperor Anselm.
1066, with House Tessaran: Serena Asterio weds Lord Lukas Tessaran.
FAM-302.secrets: Since 1101 Corvin Asterio has sold Albina copper to Prince Andros's mint at Calossa through Hektor Wain's carters.

FAM-303.y1105: Prince Andros's mother's house and the leaders of the Dawn-faith north. Rich in seized Temple land and deep in debt to Velgrad.
FAM-303.arms: a black ford-stone on a red dawn, over a field of cedar green
FAM-303.words: The Dawn Comes from the North
FAM-303.founder: Lord Basil Ordane the Elder (699–770), confirmed lord of Calossa by Theron I
FAM-303.power: Calossa Castle and the lordship of Calossa North; the Temple's northern estates seized in 1061, about a tenth of the north's farmland; the chancellorship of Prince Andros; the northern lords' levies; debts of 40,000 marks to House Koren of Velgrad with half the Calossa lands pledged.
FAM-303.branches: The lords of Calossa (main line); The Ordanes of Vitella, who hold the Vitella road
FAM-303.history: House Ordane holds Calossa, the hill town that Solen troops burned in 393. The Ordanes say one of their ancestors lived through the Burning at the bottom of a dry well, and the family has kept a copy of Severan's order ever since. What is certain is that they were hill lords of Calossa by the 8th century. When the Luminary of Tessar joined the Dawn Schism in 734, the Ordanes took the Dawn faith with the whole of Calossa, and in 742 King Theron I confirmed Basil Ordane the Elder as lord of Calossa under the Edict of the Two Altars. Since then the Ordanes have been the first family of the Dawn north, and their priests have taught reading in Eastfolk in the monastery schools. Under the empire they guarded the road to Lake Ostec. After Radoslav the Bear's victory there in 957, Calossa became the base of the northern border, and the Ordanes grew rich on fees from the Velgrad trade and close to Velgrad itself. They began to borrow from Velgradan lenders in the famine of 991. In 1045 Lady Irena Ordane (1025–1080) married Prince Damian Tessaran, Anselm's brother, who held the northern lands. Their son Andros was born at Calossa in 1047. When Anselm died in 1061, Irena's brother Lord Teodor Ordane (1022–1078) led the northern lords who proclaimed the boy king at Calossa on 12 April 1061. That year House Ordane seized the Temple's northern estates, about a tenth of the north's farmland, to pay the levies. The Temple has not forgotten, and any peace that returns those estates would ruin the house. Basil Ordane, Teodor's son and Andros's first cousin, fought at Vitella in 1068, became head of the house in 1078 and has been Andros's chancellor since 1080. He runs the prince's council at Calossa while the army winters at Coreria. The house's strength is also its weakness. After 1096 Basil borrowed from Lord Zoran Koren of Velgrad to keep the northern levies paid, and House Ordane now owes Koren 40,000 marks, with half the Calossa lands pledged as security. Basil wants Andros crowned in Tessar with every seized estate kept. He does not know that Andros's clerk is negotiating a partition at Ostra that would shut both churches out of the Neck and might hand the estates back as the price of peace.
dead: Basil Ordane the Elder (699–770): Took Calossa into the Dawn faith and was confirmed lord by Theron I.
Irena Ordane (1025–1080): Wife of Prince Damian and mother of Prince Andros.
Teodor Ordane (1022–1078): Proclaimed the boy Andros king at Calossa in 1061 and seized the Temple estates.
marriages: 1045, with House Tessaran: Irena Ordane weds Prince Damian Tessaran.
FAM-303.allies: House Tessaran, House Koren, The Priests of the East Gate
FAM-303.secrets: House Ordane owes Zoran Koren of Velgrad 40,000 marks and has pledged half the Calossa lands; if Velgrad calls the debt, the house falls.

FAM-304.y1105: Mint-masters of Tessar and the queen's secret envoys to Ostra. They serve Livia and do not love her.
FAM-304.arms: a silver coin pierced by a black quill on a field of green
FAM-304.founder: Aurel Mentis (893–960), mint clerk who struck the first Leontine
FAM-304.power: The Tessar mint and its dies; the right to assay every coin that enters the queen's treasury; the queen's envoy's seat at the Lunetti table in Ostra; knowledge of the lead gold.
FAM-304.history: House Mentis are the money-keepers of Tessar. Aurel Mentis, a mint clerk trained at Ostra, struck the first Leontine for King Leontius in 927, and his family has run the Tessar mint ever since. Olivar Mentis, born in 980, rose to Grand Treasurer of the empire. He signed the Gold Pledge of 1027, paid herders to poison 30 cattle near the Widow's Crag in 1042, sent 46 lead bars skinned with gold to Ostra in 1043, and kept a second ledger showing that Emperor Anselm took a fifth of every loan. On 11 April 1047 the mob hanged him at the treasury gate; Anselm had the prison door left open. His son Varro Mentis (1010–1082) kept the mint anyway, because nobody else could strike an honest coin. Varro told his daughter Cassia the secret of the lead gold on his deathbed in 1082. Cassia struck the debased Leontine of 1083 on the queen's order and the queen's new Leontine of 1094. Since 1102 she has been the queen's secret envoy at Ostra. She has read her grandfather's second ledger three times in Patriarch Bogdan's library. It would clear Olivar's name and blacken the queen's father.
dead: Aurel Mentis (893–960): Struck the first Leontine in 927.
Olivar Mentis (980–1047): Grand Treasurer, hanged by the mob of Tessar.
Varro Mentis (1010–1082): Kept the mint after his father's hanging.
FAM-304.secrets: Cassia Mentis knows the lead gold and has read Olivar's second ledger behind the queen's back.

FAM-305.y1105: The Dawn Church's family inside Queen Livia's capital. Its head is lesser Patriarch of Tessar and holds both Olivar's second ledger and a key to the East Gate postern.
FAM-305.arms: a red lamp-flame over a gate on a field of white
FAM-305.words: The Lamp Waits at the Gate
FAM-305.founder: Father Anatol of Tessar (701–768), chaplain of the Luminary who joined the Dawn Schism
FAM-305.power: The Church of the East Gate and the lesser patriarchate of Tessar; the Dawn Faithful of Tessar, perhaps a quarter of the city; Olivar Mentis's second ledger; access to the East Gate postern.
FAM-305.branches: The East Gate line of Tessar
FAM-305.history: The priests of the Church of the East Gate are a Dawn family in a Temple city. Their founder, Father Anatol of Tessar, was chaplain to the Luminary of Tessar who followed Bogumil into the Dawn Schism in 734. Anatol married, as Dawn priests may, and his sons kept the East Gate church after him. Under the Edict of the Two Altars the lesser Patriarch crowned each Tessarian king at dawn beside the Temple's Luminary at noon, and six of the lesser Patriarchs of Tessar have been East Gate men. In 1047 Father Matvei of the East Gate (1012–1079) heard Olivar Mentis's last confession before the mob hanged him, and was given a prayer book to keep. His son Bogdan found Olivar's second ledger sewn into its binding when Matvei died in 1079. When the Temple crowned Livia in 1061, the lesser Patriarch of the day refused to crown her at dawn, and the Double Crowning ended. Bogdan was ordained in 1062 and became lesser Patriarch in 1090. The family has kept the Dawn congregation alive inside the queen's walls for 43 years. Bogdan means to open the East Gate postern to Andros in spring. In 1105 this small line has more power over the war than any lord of the south: it holds the ledger and the gate.
dead: Father Anatol of Tessar (701–768): Founded the line when the Luminary of Tessar joined the Dawn.
Father Matvei of the East Gate (1012–1079): Heard Olivar Mentis's last confession and kept his prayer book.
FAM-305.allies: House Ordane, Patriarch of Dawn at Velgrad
FAM-305.secrets: Olivar's second ledger is sewn into a Dawn prayer book in Bogdan's library; he plans to open the East Gate postern to Andros.

FAM-921.y1105: Royal house of the Amber Isles since 890. Sultan Iskandar has the storm-sense, has not yet named an heir, and has married his sister Laila into Kesh, whose infant heir may now carry the gift.
FAM-921.arms: a blue conch shell under a grey storm cloud, on gold
FAM-921.founder: Bima Maruang the Stormwise (821-879), chief of Amberport
FAM-921.power: The sultanate: a fifth of all spice and the monopoly of Amberport's scales, the royal clove gardens of the Isle of Cloves, the harbor fee (one part in twenty) and the water-tax. 18,000 standing troops and 72,000 at full levy, 55 war galleys and 140 armed spice ships, the 2,400 Sultan's Marines. The storm-sense itself, which calls the fleets home a day before a cyclone. Debts of about 300,000 suns to House Doravelli, plus 150,000 more pledged on the 1106 cloves.
FAM-921.branches: the Sultan's line at Amberport (Iskandar; his sons Harun, born 1086, and Daud, born 1090; his daughters Salma and Aisha); the line of Adil (Adil's daughter Zahra, Iskandar's queen and cousin); Princess Laila at Kesh, born of the house and married to Prince Amani Keshari in 1101, and her son Nuru Keshari (born 1103)
FAM-921.history: The Maruang were a harbor family of Amberport with boats and clove gardens. Bima Maruang, chief from 846, was the first of them known to feel storms coming. In September 858 he kept Amberport's boats in harbor while the fleets of Tekook and Luesa drowned in the Great Cyclone, and in 859 both harbors submitted to him. His son Suria, who had the same ache, took the Path of the Well in 890, renamed himself Daud and became the first Sultan. Daud watched his sister's children cry before storms and understood that the gift ran in daughters too. In 895 he made the Law of the Closed Harbor: a Maruang daughter may marry only a cousin or a man who takes the Maruang name and lives in the palace. For two centuries the house kept its blood behind that law. Ismail built the Storm Room in the Sea Fort in 928, and from then on a Maruang with the gift, the Warden of the Winds, sat there every cyclone season. Yusuf made the spice a monopoly in 945. Harun the Stormwise let the clove lords' rebel fleet sail into a cyclone in 1009; his heir Salim, who also had the gift, was killed by an Amber Wyrm in March 1022, and Harun passed over an elder son without it to name Idris, who had it. Idris broke his father's rule. He named his elder son Harun II heir though Harun had no gift, and set the younger, Adil (1034-1070), in the Storm Room. Harun II married his cousin Maryam, who had the gift; she bore Iskandar in 1064 and Laila in 1080, and both inherited it from her. The house hid Harun's lack until Adil drowned off Tekook in 1070 and the blind fleet was broken off Kesh in October 1071. The Well-Keepers' price for silence was the Storm Watch of 1073, and Iskandar passed it in 1076. He married his cousin Zahra, Adil's daughter, in 1084. Their son Harun (born 1086) has no gift; their son Daud (born 1090) and daughter Salma (born 1088) have it. Iskandar has not named an heir, because naming the younger boy over the elder would split the court before the war. In 1101 he broke the Law of the Closed Harbor to buy Keshi ships, sending Laila to marry Prince Amani Keshari. She was born a Maruang and remains one by blood; her son Nuru, born at Kesh in 1103, is the first child of the blood born outside the house since 895.
dead: Bima Maruang the Stormwise (821-879): First known carrier of the storm-sense; won the isles in the cyclone of 858.
Daud Maruang the Convert (850-912): First Sultan; made the Law of the Closed Harbor. *Ruler:* Daud Maruang (Daud I the Convert), Sultanate of the Amber Isles, 890–912 (RUL-9101).
Sultan Harun Maruang (955-1022): The Stormwise; drowned the clove lords' rising in 1009. *Ruler:* Sultan Harun Maruang (Harun I the Stormwise), Sultanate of the Amber Isles, 980–1022 (RUL-9104).
Prince Salim Maruang (978-1022): Heir killed by an Amber Wyrm.
Prince Adil Maruang (1034-1070): Warden of the Winds who felt the storms for his brother; drowned off Tekook.
Harun II Maruang the Proud (1030-1099): Sultan who had no storm-sense and lost the fleet off Kesh. *Ruler:* Harun Maruang (Harun II the Proud), Sultanate of the Amber Isles, 1051–1099 (RUL-9106).
marriages: 1060, with House Maruang: Harun II married his cousin Maryam Maruang, who carried the gift; mother of Iskandar and Laila.
1084, with House Maruang: Iskandar married his cousin Zahra, daughter of Prince Adil.
1101, with House Keshari: Laila Maruang married Prince Amani Keshari, the first Maruang daughter with the gift to marry out since 895.
FAM-921.allies: House Keshari, House Rawang, House Karang
FAM-921.rivals: House Merah, House Ranavir, the Cloudfolk clans
FAM-921.secrets: Harun II never had the storm-sense, which is why the fleet sailed blind into the cyclone of 1071. Iskandar means to turn on the Keshi once the Isle of Pearls is taken. His nephew Nuru of Kesh may carry the storm-sense.

FAM-922.y1105: Sea lords of Tekook and admirals of the Amber fleet since 1031. Jaya Rawang commands the fleet and has secretly promised the Keshi twice what the sultan agreed.
FAM-922.arms: a bronze galley ram on dark blue
FAM-922.founder: Harith Rawang, first sea lord of Tekook (996-1058)
FAM-922.power: The Tekook naval yard and the fleet: about 55 war galleys and 9,000 rowers and sailors. Tekook (21,800 people) and its harbor dues. The office of Admiral of the Fleet.
FAM-922.branches: the sea lords of Tekook (Jaya); the Rawang galley captains, cousins who command a dozen war galleys
FAM-922.history: The Rawang were harbor chiefs of Tekook before the Maruang were anything. In the Great Cyclone of 858 their fleet was caught at sea and destroyed, and in 859 they yielded Tekook to Bima Maruang. For 170 years they were captains, not lords. Then Sultan Idris, who wanted the fleet away from the clove lords' spies at Amberport, built the naval yard at Tekook in 1031 and made Harith Rawang its first sea lord. The Rawang have led the fleet since. Jaya's father, Razak Rawang (1032-1091), commanded it in the Spice War; ten-year-old Jaya, born into the house in 1060, was aboard his galley in the battle off Tekook in 1070. A thunderbird killed Jaya's younger brother Hadi on a hunt in 1085. Jaya escorted Princess Laila to her wedding at Kesh in 1101 and became Admiral when Iskandar was crowned. In 1104 he promised the Keshi admiral Jabari Tide a third of the Isle of Pearls banks, twice the sultan's offer, to get every Keshi ship. If the sultan learns of it, the Rawang could lose the fleet they have led for 74 years.
dead: Harith Rawang (996-1058): First sea lord of Tekook.
Razak Rawang (1032-1091): Admiral in the Spice War.
Hadi Rawang (1066-1085): Killed by a thunderbird on Great Amber.
marriages: 1058, with the pilot families of Tekook: Razak Rawang married a Tekook pilot's daughter.
FAM-922.allies: House Maruang, the Keshi admiral Jabari Tide
FAM-922.secrets: Jaya has promised the Keshi a third of the Isle of Pearls banks without the sultan's knowledge.

FAM-923.y1105: Pilot family of Amberport and keepers of the floating lodestone needle. Bayu Karang heads the Pilots' Brotherhood and will not let a Keshi pilot aboard the joint fleet.
FAM-923.arms: a silver star over a black reef, on sea green
FAM-923.words: We steer by what we keep.
FAM-923.founder: Laut Karang, first sworn pilot of the Sultan (872-941)
FAM-923.power: The Pilots' Brotherhood of Amberport; the secret of the floating lodestone needle; the charts of the Eastern Gulf's shoals and reefs; a seat on the sultan's council as Master of Pilots.
FAM-923.branches: the house at Amberport (Bayu); the sworn pilot families bound to the house, who serve but are not of the blood
FAM-923.history: Laut Karang was the pilot who steered Sultan Daud's ships in the 890s, and Daud made him his sworn pilot; the office stayed in the family. The Karang kept the charts of every shoal of the Eastern Gulf, and from about 1040, in the reign of Idris, they began to steer by the floating lodestone needle, which only the pilots of Amberport, Greyhaven and Lucerna use. House law since then allows only born Karang to carry the needle bowl; pilots of the bound families steer but never touch it. Bayu, born into the house in 1057, steered a spice ship home through the cyclone that broke the fleet off Kesh in 1071 by the needle alone, at 14. He became Master of Pilots in 1090. In 1099 he broke his own house law and swore a Greyhaven boy, Col, into the house as Kalu, sent in secret by the Greyhaven pilot Garth Ferris. In 1105 the needle is the house's power and its fear: Bayu leads the Silent Needle faction and would rather sink a ship than let a Keshi pilot see the bowl.
dead: Laut Karang (872-941): First sworn pilot of the Sultan.
marriages: 1080, with House Rawang: Bayu's sister married a Rawang galley captain.
FAM-923.allies: House Maruang, the pilots of Greyhaven
FAM-923.rivals: House Rawang, the pilots of Kesh
FAM-923.secrets: The house has taken in a foreign-born boy, Kalu of Greyhaven, against its own law. A bound pilot, Arif Senyap, drowned a ship's boy who lifted the needle-box lid in 1096.

FAM-924.y1105: The greatest clove lords of the Isle of Cloves and leaders of the Clove Lords faction. Lady Dewi Merah refuses to fund the Pearl war and smuggles surplus cloves to Kesh.
FAM-924.arms: three red clove buds on white, with a green border
FAM-924.words: The tree remembers who planted it.
FAM-924.founder: Kasim Merah, clove lord of Luesa (771-838)
FAM-924.power: The largest clove gardens of the Isle of Cloves outside the sultan's own, perhaps a quarter of all cloves; the port of Luesa (3,000 people); the leadership of the clove lords, who pay most of the spice fifth; tappers in the highland amber-gum forests.
FAM-924.branches: the Luesa line (Dewi, the only child of the last lord); the Paamu cousins, nutmeg growers of the Nutmeg Bays
FAM-924.history: The Merah were planting clove gardens at Luesa on the Isle of Cloves by 800, when Kasim Merah fenced the wild clove groves of the west coast and made them gardens. By the 850s they were the richest family of the isles. Their fleet was caught at sea in the Great Cyclone of 858, and in 859 they swore to sell their cloves through Amberport. For the next 150 years the Merah fought the Maruang with money instead of ships. They sold cloves privately to Keshi and Ranpuri captains in the Luesa roads until Sultan Yusuf's Law of the Scales in 945 made it a crime. In September 1009 Lord Anwar Merah led the clove lords' rising, 44 ships sailing to take Tekook. A cyclone that Sultan Harun had felt coming wrecked them on the Tekook shoals, and Harun took Luesa. Anwar was spared, but the house paid 5,000 dinars and lost the right to keep armed ships. The Merah turned to the courts and the council. In the Spice War they took a share of the Keshi harbor fees and supplied cloves for the fleet's loans; at the Treaty of Madamo in 1072 Dewi's father lost the fees, which Kesh had refused, and never forgave the court that bargained them away. Dewi, born into the house in 1058 as its only child, ran the gardens from 1080 and became head in 1088. She watched the sultan's men burn 2,000 bales of Merah cloves in Amberport harbor in 1101, and since 1102 she has sold about 300 bales a year of the cloves meant for burning through Keshi smugglers at Madamo. In the hills her tappers are raided every season by the Cloud Ridge clan, which spares House Batu's. She leads the Clove Lords on the council and means to refuse the spice fifth for the Pearl war unless the Keshi harbor fees are restored. She does not know that the Grand Vizier has already pledged the 1106 crop, much of it hers, to House Doravelli. She has no child, and the Paamu cousins who grow nutmeg in the Nutmeg Bays wait to inherit; the Chief Well-Keeper, Hamid Sari, was born at Paamu and listens to her grievance. If the Merah refuse the fifth, the sultan loses about a quarter of his spice income in the year he most needs it. The house keeps its nutmeg ledgers in the Paamu well-house, where only a Merah steward may read them.
dead: Kasim Merah (771-838): Made the wild clove groves of Luesa into gardens.
Anwar Merah (968-1031): Led the clove lords' rising of 1009.
Rashid Merah (1026-1088): Dewi's father; lost the Keshi harbor fees at Madamo.
marriages: 1056, with the Paamu nutmeg growers: Rashid Merah married a nutmeg grower's daughter of Paamu.
FAM-924.allies: the Well-Keepers of Amberport, Keshi smugglers of Madamo
FAM-924.secrets: Dewi smuggles about 300 bales of cloves a year to Kesh against the Law of the Scales.

FAM-925.y1105: Frontier lords of the Highland March and amber-gum tappers. Hamzah Batu is Warden of the Highlands and keeps a secret truce with the Cloud Ridge clan.
FAM-925.arms: a black spear across a green mountain, on amber
FAM-925.founder: Hasan Batu, first Warden of the Highlands (1001-1063)
FAM-925.power: The Highland March and the Aming Stockade; the 4,000 Highland Spears; the Spear Yard of Aming; the wyrm bounty, which the Warden pays out (more than 40,000 dinars since 1094); the house's own amber-gum tapping camps, spared by the Cloud Ridge clan.
FAM-925.branches: the Warden's line at Aming (Hamzah); the tapper families of Wean and Warira who work for the house
FAM-925.history: Hasan Batu was a tapper's son of Great Amber who killed eleven Amber Wyrms for the bounty Sultan Harun set after 1022. When Sultan Idris crossed the Moss Line in 1034, he gave Hasan the new Highland March and the stockade at Aming. The Batu have held the march since, and they are hated by the Cloudfolk and envied by the coast. The house fights every dry season. Hamzah, born into it at Aming in 1062, led his first spear patrol at 18 and survived three days of bleeding after a young wyrm bit him in 1084. His Spears killed the Cloud Ridge chief in 1086. He became Warden in 1094 and has paid out more than 40,000 dinars in wyrm bounty since. In 1100 he met the dead chief's son, Lintang Cloudwalker, alone at Amtiuan Falls and made a secret bargain: the clan sells Batu amber-gum cheap and raids only other houses' tappers. At court he calls Lintang his worst enemy and asks for 1,000 more spearmen. His father Yusri, Warden before him, died of a wyrm bite in 1094, and the house has buried four of its men to the same venom since 1034.
dead: Hasan Batu (1001-1063): First Warden of the Highlands.
marriages: 1085, with the tapper families of Wean: Hamzah married a tapper headman's daughter of Wean.
FAM-925.allies: the Spear Yard of Aming, TRB-901 (in secret)
FAM-925.rivals: House Merah, House Rawang, the Grand Vizier Rahim Sulong
FAM-925.secrets: House Batu's truce with the Cloud Ridge clan means the clan's raids fall on House Merah and the Vizier's licence-holders.

FAM-221.y1105: Leading pirate family of Blackreef, the only crew-family with a house name. Captain-General Nell Brine has held the Table since 1094, but land-sickness keeps her at sea and Ima Redsail wants her seat.
FAM-221.arms: a white gull riding a black wave, on sea green
FAM-221.words: The Sea Stands Still For Us
FAM-221.founder: Mag Brine (1020–1078), son of Tamsin of Brinehole, Captain-General from 1050
FAM-221.power: The Captain-General's chest at the Shrine of the Dice; the flagship Drowned Queen and about eight galleys crewed by Brine kin and sworn men; command of the Forty and the Ratrock oil caves through the Oil-Keeper Sten the Quiet; the secret oil compact with Sabra; the sealed 1011 Tessarian contract; the 800 Reef Crossbows hired to Queen Livia; the loyalty of the Quartermaster Jonas Keel.
FAM-221.branches: Nell's line at the Shrine of the Dice; The Brinehole cousins, salt-boat families descended from Tamsin's other children, who crew the Captain-General's galleys
FAM-221.history: The Brines take their name from Brinehole, a salt-boat hamlet on Blackreef Isle. Tamsin of Brinehole, born in 998, rowed the salt boats in any sea and was never sick; she handfasted with an oarsman of Harl Gannet's galley about 1018, and their son Mag was born in 1020. Mag went to sea at six. The crews called him Mag of Brinehole and then Mag Brine, and his children kept the name, the only house name the Brotherhood allows. In the hungry winter of 1049–1050 Mag sailed to Sabra and back through the storms, and the Table voted out the Gannets and elected him. In April 1051 he made the secret oil compact with Emir Farid, and on 12 July 1051 he burned three Lucernan ships in the Strait and gave the Middle Sea its dragon. He won the Corsair War without a battle in the open and made the Peace of Ratrock in 1056. On land he suffered: for days after every voyage the ground swayed under him. He died ashore on 3 April 1078 after a fall on a stair. His son Rook, born in 1040, had the same balance and was elected at once. Rook handfasted with a salter's daughter of Gull Isle, kept the toll, the oil and Lucerna's fifth, and kept the peace with the Sunland ports. The balance that saved his father in winter storms made him trust weather his crews feared, and in October 1094 he and all 90 aboard his galley drowned off Wreck Isle. His daughter Nell, born in 1061, sailed from six and has never been seasick. The Table elected her in November 1094. She has kept Emir Karim's oil coming since 1086 and hired the Reef Crossbows to Queen Livia in 1104. Since about 1100 the land-sickness has not left her between voyages, and she spends more days at sea each year, which leaves the Shrine of the Dice to her Quartermaster and the Table to her rivals. She has one son, born in 1084, who sails on the Drowned Queen and has the Brine balance; the Table owes him nothing. The Brines hold the Brotherhood's two great secrets, the oil and the 1011 contract, and Nell has secretly offered the second to King Aurelio II of Morhaven for 20,000 suns.
dead: Tamsin of Brinehole (998–1061): First of the sea-steady; rowed the salt boats in winter.
Mag Brine (1020–1078): Captain-General 1050–1078; made the oil compact and Dragon Night. *Ruler:* Mag Brine (of the Dragon Night), Blackreef, 1050–1078 (RUL-2205).
Rook Brine (1040–1094): Captain-General 1078–1094; lost at sea off Wreck Isle. *Ruler:* Rook Brine, Blackreef, 1078–1094 (RUL-2206).
marriages: 1018, with The Gannets: Tamsin of Brinehole handfasts with an oarsman of Harl Gannet's galley; their son is Mag Brine.
1059, with Salters of Gull Isle: Rook Brine handfasts with a salter's daughter; their daughter is Nell.
FAM-221.allies: House Sabrani, House Doravelli, House Vanni, The Coyle kin
FAM-221.rivals: The Redsails, House Falcone, The Gannets
FAM-221.secrets: The Brines keep the truth of the dragon, Lucerna's secret fifth and the sealed Tessarian contract of 1011. Nell has offered the contract to Morhaven without the Table's vote, a breach of the Articles.

FAM-222.y1105: A crew-family of Ratrock that has raided for three generations. Ima Redsail commands nine ships, leads the Old Articles and means to vote Nell Brine out.
FAM-222.arms: a red sail on a black hull, on grey
FAM-222.founder: Hob Redsail (1002–1060), a Ratrock captain who dyed his sails with madder taken from a Lucernan prize in 1031
FAM-222.power: Nine galleys and about 700 sworn crew, the largest following after the Brines; the Old Articles faction of the young crews; boarders trained at the Dice Yard; a spy on the Captain-General's flagship; debts of 300 marks to the Caulkers of Ratrock.
FAM-222.branches: The Ratrock crews of the Red Dice and eight other galleys
FAM-222.history: Hob Redsail was a Ratrock captain under the Gannets who took a Lucernan cloth ship in 1031 and dyed every sail of his crew red with its madder, so that merchants would know whose ships they were before they could run. The name stuck. Hob voted for Mag Brine in 1050 and sailed on Dragon Night in 1051. The dragon toll of 1056 made the Redsails poorer, because a ship that has paid may not be taken, and raiding is what the Redsails know. Hob's son Cob, born in 1040, took the crews in 1060 and chafed under Rook Brine's peace. In July 1096 Cob took five galleys to raid Felano without the Captain-General's leave. Dame Serena Falcone saw them 28 km out, the harbor chain rose, and Cob was hit by a tower crossbow and died at sea on the way home. His daughter Ima, born in 1070, was chosen captain of the Redsails in 1097 and has built them up to nine ships. She has spoken against Lucerna's fifth of the toll at every Share Day since 1100. In 1102 she took a Varennan cog that had paid the toll, killed its crew and scuttled it; Varenna's admiral lists it as sunk by Old Ironjaw. She wants Nell Brine's seat, an end to the fifth, and open raiding again.
dead: Hob Redsail (1002–1060): Dyed the sails red in 1031; sailed on Dragon Night.
Cob Redsail (1040–1096): Raided Felano without leave and died of a tower crossbow bolt.
FAM-222.rivals: The Brine line, The Coyle kin, House Falcone
FAM-222.secrets: In 1102 Ima Redsail took and scuttled a Varennan cog that had paid the dragon toll, a breach of the Articles and of the Peace of Ratrock that Varenna blames on Old Ironjaw.

FAM-223.y1105: Toll-takers and fish-salters of Gull Isle and Ratrock. Wystan Coyle is Toll-Master of the Strait, skims the toll and lets Sarto ships pass unpaid.
FAM-223.arms: a silver fish over a gold coin, on blue
FAM-223.founder: Aled Coyle (1026–1088), a Gull Isle fish-salter who became one of the first toll-takers after the Peace of Ratrock
FAM-223.power: The office of Toll-Master and the toll boats of Ratrock, which collect about 45,000 marks a year in Lucernan crowns; about 40 salt-fish boats working the Bone Coast; the salting camps of Gull Isle; a skim of about 1 crown in 25; wine and grain from the Isle of Vines each autumn.
FAM-223.branches: The Ratrock toll boats; The Gull Isle salting camps and the Bone Coast fishing boats
FAM-223.history: The Coyles were fish-salters of Gull Isle who worked the cold waters off the Bone Coast. When the Peace of Ratrock began the dragon toll in 1056, the Brotherhood needed men who could count and who knew every boat on the Strait lane. Aled Coyle was one of the first toll-takers, and his kin have run the toll boats since. His son Wystan, born on Gull Isle in 1055, sailed the toll boats from 1071 and became Toll-Master in 1089. In 1090 Wystan made a private deal with Lord Enzo Sarto of Ostra: Sarto ships pass the Strait untolled, and wine and grain from the Isle of Vines come to Blackreef each autumn through Jonas Keel. Since the dry winter of 1093 he has under-reported the toll by about 1 crown in 25 and kept the difference for the Coyle salt-fish boats. In 1099 a toll-boat hand was drowned at the Drowning Post for a short count that was Wystan's own skim; the dead man's son, the Shoal Pilot Lark Shoalwise, knows it. Wystan now wants the toll raised to 1 in 30 when the sea opens, against the wishes of Lucerna's Doge and of Nell Brine.
dead: Aled Coyle (1026–1088): One of the first toll-takers of 1056.
FAM-223.secrets: Wystan Coyle skims the dragon toll, a Drowning Post crime under the Articles, and let an innocent toll-hand drown for it in 1099.

FAM-224.y1105: The founding crew-family of the Brotherhood, which held the Captain-General's seat three times before 1050. In 1105 the Gannets captain three galleys out of Anchorwharf and vote with the Old Articles.
FAM-224.arms: a white gannet diving, on dark blue
FAM-224.founder: Harl Gannet (951–1004), a Tessarian galley master who became the first Captain-General
FAM-224.power: Three galleys and about 250 sworn crew at Anchorwharf; three votes at the Captains' Table; the memory of the Articles, which Harl Gannet wrote.
FAM-224.history: Harl Gannet was a galley master of the Tessarian navy, paid off after the Peace of Talim in 989. He sailed west with his crew to the Corsair Isles, where he found a dozen quarrelling captains and no law. In 990 he got them to swear the Articles at the Shrine of the Dice, and they elected him the first Captain-General. He taught them to fight a navy the way he had been taught to fear: at night, in the shoals, never in open water. He died ashore in 1004. His daughter Sabel was elected after Brask Ninefingers died at Morhaven in 1011. She rebuilt the fleet and kept the sealed Tessarian contract in the chest, hoping the unpaid 30,000 Leontines would one day come. Her son Corrin, elected in 1027, sold captured galleys to Sabra's rebels and grew rich on Lucernan grain ships, but in the hungry winter of 1049 he kept the fleet beached while Mag Brine sailed to Sabra for grain. The Table voted him out in January 1050. The Gannets have never won the seat back. They captain three galleys out of Anchorwharf, remember that Mag Brine's father rowed on a Gannet galley, and vote with Ima Redsail's Old Articles, which they say keep Harl's law better than the Brines do.
dead: Harl Gannet (951–1004): Wrote the Articles; first Captain-General. *Ruler:* Harl Gannet (the Founder), Blackreef, 990–1004 (RUL-2201).
Sabel Gannet (979–1027): Captain-General 1011–1027; kept the Tessarian contract. *Ruler:* Sabel Gannet (the Keeper), Blackreef, 1011–1027 (RUL-2203).
Corrin Gannet (1001–1063): Captain-General 1027–1050; voted out for Mag Brine. *Ruler:* Corrin Gannet, Blackreef, 1027–1050 (RUL-2204).
marriages: 1018, with The Brine line: An oarsman of Harl Gannet's galley handfasts with Tamsin of Brinehole, mother of Mag Brine.
FAM-224.secrets: Sabel Gannet kept a copy of the 1011 contract's terms in her own share-book, which the Gannets still hold; they could prove the second 30,000 was promised even if the Brines sell the original.

FAM-521.y1105: Ruling clan of the Tusk Clans. Urza is War-Mother and holds the toll chests at Grakmar, but she fainted from heat at the Great Ride of 1104, and her heir Shara is 18 and untried.
FAM-521.arms: a red woolly rhino horn on undyed grey hide, beneath two crossed spears
FAM-521.power: The War-Mother's toll chests at Grakmar, which take in about 120,000 suns a year in silver and goods and hold about 200,000; one horse in twenty-five from every clan; the Ironhide Hearth Band of 800; command of a full levy of about 40,000; the clan's own herds of about 30,000 horses; Drevna's 2,000 bushels of winter rye, received in the War-Mother's name.
FAM-521.branches: The Grakmar hearth: Urza and her children Shara (born 1086), Grak (1089) and Tuv (1092); The married-out lines of Grakka's children in the Whitehorn, Kraoth, Gorak, Turquoise Hills and March clans; carriers among them take the Ironhide name at 13 and ride in the Hearth Band; Uzma's younger lines, herd-masters at the Gnarkul camp
FAM-521.history: Clan Ironhide was the Grakmar clan until a girl named Uzma, born in 971, showed what its blood could do. As a child she never cut her feet on the stony ground. In January 988, at 17, she took three knife cuts in a fight over a stolen mare that barely passed her skin, and killed both her attackers. Four of her seven children had her thick hide. When Uzma became clan-mother in 1003 the whole clan took the name Ironhide, and its thick-skinned riders rode at the front of every raid. She died in 1022. Her daughter Kesha (994–1047) was clan-mother when Gorath's envoys came to Grakmar in June 1042, and sent them home with their 300 horses: no living chief is holy. In July 1047 Kesha died of heat on a summer ride to Kraoth, the first of the line whose death the hides blame on the sun, and her daughter Grakka became clan-mother at 17. Grakka married Harn the Quiet, a caravan guard of the Kraoth clans, in 1045; he died in 1071. She bore nine children. In the six summers from 1056 she promised or married most of them, and six of her sisters' children, into 19 clans, choosing by skin so that the thick hide stayed at Grakmar. The eldest, the twins Bruk and Hessa, were born in 1046. Her eldest son, Bruk, was killed at the gate of Zorin in 1063. On 21 June 1062 she killed the year's rhino and 31 clans swore to her. She won the Tusk War, made the Toll of Kraoth and ruled the league for 18 years, and died of heat at the Great Ride of 1080. By eastern custom the youngest daughter keeps the mother's hearth, and Grakka's youngest daughter was Urza, born in 1066. The clan-mothers chose her at 14, with Mother Krasha's council ruling until 1082. Urza married Toren of the Gorak clans in 1084; he died in 1099. Their only daughter, Shara, born in 1086, is heir; their sons Grak and Tuv do not carry the hide. Shara joined the Ironhide Hearth Band at 13. Urza, who had lost her brother Bruk at Zorin, held her back from the rhino trial until she was 18, and she won her right to speak in council in the spring of 1104, at a rhino trial where in truth Garn Hornbreaker made the kill. That June Urza fainted from heat in her tent at the Great Ride. The Ironhide Hearth Band, formed by Grakka in 1066 with 400 riders and 800 strong since the Second Spear of 1098–1103, is made of carriers from every branch of the clan. Any child of Ironhide blood who shows the hide takes the Ironhide name at 13 and rides in it, wherever it was born. So the clan's blood runs through half the league, and every carrier answers to Grakmar.
dead: Uzma Ironhide (971–1022): First carrier of the thick hide; gave the clan its name.
Kesha Ironhide (994–1047): Turned away Gorath's envoys in 1042; died of heat.
Grakka Ironhide (1030–1080): First War-Mother of the Tusk Clans; won the Tusk War. *Ruler:* Grakka Ironhide (the Rhino-Taker), League of the Tusk Clans, 1062–1080 (RUL-5011).
Bruk Ironhide (1046–1063): Grakka's eldest son; killed at the gate of Zorin.
marriages: 1045, with The Kraoth toll clans: Grakka marries Harn the Quiet, a caravan guard; father of her nine children.
1061, with The Tallyhands of Kraoth: Grakka's daughter Tula marries into the Tallyhands of Kraoth.
1060, with The Whitehorn line: Grakka's daughter Hessa marries into a Whitehorn camp of the Tuknak.
1084, with The Gorak clans: Urza marries Toren; father of Shara, Grak and Tuv.
FAM-521.allies: The Tallyhands of Kraoth, The Whitehorn line, Clan Harrak
FAM-521.rivals: The Line of Gorath, House Dravic, House Zorac
FAM-521.secrets: Urza fainted from heat at the Great Ride of 1104. Shara froze at her rhino trial and Garn Hornbreaker made the kill.

FAM-522.y1105: Chiefs of the five Whitehorn clans, the largest kin of the central steppe. Hrok Whitehorn is War-Captain of the Tusk Clans and leads the Plough-Burners against Drevnan settlers.
FAM-522.arms: a white rhino horn on red-brown hide
FAM-522.power: About 120,000 people in five sworn clans and about 3,000 riders; the Tuknak grass and the far rhino valleys; the Otsai horse lines; the War-Captain's post; the first right to the Tuknak rhino trials, granted by Grakka in 1062.
FAM-522.branches: The Tuknak chiefs' line, Hrok's own; The Otsai horse-masters, who keep the Wind horse lines taken in 916; The camp of Grakka's daughter Hessa, married into the Tuknak in 1060
FAM-522.history: About 790 a young clan-mother named Tarsha killed on foot, with one spear, a woolly rhino with a pale horn on the Tuknak grass. It was the first white horn in the songs. The kill won her kin the Tuknak valleys from two rival camps, and they took the name Whitehorn. Tarsha died about 841. Her clans made the rhino trial their law more strictly than any other, and their youths still face more rhinos each spring than any other kin. The Whitehorns paid one horse in ten to the Wind camp at Otsai from 889. In August 916, with the Black Cough killing the garrison, they burned the camp and drove off its 900 horses, and lost about 1,500 of their own to the cough that winter. The Otsai horse lines are still the best mounts on the Tuknak grass. The Whitehorns were the last of the 31 clans to agree to Grakka's oath. Their price was the first right to the Tuknak rhinos, and in 1060 they took one of Grakka's daughters, Hessa, into a Whitehorn camp. Their chief, Ruk Whitehorn (1022–1064), was killed leading the Whitehorn wave at Zorek in 1064. His sister Mother Olva (1040–1094) led the clans for 30 years. Olva's son Hrok, born in 1068, stood among the Whitehorn youths at the Great Ride of 1080 when Grakka fell in the heat. In the spring of 1083 he killed a woolly rhino with a pale horn on foot with one spear, the first white horn since Tarsha, and the clans took it as a sign and gave him the name. He became chief at Olva's death in 1094 and War-Captain of the Tusk Clans in 1098. Hrok has burned every Drevnan plough found east of the cairns since then. In November 1104 his riders burned two farms past the Thardush line and a family of six died in one; he told the War-Mother the settlers had fled. His scouts saw who really killed the heir's rhino in 1104, and he keeps that knowledge for the day the clan-mothers choose the next War-Mother.
dead: Mother Tarsha White-Horn (about 772–841): Killed the first white-horned rhino; founder of the Whitehorn clans.
Ruk Whitehorn (1022–1064): Chief of the Whitehorns; killed at Zorek.
Mother Olva Whitehorn (1040–1094): Led the Whitehorn clans 1064–1094; Hrok's mother.
marriages: 1060, with Clan Ironhide: Grakka's daughter Hessa marries into a Whitehorn camp.
1079, with Clan Harrak: A Whitehorn rider marries Mother Hurga of Clan Harrak; father of the twins Morga and Zagra.
FAM-522.rivals: The Tallyhands of Kraoth, Clan Harrak, House Zorac, House Dravic
FAM-522.secrets: Hrok's riders killed a family of six in November 1104. His scouts saw Garn Hornbreaker kill the heir's rhino.

FAM-523.y1105: Counting family of the Kraoth toll clans. Gurz the Toll-Keeper, Master of the Silk Tolls, counts every bolt of silk that goes west, means to raise the toll again and banks toll silver in Drevna.
FAM-523.arms: a knotted counting cord with a silver bead, on undyed felt
FAM-523.power: The count of the Kraoth toll, one part in ten of every silk caravan, about 40 caravans a year; one part in five of the toll kept at Kraoth for the counters and the 1,600 Toll Riders; the earth-walled toll camp and its storehouses; about 12,000 suns on deposit with House Lubec at Lubany since 1099; leadership of the four Kraoth toll clans, about 78,000 people.
FAM-523.branches: Hulda's line: Gurz and his sisters, who keep the Kraoth count; The Thardush tally-keepers, who count the Drevnan rye and the western toll camp; Tula Ironhide's children, born to the Tallyhands after 1058
FAM-523.history: Kraoth is the first camp on the silk road from the east, and its kin took gifts from caravans before anyone counted them. Around 840 Mother Zelga of Kraoth began to count the caravans and their gifts on knotted cords, one knot for a bolt, a bead for a horse, and her kin were called the Tallyhands. Zelga died about 880. Her daughters learned the trade-speech of the caravans and adopted human and half-orc guides into the camp. From 889 to 916 the Wind camp at Otsai took a tenth of every caravan's goods, and the Tallyhands counted it for the Khan's men. They learned what one toll in one place could bring in. When the Wind camps fell, the road went back to camp gifts, and for 150 years the Tallyhands counted gifts that every camp from Kraoth to the Lakeland took in turn. In 1061 Grakka Ironhide's daughter Tula married into the family, and the Kraoth clans swore to Grakka in 1062. In June 1067 Grakka made the Toll of Kraoth: one part in twelve, at Kraoth only. The Tallyhands agreed because they would keep the count while the chests stood at Grakmar, and because a single toll guarded by Toll Riders would bring more caravans. It did: from about 20 to about 40 a year by 1080. Mother Hulda Tallyhand (1035–1088) kept the count for 21 years and kept it flowing through the regency years of 1080 to 1082. Hulda's son Gurz, born in 1061, learned to count at six, as toll children do. When Hulda died in March 1088, War-Mother Urza made him Master of the Silk Tolls over two older Tallyhands. In 1098 he made Toruk Chainsilver captain of the Toll Riders. He raised the toll to one part in eleven in 1100 and to one part in ten in 1103, and since 1099 he has kept about 12,000 suns of Kraoth toll silver with House Lubec at Lubany, a Drevnan house the Plough-Burners would call the enemy. The Tallyhands live half like merchants: they keep silver in chests, not herds, and the other clans look down on them a little. They want peace with Drevna and Velgrad above all, because a war on the Thardush line would empty the road.
dead: Mother Zelga Tallyhand (about 815–880): First counter of the caravans.
Mother Hulda Tallyhand (1035–1088): Kept the Kraoth count from 1067 to 1088.
marriages: 1061, with Clan Ironhide: Grakka's daughter Tula marries Hulda's brother Orm Tallyhand.
1082, with The Kraoth toll clans: Gurz marries Mother Ysha of a Kraoth guide kin.
FAM-523.rivals: The Whitehorn line, The Caravan Guides' Fire, House Sevrin
FAM-523.secrets: Gurz banks about 12,000 suns of toll silver with House Lubec at Lubany (since 1099). Toruk Chainsilver, his captain, killed and buried a young guide under the Kraoth horse pens in 1103.

FAM-524.y1105: The Eldest Clan-Mother's clan. Mother Krasha leads the council of 31 clan-mothers, which can overrule the War-Mother on grazing and law, and quietly promises her granddaughter Morga as War-Mother if Urza falls.
FAM-524.arms: a broken halter on black felt
FAM-524.power: About 18,000 people and 9,000 horses at Burnak; Krasha's place as Eldest Clan-Mother at the head of the council of clan-mothers; the memory of her regency of 1080 to 1082 and the hay law that saved the herds in 1081; her friendship with Bolg the Drummer and Grel Rhinospear.
FAM-524.branches: Krasha's line at Burnak: her granddaughter Morga (born 1080) and Morga's children; Zagra Grassless, Morga's twin, cast out in 1095 and now a scout-captain of Drevna
FAM-524.history: Clan Harrak was born of slaves. Harrak the Lame was an orc thrall of the Wind garrison at Temul, lamed by a garrison horse. When the Black Cough killed the garrison in 916, he led about 300 freed thralls and their children to the Burnak grass near Grakmar and made them a clan. Its words, 'No one's horse', and its broken halter remember it. Harrak died about 951. The clan stayed small and proud, and its clan-mothers married into Grakmar more than anywhere else. Krasha was born at Burnak in 1050. At 14 she rode with Grakka's drummers at Zorek on 11 May 1064. In 1065 she bore her daughter Hurga, and in 1066 she helped make the Treaty of Thardush. When Grakka died in 1080, the clan-mothers set Krasha, 30, at the head of the council that ruled for the 14-year-old Urza. Her council's hay law saved the horses in the Great Blizzard of February 1081. She handed back the War-Mother's spear in 1082 but kept the council's powers, and she has been Eldest Clan-Mother since 1089. Hurga married a Whitehorn rider in 1079 and bore twins, Morga and Zagra, in 1080. Hurga died in a fall from her horse in 1093, and Krasha raised the girls. In October 1095 a guest of Clan Harrak was stabbed to death at Burnak in a feud over winter grass. Morga did it. Zagra, 15, took the blame so that Morga could stay Krasha's heir, and Krasha let the clan-mothers cast her out. Zagra crossed the line in 1097, hired herself to House Zorac, and since 1102 has been Drevna's scout-captain against the clans; she means to guide the Zorin crossbows to the Whitehorn camp at Thardush in the spring. Krasha wants the rye settled by talks under the Law of the Grass, not by Hrok Whitehorn's war, and she has not said no to Hodd Ryeseed's ploughing. She does not think Shara is ready. If Urza falls, she will offer the clan-mothers Morga.
dead: Harrak the Lame (about 884–951): Freed thrall of the Wind camp at Temul; founder of the clan.
Mother Hurga (1065–1093): Krasha's daughter; mother of Morga and Zagra.
marriages: 1064, with The Gorak clans: Krasha marries a Gorak rider; father of Hurga.
1079, with The Whitehorn line: Hurga marries a Whitehorn rider; father of the twins.
FAM-524.allies: Clan Ironhide, The Tallyhands of Kraoth
FAM-524.secrets: Morga, not Zagra, killed the guest in 1095. Krasha is promising the clan-mothers Morga as the next War-Mother.

FAM-732.y1105: Gone in its own name since 868. Its blood runs only in House Tamaren, whose founder Nefira was a Sethepi of Marira and whose kings descend from Queen Neferu.
FAM-732.arms: a papyrus stalk in gold on black river silt
FAM-732.founder: Sethep I, delta lord of Marira and king (about 260–205 BR)
FAM-732.power: None in 1105. At its height the Old Kingdom's crown lands and granaries; later the papyrus beds and reed estates of Marira.
FAM-732.branches: The royal line of the Old Kingdom (231–12 BR); The temple-kings of 144–210 AR; The Marira line, which bred Nefira and died out in 868; House Tamaren (see FAM-731)
FAM-732.history: House Sethepi was the last royal house of the Old Kingdom of Tamar and the root of House Tamaren. Sethep I, a delta lord of Marira, married the daughter of the last king of the old house and was crowned on the day of the Tears in 231 BR. His son Nebhet sent the first grain gift to the cattle kings of Abara about 190 BR. The house ruled for 219 years and ended in October 12 BR, when a starving crowd killed Sethep III on the Flood Stairs after the third failed flood. Its delta branch survived at Marira through the age of the temple-towns. In 144 AR the High Flood-Priest crowned one of them, Ankhaf the Reuniter, and his temple-kings ruled the valley again until the Solen took Tamar in 210 and King Khaset died in his palace. Under the Solen the Sethepi kept their papyrus beds and reed estates at Marira and married into the delta's fowling and fishing families. In 639 Nefira, daughter of the lord of Marira, borrowed silver from Lucerna and raised the delta, and in 640 she was crowned; her line took the name Tamaren. The older Marira line lived on as delta landholders and died out in 868, when its last lord left the papyrus beds to the crown. Its blood runs today only in House Tamaren, through Nefira and, since 989, through Queen Neferu.
dead: Sethep I the Delta Lord (about 260–205 BR): Founder; first Sethepi king. *Ruler:* Sethep the Delta Lord (Sethep I), Old Kingdom of Tamar, 231–205 BR (RUL-7008).
Nebhet the Giver (about 228–170 BR): Sent the first grain gift to Abara. *Ruler:* Nebhet Sethepi (the Giver), Old Kingdom of Tamar, 205–170 BR (RUL-7009).
Sethep III the Last (58–12 BR): Last king of the Old Kingdom; killed on the Flood Stairs. *Ruler:* Sethep the Last (Sethep III), Old Kingdom of Tamar, 31–12 BR (RUL-7010).
Ankhaf the Reuniter (about 110–171 AR): Crowned in 144; first of the temple-kings.
Khaset the temple-king (about 165–210 AR): Last temple-king; killed when the river gate was opened to the Solen.
marriages: 231 BR, with the twenty-eighth royal house: Sethep I married the last king's daughter and took the throne.
FAM-732.secrets: King Khaset did not walk into the river in 210: the High Flood-Priest opened the gate and Solen soldiers killed him in his palace.

FAM-106.y1105: Extinct. The male line ended when Aurelian the Pretender was strangled in 625 and his infant son died in the same summer's flux. Its blood runs on only through the women who married into House Orsano and House Brennus.
FAM-106.arms: a mailed fist holding a gold sun, on red
FAM-106.founder: Titus Ferrano (about 290-352), captain of the Felano legion, granted land at Felano after the Reform of 318
FAM-106.power: Extinct. At its height the house held the imperial throne, the Felano estates and the loyalty of the Solenne legions; Severan's household paid the legions from its own Felano olive rents in the first year of his reign.
FAM-106.branches: The imperial line of Severan the Iron (379-625); The Calena line: Honoria's husband Quintus of Calena and his heirs, who took the Ferrano name in 529
FAM-106.history: House Ferrano was a soldier family of Felano on the Morhaven coast. Its founder Titus Ferrano was a captain of the Felano legion who got land there after the Reform of 318. His grandson Severan rose to command the legions in Solenne and married into the imperial family, becoming the cousin by marriage of Cassian II. In September 379 a cupbearer paid from Severan's household poisoned Cassian with wolfsbane, and the legions acclaimed Severan. He was crowned on 1 October, not on Return Day, for fear the truth would come out, and he spent his reign in the Marches War (WAR-08), whose burning of Calossa still shames the Solen name among Marchfolk. The Ferrano emperors ruled for 233 years: Severan the Iron, Honorius the Patient, Lucian the Fair, Octavian the Wallbuilder, Aldric IV the Scholar, Honoria, Justinian III and Justinian IV. They built the Imperial Post, the Sun Road, the Crown Road and the Crown Wall, and they wrote the Twelve Books. They took the old Corvane name 'Aldric' for one of their emperors to borrow the Sunbringer's glory. When Aldric IV died without a son in 529, his daughter Honoria took the throne, and her husband Quintus of Calena took the Ferrano name, as Solen heiresses' husbands did. Justinian IV married Lady Serena of Lorina, a daughter of House Brennus, in secret in 584. Their son Aurelian was crowned by the palace guard at Midwinter 612 and called the Pretender, because the marriage record had gone missing. Valerian II had him strangled at the harbor in 625 and later paid the Needle-Keepers to keep the record hidden. It lies misfiled under 591 in the Temple archive, where the scrivener Otto Quire found it in 1099.
dead: Severan the Iron (346-409): Founder of the dynasty; conqueror of the Marches. *Ruler:* Severan the Iron, Solen Empire, 379–409 (RUL-1016).
Octavian the Wallbuilder (431-497): Destroyed the Old Horde and built the Crown Wall. *Ruler:* Octavian the Wallbuilder, Solen Empire, 462–497 (RUL-1019).
Honoria (490-553): First empress in her own right. *Ruler:* Honoria (the Empress), Solen Empire, 529–553 (RUL-1021).
Justinian IV (548-612): Last undisputed Ferrano emperor. *Ruler:* Justinian IV, Solen Empire, 584–612 (RUL-1023).
Aurelian the Pretender (585-625): The true son, strangled after the fall of Solenne. *Ruler:* Aurelian the Pretender, Solen Empire, 612–625 (RUL-1024).
marriages: 380, with House Corvane: Severan's sons married the daughters of the murdered Cassian II.
529, with The lords of Calena: Honoria's husband Quintus of Calena took the Ferrano name.
584, with House Brennus: Justinian IV secretly married Serena of Lorina of House Brennus.
FAM-106.secrets: The house began with a poisoned cup and ended with a hidden marriage; both proofs lie in the Holy See's archive.

FAM-107.y1105: Extinct in the male line since Constantine IX was killed in 759 and his two cousins died in Temple houses. A Marchfolk family on the lower Tirana truly descends from Maximus the Fair, Valerian II's grandson, and the adventurer Marek Ferryman has bought its name and story.
FAM-107.arms: a black bear standing under a gold sun, on white
FAM-107.founder: Marco Orsano (about 440-512), captain of the Crown Road forts, granted Vitia in 489
FAM-107.power: Extinct. Before 613 the house held the citadel of Vitia and the Vitia uplands; as emperors it held Solenne, the Valerian Wall and a shrinking empire that paid its soldiers in coin one part silver in four by 752.
FAM-107.branches: The imperial line of Valerian II (613-759); The Ferryman line: descendants of Maximus the Fair on the lower Tirana, unacknowledged
FAM-107.history: House Orsano were lords of Vitia in the western Sunlands. Marco Orsano, a captain of the Crown Road forts, was granted the Vitia ridge and its citadel in 489, when the Crown Wall was finished and the empire rewarded its frontier men. In the 570s an Orsano lord married Princess Cassia Ferrano, sister of Justinian IV, and their grandson Valerian was the only adult male of imperial blood in the west when Justinian died in 612. The western legions raised him at Varenna in 613. After Venora he fell back to his own citadel of Vitia and held the west on Varenna's wheat. He won the War of the Three Emperors (WAR-13) by poison and by buying the Temple, and was crowned Valerian II in 625. His house ruled for 134 years: Valerian II, Theodoric I, Justin V, Honorius II and Constantine IX, with the rival Maximus the Fair crowned by the eastern bishops. The Orsano emperors built the Valerian Wall and lost Tamar, the Southland ports, the Neck, the east and finally Varenna. Their own Vitia fell to Galen Valdane's siege in 747. When Constantine IX was killed on Ash Night 759, his cousins were sent to Temple houses and died without heirs. Maximus the Fair had two sons by a Marchfolk wife while he lived as a ferryman on the Tirana; his imperial sun ring lies in a Marchland saints' shrine on the lower Tirana. In 1094 Marek Ferryman, son of a Varennan deserter, paid that family 40 suns for its name and tale.
dead: Valerian II (590-654): Won the War of the Three Emperors. *Ruler:* Valerian II, Solen Empire, 625–654 (RUL-1026).
Theodoric I (631-702): Won the Second Succession War; made the Law of the Eldest. *Ruler:* Theodoric I (the Restorer), Solen Empire, 654–702 (RUL-1027).
Maximus the Fair (633-694): Rival emperor who vanished into the Marches. *Ruler:* Maximus the Fair, Solen Empire, 654–667 (RUL-1028).
Constantine IX the Unlucky (721-759): Last Solen emperor. *Ruler:* Constantine IX the Unlucky, Solen Empire, 748–759 (RUL-1031).
marriages: 571, with House Ferrano: An Orsano lord of Vitia married Princess Cassia Ferrano, grandmother of Valerian II.
664, with The royal house of Tamar: Theodoric I married Meret, daughter of Queen Nefira, and gave up Rashira and Kadah.
FAM-107.secrets: Valerian II bought the eastern army by poisoning Octavian and paid to hide the marriage that made Aurelian the true heir. Maximus the Fair's line survives in the Marches.
