FAM-231.y1105: Extinct since Hadric III died without a son in 412 BR. Its blood passed into House Kelder through Hadric's niece, and was buried with Haldor in 13 BR.
FAM-231.arms: a copper hammer under a smoking mountain, on black
FAM-231.founder: Brannoc the Coppergate (738–676 BR), chief of the Haelwater copper clan
FAM-231.power: None in 1105. In its time: the copper lodes under Mount Hael, the furnaces of Haelhold, the tin road to Frostholm from 632 BR, and the Ash Range valleys north to Lindcester.
FAM-231.branches: The royal line of Haelhold; The copper lords of the northern valleys, descended from Queen Selwen's daughters
FAM-231.history: The Brannocs were the Haelwater clan, copper-smelters of the valley directly under Mount Hael. About 720 BR their chief Brannoc won that valley and the beach below it from the rival clans, and about 700 BR he built Haelhold and made himself king. Twelve Brannocs ruled for 288 years. Orm the Smelter turned copper into cast bronze. Brannoc II died under a fallen gallery in the deep mine. His daughter Eldra the Tin-Queen opened the sea road to the giants of Frostholm in 632 BR, the single act that made Hael rich. Hadric I, Orm II and Orm III carried the kingdom north along the Ash Range to Coldfield, Kettleholt and Lindcester, and Brannoc III the Builder raised the Copper Gate of Haelhold in 545 BR. Queen Selwen married her daughters to the copper lords of the northern valleys, which bound them to the crown for a century. The house ended with Hadric III the Last, who died in 412 BR without a son. His nephews and the copper lords fought for the crown through one summer, until the admiral Kelder married Hadric's niece and took it.
dead: Brannoc the Coppergate (738–676 BR): Founder of Haelhold and the kingdom. *Ruler:* Brannoc the Coppergate (Brannoc I), Kingdom of Hael, 700–676 BR (RUL-2301).
Eldra the Tin-Queen (668–611 BR): Opened the tin road to Frostholm. *Ruler:* Eldra the Tin-Queen, Kingdom of Hael, 640–611 BR (RUL-2304).
Brannoc the Builder (598–531 BR): Raised the Copper Gate. *Ruler:* Brannoc the Builder (Brannoc III), Kingdom of Hael, 560–531 BR (RUL-2307).
Hadric the Last (478–412 BR): Died without a son; the last Brannoc king. *Ruler:* Hadric the Last (Hadric III), Kingdom of Hael, 441–412 BR (RUL-2312).
marriages: 412 BR, with House Kelder: Hadric III's niece marries the tin-admiral Kelder, who takes the crown.
FAM-231.secrets: The Brannoc kings bought dwarf tin through the Neck before 632 BR at a price that nearly ruined them, and hid it by mixing less tin into their bronze.

FAM-232.y1105: Extinct since August 13 BR, when King Haldor and his court died at Haelhold under the eruption of Mount Hael. The Ashen's hidden priests claim to descend from the star-house priests the Kelders endowed.
FAM-232.arms: a white sail over a copper ingot, on sea blue
FAM-232.founder: Kelder the Tin-Admiral (455–398 BR), admiral of the tin fleet
FAM-232.power: None in 1105. In its time: the tin fleet of up to 40 ships, the copper of Hael, the star-house on the mountain and a fixed bronze price paid by the Solen towns.
FAM-232.branches: The royal line of Haelhold; The fleet captains of the tin road, who ended with the fleet
FAM-232.history: Kelder was the admiral of the tin fleet under Hadric III. When Hadric died without a son in 412 BR, Kelder married Hadric's niece, landed 2,000 oarsmen at Haelhold and was crowned, because the copper lords could sell nothing without his tin. Sixteen Kelders ruled for 399 years. Kelder II built the fleet to 40 ships. Kelder III the Bronze-Proud won the Bronze Feud against the Solen towns and fixed the bronze price in silver in 326 BR. Garrow the Star-King endowed the star-house on the mountain's shoulder in 240 BR, where priests cut the eclipse records into copper plates, and Rhoswen II gave those priests a tenth of the copper. The later Kelders ruled a shrinking trade: the Solen turned to iron, the upper lodes ran thin, Kelder VI closed the northern towns, and the fleet fell to 15 ships. Haldric dug deep mines into the mountain's flank, and his son Haldor, crowned in 33 BR, would not leave them. When the mountain warned from 16 BR, Haldor closed the roads. In August 13 BR the eruption buried him, his court and about 70,000 of his people. No Kelder is known to have escaped.
dead: Kelder the Tin-Admiral (455–398 BR): Won the crown by holding the tin road. *Ruler:* Kelder the Tin-Admiral (Kelder I), Kingdom of Hael, 412–398 BR (RUL-2313).
Kelder the Bronze-Proud (380–322 BR): Won the Bronze Feud. *Ruler:* Kelder the Bronze-Proud (Kelder III), Kingdom of Hael, 349–322 BR (RUL-2316).
Garrow the Star-King (282–219 BR): Endowed the star-house and its copper plates. *Ruler:* Garrow the Star-King (Garrow I), Kingdom of Hael, 248–219 BR (RUL-2320).
Haldor the Last King (60–13 BR): Closed the roads and died in the eruption. *Ruler:* Haldor the Last King, Kingdom of Hael, 33–13 BR (RUL-2328).
marriages: 412 BR, with House Brannoc: Kelder marries the niece of Hadric III, the last Brannoc.
FAM-232.secrets: Haldor's own priests warned him in writing; the copy of their scroll at the Ashen altar names him as the man who killed Hael.

FAM-702.y1105: Extinct in its own name since 803. It lives on only through House Zahiri, the branch descended from Emir Marwan's elder son Nadim.
FAM-702.arms: a silver camel on sea blue
FAM-702.founder: Kamil Idrisi, first hereditary Emir of Qadir (600–671)
FAM-702.power: None in 1105. At its height, about 760, the emirate's harbor dues, the water-tax of a tenth, Sunwall copper, 30 galleys and a garrison of 4,000.
FAM-702.branches: The emirs' line (Kamil I to Kamil II), ended 803; House Zahiri, from Nadim Idrisi's son Zahir (see FAM-701)
FAM-702.history: House Idrisi ruled Qadir as emirs for 146 years. Its founder, Kamil Idrisi, was the richest shipowner of Qadira when the Well-Keepers chose him as the third Emir in 644. He claimed descent from Prince Idris of Qadira, who fought the Solen conquest from the Sabun Pass in 258–262 and died on a Solen pension in 280, and the claim won him the town. In 668 he made the Kamil Settlement: his son Ghalib was confirmed as heir before the House of Water, and every later heir had to be confirmed the same way. The Idrisi were traders on a throne. Hisham built caravan inns with the Water Endowment, Adnan carried southern goods by sea while the Neck road was closed, Wasim built 30 galleys, and Marwan sold grain north at four times its price in the Hungry Years of 766. The house broke on its own rule. Marwan's elder son Nadim died in 770, and when Marwan died in 771 the younger son, Kamil II, took the seat over Nadim's 11-year-old son Zahir with the garrison's help. Kamil exiled Zahir in 778. In 790 Zahir came back across the Burning Waste, and Kamil fled by ship to Lucerna, where he died in 799. His son Talal hired 900 Lucernan men and landed at Miruma in 803; he was killed on the beach with most of them, and the emirs' line ended. Nadim's line kept the throne under a new name, Zahiri, after its founder.
dead: Prince Idris of Qadira (died 280): Led the Qadiri towns against the Solen conquest; the house claimed him as ancestor.
Kamil Idrisi (600–671): Third Emir and first of the house; made the Kamil Settlement (668). *Ruler:* Kamil Idrisi (Emir Kamil I the Settler), Emirate of Qadir, 644–671 (RUL-7073).
Marwan Idrisi the Grain-Seller (716–771): Richest of the emirs; grandfather of Zahir the Thirstless. *Ruler:* Marwan Idrisi (Emir Marwan the Grain-Seller), Emirate of Qadir, 752–771 (RUL-7078).
Nadim Idrisi (738–770): Marwan's elder son and admiral of the galleys; father of Zahir.
Kamil Idrisi the Younger (742–799): Took the seat from his nephew; fled to Lucerna in 790. *Ruler:* Kamil Idrisi the Younger (Emir Kamil II the Usurper), Emirate of Qadir, 771–790 (RUL-7079).
Talal Idrisi (768–803): Kamil II's son; killed landing at Miruma with 900 hired men.
marriages: 652, with House Alami: Kamil Idrisi's son Ghalib married an Alami woman, tying the emirs to Samar's kin and the House of Water.
759, with a Tamari scribe family of Marira: Nadim Idrisi married a Marira merchant's daughter, which is why Zahir found friends at Tamar in 778.
FAM-702.secrets: The house's descent from Prince Idris was written up for Kamil Idrisi in 644. A Solen pension roll in the Holy See archive shows Idris died at Solenne in 280 without sons.
